tatrātidūrāttāvat tadyathā proḍḍīnasya śakuneḥ / atisāmīpyādañjanaprabhṛtīnām / indriyaghātācchabdādīnām / mano 'navasthānācchakaṭādīnām / saukṣmyāttruṭyādīnām / vyavadhānāddhiraṇyādīnām / abhibhavātsūryaprakāśādgrahādīnām / samānābhihārādanekapradīpaprabhāṇām / caśabdādaiśvaryayogāddevādīnām / na cārhati bhavituṃ dharmasāmānyānupapatteḥ / tasmādayuktaṃ sarvamatīndriyamanumānagrāhyamiti /
  ucyate- śakyaṃ tāvatkāraṇāntarato 'nupalabhyamānaṃ kiṃcitsāmānyatodṛṣṭādanumānādadhigantum / tadyathā samīpāvasthitasya śakunerayatnena cakṣuṣā grahaṇaṃ, yathā yathā tu viprakarṣaṃ pratipadyate praṇidhāya cakṣurgṛhyate tāvadyāvatkrameṇādarśanamupasaṃprāptaḥ / tatra deśaviprakarṣe pracīyamāne 'darśanamupacīyamānamavagamyātyantādarśanamapi paścāttaddhetukamanumīyate / tathā nātisamīpāvasthitasya dravyasyāsphuṭamākāramavadhārya paścādyathā yathārādupasaṃpadyate tathā tathā pratipadyamānadarśanaśaktayo 'numātāraḥ kṛṣṇasārāñjanaprabhṛtīnāmagrahaṇamatisāmīpyādanumīyate / tathā girisaritsamudrasamīpavartinaṃ śravaṇapratighātinaṃ prāk śabdamupalabhya paścāttasminneva deśe śabdamagṛhṇānāḥ śravaṇopaghātamanumimate /
children.translated_text: Among these, [non-perception] due to excessive distance is, for example, of a bird that has flown far away. Due to excessive proximity, of collyrium and the like. Due to impairment of the sense organs, of sounds and the like. Due to instability of the mind, of a cart and the like. Due to subtlety, of the sub-atomic particles (<s>truṭi</s>) and the like. Due to concealment, of gold [hidden underground] and the like. Due to suppression, of the planets and the like by the light of the sun. Due to intermixture with what is similar, of the lights of multiple lamps. By the word 'and,' [non-perception] due to the supernatural power of <s>yoga</s>, of gods and the like. And it should not be the case that [all supersensory entities share these causes of non-perception], because of the inapplicability of a common property. Therefore it is unjustified to say that everything supersensory is to be grasped only by inference. It is replied: it is indeed possible to comprehend something that is not apprehended due to some other cause through <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> inference. For example, a bird situated nearby is grasped by the eye without effort; but as it moves further away, it is grasped only by fixing the eye, until gradually non-perception is reached. There, as the spatial distance increases, one understands that non-perception also increases, and subsequently infers that complete non-perception too is caused by that [same distance]. Similarly, having ascertained the indistinct form of a substance not situated too close, and then, as one approaches, understanding the powers of perception that progressively increase, the reasoners infer that the non-apprehension of black collyrium and the like is due to excessive proximity. Likewise, having previously perceived a sound that impairs hearing near a mountain, river, or ocean, and subsequently not grasping the sound in that very place, they infer the impairment of hearing.
And what is not established even through that is to be proved from trustworthy scripture, being beyond perception. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 6b)

tasmādapi cāsiddhamityanenāgamaviṣaye sāmānyatodṛṣṭasyānavatāramācaṣṭe / parokṣamiti viṣayaṃ prati nirdiśati / āptāgamātsādhyamiti viṣayiṇamāha / etaduktaṃ bhavati- tasmādapi sāmānyatodṛṣṭādanumānādyanna siddhyati pratyakṣagrāhyamapi svayamadṛṣṭaṃ kāraṇāntarapratibaddhaviṣayabhāvamatyantaparokṣaṃ vā svargāpavargadevatādi dharmasāmānyarahitaṃ tadāptāgamātsādhyam /
  sarvavādasiddhiprasaṅgādaprāmāṇyamiti cet syādetat, yadi tarhyāgamaḥ pramāṇīkriyate tena pratiśāstraṃ ye 'bhiyuktāsteṣāṃ prāmāṇyamityavaśyamabhyupagantavyam / evaṃ sati sarvācāryaprāmāṇyādanekavikalpavicitrā tarkavṛttirityapariniścitatvādbhrāntiḥ prasajyeta / tathā ca sati jijñāsūnāmapavargaprāptivighātaḥ syāt / tasmādbhiṣajeva bhavatā paropadeśaḥ prayukto nāsmānayaṃ prīṇāti / etaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? āptalakṣaṇasyānavadhāritatvāt / vyapagatarāgādidoṣāṇāmasandigdhamatīnāmatīndriyārthadṛśvanāmīśvaramaharṣīṇāmāptatvamācakṣmahe, na sarveṣām / yadi cānyo 'pyevaṃdharmo 'sti bhavatu pramāṇam / kiṃcānyat / svaviṣaye ca tatprāmāṇyasyādoṣavattvāt / yasya khalvapi yo viṣayastasya tasminviṣaye vaco 'ntareṇāpi sādhanaṃ pramāṇamityavaśyamabhyupagantavyam / itarathā pratiśāstramācārasthitiniyamānāmadṛṣṭārthānāmapratipattiḥ syāt / etenākhilaliṅgādāgamo 'rthāntaram / yasmānmahatābhidhānena yuktiranviṣyate tasmādyuktyapekṣālliṅgādāgamo 'rthāntaramiti /
  āha na, anvayavyatirekābhyāmadhigamahetutvāt / yathā kṛtakatvādidharmo 'nityatvādau viṣaye dṛṣṭastadabhāve cādṛṣṭa ityanitye 'rthe niścayamādadhāti evaṃ śabdo 'pi svārthe tajjātīye na dṛṣṭaḥ pratipattiheturbhavati / tasmādanumānādabhinna evāyamiti /
  ucyate- candrādiṣvidānīmasādhāraṇaviṣayeṣu kā pratipattiḥ syāditi ?
  āha- avayavāpekṣatvāccandraśabdo hyanekeṣu vacaneṣu vartate, jātidravyaguṇakriyāsu ca, tathā ḍitthādiśabdaḥ, tasmādevaṃjātīyakānāmapi cānumānādabhedaḥ /
  ucyate- svargādīnāṃ tarhi kathamanumānatvamiti ?
  āha- āptavaco 'visaṃvādasāmarthyāt / yathā hairaṇyakaprabhṛtīnāmāptānāṃ vākyamavyabhicāri evamīśvaramaharṣayo 'pi cāptāḥ / tasmādeṣāmapi vākyamavyabhicārīti śakyamatrāpi sāmānyaviṣayatvaṃ kalpayitum / evamanumānamevāgama iti /
  ucyate- yaduktamanvayavyatirekābhyāmadhigamahetutvācchabdo 'numānamiti atra brūmaḥ na, apratijñānāt / na hi vayaṃ vyavahārānupātināṃ vṛkṣādīnāmāgamatvamācakṣmahe, kiṃ tarhi svargādīnāmatyantaparokṣaviṣayāṇām / tasmādapratijñānādanupālambho 'yamiti / upetya vā vaktrapekṣatvāt / athavopetyāpi sarvaśabdānāmāgamatvamanumānādarthāntarabhāvaṃ brūmaḥ / tathā hi kṛtakatvāditi liṅgaṃ caṇḍālakāpālikairapi prayujyamānaṃ sāhacaryāpekṣaṃ niścayamādadhāti / na vaktṛviśeṣamapekṣate / vaktṛviśeṣāpekṣastu śabdaḥ / tasmānna liṅgam / kiṃ cānyat viparyayāt / na hi liṅgaṃ deśāntare viparyeti / śabdasya tu dṛṣṭo viparyayaḥ / sa eva hi śabdo deśāntare, kālāntare tu svārthaṃ na pratyāyayati arthāntaraṃ ca praśaṃsati /
  sambandhānupalabdheriti cet syādetat, sambandhāntaraṃ deśāntare 'nupalakṣitam / tasmācchabdārthaviparyaya iti / etadanupapannam / liṅgavaidharmyāt / na hi pratyakṣābhimatasya liṅgina upalabdhau gavāderliṅgaṃ nopalabhyate / śabdastūpalabhyamāno gavādau nopalabhyate / tasmānna liṅgam / kiṃcānyat / deśaniyamāt / na hi liṅgasya deśaniyamo dṛṣṭaḥ / asti tu śabdasya deśaniyamaḥ / tadyathā śavatirgatikarmā kāmbojeṣveva bhāṣyate / raṃhatiḥ prācyeṣu, tathā dātirlavanārthaḥ, dātramudīcyeṣu nānyatra / tasmānna śabdo liṅgam / kiṃcānyat, iṣṭato viniyogāt / svābhāvikaṃ liṅgam / na hi dhūmognerapakṛṣya śakyate 'psu vāyāvākāśe 'nyatra vā niveśayitum / śabdastu yatra vakturabhiprāyastatra tatra viniveśyate / yatha vṛddhyādayaḥ śabdāḥ svārthābhyuccayādiṣu prasiddhā ādaikṣu viniveśyante / tasmānna te liṅgam /
  sarvābhidhānaśaktitvācchabdasyādoṣa iti cet syānmataṃ sarvābhidhānaśaktiḥ śabdaḥ sarvābhidheyaśaktiścārthastayoḥ puruṣavyāpāreṇa śaktyavavacchedaḥ kriyate / katham ? ayameva śabdo 'syārthasya pratyāyako bhavatu / ayameva cārtho 'nena śabdenābhidhīyatām / etāvati puruṣavyāpāraḥ / tasmācchabdasya svābhāvikaḥ sambandho vaktrapekṣayā vyajyata iti / etadapyanyupapannam / kasmāt ? sutarāmanumānādarthāntaratvaprasaṃgāt / evamapi kalpayitvānumānātsutarāṃ śabdasyārthāntaratvamāpadyate / kasmāt ? na hi yathā vakrapekṣayā sarvārthasya sataḥ śabdasya śaktyavacchedastathā sarvārthaṃ liṅgaṃ vaktrapekṣayārthāntarādavacchidyate / yathā caikaḥ śabdo jagatyevamuditaḥ puruṣaviniyogāpekṣaḥ sarvamarthamabhidhātuṃ samarthastathaikaṃ liṅgaṃ kayācidyuktyā sarvārthapratyāyanasamartham / tasmānna śabdo liṅgam / yatpunaretaduktam candrādīnāmavayavāpekṣaṃ sāmānyamabhyupagamyate / tadayuktam / asādhāraṇatvāt / anumānābhāve śabdaprasiddho 'rtha iti vyāghātaḥ / kiṃ cānyat / jātyādisādhyatvāt jātiguṇadravyakriyāṇāṃ ca parasparato 'rthāntaratvaṃ, samudāyaśca sādhyaḥ / tasmādayuktameṣāṃ tadapekṣayā sāmānyaviṣayatvam / yadapyuktamāptavādāvisaṃvādasāmānyātsvargādiśabdānāmanumānatvamiti, atra brūmaḥ- etadapyanupapannam / kasmāt ? pramāṇaviṣayatvāt / satyamastyeṣāṃ sāmānyaparikalpanā, sā tu pramāṇaviṣayā na tu prameyaviṣayā / prameyaṃ tu sāmānyamanumānamasyetyayamabhyupagamo vaḥ / taccāsādhāraṇatvātsvargādīnāṃ pratiṣiddham / tasmāttyajyatāmiyamāśaṅkānumānamevāgama iti /
  anyaḥ punaranumānāgamayorabhedapratijña idamāha / svargādayaḥ śabdā na pramāṇam / kasmāt ? pramāṇāntareṇa tadarthānupalabdheḥ / yasya hi śabdasyārthaḥ pratyakṣato 'numānato vā nopalabhyate sa na pramāṇam / itarastu pramāṇam / tadyathā nadyāstīre pakvamāmravanaṃ, pathi guḍaśakaṭaṃ viparyastamiti / na ca svargādiśabdānāmarthaḥ pramāṇāntareṇopalabhyate / tasmādyathā vibhurātmā sarvatra sukhādisambhavādityevamādayo bauddhaṃ prati dharmyasiddhatvādayo yathārthāstathā vedaśabdā api prāyeṇeti / etattu na yuktarūpam / kasmāt ? anyāyena sarvaśabdāpavādāt / kā hyatra yuktiryadasmadādibhiranupalabhyamānārthaṃ pramāṇabhūtānāmapi vākyamayathārthaṃ syāt ? saveṇa cāvaśyaṃ kaścidāptastasya ca vākyamadṛṣṭārthamityabhyupagantavyam / ato 'yaṃ tavātrāpi samānaḥ prasaṃgaḥ / na ca pramāṇaṃ svārthasiddhaye pramāṇāntaramapekṣate / tatra yadi śabdasya pramāṇāntarāpekṣaṃ yathārthatvamāśrīyate tena na kevalaṃ svargādayaḥ kiṃ tarhi śabdā evāpramāṇamiti prāptam / anumānasya ca pramāṇāntaranirapekṣasya gamakatvābhyupagamādāgamasya tato 'rthāntaratvaṃ sutarāṃ prasajyate / tasmādyuktāgamavirodhina evaṃvidhā nāstikavādāḥ śreyo 'rthibhirdūrādapohyā iti sthitametat- anumānādasiddhaṃ vastu yattadāptāgamātsādhyamiti /
  evamasya trividhasya pramāṇasyaindriyikaṃ kāraṇāntarato 'nupalabhyamānaṃ ca prameyaṃ vyākhyātam / etasmāttu yadanyattadasaditi pratyavagantavyam // 6-7 //
children.translated_text: By the phrase 'and what is not established even through that,' he indicates that <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> [inference] has no scope in the domain of scripture. By '<s>parokṣa</s>' (beyond perception) he refers to the object. By 'to be proved from trustworthy scripture' he refers to the knower [i.e., the means of knowledge]. This is what is said: that which is not established even through <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> inference — whether it is something that, though within the range of perception, has not been seen by oneself because the capacity for objecthood is obstructed by some other cause, or whether it is completely beyond perception, such as heaven, liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), deities, and the like, which lack a common property [with perceived things] — that is to be proved from trustworthy scripture (<s>āptāgama</s>). If one objects that this would entail the consequence of establishing all doctrines — one might say: if scripture is made a means of valid knowledge, then the authoritativeness of those who are proficient in each system must necessarily be accepted. In that case, since the activity of reasoning is varied with manifold alternatives due to the authoritativeness of all teachers, confusion would follow from the lack of determination. And if so, there would be an obstruction to the attainment of liberation for those who seek knowledge. Therefore, like a physician, you have prescribed instruction for others — this does not please us. But this [objection] is unjustified. Why? Because the definition of '<s>āpta</s>' (trustworthy) has not been properly considered. We declare that the status of being trustworthy belongs to <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) and the great <s>ṛṣi</s>s (seers) — those who are free from the faults of passion and the like, whose understanding is free from doubt, and who perceive supersensory objects — not to all persons. And if anyone else has these same qualities, let him too be a valid authority. Moreover, the authoritativeness of each [teacher] in his own domain is not faulty. For whatever domain belongs to whomever, in that domain his speech must necessarily be accepted as a valid means of knowledge even without additional proof. Otherwise there would be no understanding of rules of conduct, established practices, and regulations in each system, which have unseen purposes. By this, scripture is shown to be different from inference involving all marks. Since reasoning is sought with great effort, scripture is different from inference, because it depends on reasoning. One objects: no, because [scripture too] is a cause of understanding through positive and negative concomitance. Just as the property of being produced, observed in the domain of impermanence and not observed in its absence, produces certainty regarding the impermanent object — so too the word, in its own object of the same class,
<s>Kārikā</s> 8

children.text:
āha, yadyevaṃ pradhānasyāsattvaprasaṅgaḥ / anupalabdau kāraṇāntaratvānupalabdheḥ / taddhi pratyakṣāviṣayatve satyatidūrādibhiranupalabdhikāraṇairnopalabhyate / tanna tāvat atidūrātsāmīpyādvyavadhānāccāsyāgrahaṇam / kasmāt ? vibhutvāt / nendriyaghātāt, avikalendriyairagrahaṇāt / na mano 'navasthānāt, avasthitamanobhiragrahaṇāt / na saukṣmyāt, śaśaviṣāṇādīnāṃ sattvaprasaṅgāt / nābhibhavāt, asambhavāt / na samānābhihārādekatvāt / tasmāt kāraṇāntarābhāvato 'nupalabhyamānasyāsattvamicchataḥ pradhānasyāpi śaśaviṣāṇādīnāmapi sattvaprasaṅgaḥ / athaitanneṣyate kāraṇāntaraṃ tarhyanupalabdhau vaktavyamiti /
  ucyate- yattāvaduktaṃ anupalabdhau kāraṇāntarānupapatteḥ pradhānasyāsattvaprasaṅga iti, atrāstu /
children.translated_text: One objects: if so, there would be the consequence of the non-existence of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter). Because when there is non-perception, no other cause of non-perception is found. For if [<s>pradhāna</s>] is not within the range of perception, it is not perceived due to causes of non-perception such as excessive distance and the rest. But its non-apprehension is not due to excessive distance, excessive proximity, or concealment. Why? Because it is all-pervading. Nor due to impairment of the sense organs, since those with unimpaired senses also do not apprehend it. Nor due to instability of the mind, since those with stable minds also do not apprehend it. Nor due to subtlety, for then the existence of hare's horns and the like would follow. Nor due to suppression, since that is impossible [in this case]. Nor due to intermixture with what is similar, since it is one [without a second]. Therefore, since there is no other cause, for one who holds that what is not perceived is non-existent, there would be the consequence that hare's horns too exist just as <s>pradhāna</s> does. If this [consequence] is not desired, then another cause of non-perception must be stated. It is replied: as for what was said — 'because of the inapplicability of another cause when there is non-perception, there would be the consequence of <s>pradhāna</s>'s non-existence' — to that:
Its non-perception is due to subtlety, not due to non-existence.

children.text: yattūktaṃ śaśaviṣāṇādīnāmapi sattvaprasaṅga iti tadayuktam / kasmāt ? sādhanopapatteḥ / asti hi pradhānasya saukṣmyāttadanupalabdhau sādhanaṃ, na śaśaviṣāṇādīnām / kiṃ tat ? ucyate
children.translated_text: As for what was said — 'the existence of hare's horns and the like would also follow' — that is unjustified. Why? Because the means of proof is applicable. For there is a means of proving the non-perception of <s>pradhāna</s> due to its subtlety, but not for hare's horns and the like. What is it? It is replied:
Its apprehension is through its effects.

children.text:
pradhānasya hi kāryata upalabdhirityetadupariṣṭātpratipādayiṣyāmaḥ / na tu śaśaviṣāṇādīnāṃ kāryamasti / tasmādviṣamo 'yamupanyāsaḥ /
  āha- evamapi pratijñāntarānarthakyam, ekena kṛtatvāt / saukṣmyāttadanupalabdhirityukte gamyata etannābhāvāditi / tasmāttadvacanamanarthakamiti /
  ucyate- na, vītāvītaparigrahārthatvāt / evaṃ siddhe yatpratijñādvayaṃ karoti tat jñāpayatyācāryaḥ vītāvītābhyāmabhipretārthasiddhiḥ / prākca saukṣmyātiśayāttadanupalabdhirityācakṣāṇaḥ pratipādayati purastādvītaḥ prayoktavyava iti / ekasmiṃśca viṣaye dvau prayuṃjānaḥ samuccayena siddhiṃ dyotayati / kiṃ siddhaṃ bhavati ? yaduktaṃ tantrāntarīyaiḥ na pṛthakpratipattihetū vītāvītāviti tadiṣṭamevaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ bhavati / tatra vītasya pratijñā saukṣmyāttadanupalabdhiḥ / tasya cāvītasya prasaṅgidharmāntaranivṛttirūpeṇa, nābhāvāt heturubhayayogī / katham ? yasya pratyakṣato 'nupalabhyamānasya kāryastadupalabdhistasya saukṣmyāttadanupalabdhirdṛṣṭā / tadyathendriyāṇi / yadi punarasyābhāvādanupalabdhissyāt, kāryato 'nupalabdhiprasaṅgaḥ / asti ceyaṃ kāryata upalabdhiḥ / tasmānnābhāvāt / na cedabhāvāt, pariśeṣataḥ saukṣmyāt tadanupalabdhiriti //
children.translated_text:
For we shall demonstrate below that <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) is apprehended through its effects. But the hare's horn and the like have no effect. Therefore, this comparison is unfair.
  [The objector] says: Even so, the other proposition is purposeless, since one [proposition] suffices. When it is said 'its non-apprehension is due to subtlety,' it is understood that this is not due to non-existence. Therefore that statement [i.e., 'not because of non-existence'] is purposeless.
  It is replied: No, because it serves the purpose of including both the <s>vīta</s> (exclusive) and <s>avīta</s> (non-exclusive) [forms of reasoning]. This being established, the teacher, by making a pair of propositions, indicates that the intended meaning is accomplished through both the <s>vīta</s> and <s>avīta</s> [forms]. Moreover, by first stating 'its non-apprehension is due to the extreme subtlety,' he demonstrates that the <s>vīta</s> [form] is to be employed first. And by employing both in a single subject, he indicates accomplishment through their combination. What is accomplished? What was said by proponents of other systems — that the <s>vīta</s> and <s>avīta</s> are not independently the means of ascertainment — that [objection] is thus embraced and accepted. There, the proposition of the <s>vīta</s> [form] is: 'its non-apprehension is due to subtlety.' And for the <s>avīta</s> [form], by way of negating other incidental properties: 'not because of non-existence' — this reason applies to both. How? That which, though not apprehended by perception, has effects by which it is apprehended — its non-apprehension is seen to be due to subtlety. Just like the senses. But if its non-apprehension were due to non-existence, there would be the consequence of non-apprehension through effects as well. But there is this apprehension through effects. Therefore, [it is] not because of non-existence. And if not because of non-existence, then by elimination, its non-apprehension is due to subtlety.

āha, kiṃ punastatkāryaṃ yadbhavānpradhānasyāstitve liṅgamācaṣṭa iti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
[The objector] asks: What, then, is that effect which you declare as the mark of the existence of <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter)?
  It is replied:

children.text: mahadādi tacca kāryaṃ prakṛtivirūpaṃ sarūpaṃ ca || 8 ||
children.translated_text: That effect, beginning with <s>mahat</s> (the great one), is both dissimilar and similar to <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 8 //

children.text:
taddhi mahadahaṃkārendriyaviśeṣāviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ pradhānena visadṛśaṃ sadṛśaṃ cetyupariṣṭātpravedayiṣyāmaḥ /
  āha- prastāvābhāvādayuktametat / kiṃ punaradhikṛtyedamucyate prakṛtivirūpaṃ sarūpaṃ ca mahadādi kāryamiti ?
  ucyate- vyaktāvyaktajñavijñānānmokṣo 'vāpyata ityetatprakṛtam / etāni ca parasparavaidharmyasādharmyapratipattimantareṇa na śakyāni vijñātumityevamarthamidaṃ prastūyate / tasmānnākasmiko vairūpyasārūpyopanyāsa iti // 8 //
children.translated_text:
We shall explain below that this effect — characterized by <s>mahat</s> (the great one), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), the senses (<s>indriya</s>s), the specific (<s>viśeṣa</s>) and the non-specific (<s>aviśeṣa</s>) — is both dissimilar and similar to <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter).
  [The objector] says: This is improper because there is no occasion for it. With reference to what is it said that 'the effect beginning with <s>mahat</s> is both dissimilar and similar to <s>Prakṛti</s>'?
  It is replied: The subject under discussion is that liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) is obtained from the knowledge of the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>), the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), and the knower (<s>jña</s>). And these cannot be known without understanding their mutual dissimilarity and similarity — it is for this purpose that this is introduced. Therefore, the presentation of dissimilarity and similarity is not without reason. // 8 //
// Thus ends the second lesson (<s>āhnika</s>) in the <s>Yuktidīpikā</s>, following the method of the seventy [kārikās]. //
<s>Kārikā</s> 9

āha- āstāṃ tāvadvairūpyasārūpyacintā / kāryamidameva tāvanmahadādi parīkṣiṣyāmahe / kiṃ prāgutpatterasti nāstīti ? kutaḥ saṃśaya iti cet syānmatam- asaṅgatārthaṃ prakaraṇāntaramupakṣipyate bhavatā / na cāvidyamānasambandhasya saṃśayasya prakaraṇāntare 'bhidhīyamānasya nirṇītiṃ sādhvīmācāryā manyante / avakāśāsambhavāditi /
  ucyate- asti saṃśayāvakāśaḥ / kasmāt ? ācāryavipratipatteḥ / prāgutpatteḥ kāryamasadityācāryāḥ kaṇādākṣapādaprabhṛtayo manyante / sadasaditi bauddhāḥ / naiva sannāsadityanye / tasmādupapannaḥ saṃśayaḥ /
  tatredānīṃ bhavataḥ kā pratipattiriti ?
  ucyate /
  nāvidyamānasya mahadādervikārasya pradhānādāvirbhāva iti pratijānīmahe / kasmāt ? sanniveśaviśeṣamātrābhyupagamāt / na hi naḥ kāraṇādarthāntarabhūtaṃ kāryamutpadyata ityabhyupagamaḥ / kiṃ tarhi viśvātmakānāṃ sattvarajastamasāmapagataviśeṣāviśeṣāḥ sanmātralakṣaṇopacayāḥ pratinivṛttapariṇāmavyāpārāḥ paramavibhāgamupasaṃprāptāḥ sūkṣmāḥ śaktayaḥ / tāsāmadhikārasāmarthyādupajātapariṇāmavyāpārāṇāṃ sanmātrānukrameṇa pracayamupasaṃpadyamānānāṃ sanniveśaviśeṣamātraṃ vyaktam / etasyāṃ kalpanāyāmasata utpattau kaḥ prasaṅga iti ? etenaiva bāhyānāṃ tantvādikāryāṇāṃ paṭādīnāṃ sanniveśaviśeṣamātratvādasata utpattiḥ pratiṣiddhā boddhavyā /
  āha- avidyamānametat / kasmāt ? asiddhe, nārthāntarasiddheḥ / yadi hi sanniveśaviśeṣamātratvaṃ kāryasya siddhaṃ syādata etadyujyate vaktum- tadabhyupagamādasadutpatteraprasaṅga iti / tattvasiddham / dravyāntarabhūtasyāvayavino niṣpattipratijñānāt / tasmāt kākaviṣāṇāt śaśaviṣāṇasiddhivadayuktaṃ sanniveśaviśeṣamātrābhyupagamātsatkāryasiddhiriti /
  itaścāsat kāryam, agrahaṇāt / iha śrotrādīnāṃ viṣayabhūtasya tatsannidhānādavaśyaṃ grahaṇena bhavitavyam / yadi ca prāgutpatteḥ satkāryaṃ syāt tadapi śrotrādisannidhānāt gṛhyeta / na tu gṛhyate / tasmādasatkāryam /
  anupalabdhikāraṇasadbhāvāditi cet, tatraitatsyāt, asti prāgutpatteḥ kāryasyānupalabdhikāraṇaṃ tasmādasya sato 'pyagrahaṇaṃ bhavati / uttarakālaṃ tadvigamāt grahaṇamiti / etaccānupapannam / kasmāt ? anupalabdhyasambhavāt / taddhi pratyakṣāviṣayatve satyatidūrādibhiranupalabdhikāraṇairnopalabhyate / na caiṣāṃ tatra sambhavaḥ / tasmādasadetat / kāraṇāntarānabhidhānāt / na cātidūrādivyatiriktamanupalabdhau kāraṇāntaramadhīdhve yato 'syāgrahaṇaṃ syāt / ataścāsadeva / kiṃ cānyat kāraṇānupalabdhiprasaṅgāt / anupalabdhikāraṇasadbhāvātkāryasyāgrahaṇamicchataḥ kāraṇāgrahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ / kasmāt ? abhinnadeśatvāt / ekendriyagrāhyatvāt sthūlatvācca / tattvaniṣṭam / tasmādayuktamanupalabdhikāraṇasadbhāvātsataḥ kāryasyāgrahaṇamiti / pramāṇāntaranivṛttiprasaṅgādayuktamiti cet, syādetat yadi tarhi pratyakṣaviṣayamevāsti / tato 'nyatrāstītyetadupagamyate / tenātīndriyaviṣayasyānumānasya nivṛttiprasaṅgaḥ / aniṣṭaṃ caitat / tasmānnānupalabdherasatkāryamiti / etadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? kriyāguṇavyapadeśāsambhavāt / yaddhi pratyakṣato nopalabhyate tatkriyayāstīti saṃsūcyate / yathā harmyāvasthitānāṃ tṛṇānāmudvahanādvāyuḥ guṇena, yathā mālatīlatāgandhena vyapadeśena vā, kāryādinā yathendriyāṇi / na tu prāgutpatteḥ kāryasya kriyāguṇavyapadeśasambhavaḥ tasmādasatkāryam /
  itaścāsatkāryam / kartṛprayāsasāphalyāt / iha prāgvyāpāropakramāt kartārastasmātphalamupalipsamānāḥ kāryaviśeṣaniyatasāmārthyaṃ sādhanamupādāya vyāpriyante / taccetprāgapi vyāpārāt syāttadarthasya parispandasyānarthakyaṃ prāptam / aniṣṭaṃ caitat / tasmāt kartṛprayāsasāphalyāt asatkāryam / pariṇāmādyupapatterna doṣa iti cet syānmataṃ kāraṇasya pariṇāmavyūhasaṃśleṣavyaktipracayakṣaṇāndharmān yasmāt kartrādīni kurvanti nānarthakāni syuḥ / sattvaṃ ca kāryasya na nirupyate / ka evaṃ sati doṣaḥ syāditi ? ucyate- na śakyamevaṃ kalpayitum / kasmāt ? mārgāntarānupapatteḥ / pariṇāmo hi nāmāvasthitasya dravyasya dharmāntaranivṛttiḥ dharmāntarapravṛttiśca / tatra sato dharmāntarasya nirodhābhyupagamādasataścotpattipratijñānānnedamarthāntaramārabhyate / evaṃ vyūhādayo 'pyupasaṃhartavyāḥ / tasmāt pariṇāmādibhirabhibhavāt kartrādīnāmarthavattvādasatkāryam / tathā coktam-

children.translated_text: When [a substance], abandoning one property, takes on another,
that property which does not deviate from its essential nature is called <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation).

[The objector] says: Let the inquiry into dissimilarity and similarity be set aside for now. Let us first examine this very effect beginning with <s>mahat</s> (the great one). Does it exist prior to its production, or does it not? If [you ask] what is the source of the doubt — [the argument would be:] you are introducing an unrelated topic. And the teachers do not consider it proper to resolve a doubt that has no established connection when it is discussed in a different context. Because there is no occasion for it.
  It is replied: There is occasion for doubt. Why? Because of the disagreement among teachers. The teachers <s>Kaṇāda</s>, <s>Akṣapāda</s>, and others hold that prior to production the effect is non-existent (<s>asat</s>). The Buddhists [hold that it is] both existent and non-existent (<s>sadasat</s>). Others [hold that it is] neither existent nor non-existent. Therefore the doubt is warranted.
  What, then, is your position on this matter?
  It is replied:
  We maintain that there is no coming into being (<s>āvirbhāva</s>) of the manifest (<s>vikāra</s>) beginning with <s>mahat</s>, which was previously non-existent, from <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). Why? Because we accept only a special arrangement (<s>sanniveśaviśeṣamātra</s>). For our position is not that an effect arises as something entirely different from the cause. Rather: the subtle powers (<s>śakti</s>s) that are universal in nature — consisting of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, free from [the distinction of] specific and non-specific, characterized merely by existence (<s>sanmātra</s>), with their transformative activity ceased, having reached the state of ultimate separation — when, through the capacity of their proper function, their transformative activity arises, and they progressively accumulate in the order of mere existence, the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) is nothing but a special arrangement. Given this conception, what relevance does the production of the non-existent have? By this very [reasoning], the production of the non-existent should be understood as refuted also for external effects such as cloth and the like from threads and the like, since they too are merely special arrangements.
  [The objector] says: This is non-existent [as a position]. Why? Because what is unestablished cannot establish something else. If the mere special-arrangement nature of the effect were established, then it would be proper to say: 'Because we accept that, there is no consequence of production from the non-existent.' But that is not established. Because you maintain the production of a whole (<s>avayavin</s>) which is a different substance [from its parts]. Therefore, just as the establishment of a hare's horn from a crow's horn [is absurd], so too is the establishment of <s>satkārya</s> (pre-existence of the effect) from the acceptance of mere special arrangement.
  Moreover, the effect is non-existent, because of non-apprehension. Here, whatever is present within the range of the senses and other [faculties] must necessarily be apprehended due to its proximity. And if the effect existed prior to its production, it too would be apprehended due to the proximity of the senses and other [faculties]. But it is not apprehended. Therefore, the effect is non-existent [before production].
  If [you say it is] because of the existence of a cause of non-apprehension — [the argument would be:] there exists a cause of non-apprehension of the effect prior to its production; therefore, even though it exists, it is not apprehended. [And] at a later time, due to the removal of that [cause], it is apprehended. And this is untenable. Why? Because of the impossibility of non-apprehension. For [something] that is not an object of perception is not apprehended due to causes of non-apprehension such as being too far away, etc. But there is no possibility of these [causes] applying there. Therefore this is non-existent [as an argument]. Because no other cause [of non-apprehension] is stated. And you do not maintain any cause of non-apprehension other than being too far away, etc., on account of which there would be non-apprehension. And therefore [the effect is] simply non-existent [before production].
  Moreover, because there would be the consequence of non-apprehension of the cause. For one who accepts that the effect is not apprehended because of the existence of a cause of non-apprehension, there follows the consequence of non-apprehension of the cause as well. Why? Because they occupy the same location. Because they are grasped by the same sense faculty. And because [the cause] is gross. This is established by the truth [of the matter]. Therefore, it is improper [to say] that the existent effect is not apprehended because of the existence of a cause of non-apprehension.
  If [you say] this is improper because it would lead to the negation of other means of valid knowledge — [the argument would be:] if only what is an object of perception exists, then it is accepted that what is elsewhere exists [only if perceived]. In that case, there follows the consequence of the negation of inference, which has super-sensory objects. And this is undesirable. Therefore, the effect is not non-existent [merely] because of non-apprehension.
  This too is improper. Why? Because of the impossibility of designation through action, quality, or name. For what is not apprehended through direct perception is indicated as existing through action, or through a quality, or through a designation — such as effects and the like. Just as wind [is known] from its lifting the straw located on a terrace, through a quality; just as [wind is known] from the fragrance of a <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) vine, through designation or [another] example; just as the senses [are known] from effects and the like. But there is no possibility of action, quality, or designation of the effect prior to its production. Therefore, the effect is non-existent [before production].
  Moreover, the effect is non-existent [before production], because of the fruitfulness of the agent's effort. Here, prior to the commencement of activity, agents who desire the fruit take up the appropriate means — which has a capacity determined for a specific effect — and engage in activity. And if [the effect] existed even prior to activity, the purposelessness of the exertion directed toward it would follow. And this is undesirable. Therefore, from the fruitfulness of the agent's effort, the effect is non-existent [before production].
  If [you say] there is no defect because of the tenability of transformation and so forth — [the argument would be:] since the agents such as the maker and others bring about the properties of transformation, arrangement, conjunction, manifestation, and accumulation of the cause, they would not be purposeless. And the existence of the effect is not thereby denied. What defect would there be in this case?
  It is replied: It is not possible to suppose thus. Why? Because of the untenable nature of the alternative path. For <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation) is the cessation of one property and the arising of another property in an abiding substance. There, from the acceptance of the cessation of an existent property and the assertion of the arising of a non-existent one, the same issue is merely restated. Arrangement and the others should similarly be dismissed. Therefore, from the overriding [force] of transformation and the like, from the purposefulness of the agent and others, the effect is non-existent [before production]. And thus it is said:

kutaśca na satkāryam ? ārambhoparamayorādyantāviśeṣaprasaṃgāt / yadi satkāryaṃ syāt tena yaḥ kriyārthaḥ sādhanānāmādau parispandaḥ so 'nte 'pi syāt / vā yo 'nte virāmaḥ sa ādāvapi syāt / kasmāt ? sadaviśeṣāt / na tu tadasti / tasmādasatkāryam /

  yatpunaretaduktamanupalabdherasatkāryamiti, atra brūmaḥ / etadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? saṃśayakāraṇatvāt / sa ca sadviṣayānupalabdhiḥ / ityetasmādeva hetossāṃśayikā vayam / tāmeva tu niścayārthamavalambamāno na yuktimārgamanuyāti / yat punaretaduktaṃ kāraṇāntarānabhidhānāditi- etadapyanupapannam / kasmāt ? abhiprāyānavabodhāt / yo hi yathā kuṇḍe badarāṇyarthāntarabhūtānyāhitāni tathā kāraṇe kāryamastītyetadācaṣṭe taṃ pratyayamupālambhaḥ syāt / vayantu anekaśaktadharmiṇaḥ sahakāriśaktyantarānugṛhītasya pūrvasyāśśaktestirobhāvamuttarasyāścāvirbhāvamupādadhānāḥ kāraṇameva kāryamityanumanyāmahe / tayostu śaktyoryugapadagrahaṇam / itaretarapratibandhahetutvāt / vastrasyāyāmavistāravat, kūrmāṅgamiva draṣṭavyam / yathā vastrasyopasaṃhārapratibandhādāyāmavistārau na grahaṇaviṣayatāṃ pratipadyete, sattāṃ vā na jihītaḥ kūrmasyevāṅgāni, tatha tantvādīnāmapi bhāvānāṃ kāraṇābhimatā kāryābhimatā cāvasthā krameṇa vā sthiraśca bhavat tannimittastadgrahaṇāgrahaṇavikalpaḥ /

  yatpunaretaduktaṃ- kartṛprayāsasāphalyādasatkāryamiti, atra brūmaḥ- etadapyayuktam / kasmāt ?
children.translated_text: And why is the effect not pre-existent [in the cause]? Because of the consequence that there would be no distinction between beginning and end, between commencement and cessation [of activity]. If the effect were pre-existent, then the initial exertion of the instrumental causes, which serves the purpose of production, would also exist at the end; or the cessation that exists at the end would also exist at the beginning. Why? Because there is no distinction in what exists. But this is not the case. Therefore the effect does not pre-exist. Furthermore, the effect does not pre-exist, because of the consequence that there would be no distinction between beginning and end with respect to the property of origination. If the effect were pre-existent, then just as the fully produced [effect] has a connection with the property of origination, so too it would have it at the beginning; and just as there is a connection at the beginning, so too there would be at the end. But what is observed is [that there is] connection and non-connection at the beginning and end [respectively]. Therefore the effect does not pre-exist. Furthermore, the effect does not pre-exist, because of the contradiction between the words 'birth' and 'existent.' Here the word 'birth' expresses the coming into being of an object that did not previously exist. But the word 'existent' expresses being the cause of another action. If there were birth of what exists, there would be synonymy between these two [words]. But this is not so. Therefore it is unjustified to say 'what exists is born.' It is replied: as for what was said — 'because of the assertion that a whole which is a different substance is produced, and since [the effect] is merely a particular configuration, the effect is [said to be] pre-existent [in the cause]' — to this we say: that is unestablished, because there is no apprehension of a difference. If there were the production of a whole that is a different substance from threads and the like, then just as a cloth is perceived as distinct in a group of threads, or just as another cloth placed in the same [group] is perceived as distinct, so too [the whole] would be perceived. But it is not perceived. Therefore it is not a different substance. If one says that the non-apprehension is due to inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) — one might say: in the case of two substances related by conjunction, when there is a relation of support and supported, apprehension of distinctness occurs. But the relation between thread and cloth is of the nature of inherence. Therefore there is no apprehension of distinctness. But this is untenable. Why? Because it is unestablished. If the separate existence of the whole and the inherence as its relation were established, all this would follow. But neither of these two is established in reality. Therefore this is unjustified. Moreover, because there is no example. A substance of great size placed elsewhere [should be perceived distinctly, but no such example is available for inherence].
Because what is non-existent cannot be produced.

children.text: yadyubhayapakṣaprasiddhasyāsataḥ kriyāyogaḥ syāt ata etadyujyate vaktum kārye sati kartuḥ prayāso 'narthaka iti / tattvasataḥ karaṇamanupapannam / tasmādayuktametat / hetvabhidhānādasiddhiriti cet syādetat- yathā niṣpannatvānmadhvādīnāṃ dhāraṇasamartho ghaṭo na kriyata ityayamapadiṣṭo heturasmābhiḥ evamitthaṃ kāryasyāsataḥ kāraṇaṃ nopapannamiti noktaṃ bhavatā / tasmādasiddhiriti / etaccānupapannam / kasmāt ? satyasati vā sambandhe doṣaprasaṅgāt / taddhi kriyamāṇaṃ sati vā sambandhe kārakaiḥ kriyate 'sati vā ? sambandhaścāsya bhavanpravṛttikāle vā kāraṇānāṃ syāt, niṣpattikāle vā ? kiṃ cātaḥ ? tanna tāvatpravṛttikāle sambandho yuktaḥ / kasmāt ? adravyatvāt / pravṛttikāle kartrādīnāṃ kriyāguṇavyapadeśābhāvādavastubhūtaṃ śaśaviṣāṇasthānīyaṃ vaḥ kāryam / na cāsti tathābhūtasya vastubhūtena sambandhaḥ / atha niṣpattikāle 'bhisambadhyate yaduktaṃ sato niṣpannatvātkriyānutpattiriti tasya vyāghātaḥ / atha matamasatyapi sambandhe niṣpattirbhavatīti tena kārakavyāpāravaiyarthyaprasaṃgaḥ / prāgapi ca kārakopādānātkāryaniṣpattiprasaṅga iti / uktaṃ ca

children.translated_text: Since it is non-existent, there is no relation with the causal factors that are connected with existence;
And for one who desires the origination of that which has no relation, there is no stable position.

If the production of the non-existent, which is accepted by both sides, were possible, then it would be justified to say that the effort of the producer when the effect [already] exists is purposeless. But in truth, the production of the non-existent is untenable. Therefore this [objection] is unjustified. If one objects that there is non-establishment because the reason has [merely] been stated — one might say: just as the reason was stated by us that 'a pot that is capable of holding honey and the like is not [re-]produced because it is already produced' — in the same way, you have not stated [a reason showing] that the non-existent effect cannot have a cause. Therefore there is non-establishment. But this is untenable. Why? Because whether there is a relation [between cause and effect] or not, a fault follows. For is that [effect] which is being produced produced by the causal factors when there is a relation [with them], or when there is none? And does this relation obtain at the time of the activity of the causes, or at the time of completion? What follows from this? First, a relation at the time of activity is not justified. Why? Because it is not a substance. At the time of activity, since the designations of action and quality are absent for the agent and the other [causal factors], your effect is a non-entity, equivalent to a hare's horn. And there is no relation of such a non-entity with a real entity. If [the effect] comes into relation at the time of completion, then there is a contradiction with what was said — 'because what exists is already produced, no action arises.' If one holds that completion occurs even without a relation, then there would be the consequence of the purposelessness of the activity of the causal factors. And there would also be the consequence that the effect is completed even before the adoption of causal factors. And it has been said:

  ārambhāya prasṛtā yasminkāle bhavanti karttāraḥ /
  kāryasyāniṣpādāttaṃ madhyamaṃ kālamicchanti // iti /
  yadā hetavaḥ pravṛttārambhā bhavantyuddiśya kāryaṃ na ca tāvannaimittikasyātmalābhaḥ saṃvartate sa madhyamaḥ kālaḥ / tasminkriyate kārakaiḥ kāryamiti /
  ucyate, na, avasthāntarānupatteḥ / prāṅniṣpatterasattā / niṣpannasya sattetyavasthādvayam / sadasadrūpā cāvasthā nāsti yo madhyamaḥ syāt / ato na yuktametaditi / kiṃcānyat / pūrvadoṣāparihārāduddiśya kāryaṃ tasyātmano lābhātmakena saha sambandha iti ? atrāpyayaṃ paryanuyogo naiva nivartata iti / tasmāccitramapi vākyaṃ prasārya na kiṃcitparihṛtaṃ bhavatā / tasmādyuktametat satyasati vā sambandhe doṣaprasaṃgādasanna kriyata iti /
  yasya punaḥ satkāryaṃ tasya doṣo nāsti / kasmāt ?
children.translated_text: One objects: but the effect is produced by the agent and other [causal factors] at the intermediate time. What then is this intermediate time? One says: 'The time when the producers have set forth toward commencement, but the effectuation of the effect has not yet occurred — that they call the intermediate time.' When the causes have begun their activity directed toward the effect, but the effectual entity has not yet come into its own being — that is the intermediate time. In that [time], the effect is produced by the causal factors. It is replied: no, because no third state is tenable. Before production there is non-existence; of what is produced there is existence — these are the two states. There is no state that is both existent and non-existent which would be the intermediate. Therefore this is not justified. Moreover, because the previous fault is not avoided — [the question remains:] what relation does [the effect] have, directed toward the effect, with [the process of] attaining its own being? Here too this objection simply does not go away. Therefore, even after spreading out an elaborate discourse, nothing has been avoided by you. Therefore this is justified: whether there is or is not a relation, since a fault follows, what is non-existent is not produced. But for one who [holds that] the effect is pre-existent, there is no fault. Why?
Because the material cause is apprehended.

children.text:
upādānamiti kāraṇaṃ tantvādyācakṣmahe / taddhi tasya kārakairgṛhyate abhisambadhyata ityarthaḥ / tasmācca nārthāntaraṃ kāryam ityataḥ kāraṇenābhisambaddhānāṃ kārakāṇāṃ kāryeṇaiva sambandho bhavatītyadoṣaḥ /
  āha- nanu ca yasyāpi satkāryaṃ tasyopādānādarthāntaraṃ tatkāryaṃ syāt / kasmāt ? kāryārthirupādānāt / yadyadarthamupādīyate tattasmādarthāntara yathā vemādibhyaḥ paṭaḥ / tantavaśca paṭādibhirupādīyante / tasmāttebhyo 'pyarthāntaraṃ paṭa iti / etena sattvaṃ prayuktam / yadyadarthamupādīyate tattasminnasat / yathā vemādiṣu paṭa iti /
  ucyate, na avayavipratiṣedhāt / pratiṣiddhastāvadavayavī dravyāntarabhūtastasmādanupapannārthametat / kiṃ cānyat /
children.translated_text: What we call <s>upādāna</s> (material cause) is the cause such as threads and the like. For that [cause] is apprehended by the causal factors — that is, it comes into relation [with them]. And since the effect is not something different from that [cause], the causal factors that are connected with the cause are thereby connected with the effect itself — hence there is no fault. One objects: but even for one who holds that the effect is pre-existent, the effect would be something different from the material cause. Why? Because one who desires the effect takes up the material cause. Whatever is taken up for the sake of something, that [something] is different from it — just as a cloth is different from the loom and so forth. And threads are taken up for the sake of cloth and the like. Therefore cloth is something different from them. By this, [the argument for] existence [of the effect in the cause] has been challenged. Whatever is taken up for the sake of something, that [something] does not exist in it — just as cloth does not exist in the loom and so forth. It is replied: no, because the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) has been refuted. The whole as a different substance has been refuted; therefore this argument is untenable. Moreover:
Because of the impossibility of [the effect] arising from everything.

children.text:
upādānasāmānyādvemādivadarthāntaraṃ paṭastantubhya iti brūvato 'rthāntaratvasāmānyāttantuvatsarvasmātkāraṇātkāryasya sambhavaḥ syāt / na tvevamasti / tasmātsarvasambhavābhāvādasamyagetat / kiṃcānyat, jātibhedaprasaṃgādarthāntarārambhaprasaṅgācca upādānasāmānyādvemādivadarthāntaraṃ paṭastantubhya iti brūvato yathā vemādibhyo bhinnajātīyo bhinnadeśaśca, tathā tantubhyaḥ paṭaḥ syāt yathā cāvasthite paṭe vemādayaḥ paṭāntaraṃ kurvanti tathā hyavasthite paṭe tantavo 'pi paṭāntaramārabheran / na caitadiṣṭam / na tarhyupādānasāmānyādvemādivattantubhyaḥ paṭasyārthāntaratvam /
  yatpunaretaduktaṃ yadyadarthamupādīyate na tat tatrāstīti, atra brūmaḥ- ayuktametat / kasmāt ? ādhārādheyabhāvānabhyupagamāt / asakṛduktamasmābhirna tantuṣu paṭo nāma kaścidasti / kiṃ tarhi tantava eva paṭaḥ / tattu sanmārgavidveṣādbhavatā na gṛhyate / kiṃ cānyat / anekāntāt / upetya vā brūmaḥ kathaṃ tāvattilāstailārthamupādīyante, bhavati cātra tailam / mṛdvīkā rasārthamupādīyate, bhavati cāsyāṃ rasaḥ / godhukca payo 'rthaṃ gāmādatte, bhavati ca tasyāṃ kṣīram / śālikalāpaśca taṇḍulārthamupādīyate, santi cātra taṇḍulā ityanaikāntiko hetuḥ /
  āha- āvaraṇopalabdherayuktam / tilādiṣvāvaraṇaṃ pratyakṣata upalabhyate / tatpratibandhāttailādīnāmagrahaṇam / vyāpāraśca kartustadvigamārtho na tu kāryasyāvaraṇamasti / tasmādviṣamo dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
  ucyate na, mārgāntaratvāt / yadyatrāsti tatra tadarthamupādīyate iti pūrvaṃ bhavatātisṛṣṭam / idānīṃ tvavagamavigamārthaṃ sato 'pyupādānamiti brūvato mārgāntaragamanaṃ pūrvavādatyāgo 'naikāntikasya cāparihāra iti / yatpunaretaduktaṃ pariṇāmādyupapatteradoṣa iti tathā tadastu / yattūktaṃ mārgāntarānupapatteriti atra brūmaḥ- etadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? pariṇāmadharmānavabodhāt / sato dharmāntarasya nirodhamasataścotpattiṃ pariṇāmamabhidadhato vyaktamayamupālambhaḥ syāt / na tvanayānusṛtyā pratiṣṭhāmahe / kiṃ tarhi sādhanānugṛhītasya dharmiṇo dharmāntarasyāvirbhāvaḥ pūrvasya ca tirobhāvaḥ pariṇāmaḥ / na cāvirbhāvatirobhāvāvutpattinirodhau / vyūhasaṃśleṣavyaktipracayāstu kimasato dharmā uta svato 'santa iti vicāryam / kiṃ cātaḥ / yadi tāvadasato dharmāḥ yathā kasyeti vācyam / atha svayamasantaḥ paścādbhavanti tadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? anarthāntaratvāt / satyarthāntarabhāve prāgasantaḥ paścādupalabhyamānāḥ satkāryavādaṃ nirākuryuḥ / sa caiṣāmarthāntarabhāvo na prasiddhaḥ / tasmātkimatropapannam ? grahaṇāgrahaṇavikalpe coktaḥ parihāraḥ / kiṃ cānyat / dravyāntarotpattivyāghātāt / upetya vaiṣāmutpattiṃ brūmaḥ- yadi hi pariṇāmavyūhasaṃśleṣavyaktipracayamātraṃ kāryamiṣyate yaduktaṃ dravyāṇi dravyāntaramārabhanta iti tasya vyāghātaḥ / kasmāt ? na hyete bhāvā dravyāntaram / tasmāddinakarakiraṇapratāpamūrchitasyeva dāvāgnyupasarpaṇadoṣonutāpāyaiva bhavataḥ pratipattiḥ /
  etenārambhoparamotpattyaviśeṣaprasaṅgo janmasacchabdaḥ pratyuktaḥ / katham ? ātmabhūtaṃ hi tantūnāṃ paṭākhyaṃ vyūhasthānīyaṃ sanniveśaviśeṣaṃ yadā kārakāṇi svena svena vyāpāreṇāviṣkurvanti tadā kriyate utpadyate jāyata ityevamādirlokasya vyavahāraḥ pravartate / yadā tu kārakāṇi śaktyantarāvirbhāvātsaṃsthānāntareṇautsukyavartitāmavasthāmupasaṃharanti tadā prāgupalabdhaṃ saṃsthānaṃ vināśaśabdavācyatāṃ pratipadyate / paramārthatastu na kasyacidutpādo 'sti na vināśaḥ / yatpunaretaduktaṃ janmaśabdaḥ prāgabhūtasyārthasya bhāvopakramamāheti tadapīcchāmātram / kasmāt ? vivādāt / sadasadviṣayaṃ janmeti vivāde 'nuṣakte janmaśabdaḥ prāgabhūtasya sadbhāvamācaṣṭa iti brūvato 'nuktasamam / puruṣādāvadṛṣṭatvādasiddhiriti cet syādetat yadi tarhi kriyate utpadyate jāyata ityeṣorthaḥ sadviṣayaḥ kalpyate, pradhānapuruṣayorapi tatprasaṃgaḥ, sadasadaviśeṣāditi / ataśca vivādāvasthamevaitatprakaraṇamiti / etaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? saṃsthānaviṣayatvāt / yadā bhāvaḥ svato 'narthāntarabhūtaṃ saṃsthānaṃ bhajate tadaite śabdāḥ pravartanta ityuktam / dṛṣṭaṃ ca loke tadyathā muṣṭigranthikuṇḍalāni karoti janayatyutpādayati, abhivyaktātmasu ca mūlodakādiṣu bhavatyutpannaṃ jātamiti / ubhayapakṣaprasiddhe tu śaśaviṣāṇādau naite śabdāḥ pravartante / tasmādbhavata evāniṣṭaprasaṅga iti / uktaṃ ca

children.translated_text: If the non-existence of pots and the like at the time of production is held to be the reason,
then, because of the equal [non-existence] in the case of a hare's horn, their production too would follow.

For one who says — on the basis of the generality of being a material cause, cloth is something different from threads, just as it is from the loom and so forth — from the generality of being different, the effect would arise from every cause, just as from threads. But this is not so. Therefore, because of the impossibility of arising from everything, this is incorrect. Moreover, because of the consequence of a difference in class and the consequence of the production of something different — for one who says that cloth is something different from threads on the basis of the generality of being a material cause, just as from the loom and so forth — just as [cloth] is of a different class and in a different location from the loom and so forth, so too cloth would be [of a different class] from threads. And just as, when a cloth already exists, the loom and so forth produce another cloth, so too, when a cloth already exists, the threads too would commence producing another cloth. But this is not desired. Therefore, cloth is not something different from threads on the basis of the generality of being a material cause, as is the case with the loom and so forth. As for what was further said — 'whatever is taken up for the sake of something does not exist therein' — to that we say: this is unjustified. Why? Because the relation of support and supported is not accepted. We have said repeatedly: there is no thing called 'cloth' existing in the threads. Rather, the threads themselves are the cloth. But this is not grasped by you due to hostility toward the correct path. Moreover, because of inconclusiveness. Or we say, granting [your premise]: how is it that sesame seeds are taken up for the sake of oil, and oil exists therein? Grapes are taken up for the sake of juice, and juice exists in them. A cowherd takes the cow for the sake of milk, and milk exists in her. And a sheaf of rice is taken up for the sake of grain, and grains exist therein. Thus the reason is inconclusive. One objects: this is unjustified because a covering is perceived. In sesame and the like, a covering is directly perceived. Due to the obstruction by that [covering], oil and the like are not apprehended. And the activity of the agent is for the purpose of removing that [covering], but there is no covering of the effect [in your position]. Therefore the example is dissimilar. It is replied: no, because this is a different line [of argument]. Previously you stated: 'if it exists therein, it is taken up for that purpose.' But now, by saying that material cause is taken up even of what exists, for the purpose of revealing and removing [the covering], you are taking a different path from your earlier position.
Thus the pre-existence of the effect (<s>satkārya</s>) is established. And the effect is pre-existent also for this reason:
Because [only] what is capable can be produced by what has the power.

children.text: śakyamidamasya, śaktaścāyamasyetyayaṃ niyamaḥ satāṃ dṛṣṭaḥ / tadyathā cakṣuṣo rūpasya / āsti cāyaṃ paṭasya vemādīnāṃ ca niyamaḥ / tasmācca satkāryam / sahakārivattanniyama iti cet syānmatam yathāpo bījāṅkurasyotpattau samarthā bhavanti na kāṣṭhādagnervā / ubhayaṃ ca tattāsu ca vidyate / bījādapāṃ vicchinnatvāt / yathā ca sūryaḥ sūryakāntādagnimutpādayituṃ samartho na candrakāntācca pānīyam / ubhayaṃ tattatra na vidyate / tathā ca tattvādīnāṃ paṭasyaiva śaktiniyamaḥ syāt / na ca paṭasya tantuṣu sattvaṃ syāditi / etaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? sādhyatvāt / aṃkurādayo 'pi kāryamabādīnām / ataḥ sādhyam / kimaṅkuro 'styatha nāstyeva / tathā sūryakānte 'gniḥ / tadarthameva cāyaṃ vivādo 'nuṣaktaḥ / yattūktamapāṃ vicchinnavānna tāsvaṅkuro 'stīti tatrāpi yāsāmapāṃ bījānupraveśadaṅkurabhāvena vipariṇāmastābhyastasyānanyatvaṃ sādhyam / ato na kiṃcidetat / kiṃ cānyat / rūpavyavasthānācca / tadyathā vijñānotpattihetutve sati na rūpaṃ dṛṣṭamiti nedānīṃ tatsāmānyāt rūpamapyarūpaṃ bhavati / evaṃ paṭakāraṇatvādvemādayo na paṭa iti nedānīṃ tantavopyapaṭaḥ / tasmādyuktametacchaktasya śakyakaraṇātsatkāryam /
children.translated_text: The rule 'this is capable for that, and that has the power for this' is observed among existing things. For example, the eye [has the power] for form. And this rule exists between cloth and the loom and so forth. Therefore the effect is pre-existent. If one objects that [this is like] the restriction due to auxiliary causes — one might say: just as water is capable of producing the sprout from a seed but not fire from wood, and both [seed and water] exist there; since [the sprout] is separate from the water of the seed. And just as the sun is capable of producing fire from a sun-stone but not water from a moon-stone, and both [fire and water] do not exist there — similarly, the restriction of capacity would be for cloth alone with respect to threads and so forth, but the existence of cloth in the threads would not follow. But this is unjustified. Why? Because it is what needs to be proved. Sprouts and the like are also effects of seeds and the like. Therefore this is what needs to be proved: does the sprout exist [in the seed] or not at all? Similarly, fire in the sun-stone. And it is precisely for this purpose that this debate has been undertaken. As for what was said — 'the sprout does not exist in the water, since it is separate from them' — there too, that [sprout's] non-difference from those waters into which the seed has entered and which have undergone transformation in the form of the sprout is what needs to be proved. Therefore this amounts to nothing. Moreover, because of the stability of form. Just as, though being a cause of the arising of cognition, form is not [itself] seen — it does not follow from that generality that form too is formless. Similarly, though the loom and so forth are causes of cloth, they are not cloth — it does not follow from that that threads too are not cloth. Therefore this is justified: the effect is pre-existent because what is capable can be produced by what has the power.
And because of the state of being a cause, the effect is pre-existent. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 9)

children.text: ihāsati kārye kāraṇabhāvo nāsti / tadyathā vandhyāyāḥ / asti ceha kāraṇabhāvastantupaṭayostasmātsatkāryam / kāraṇāntarātkāryotpattidarśanādanyatra tadbuddhiriti cet syānmataṃ prākkāraṇāntarātkāryāntarasyāsata utpattimupalabhya paścātkāraṇāntare kāraṇabuddhirbhavatīti / etaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? anabhyupagamāt / asataḥ kāryasyotpattireva na siddhā śaśaviṣāṇādiṣvasiddhatvāt / kutaḥ punastannimittākārabuddhiḥ ? kāraṇabhāvāditi cet - syādetat, asattvāviśeṣe 'pi paṭasya kāraṇaṃ samavāyyasamavāyinimittalakṣaṇamasti / tasmātpaṭa ucyate, na śaśaviṣāṇasyeti / etaccāyuktam / kutaḥ hetvabhāvāt / asattvāviśeṣe 'pi paṭasya kāraṇamasti na śaśaviṣāṇasyetyatra heturanuktaḥ / puruṣavaditi cet syādetat, yathā tulyatve sattve paṭasya kāraṇamasti na puruṣasya, evamasattve paṭasya saṃsthānaṃ na śaśaviṣāṇasyetyetadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? uktatvāt / saṃsthānaṃ kāryaṃ paṭasya / saṃsthānaṃ na puruṣasyetyuktaṃ prāk / saṃsthānavattadviśeṣa iti cet syānmataṃ yathā sattvāviśeṣe paṭaḥ saṃsthānaṃ na puruṣa evamasattvāviśeṣe paṭaḥ kāryaṃ na śaśaviṣāṇamiti / etadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvāt / sāmānyasya hi viśeṣaparigrahaḥ saṃsthānam / na tvayamasti cetanāśaktau vikalpaḥ / tasmānna puruṣaḥ saṃsthānam / asatastu nirātmakatvādviśeṣo durupapādaḥ / tadupapattau vā sattvaprasaṃga iti / āha ca-

children.translated_text: Since all non-existent things are devoid of essence, they are undifferentiated;
if you [assert] a distinguishing feature, you must accept that what is different from them has existence.

Here, when the effect does not exist, the state of being a cause does not exist — as, for example, in the case of a barren woman. But here, the state of being a cause does exist between thread and cloth; therefore the effect is pre-existent. If one objects: 'The notion of cause arises elsewhere from seeing that the effect arises from another cause' — one might say that, having previously observed the origination of a different effect from a different cause, one subsequently has the notion of cause in another [pair]. But this is unjustified. Why? Because it is not accepted. The origination of a non-existent effect is itself not established, since it is unestablished in the case of hare's horns and the like. How then can the notion of cause arise on account of that? If one says 'because of the state of being a cause' — one might say: even though there is no distinction in non-existence, there is a cause for cloth characterized as inherent, non-inherent, and instrumental. Therefore cloth is spoken of [as having a cause], not a hare's horn. But this is unjustified. Why? Because no reason is given. No reason has been stated for why, despite the non-distinction in non-existence, cloth has a cause but a hare's horn does not. If one says 'like <s>puruṣa</s>' — one might say: just as, despite the equality in existence, cloth has a cause but <s>puruṣa</s> does not — so too, despite the equality in non-existence, cloth has a configuration but a hare's horn does not. But this too is unjustified. Why? Because it has been stated. Configuration is the effect of cloth; configuration does not belong to <s>puruṣa</s> — this was stated before. If one says 'like a specific [difference] within configuration' — one might hold: just as despite the non-distinction in existence, cloth has configuration but <s>puruṣa</s> does not, so despite the non-distinction in non-existence, cloth is an effect but a hare's horn is not. But this too is unjustified. Why? Because of the relation of universal and particular. For configuration is the particular's inclusion within the universal. But this distinction does not apply to the power of consciousness. Therefore <s>puruṣa</s> is not a configuration. But for the non-existent, since it is devoid of essence, a particular difference is difficult to establish. And if it were established, the consequence of existence [would follow]. And it is said:

children.text:
tasmādyuktametatkāraṇabhāvācca satkāryam / evaṃ tāvadvaiśeṣikamatenāsatkāryavādo na vimardasahaḥ /
  bauddhapakṣe tu bhūyāndoṣaḥ / kathaṃ tarhi dravyāntaraṃ paṭo neṣyate ? "tantuṣveva tathāstheṣu paṭa ityādibuddhayaḥ" ityevamādinā nyāyenāvayavipratiṣedhātsaṃyogo 'pi na saṃyogibhyasteṣāmarthāntaramiṣṭaḥ / tatraitāvatī parikalpanā syāt- yaduta tantusaṃyogo vā paṭaḥ, saṃyogakāraṇaṃ vā dravyāntaram ? ubhayaṃ ca teṣāṃ nārthāntaram / athotpattivināśau kasyāpīti māyākāraceṣṭitam / tadapi citrataro 'yamupanyāsaḥ / kāṇādānāṃ tu dravyāntarottpativināśābhyupagamānna tārkikasadṛśo vicāraḥ / tasmātpāramarṣa eva pakṣo jyāyān / yathā cāsatkāryaṃ na saṃbhavati tathā caśabdātsadasatkāryamapi /
  parasparavirodhāt naiva sannāsaditi eke / etadapyanupapannam / kasmāt ? sattve hetvabhidhānānniścitaḥ prāgutpatteḥ kāryasya sadbhāvaḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text:
Therefore, this is proper: the effect pre-exists in the cause (<s>satkārya</s>), because of its [relation of] being a cause. Thus, according to the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> view, the doctrine of non-pre-existence of the effect (<s>asatkāryavāda</s>) cannot withstand scrutiny.
  In the Buddhist position, however, there is an even greater defect. How is it that cloth is not accepted as a different substance? By the reasoning of 'When the threads remain in the same condition, cognitions such as "this is cloth" arise' — since they deny the whole (<s>avayavin</s>), conjunction too is not accepted by them as something different from the things conjoined. In that case, only this much could be supposed: Is cloth the conjunction of threads, or is it a different substance that is the cause of conjunction? And for them, neither alternative is something different [from the parts]. If then [one asks]: production and destruction belong to what exactly? — this is the performance of a magician. And this presentation is even more extraordinary. But for the followers of <s>Kaṇāda</s>, because they accept the production and destruction of a different substance, the inquiry is not similar to that of the logicians. Therefore, the position of the <s>Ṛṣi</s>s [i.e., the Sāṃkhya view] alone is superior. And just as the non-pre-existence of the effect (<s>asatkārya</s>) is impossible, so too is the [doctrine of] the effect being both existent and non-existent (<s>sadasatkārya</s>), from [the force of] scripture.
  Some [hold that the effect is] neither existent nor non-existent, because of their mutual contradiction. This too is untenable. Why? Because, since reasons have been stated for [its] existence, the existence of the effect prior to its production is established with certainty. // 9 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 10

children.text:
prakṛtamidānīṃ vakṣyāmaḥ / kiṃ ca prakṛtam ? mahadādi tacca kāryaṃ prakṛtivirūpaṃ sarūpaṃ ceti vacanādvairūpyam /
  āha- prāksārūpyagrahaṇaṃ, sukhapratipattihetutvāt / adhigatasārūpyasya hi sukhaṃ vairūpyasya pratipattirbhavatīti prāksārūpyagrahaṇaṃ kartavyam / yathā tantrāntarīyāṇāṃ sadanityaṃ dravyavatkāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣavaditi dravyaguṇakarmaṇāmaviśeṣasāmānyamuktvā dravyāṇi dravyāntaramārabhante guṇāśca guṇāntaramityevamādiḥ viśeṣo 'bhidhīyate /
  ucyate- tadanupapattiḥ / aviśeṣāt / yathaivādhigatasārūpyasya laghīyasī vairūpyapratipattirevamadhigatavairūpyasya laghīyasī sārūpyapratipattiḥ / kasmāt ? parasparāpekṣatvāt / vairūpyāpekṣaṃ hi sārūpyaṃ, sārūpyāpekṣaṃ ca vairūpyamiti /
  āha- evamapi vairūpyasya prāgabhidhāne prayojanavacanam / dvayoraviśeṣe 'nyatarasya prāgabhidhāne niyamaheturvaktavya iti /
  ucyate na, vairūpyasya prakaraṇānaṅgabhāvāt / vicchinnaṃ hi vairūpyamatastatpūrvamabhidhāya prakaraṇāṅgaṃ sārūpyaṃ sukhamabhidhātumityevamarthamācāryeṇaivaṃ kriyate / kathaṃ sārūpyasya prakaraṇāṅgatvamiti cet traiguṇyābhidhānadvāreṇa guṇalakṣaṇopadeśāt /
tatsiddhau cāvivekyādīnāṃ vyaktasiddheḥ, kāraṇaguṇātmakatvācca kāryasya pradhāne traiguṇyādipratipatteḥ, kāryakāraṇabhāvāsandehācca pradhānāstitvaprasiddhyapadeśāttatsiddhau ca bhogyasya bhoktrapekṣatvāt puruṣasiddheradhigatabhoktṛbhogyasya tatsaṃyogasya ca sukhapratipādyatvāttādarthyācca tattvabhūtabhāvasargāṇām / tasmādyuktametatprakaraṇāṅgatvātsārūpyaṃ paścānnirdiśyate / tadasambandhāditaratprāgiti /
  āha- yadi tarhi bhavānprāgvairūpyābhidhānaṃ nyāyyaṃ manyate tadvaktavyaṃ kiṃ punaridaṃ vairūpyamiti /
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
We shall now discuss what was introduced. And what was introduced? [The statement that] 'the effect beginning with <s>mahat</s> is both dissimilar and similar to <s>Prakṛti</s>' — from this statement, [we begin with] dissimilarity (<s>vairūpya</s>).
  [The objector] says: Similarity (<s>sārūpya</s>) should be presented first, because it serves as the cause of easy understanding. For one who has grasped similarity easily understands dissimilarity. Therefore, similarity should be presented first. Just as proponents of other systems [say]: 'The existent, non-eternal, substance-possessing effect is a cause possessing universals and particulars' — having first stated what is common (<s>aviśeṣa</s>) to substance, quality, and action, they then state the particular: 'Substances produce other substances, and qualities produce other qualities,' and so forth.
  It is replied: That is untenable. Because there is no difference [in ease of understanding]. Just as the understanding of dissimilarity is easier for one who has grasped similarity, so too the understanding of similarity is easier for one who has grasped dissimilarity. Why? Because they are mutually dependent. For similarity depends on dissimilarity, and dissimilarity depends on similarity.
  [The objector] says: Even so, a reason must be stated for presenting dissimilarity first. When there is no difference between the two, a determining reason must be given for presenting one before the other.
  It is replied: No, because dissimilarity is not a limb of the [main] topic. For dissimilarity is disconnected [from the main argument]. Therefore, by stating it first, the teacher does this so that similarity, which is a limb of the topic, can be stated easily afterward. How is similarity a limb of the topic? Because through the statement of the three <s>guṇa</s>s, the characteristics of the <s>guṇa</s>s are taught.
  And when that is established, from non-discrimination (<s>aviveka</s>) and the like, the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) is established; and because the effect is of the nature of the <s>guṇa</s>s of its cause, the three <s>guṇa</s>s and the like are understood in <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter); and because there is no doubt about the cause-effect relationship, the existence of <s>pradhāna</s> is demonstrated; and when that is established, because what is enjoyed (<s>bhogya</s>) requires an enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>), <s>Puruṣa</s> (the self) is established; and having understood the enjoyer and the enjoyed, their conjunction is easily taught; and because the categories (<s>tattva</s>s), elements (<s>bhūta</s>s), and creation (<s>sarga</s>) serve that purpose. Therefore, it is proper that similarity, being a limb of the topic, is stated afterward. And dissimilarity, being unrelated [to the main topic], comes first.
  [The objector] says: If you consider it proper to state dissimilarity first, then it should be stated: what exactly is this dissimilarity?
  It is replied:

[The manifest is] caused (<s>hetumat</s>), non-eternal (<s>anitya</s>), non-pervasive (<s>avyāpin</s>), active (<s>sakriya</s>), manifold (<s>aneka</s>), dependent (<s>āśrita</s>), an inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>),
having parts (<s>sāvayava</s>), and subordinate (<s>paratantra</s>) — [such is] the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>). The unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is the opposite. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 10 //

children.text:
tatra hetuḥ kāraṇamityanarthāntaram / tadasyāstīti hetumat / nityaṃ dhruvam / na nityamanityam / vyāpnotīti vyāpi / na vyāpyavyāpi / asarvagatamityarthaḥ / saha kriyayā sakriyam / anekaṃ bhinnam / āśritamādheyam / liṅgaṃ tallakṣaṇopapannam / avayūyanta ityavayavāḥ / pṛthagupalabhyanta ityarthaḥ / sahāvayavaiḥ sāvayavam / paratantramanyādhīnam / ete hetumadādayaḥ paratantrāntā nirapavādāḥ vyaktasyāsādhāraṇā pradhānapuruṣābhyāṃ dharmāḥ /
  āha- hetumadityaviśeṣaḥ sarvatra sadbhāvāt / vyaktāvyaktapuruṣāṇāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ heturastīti aviśeṣa evāyaṃ paṭhitavyaḥ /
  ucyate na, kārakaparigrahāt / yadyapi vyaktāvyaktapuruṣāṇāmaviśiṣṭaṃ hetumattvaṃ tathāpi viśiṣṭasya kārakasya hetoḥ parigrahaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / sa ca vyaktasyaiva nānyasyeti nāyamaviśeṣo bhaviṣyati /
  āha- tadanupapattiḥ, viśeṣānupādānāt / heturiti sāmānyaśabdo 'yam / sāmānyaśabdāśca nārthaprakaraṇaśabdāntarābhisambandhamantareṇa viśeṣe 'vatiṣṭhanta iti viśeṣa upādeyaḥ syāt / sa tu nopādīyate / tasmātte aviśeṣā eveti /
  ucyate na, sarvasambhavino 'bhidhānasya prakarṣārthatvāt / iha yaḥ sarvasaṃbhavī dharma ekaviṣaya upādīyate tasmātprakarṣo vijñāyate / tadyathā bhoktā māṇavaka ityukte sarveṣāṃ bhoktṛtvasya saṃbhavādevaṃ vijñāyate prakarṣeṇāyaṃ bhokteti, evamihāpi sarvasambhavītyāhācāryo vyaktaṃ hetumaditi / tena vayamasmātprakarṣaṃ vijñāsyāmaḥ / kaśca prakarṣaḥ ? kārakajñāpakayorubhayorapi sambhave kārakasyaiva grahaṇam / anityaśabdasambandhādvā / athavāyamācāryo hetumadityuktvānityamiti paṭhati / śabdāntarābhisambandhāt / yo 'nityasahacaro hetustasyeha grahaṇaṃ gamyate / kaścānityasahacaro hetuḥ ? kārakaḥ /
  āha evamapyanupapannametat / kasmāt ? ubhayatra tatsaṃbhavāt / utpādyavyaṅgyayorhi vināśaṃ paṭādiṣu dṛṣṭatvāt avyabhicārāttantrāntarīyā manyante / tasya vā parihāro vaktavyaḥ / na vā vaktavyo viśeṣe sthitirastīti /
  ucyate na, ekāntavādaprasaṅgāt / sarveṇa hi vādināvaśyaṃ kiṃcinnityamabhyupagantavyam / antato vināśe 'pi na kaścidarthaḥ śabdabuddhibhyāṃ na vyajyate / tathā satyekāntavādo 'yaṃ syāt / sa ca yuktimadbhirneṣyate / tathā ca saṃskṛtamapyevaṃ kalpyamāne vināśi syāt / tasmādutpādyavyaṅgyayorvināśaṃ bruvato 'tisāhasam /
  āha- anityatvānupapattiḥ satkāryavādābhyupagamāt / yathaiva hi nāsata utpattirastyevaṃ sato 'pi vināśena na bhavitavyam / atha sato 'pi vināśo 'bhyupagamyate tena pralayakāle vinaṣṭānāṃ tattvādīnāṃ praścādasatāmutpattiḥ satkāryavādaṃ nirākuryāt / tasmādanityaṃ vyaktamityayuktam /
  ucyate- na, vyaktyapagamapratijñānāt / sadā vayaṃ sato 'vināśamācakṣāṇāḥ (na ?) satkāryavādaṃ pratyācakṣīmahi / kāraṇānāṃ tu yaḥ parasparaṃ saṃsargāt saṃsthānaviśeṣaparigrahastasya virodhiśaktyantarāvirbhavādvyaktistirodhīyata ityetad vināśaśabdena vivakṣitam / tathā ca vārṣagaṇāḥ paṭhanti- "tadetat trailokyaṃ vyakterapaiti, na sattvādapetamapyasti vināśapratiṣedhāt / asaṃsargāccāsya saukṣmyaṃ saukṣmyāccānupalabdhistasmādvyaktyapagamo vināśaḥ / sa tu dvividhaḥ- ā sargapralayāt tattvānāṃ kiñcitkālāntarāvasthānāditareṣām" iti /
  āha- ayuktametat / kasmāt ? vipratipatteḥ / sarvameva kṣaṇikaṃ buddhibodhyamākāśanirodhavarjitamiti śākyaputrīyāḥ pratipannāḥ / teṣāṃ pratiṣedho vaktavyo vā na vaktavyaṃ dvividhamanityamiti / ucyate- na, hetvanupagamāt / pratikṣaṇamucchidyate trailokyamityatra liṅgamabhiyuktā api nopalabhāmahe / tasmāt naitadasmākaṃ buddhāvavatiṣṭhata iti /
  āha- ante kṣayadarśanāt, iha yasyānte kṣayastasya kṣaṇikatvaṃ dṛṣṭam / tadyathā, pradīpajvālābuddhiśabdānām / asti cānte kṣayaḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ tasmāt kṣaṇikāḥ ucyante / tadanupapattiḥ, sādhyatvāt / iha tu siddhenātideśo bhavati / tad yathā gavā gavayasya / na tu pradīpajvālābuddhiśabdānāṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ prasiddham / ato na kiñcidetat /
  āha- naitadaprasiddham / kasmāt ? vṛddhyadarśanāt / yadi hi avinaṣṭāyāṃ jvālāyāmindhanāntarāle jvālāntaramutpadyeta vṛddhirapi syāt, na tu dṛśyate / tasmādanavasthitā pradīpajvālā / kiñcāśrayābhāvāt / yadāśrayā jvālotpattistadutpadyamānaivāsau niruṇaddhīti na yuktamasyā vināśrayeṇāvasthātum / upayuktendhanāyā apyavasthānaprasaṅgāt / kiñcāvaraṇoparipātena prabhābhedaprasaṅgāt / jvālānāmavasthānamicchata upariṣṭādāvaraṇopanipātāt prabhāyāstantoriva dvaidhīkaraṇaṃ syāt / aniṣṭañcaitat / tasmānna dīpe jvālānāmavasthitirastīti / etena śabdo 'pi pratyuktaḥ / katham ? tasyāpi yadi vināśo na syāt, drutapavanāmbudhārābhighātāt pratikṣaṇamapūrvaśabdāvirbhāvāt pūrvaśabdavināśācca vṛddhiḥ syāt / adṛṣṭā cāsau / kiñca, pratyakṣata upalabdheḥ / pāṇyupaghātajo hi śabda utpatterūrdhvaṃ na bhavatīti pratyakṣasiddham / abhivyaktiriti cenna, niyamādarśanāt / śabdānāṃ vācyavaktṛbhedabhinnānāṃ kāraṇaniyamo dṛṣṭaḥ / na caitadasti samānendriyagrāhyāṇām / kiñca- pṛthak śruteḥ / abhivyaktikāraṇadeśācca pṛthak śrūyate śabdaḥ / na caitadabhivyaṅgyānāṃ ghaṭādīnāṃ dṛṣṭamiti / kṣaṇikabuddhestu prāgevoktā nāśahetavaḥ / tatra yaduktaṃ sādhyatvāt pradīpajvālābuddhiśabdādīnāṃ kṣaṇikatvasya na saṃskārāḥ kṣaṇikā ityetadayuktam /
  ucyate- yaduktaṃ vṛddhyadarśanāditi, atra brūmaḥ- ayuktametat / kasmāt ? viśeṣapratipatteḥ / kṣaṇikamityuktaparimāṇo 'yaṃ kālanirdeśa āśrīyate, vṛddhyabhāvādibhyaśca kadācidvināśamātraṃ pratīyate / sa tu vināśa ekakṣaṇamavasthitānāṃ jvālānāṃ bhavati na punaḥ kṣaṇadvayamityetadapramāṇakamājñāmātrañca gṛhītaśikṣākaḥ kaḥ pratipattumutsaheta ? yattūktamāvaraṇopanipātāt prabhābhedaprasaṅga iti, etadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? ubhayathānupapatteḥ / kiṃ tāvadyasya dvaidhībhāvo dṛṣṭastadakṣaṇikamāhosvid yasya na dṛṣṭastat kṣaṇikamiti / kiñcātaḥ ? tadyadi tāvadevamabhyupagamyate yasya dvaidhībhāvastadakṣaṇikamiti tantorakṣaṇikatvaprasaṅgaḥ / atha mataṃ yasya dvaidhīkaraṇaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ tat kṣaṇikamiti yathā kimatrodāharaṇam / kutaḥ ? yasmāt na hyanudāhṛto vādaḥ / etena śabdavṛddhiḥ pratyuktā / yatpunaretaduktaṃ pāṇyupaghātajaśabdānavasthānāditi, tatra bhavataivoktaṃ vyaṅgyatvāditi / yattūktaṃ niyamadarśanānna vyaṅgyaḥ śabda iti tadayuktam, anekāntāt / yathā śuklakṛṣṇau niyamataḥ śuklakṛṣṇaśabdābhyāṃ pratyāyyete, na ca tau tayorna vyaṅgyau / evaṃ śabdasyāpi vaktyavādiniyamaḥ syāt, na cāvyaṅgyaḥ syāt / yadapyuktaṃ vyaṅgyavyañjakayordeśabhedānupapatterna vyaṅgyaḥ śabda iti, tadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? cakṣurvat tatsiddheḥ / tadyathā- cakṣuṣo rūpasya ca deśabhede 'pi vyaṅgyavyañjakabhāvaḥ, evaṃ śabdasyāpi syāt / tasmānna śabdo 'pi kṣaṇikaḥ / buddhestu svādhikāra eva kṣaṇikatve heturiti karaṇo (kāraṇam ?) vakṣyāmaḥ / tatra yaduktamante kṣayadarśanāt pradīpajvālābuddhiśabdavat kṣaṇikāḥ saṃskārā ityetadayuktamiti / āha- itastarhi pradīpādīnāmanyeṣāṃ ca bhāvānāṃ kṣaṇikatvam / kutaḥ ? anavasthānahetvabhāvāt / naṣṭaścedartho 'bhyupagamyate nanu prāptamidamutpannamātrasyāsya vināśavighno nāstīti kauṭasthyaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ prāptamiti / ucyate- na, kāraṇopapatteḥ / adhikāro hi sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃskāravaśādutpattistadavasthānameva
teṣāmalaṃ sthitaye / sati vinaśvaratve saṃskāropayoge tu sthityapabhraṃśa ityato 'sti kiñcitkālamavasthānaṃ bhāvānām / na ca kauṭasthyaprasaṅgaḥ / kiñcānyat- santativināśaprasaṅgāt / naṃṣṭuścedutpattisamanantaraṃ vināśa iṣyate, santatirapyante kṣayadarśanāt naṃṣṭrī / tasyā api tathaiva vināśaḥ prāptaḥ / tataśca taḍidvilasitavatkṣaṇadṛṣṭanaṣṭasya trailokyasyābhāve saṃsārocchedaprasaṅgaḥ / tasmādayuktaṃ naṃṣṭurutpattisamakālameva vināśa iti / kāraṇāvasthānāt na doṣa iti cet- syānmatam, asti kāraṇaṃ pūrvotpanno bhāva uttarasyotpattau / sa cāpyuttarasya, ityevaṃ santateranucchedo virodhibhāvāntarasaṃsargāt tūbhayatastathotpatterbhraṃśa iti / etadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? pūrvahetutyāgāt / prāguktaṃ yena naṃṣṭavyamasau mantrauṣadhaprayogairapi kṣaṇādūrddhvaṃ nāvatiṣṭhate / sāmprataṃ tu naṃṣṭrī santatiḥ kāraṇavaśādeva tiṣṭhatīti so 'yaṃ pūrvahetutyāgaḥ / vināśahetvabhāvāt kṣaṇikatvamiti cet, syādetat nāsti bhāvānāṃ vināśahetorupalambha iti / ataḥ svābhāvikaḥ pradhvaṃsaḥ / tasmādutpattisamakālamasau kena vāryate / idamapyayuktam / kasmāt ? anabhyupagamāt / ko hyetadavamaṃsyati ahetuko vināśaḥ / kiṃ tarhi prāgevoktamarthavaśādbhāvānāṃ sthitistadava....virodhidravyāntarasambandhenādhyātmikādinā bhavatīti / vināśasya vināśaprasaṅgādayuktamiti cet, yadi tarhyabhāvo 'pi hetumān parikalpyate; prāptamasyāpi ghaṭavad vināśitvam / aniṣṭaṃ caitat / tasmādahetuko vināśa ityetadayuktam / kasmāt ? vyaktyapagamapratijñānāt / bhāvavināśinaṃ prati satyamevāyamupālambhaḥ syāt / vyaktyapagamastu no vināśaḥ / sa tu hetumattvena kathaṃ virotsyata iti / tasmānna vināśahetvabhāvāt kṣaṇikaṃ saṃskṛtamiti / itaśca na kṣaṇikam / kasmāt ? agrahaṇaprasaṅgāt / ihāsato 'grahaṇaṃ dṛṣṭam / tadyathā dvitīyasya śirasaḥ / kṣaṇādūrdhvaṃ ca te ghaṭādayo na bhavanti / tasmātteṣāmapyagrahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ / tatsadṛśotpatteradoṣa iti cet syādetat - utpattisamakālaṃ nirodhe 'pi ghaṭasyānyasya tādṛśasyotpattirbhavati, tannirodhe 'nyasyetyevamavicchedena
grahaṇaṃ bhavati, jvālānadīsroto 'nusandhānavaditi / etadapyayuktam / kutaḥ ? kāraṇābhāvāt / syādetadevaṃ yadi tadānīṃ sadṛśotpattau kāraṇaṃ syāt / na tu tadasti, prāgeva nirodhāt / tasmādasadetat / pūrvotpannasya kāraṇabhāvāttatsiddhiriti cenna, upādānāt tanniṣpattiprasiddheḥ / ihopādānānmṛtpiṇḍakasaṃjñakālloke ghaṭaniṣpattiḥ prasiddhā / na ca tadānimasti mṛtpiṇḍaḥ / kiñca kramanupalabdheḥ / iha śibikādīnāmanukrameṇa ghaṭotpattirupalabhyate / na cānukramo 'sti / kiñca kārakasāmagryābhavāt / iha kumbhakāradaṇḍacakrasūtropalasāmagryād ghaṭaniṣpattiḥ prasiddhā / na cāstyeṣāṃ tatra sambhavaḥ / kiñca tadutpādyāntarotpādyasyāniṣpatteḥ / iha ghaṭād ghaṭe nirvṛttirna prasiddhā loke / na cāprasiddho 'sti dṛṣṭāntaḥ / buddhiśabdavaditi cet syādetat yathā buddhirbuddhyantaraṃ sadṛśaṃ sūte, śabdaśca śabdāntaramevaṃ ghaṭādghaṭaniṣpattirbhavati iti / etadapyasat / kasmāt ? siddhaṃ hi buddherbuddhyantaraṃ śabdācca śabdāntaraṃ jāyata ityetadapyasmākaṃ prasiddham / tasmātpralāpamātrametat / tatra yaduktaṃ sadṛśotpatteḥ so 'yamiti grahaṇamavicchinnaṃ kṣaṇikatve 'pi bhāvānāmityetadayuktam / kiñcānyat / kāryotpattikāle kāraṇanivṛtteḥ / yadā na kāraṇamasti na tadā kāryamutpadyate dvayorghaṭayoryugapadupalabdhiprasaṅgāt / yadā tu kāryamutpadyate tadā kāraṇaṃ niruddhamiti nirbījaḥ pradurbhāvaḥ prāpnoti / aniṣṭaṃ caitat, satatotpattiprasaṃgāt / anutpanne hetusāmarthyādadoṣa iti cet syāttadanutpanne kārye kāraṇena prayojanam / utpanne tadvyāpārānarthakyāt / asti cānutpanne kārye kāraṇam / ato na nirbījaḥ prādurbhāva iti / etadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? abhāve 'pi tadutpattiprasaṅgāt / aṃga tāvat aṇuśo vibhajyatāmagnau vā kṣipyantām,
tantavastadāpi prasiddhavināśānāmabhūvanniti śakyamupadeṣṭuṃ, yadi tebhyaḥ paṭa utpadyate / tasmādbhrāntiriyam / yugapatkāryakāraṇayorutpattinirodhau tulānatonnatavaditi cet syādetadyathā nāmonnāmau tulāntaryā (?) yaugapadyena bhavata evamutpattivināśau kāryakāraṇayoriti / tadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? kāryakāraṇabhāvādarśanāt / kimidamudake nimajjadbhiḥ phenamavalambyate ? tulyā tasya hyekasyāvanatiravasthā tad dvitīyasyonnataye heturbhavati, bhavataḥ kāraṇavināśaḥ kāryotpattiśca yaugapadyena bhavataḥ / na ca tayorhetumadbhāvaḥ śakyaḥ kalpayitum / tasmādayuktametat / viśeṣagrahaṇāt kṣaṇikatvasiddhiriti cet syānmatam- yadyutpannamātroparatirnāsti bhāvānāṃ, kiṃkayutaḥ śarīrādīnāṃ prāṇāpānaśramarūpādikṛto 'bjāśmaprabhṛtīnāṃ ca śītoṣṇasparśakṛto bhedaḥ ? ghaṇṭādīnāṃ cāśabdakānāṃ paścācchabdavatāṃ grahaṇam, tasmādaniṣiddhaḥ kṣaṇabhaṅga ityetaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? uktatvāt / uktamatrottaraṃ kāraṇābhāve 'nutpattiprasaṅgāediti / kiñca saṃsthānāntarānupaladheḥ / na hyatra pūrvasaṃśānaviparītaṃ saṃsthānāntaraṃ gṛhṇīmahe / tasmādaviśiṣṭāsta ityevamavagamyatām / viśeṣagrahaṇantvavastvantarānugrahe śaktyantarāvirbhāvāt / uuktaṃ ca- "vyakterapagamo 'bhīṣṭaḥ pūrvasaṃsthānahānitaḥ / tadabhāvādasidho 'sya viśe....
