āha evamapyasya vyaktahetutvamanupapannam, ekatvāt / bahūnāṃ kāryārambho dṛṣṭastantvādīnām / ekaṃ pradhānaṃ, tasmānna tadārambhaśaktiyuktamiti /
  ucyate- yadyapi guṇānāṃ pradhānalakṣaṇamavasthāntaramabhinnabuddhinimittatvādekamapi kāryakāle kiṃcidvaiṣamyopajanitavyapadeśyarūpābhiritaretaropakāriṇībhiḥ śaktibhiḥ smudāyatvamāpadyate / tasmādidānīṃ
children.translated_text:
[The objector] says: Even so, its being the cause of the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) is untenable, because of its oneness. The commencement of an effect by multiple [causes] is observed — such as threads and the like. <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) is one; therefore it is not endowed with the power to produce [effects].
It is replied: Although the state called <s>pradhāna</s> — which is another condition of the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents) — is one, due to being the cause of an undifferentiated cognition, still at the time of effect-production, through a certain disequilibrium, with powers that are mutually assisting — [each being] of inexpressible form — it attains the state of being an aggregate. Therefore now —
[The manifest] proceeds from the three <s>guṇas</s> and from [their] aggregate.

children.text:
pravartate ityanenotpattimācaṣṭe / triguṇata ityavyapadeśyarūpāṇāṃ pradhānāpradhānabhāvena guṇaśaktīnāṃ vaiṣamyādvyapadeśyarūpāntaramāha / yatraitacchakyate vaktuṃ trayaḥ sattvādaya iti tadavasthānaṃ kāryārambhakamiti / samudayādityanena parasparāpekṣāṇāmārambhaśaktimavadyotayati / etaduktaṃ bhavati- kāryakāle guṇāḥ parityaktapūrvāvasthā bhedaṃ pratilabhya parasparopakāreṇa saṃhanyate / saṃhatāśca vyaktamutpādayanti / tasmānnāvasthāntarasyābhinnabuddhinimittatvātpradhānaikatvadoṣaḥ guṇabhedānnaikasya kāryārambha iti /
  āha, niṣkriyatvāttarhi prakṛteḥ kāryārambho 'nupapannaḥ / kriyātvānabhyupagame vā vyaktavaidharmyavirodha iti /
  ucyate- na, kriyāvaidharmyabhedāt / dvividhā hi kriyā praspandalakṣaṇā pariṇāmalakṣaṇā ca / tatra praspandaḥ pradhānasya saukṣmyātpratiṣidhyate /
children.translated_text:
'Proceeds' — by this he indicates origination. 'From the three <s>guṇas</s>' — he states another [mode], whose form is expressible, [arising] from the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇa</s>-powers — which [in their prior state] are of inexpressible form — through [their assuming] relations of predominance and subordination. That condition where one can say 'these three are <s>sattva</s> and the rest' — that state is the productive [one] of the effect. 'From the aggregate' — by this he illuminates the productive power of those that are mutually dependent. The meaning stated is this: at the time of effect-production, the <s>guṇas</s>, having abandoned their previous state, having attained differentiation, combine through mutual assistance. And being combined, they produce the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>). Therefore, there is no fault of <s>pradhāna</s>'s oneness due to its other state being the cause of undifferentiated cognition; and there is no [fault that] a single [thing] cannot commence an effect, because of the differentiation of the <s>guṇas</s>.
[The objector] says: Then, because of <s>Prakṛti</s>'s inactivity (<s>niṣkriyatva</s>), the commencement of the effect is untenable. Or if activity is not accepted, there is a contradiction with the dissimilarity from the manifest.
It is replied: No — because of the distinction in the types of activity. For activity is twofold: characterized by vibration (<s>praspanda</s>) and characterized by transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>). Therein, vibration is denied of <s>pradhāna</s> due to its subtlety.
[But] through transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>)

children.text:
tu tatkāryamārabhate iti /
  āha- nanu ca pariṇāmo 'pi saukṣmyātpradhānasya nopapadyate / kasmāt ? na hi saukṣmyātsūkṣmasyākāśādervipariṇāmo dṛṣṭa iti /
  ucyate-
  saṃskārasya saukṣmye 'pi pariṇāmo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ / tasmād yuktaḥ sūkṣmapariṇāmīti //
children.translated_text:
it commences its effect.
[The objector] says: But transformation too is untenable for <s>pradhāna</s> due to its subtlety. Why? Because transformation of something subtle like space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is not observed due to subtlety.
It is replied:
Even given the subtlety of an impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>), transformation must be admitted. Therefore it is proper [to say that] the subtle undergoes transformation.

children.text:
āha, kaḥ punarayaṃ pariṇāmo nāma ?
  ucyate-
  jahaddharmāntaraṃ pūrvamādatte yadā param /
  tattvādapracyuto dharmī pariṇāmaḥ sa ucyate // iti /
  yadā śaktyantarānugrahātpūrvadharmān tirobhāvya svarūpādapracyuto dharmī dharmāntareṇāvirbhavati tadavasthānamasmākaṃ pariṇāma ityucyate /
  āha, naitadabhidhānamātraṃ dṛṣṭāntamantareṇa pratipadyāmahe / tasmādyathā kimiti vaktavyam /
  ucyate- yathā pālāśaṃ palāśādapracyutanimittāntarasyātapāderanugrahācchyāmatāṃ tirobhāvya pītatāṃ vrajati tathedaṃ draṣṭavyam /
  āha na, anyathotpatterapratiṣedhāt / kathaṃ punaretavagamyate pālāśaṃ svarūpādapracyutaṃ dharmāntarasya parityāgamupādānaṃ ca karoti, na punaranyathā cānyathā copapadyata iti ?
  ucyate- kṣaṇabhaṅgapratiṣedhāt prāgeva kṣaṇabhaṅganirdiṣṭaṃ vinaṣṭānāṃ bhāvānāṃ punarutpattau nāsti kāraṇam / tadabhāve cotpattirayukteti /
  āha, dharmadharmiṇorananyatvābhyupagamāddharmotpattivināśe dharmyutpattivināśaprasaṃgaḥ / na hi vo dharmebhyo 'nyo dharmī / tatra yadi dharmasya nivṛttirabhyupagamyate dharmiṇo 'pi nivṛttirananyatvātprāptā / dharmotpattau tadutpattiḥ / tatra yaduktaṃ dharmotpattivirodhe dharmīsvarūpāvasthānamiti etadayuktam /
  ucyate na, senādivadvyavasthānopapatteḥ / tadyathā senāṅgebhyo 'nanyatvaṃ senāyāḥ / na ca senāṅgānāṃ vināśe senāvināśaḥ / tadyathā nānyaḥ paṭaḥ / bauddhānāṃ saṃyogāvayavipratiṣedhāt / na ca paṭavināśe tantuvināśaḥ / tatra yaduktaṃ dharmivināśe dharmavināśa iti etadayuktam /
  āha, evamapyayuktam / tatkasmāt ? sāmānyaviśeṣayordharmisvarūpaparikalpanānupapatteḥ / iha rūpādisāmānyaṃ vā dharmirūpatvena parikalpyamānaṃ parikalpyeta rūpādiviśeṣo vā ? kiṃ cātaḥ / tatra tāvadrūpādisāmānyaṃ dharmisvarūpamiti śakyaṃ kalpayitum / kasmāt ? asambhavāt / yadi tāvatpṛthivī sāmānyaṃ ghaṭādirviśeṣastena pṛthivyapi tanmātrāpekṣayā viśeṣaḥ / yāvatpradhānamiti nāsti sāmānyam / tadabhāvād dharmisvarūpābhāvaḥ / atha viśeṣā ghaṭādayasteṣāṃ viśeṣāntareṇa sahāvasthānāddharmisvarūpānavasthānāt / tataśca yaduktaṃ svarūpādapracyuto dharmī dharmāntaraṃ vijahāti, dharmāntaramupādatte iti tadvyāhanyata iti /
  ucyate- yaduktaṃ rūpādisāmānyaviśeṣayordharmisvarūpaparikalpanānupapattiriti, astu sāmānyam / yattūktaṃ sāmānyaṃ sāmānyāntarāpekṣaṃ viśeṣatvamiti na pratyayanivṛttau sāmānyābhāvāvasthitestataśca dharmisvarūpasiddheḥ, yāvatpṛthivītyayaṃ pratyayo na nivartate sāmānyaṃ ghaṭādirviśeṣaḥ, dravyatvaṃ cāsau, dharmāntaraparivarteṣu tadākārapratyayotpattitaḥ svarūpāvasthānasiddherdharmā ghaṭādayaḥ / yadā tu pṛthivīpratyayanivṛttistadā tanmātrāṇāṃ sāmānyabhāvo dravyatvaṃ ca viśeṣo dharma iti yāvatpradhānaṃ tasya tu sāmānyāntarānupapatteḥ kauṭasthyameva / yatra sarvaviśeṣābhāvastatpradhānam / yadi tu pṛthivyādīnāṃ nityamavyāvṛtaṃ sati kauṭasthyameṣāṃ prāptam / tasmānna dharmisvarūpābhāvaḥ / śaktervā sāmānyabhāvābhyupagamāt / athavā sukhaduḥkhamohaśaktaya eveha mahadādinā viśeṣāntena liṅgena pariṇāmaṃ pratipadyante / tāsāṃ ca satataṃ sāmānyapratyayanimittatvātsvarūpādapracyute taddravyatvaṃ liṅgasya dharmatvam / aprasiddherayuktamiti cennoktatvāt / prāguktametatsukhādipūrvakaṃ viśvamiti /
  āha- evamapi vaiśvarūpyānupapattiḥ / kāraṇaviśeṣāt / yadi sukhādiśaktaya eva pariṇāminyo yadidaṃ brahmādi sthāvarāntaṃ vaiśvarūpyaṃ tannopapadyate /
  kasmāt ? na hyabhinnaṃ kāryamutpadyata iti /
  ucyate- śaktitaśca pariṇāmini, bhavati tena vaiśvarūpyam / katham ?
children.translated_text:
[The objector] asks: What then is this thing called transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>)?
It is replied:
'When, abandoning a prior property, [a substance] assumes another [property], while the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) does not deviate from its own nature — that is called transformation.'
When, through the assistance of another power, a property-bearer causes its prior properties to disappear and manifests with another property without deviating from its own nature — that state is what we call <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation).
[The objector] says: We do not comprehend this mere statement without an example. Therefore tell us: how is it, like what?
It is replied: Just as a <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) leaf, without deviating from its own nature, through the assistance of another cause such as the sun's heat, causes its dark-green color to disappear and becomes yellow — so should this be understood.
[The objector] says: No — because production in another manner is not ruled out. How do we know that the <s>palāśa</s> leaf, without deviating from its own nature, performs the abandonment of one property and the assumption of another, rather than [the situation being explicable] in some other way?
It is replied: Because momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇa-bhaṅga</s>) is refuted. We have previously stated in the refutation of momentary destruction: for things that have perished, there is no cause for re-arising. And in the absence of that [cause], arising is unjustified.
[The objector] says: Since the non-difference of property (<s>dharma</s>) and property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) is accepted, upon the arising and destruction of the property there would be the undesired consequence of the arising and destruction of the property-bearer. For according to you, the property-bearer is not different from the properties. Therein, if the cessation of a property is accepted, the cessation of the property-bearer too is entailed, due to non-difference. And upon the arising of a property, [there would be] its [the property-bearer's] arising. Therefore what was said — that 'the property-bearer persists in its own nature despite the arising and perishing of properties' — that is unjustified.
It is replied: No — because an arrangement is possible, as with an army and the like. For example, the army is non-different from its limbs. Yet there is no destruction of the army upon the destruction of [some of] its limbs. Similarly, the cloth is not different [from its threads] — due to the Buddhists' denial of conjunction and wholes (<s>avayavin</s>). Yet there is no destruction of threads upon the destruction of the cloth. Therefore what was said — 'upon the destruction of the property-bearer there is destruction of the property' — that is unjustified.
[The objector] says: Even so it is unjustified. Why? Because the property-bearer's essential nature cannot be constructed from either the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) or the particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>) of form and the like. Here, would the universal of form and the like be construed as the property-bearer's essential nature, or the particular of form and the like? What follows from this? First, the universal of form and the like cannot be construed as the property-bearer's essential nature. Why? Because of impossibility. If earth is the universal and pot etc. are the particular, then earth too is a particular relative to the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). [This continues] up to <s>pradhāna</s> — thus there is no [ultimate] universal. In its absence, there is no property-bearer's essential nature. Or if the particulars are pot etc., because of their co-existence with other particulars, the property-bearer's essential nature has no [stable] abiding. Therefore what was said — 'the property-bearer, without deviating from its own nature, abandons one property and assumes another' — that is contradicted.
It is replied: As for what was said — that the property-bearer's essential nature cannot be constructed from either the universal or particular of form and the like: let the universal exist! As for what was said that a universal is a particular relative to another universal — [we reply:] since the universal does not cease upon the cessation of the [specific] cognition [of it], and since the property-bearer's essential nature is established thereby — as long as the cognition 'earth' does not cease, [earth] is the universal, pot etc. are the particular, and it is also a substance (<s>dravya</s>); and since, even amid the changes of properties, the arising of a cognition of that form [i.e., 'earth'] establishes the persistence of the essential nature — the properties are pot and the like. But when the cognition 'earth' ceases, then the <s>tanmātras</s>' universal status and substance-hood [obtain], and the particular is the property — [and this continues] up to <s>pradhāna</s>. But for that [pradhāna], since no other universal is possible, there is absolute permanence (<s>kūṭasthatva</s>) alone. Where all particulars are absent — that is <s>pradhāna</s>. But if for earth and the like there is constant, uninterrupted [identity], then their permanence would follow. Therefore there is no absence of the property-bearer's essential nature. Or, because the <s>śakti</s> (power) is accepted as having the nature of a universal. Or alternatively, the powers of pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>) alone here undergo transformation through another particular sign (<s>liṅga</s>) such as <s>mahat</s> and the rest. And since those [powers] are constantly the cause of [the same] universal cognition, while not deviating from their own nature — that is their substance-hood; the property-hood belongs to the sign (<s>liṅga</s>). [If one objects:] 'This is unjustified because [such powers are] not well-established' — no, because it has been stated [previously]. It was earlier stated that 'the entire universe is preceded by pleasure and the like.'
[The objector] says: Even so, the diversity [of creation] is untenable — because of the [lack of] specific difference in causes. If the powers of pleasure etc. alone are what transforms, then this diversity — from <s>Brahmā</s> down to stationary beings — is untenable.
Why? Because an undifferentiated effect does not arise.
It is replied: Through the [diversity of] powers and their transformation, that diversity comes about. How?
Like water — due to the specific difference of the substrate of each respective <s>guṇa</s>. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 16 //

children.text: yathāntarikṣāviśiṣṭasyāmbhasaḥ pracyutirāśrayeṇa gobhujaṅgamoṣṭrādīnāṃ, viśeṣātkṣīramūtraviṣādivaiśvarūpyaṃ copapadyate / tathā guṇaśaktayo viśiṣṭāḥ parasparāśrayaviśeṣād brahmādi stambāntaṃ jātyākṛtivāgbuddhisvabhāvāhāravihārarūpaṃ vaiśvarūpyaṃ pratipadyante / tasmātsiddhametat prakṛtireva sarvabhāvanāṃ prasavitrī / na ca kaściddoṣa iti // 16 //
children.translated_text: Just as water — indistinguishable from space [i.e., pure and formless when] falling — through the specific quality of its substrate in cows, snakes, camels, and the like, [acquires] the diversity of milk, urine, poison, and the like — that is indeed possible. So too the <s>guṇa</s>-powers, being variously qualified through the specific quality of their mutual substrates, undergo the diversity of form encompassing species, shape, speech, intellect, nature, diet, and behavior — from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a pillar [i.e., from the highest sentient being to insentient matter]. Therefore it is established that <s>Prakṛti</s> alone is the progenitrix of all entities. And there is no defect [in this position]. // 16 //
// Thus ends the fourth lesson in the <s>Yuktidīpikā</s>, following the method of the seventy <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [kārikās]. //
<s>Kārikā</s> 17

children.text: āha, samadhigataṃ pradhānam / puruṣa idānīṃ kāryakāraṇavyatirikto 'stītyetatpratipādyam / kutaḥ saṃśaya iti cet anupalabhyamānasyobhayathā dṛṣṭatvādityuktam / kiṃ cānyat / ācāryavipratipatteḥ / vijñānaskandhavyatirikto nāsti kaścidartha iti śākyaputrīyāḥ pratipannāḥ / kasmāt ? sarvapramāṇānupalabdheḥ / iha yadasti tatpratyakṣādinā pramāṇenopalabhyate, tadyathā rūpādi / tataśca tāvadayamātmā na pratyakṣata upalabhyate / kasmāt ? aśabdādilakṣaṇāt / nāntaḥpratyakṣataḥ / kasmāt ? triguṇādiviparītasya tadaviṣayatvāt / na pūrvavaccheṣavadbhyām / kāryakāraṇānupapatteḥ / na ca sāmānyatodṛṣṭāt / dharmasāmānyābhāvāt / nāptavacanāt / anabhyupagamāt / na hi bauddhānāṃ śrutismṛtipurāṇetihāsāḥ pramāṇam / yaścaiṣāmāgamaḥ, sa evamāha

children.translated_text: 'The self (<s>ātman</s>) indeed does not exist for the self; it is imagined through perversion.
There is no being (<s>sattva</s>) here, no self — these are merely <s>dharmas</s> (factors), together with their causes.

[The objector] says: <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) is now understood. Now this must be established: that <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self) — distinct from the effect-cause [complex] — exists. If [one asks:] whence the doubt? It has been stated: because of both modes of apprehension of what is not [directly] perceived. What else? Because of the disagreement among teachers. The followers of the <s>Śākya</s>'s son (i.e., Buddhists) maintain that nothing exists apart from the aggregate of consciousness (<s>vijñāna-skandha</s>). Why? Because it is not apprehended by any means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Here, whatever exists is apprehended by a means of valid knowledge such as <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) and the like — for example, form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like. Therefore, first of all, this Self is not apprehended through <s>pratyakṣa</s>. Why? Because it is not characterized by sound and the like. Nor through internal perception. Why? Because, being the opposite of the three <s>guṇas</s> and the like, it is not an object of that [internal perception]. Nor by inference, as in the previous cases, through remainder (<s>śeṣavat</s>). Because the cause-effect [inference] is untenable. Nor through inference by general similarity (<s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>). Because of the absence of a common property (<s>dharma-sāmānya</s>). Nor through the word of authority (<s>āpta-vacana</s>). Because it is not accepted [by them]. For the Buddhists do not accept the <s>Śrutis</s>, <s>Smṛtis</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and <s>Itihāsas</s> as authoritative. And their own scripture (<s>āgama</s>) says thus:
Your twelve constituents are only the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and <s>dhātus</s> (elements).
Having examined all these, no <s>pudgala</s> (person) is found.'
'Know the internal to be empty (<s>śūnya</s>); see the external as empty.

children.text: na dṛśyate so 'pi kaścidyo bhāvayati śūnyatām //
children.translated_text: He too is not seen — the one who cultivates emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>).'

children.text:
punarapyāha "asti karmāsti vipākaḥ, kārakastu nopalabhyate ya imānsvāndharmānākṣipati / anyāṃśca prati sandadhāti, anyatra dharmasaṃketāt / tasmātsarvapramāṇānupalabdhernāstyātmeti /
  ucyate- yattāvaduktaṃ pratyakṣataḥ pūrvavaccheṣavadbhyāṃ cātmano nopalabdhiriti, satyametat / yattūktaṃ sāmānyatodṛṣṭādanupalabdhirātmasāmānyānupapatteriti, tadayuktam /
  kasmāt ?
children.translated_text:
And again [their scripture] says: 'There is action (<s>karma</s>), there is fruition (<s>vipāka</s>); but no agent (<s>kāraka</s>) is found who throws off these his own <s>dharmas</s> and takes up others — apart from the conventional designation of <s>dharmas</s>.' Therefore, since it is not apprehended by any means of valid knowledge, the Self does not exist.
It is replied: As for what was first said — that the Self is not apprehended through direct perception, nor through [inference by] precedent and remainder — that is true. But what was said — that it is not apprehended through the inference by general similarity because the Self lacks a common property — that is unjustified.
Why?
Because aggregates serve another's purpose (<s>saṃghāta-parārthatva</s>)

children.text:
iha saṃghātāḥ parārthā dṛṣṭāḥ / tadyathā śayanāsanarathacaraṇādayaḥ / asti cāyaṃ śarīralakṣaṇaḥ saṃghātaḥ / tasmādanenāpi parārthena bhavitavyam / yo 'sau paraḥ sa puruṣaḥ / tasmādasti puruṣaḥ /
  āha, saṃghātaparārthatvopalabdheḥ / śayanādayo hi satyapi parārthatve saṃghātārthāḥ / yadi ca tairatideśaḥ kāryakāraṇasaṃghātasya kriyate prāptamasya tadvatsaṃghātārthatvam / evaṃ puruṣaviparītārthasiddhiprasaṃgaḥ / athaitadaniṣṭaṃ, na tarhi cakṣurādayaḥ parārthāḥ /
  ucyate- na śakyametadāpādayitum / kasmāt ? asaṃhatatvasiddhau vādapravṛtteḥ / siddhe satyasaṃhatatve puruṣasyāyaṃ vādaḥ pravṛttaḥ / tasmānna pārārthyamanena bādhyate / kathamavagamyata iti cet, pratyakṣato 'nupalabdheḥ / sati hi saṃghātatve devadattādivadayaṃ puruṣaḥ pratyakṣata evopalabhyeta / tathā ca sati saṃśayābhāvātpravṛttirevāsya vādasya na syāt / tasmādayuktaṃ saṃhatārthāḥ śayanādivaccakṣurādayaḥ /
  āha, parasparopakāritvātpārārthyasiddhiḥ / iha kṣetrodakasūryādayaḥ śasyādīnāmupakārakāḥ / tathā kāryakāraṇatvātsaṃghātaśca / yathoktaṃ tasmādayuktameteṣāṃ pāratantryamiti /
  ucyate- na śayanādivattato 'nyenārthavattvāt / tadyathā śayanādyaṅgānāṃ sati parasparopakāritve tato 'nyenārthavattvāttadabhāve cārthānarthakyam / evaṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ sati parasparopakāritve tato 'nyenārthavattvaṃ bhavitumarhati / tadabhāve cārthānarthakyamiti /
  āha, śayanādīnāṃ devadattārthatvāttasya ca bhedā bahirbhāvātparasparārthatvaprasaṃgaḥ / evaṃ śayanādayo devadattārthāḥ, kāryakāraṇasaṃghātaśca devadattaśabdavācyastatra bhedānāmeva bhedārthatvātpuruṣārthasiddhiḥ / dṛṣṭāntābhāvo vā / atha mataṃ śayanādayo na devadattārthāḥ, kiṃ tarhi kṣetrajñārthāḥ / tathā sati sādhyasamo dṛṣṭānta iti /
  ucyate- na, prasiddhyanurodhāt / satyaṃ kāryakāraṇasaṃghātasya pārārthyam / bhoktṛtvaṃ nopapadyate / loke tu devadattārthatvaṃ śayanādīnāṃ prasiddham / atastadanugacchanto vayamapyevaṃ brūmaḥ / kasmāt ? prasiddheḥ / prasiddhena hyaprasiddhaṃ taddharmatāmāpadyate bhavadbhirapyuktaṃ "yasya hi pratikṣaṇamanyathātvaṃ nāsti tasya bāhyapratyayayoḥ bhedaḥ, paścādviśeṣagrahaṇe nāsti / tadyathā bhūmerapacyamānāyāḥ pākajānām /" na ca bhūmeḥ pratikṣaṇamanyathātvaṃ nāsti, akṣaṇikatvaprasaṃgāt / saukṣmyādduradhigamo bheda iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ prayuktaḥ / tasmātsiddhaṃ saṃghātaparārthatvādasti puruṣaḥ /
  itaśca-
children.translated_text:
Here, aggregates are observed to serve another's purpose — for example, beds, seats, chariots, legs [of furniture], and the like. And this body-aggregate exists. Therefore this too must serve another's purpose. That 'other' is the <s>Puruṣa</s>. Therefore <s>Puruṣa</s> exists.
[The objector] says: [This follows] from the observation that aggregates serve another's purpose. For beds and the like, even while serving another's purpose, are [themselves] purposes of [their own] aggregates [of parts]. And if an analogy is drawn with the effect-cause aggregate, it follows that it too serves the purpose of [another] aggregate. Thus there would be the undesired consequence of establishing the opposite of [what you intend about] <s>Puruṣa</s>. If this is undesirable, then the eyes and the like are not for another's purpose.
It is replied: This [objection] cannot be sustained. Why? Because this argument proceeds [only] upon the establishment of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s non-composite nature (<s>asaṃhatatva</s>). [This] argument has been advanced given the already established non-composite nature of <s>Puruṣa</s>. Therefore his [serving] another's purpose is not contradicted by this [objection]. How is [the non-composite nature] known? Because [Puruṣa] is not apprehended through direct perception. For if [Puruṣa] were a composite (<s>saṃghāta</s>), he would be directly perceived, like <s>Devadatta</s> and the like. And that being so, since there would be no doubt, there would be no occasion for this argument to proceed at all. Therefore it is unjustified [to say] that the eyes and the like, like beds, serve an aggregate's purpose.
[The objector] says: Because of mutual assistance (<s>parasparopakāritva</s>), 'serving another's purpose' is established. Here, fields, water, sun, and the like assist grain and the like. Likewise, the aggregate too [mutually assists] through the cause-effect [relationship]. As has been said, therefore it is unjustified that these [organs] are dependent [on something else].
It is replied: No — because they have purposefulness through something other [than themselves], unlike beds [which are complete unto themselves]. For example: the limbs of beds and the like, while having mutual assistance, have their purposefulness through something other [i.e., the person who uses them]; and in its absence, [they become] purposeless. Similarly, the eyes and the like, while having mutual assistance, ought to have their purposefulness through something other; and in its absence, [they would be] purposeless.
[The objector] says: Since beds and the like serve <s>Devadatta</s>'s purpose, and since he is differentiated [from them as] external, there is the [unwanted] consequence of mutual purpose-serving [without a further recipient]. Similarly, beds etc. serve <s>Devadatta</s>'s purpose, and the effect-cause aggregate — which is denoted by the word '<s>Devadatta</s>' — [is such that] since the parts serve the purpose of [other] parts alone, <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose is [already] established. Or there is no example. If you think that beds etc. do not serve <s>Devadatta</s>'s purpose but rather serve the <s>kṣetrajña</s>'s (field-knower's) purpose — in that case the example is equal to what is to be proved.
It is replied: No — because of conformity with what is well-known. True, the effect-cause aggregate does serve another's purpose. [But] the status of experiencer (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) is not established [for the aggregate itself]. However, in the world, [the fact] that beds and the like serve <s>Devadatta</s>'s purpose is well-known. Therefore, following that, we too say the same. Why? Because of [this] being well-known. For the unknown, through the well-known, attains the status of having that property. Even you [Buddhists] have said: 'For that which does not have moment-by-moment change of state, there is no distinction between an external and a subsequent specific apprehension — just as for earth, when not being fired, there is no [distinction regarding] its fire-born [modifications].' Yet earth does not have moment-by-moment change of state — [otherwise] there would be the consequence of non-momentariness. [You say:] 'The distinction is difficult to discern due to subtlety' — [and] the example is employed [precisely because of this]. Therefore it is established: because aggregates serve another's purpose, <s>Puruṣa</s> exists.
And for this further reason —
Because of [the inference from] the opposite of the three <s>guṇas</s> and the rest (<s>triguṇādi-viparyaya</s>)

children.text:
triguṇamaviveki viṣayaḥ sāmānyamacetanaṃ prasavadharmi ca bāhyādhyātmikaṃ tathā pradhānam / tatra yadyetāvadetatsyāt kimapekṣya vyaktāvyaktayostraiguṇyāditi ?
  kiṃ cānyat /
children.translated_text:
[The manifest is] possessed of the three <s>guṇa</s>s, non-discriminating, an object [of experience], common, non-conscious, and productive — both external and internal — such is <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). If this were all there is, then with reference to what would the three <s>guṇa</s>s of the manifest and the unmanifest [be established]?
  Moreover:
Because of governance (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>).

children.text:
ihākasmikyāṃ pradhānapravṛttāvarthavaśaḥ sanniveśaniyamo na syāt / śrotrādi pṛthivyādīnāṃ devamānuṣatiryakṣu hitayogārthaścāpratiṣedhārthaśca saḥ / tasmādasti tadvyatirikto yadadhiṣṭhitānāṃ guṇānāmayaṃ citrarūpo vipariṇāmaḥ /
  kartṛtvaprasaṃgādadhiṣṭhānānupapattiriti cet, syānmataṃ yadi guṇānāṃ puruṣādhiṣṭhitānāṃ pravṛttirabhyupagamyate, kartṛtvamasya prāptam / athākartā na tarhyastyadhiṣṭhātṛtvamiti / etaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? arthe tadupacārāt / yathāpuruṣārthaḥ siddhyati tathā guṇā kāryakāraṇabhāvena vyūhyanta ityatastatpāratantryādeṣāmadhiṣṭhitatvamupapadyate, puruṣasya cādhiṣṭhitṛtvam / ato nāsya kartṛtvaprasaṃgaḥ / tasmādyuktametat adhiṣṭhānātpuruṣaḥ /
  kiñcānyat /
children.translated_text:
Here, if the activity of <s>pradhāna</s> were random, there would be no orderly arrangement determined by purpose. The [arrangement of] the ear and other [senses], of earth and other [elements], in gods, humans, and animals serves both the purpose of beneficial connection and the purpose of non-obstruction. Therefore, there exists [a being] distinct from these, by whose governance the <s>guṇa</s>s undergo this variegated transformation.
  If [you say] that the consequence of agency makes governance untenable — [the argument would be:] if the activity of the <s>guṇa</s>s under the governance of <s>Puruṣa</s> is accepted, then agency accrues to him. And if he is a non-agent, then there is no governance. And this is improper. Why? Because that [term] is figuratively applied in reference to the purpose. The <s>guṇa</s>s arrange themselves in their cause-effect relation in such a way that the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is accomplished — and therefore, from their being subordinate to that [purpose], their being governed is tenable, and <s>Puruṣa</s>'s being the governor [is tenable]. Hence, the consequence of agency does not apply to him. Therefore this is proper: <s>Puruṣa</s> [is established] from governance.
  Moreover:
<s>Puruṣa</s> exists because of [the necessity of] an enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛbhāva</s>).

children.text:
iha sukhaduḥkhamohātmakatvādacetanaṃ vyaktamavyaktaṃ ca, tasmādasya paraspareṇa bhogo nopapadyate, ityavaśyaṃ bhoktrā bhavitavyam / yo 'sau bhoktā sa puruṣaḥ /
  āha, kaḥ punarayaṃ bhogo nāma ?
  ucyate- bhoga upalabdhisadbhāvāt /
  vijñānameva hi viṣayopalabdhisamarthamityatastāvanmātramevāstu kiṃ puruṣeṇa parikalpiteneti ?
  ucyate- kiṃ punaridaṃ vijñānaṃ nāmeti ?
  āha, cittaṃ mano vijñānamiti / tacca ṣaḍvidhaṃ jñānaṃ- cakṣurvijñānaṃ, śrotravijñānaṃ, ghrāṇavijñānaṃ, jihvāvijñānaṃ, kāyavijñānaṃ, manovijñānamiti / tatra rūpaṃ pratītya cakṣuścotpadyate cakṣurvijñānam / evaṃ śrotraśabdaghrāṇagandhajihvārasamanodharmāścittamutpādayanti / tasya dharmāḥ - vedanā, saṃjñā, sparśo, manaḥ, saṃskāra evamādayaḥ tasmādvijñānaskandhasyaivopabhogasāmarthānnāstyātmeti /
  ucyate- na, acetanavikārasya cetanānupatteḥ / tattu khalvidamiṣyate rūpaṃ pratītya cakṣuścotpadyate cakṣurvijñānamityādi, tenācetanavikāratvāttadacetanaṃ ghaṭādivadityāpannam / tasmānmanodharmaścetaneti manorathamātrametat / vilakṣaṇakāryotpattidarśanāttatsiddhiriti cet, syānmataṃ nāyaṃ niyamaḥ yaduta yajjātīyaṃ kāraṇaṃ tajjātīyakena kāryeṇa bhavitavyam / kiṃ tarhi vilakṣaṇakāryotpattiriti bhāvānāmupalabhyate / tadyathā- śṛṅgāccharo jāyate, golomāvilomabhyo dūrvā / vatsatarānmuka_yaścandrakāntendusaṃyogātsalilam / sūryakāntagomayārkasamparkāt sudhodakasamparkādaraṇīnirmathanāccāgniḥ / evamacetanebhyo rūpādibhyaścetanamutpadyata iti / etaccāyuktam, cetanācetanotpattiniyamavattanniyamāt / yathā satyetasminvilakṣaṇakāryaprādurbhāve bhavataścetanāccittānnācetanaṃ ghaṭādyutpadyata iti niyamaḥ, tathā satyetasminvilakṣaṇakāryaprādurbhāve nācetanebhyo rūpādibhyaścetanaṃ cittamutpadyata ityayaṃ niyamo naḥ / tasmādeṣāṃ dṛṣṭānāṃ sati bahutve māyākāranagaravinyāsavadayathārthajñānaviṣayatvādasādhīyastvam / pradīpavattadvyavastheti cet, syādetat yathācetanebhyaḥ sattvādibhyo 'vyavasāyakaṃ ghaṭādyutpadyata iti nedānīṃ vyavasāyako mahānnotpadyate / evaṃ rūpādibhyo 'cetanaṃ ghaṭādyutpadyata iti nedānīṃ cetanaṃ cittaṃ notpadyata iti / etadapyanupapannam / kasmāt ? śaktibhedāt / prakāśasvābhāvyādvyavasāyātmakaṃ sattvam / tadyuktaṃ yadi tatprānyādvyavasāyātmako mahānutpadyate / tamaḥ prādhānyādvyavasāyakā ghaṭādayaḥ / bhavatastvekākārāḥ rūpādayaḥ tasmādāyamasamaḥ samādhiriti /
  āha, kiṃ vyavasāyacaitanyayoḥ kaścidrūpabhedo 'sti na veti ?
  ucyate- kiṃ tarhi traiguṇyātsati pratyayarūpatve saṃvedyā buddhiryathā tu vyavasāyarūpaṃ tathā caitanyarūpamiti / tathā ca vārṣagaṇāḥ paṭhanti- buddhivṛttyāviṣṭo hi pratyayatvenānuvartamānāmanuyāti puruṣa iti / āha ca

children.translated_text: Just as <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) [reflects objects], so <s>Puruṣa</s> (the self) appears as if having the form of the object.
Appearing thus through <s>buddhi</s>, the knower is said to be like a crystal (<s>maṇi</s>).

Here, because the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) and the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) are non-conscious — being of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion — therefore experience (<s>bhoga</s>) between them is untenable. Hence, there must necessarily be an enjoyer. That which is the enjoyer — that is <s>Puruṣa</s>.
  [The objector] asks: What, then, is this experience (<s>bhoga</s>)?
  It is replied: Experience is the existence of apprehension (<s>upalabdhi</s>).
  [The Buddhist asks:] Since cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) alone is capable of the apprehension of objects, let there be just that much. What need is there for a postulated <s>Puruṣa</s>?
  It is replied: What, then, is this 'cognition' (<s>vijñāna</s>)?
  [The Buddhist] says: <s>Citta</s> (mind), <s>manas</s> (thought), <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) [are synonymous]. And this cognition is sixfold: visual cognition, auditory cognition, olfactory cognition, gustatory cognition, tactile cognition, and mental cognition. Of these, dependent on form and the eye, there arises visual cognition. Likewise, the ear and sound, the nose and smell, the tongue and taste, the mind and <s>dharma</s>s produce <s>citta</s>. Its <s>dharma</s>s are: feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), contact (<s>sparśa</s>), thought (<s>manas</s>), dispositions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and so forth. Therefore, since the consciousness-aggregate (<s>vijñānaskandha</s>) alone has the capacity for experience, there is no self (<s>ātman</s>).
  It is replied: No, because consciousness does not arise from non-conscious transformations. What is accepted [by you] — namely, that dependent on form and the eye there arises visual cognition, etc. — from that, because it is a transformation of the non-conscious, it follows that it too is non-conscious, like a pot and the like. Therefore, [to say] that a property of mind (<s>manas</s>) is conscious is nothing but wishful thinking. If [you say] it is established from the observation that products of a different character arise [from their causes] — [the argument would be:] this is not an absolute rule, that the effect must be of the same class as the cause. Rather, the production of effects of a different character is observed among things. For example, from a horn arises a reed; from cow-hair, goat-hair, and others arise <s>dūrvā</s> grass; from a young bull arise the <s>muka</s>_ [insects]; from the conjunction of the moonstone and the moon arises water; from the conjunction of the sunstone, cow-dung, and the sun, or from the contact of water and lime, or from the churning of fire-sticks arises fire. Likewise, from non-conscious things — form and the like — consciousness arises.
  And this too is improper, because just as there is a rule regarding the production of conscious from conscious and non-conscious from non-conscious, so [there is an opposite] rule. Just as, given this manifestation of products of a different character, you have the rule that from the conscious <s>citta</s>, a non-conscious pot and the like does not arise — so too, given this manifestation of products of a different character, we have the rule that from non-conscious form and the like, conscious <s>citta</s> does not arise. Therefore, these examples, though many, like the arrangement of a magician's illusory city, are of inferior [probative value], because they are objects of erroneous cognition. If [you say] 'It is determined like a lamp' — [the argument would be:] just as from the non-conscious <s>sattva</s> and the like, a non-determining pot and the like is produced, but a determining <s>mahat</s> is not produced now [i.e., from tamas-predominant causes]. Likewise, from non-conscious form and the like, non-conscious pot and the like is produced, but conscious <s>citta</s> is not produced now. And this too is untenable. Why? Because of the difference in powers. <s>Sattva</s>, by its nature of illumination, is of the nature of determination. It is proper, then, that from its predominance, the determinative <s>mahat</s> arises. From the predominance of <s>tamas</s>, non-determinative pots and the like [arise]. But for you, form and the like are of a single character. Therefore, this resolution is unequal.
  [The Buddhist] asks: Is there any difference of form between determination (<s>vyavasāya</s>) and consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>), or is there not?
  It is replied: [There is no essential difference;] rather, because of the three <s>guṇa</s>s, when <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) has the nature of a cognition, it is experienced — just as it has the form of determination, so too it has the form of consciousness. And thus the <s>Vārṣagaṇa</s>s teach: '<s>Puruṣa</s>, pervaded by the activity of <s>buddhi</s>, follows along as if it were a cognition.' And he says:

children.text: yathā yathā manovṛttiḥ puruṣo 'sti tathā tathā /
children.translated_text: In whatever manner the activity of the mind (<s>manas</s>) [operates], in that manner <s>Puruṣa</s> exists.
Being conscious, [yet] dependent on another, [<s>Puruṣa</s>] assumes the form of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect).

children.text:
āha, rūpābhedātpuruṣāntaḥkaraṇayoranyataraparikalpanānarthakyam / yadi tarhi yathā vyavasāyarūpaṃ tathā caitanyarūpam, evaṃ sati vyavasāyamātraṃ parikalpanīyaṃ caitanyamātraṃ vā ? kasmāt ? na hyekāntakāriṇoryugapat kalpane sāmarthyamasti / rūpāntarābhidhānaṃ vā / atha vyavasāyacaitanyayoḥ padārthānāmantarameveti nityato viśeṣyate, tarhi vaktavyamidamamuṣyaiva rūpaṃ nāmuṣyeti /
  ucyate- ya evamāha rūpābhedādarthābheda iti sa tāvadidaṃ praṣṭavyaḥ- atha kim ? bhavataḥ kiṃ vijñānaviṣayayorākārahedo 'sti uta nāstīti ?
  netyāha / kasmāt ? ākārāntare sati viṣayaparicchedānupapatteḥ / na hi viṣayasya vijñānapratyavabhāsamantareṇa śakyaṃ svarūpaṃ paricchettum / tatra yadanyākāro gauranyākāraṃ govijñānaṃ syāttena yathānyākāreṇāśvavijñānenānyākārasya goraparicchedaḥ, evamanyākāreṇa govijñānenānyākārasya goparicchedaḥ syāt / tasmānnāsti viṣayavijñānayorākārabheda iti /
  ucyate- tayoridānīṃ viṣayaviṣayavijñānayoḥ kimubhayatvamutābheda iti ?
  āha, kasmāt ? jñāpyajñāpakabhāvāditi /

children.translated_text: It is replied:
Just as there is a difference between knowledge and the knowable, even when there is no difference of form,
through the relation of apprehended and apprehender — so too between the self (<s>ātman</s>) and its manifestation.

[The objector] says: Because of the non-difference of form, the postulation of either <s>Puruṣa</s> or the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is purposeless. If the form of consciousness is the same as the form of determination, then either determination alone should be postulated, or consciousness alone. Why? Because when two [principles] invariably [produce the same result], there is no capacity for simultaneously postulating both. Or else a different form must be stated. If the difference between determination and consciousness as two categories is always maintained, then it should be stated: 'this form belongs to this one alone, not to the other.'
  It is replied: To the one who says this — that non-difference of form implies non-difference of things — he should first be asked: Well then, is there a difference of form between cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) and its object (<s>viṣaya</s>) for you, or is there not?
  [The Buddhist] says: There is not. Why? Because if there were a difference of form, the delimitation of the object would be untenable. For the essential nature of the object cannot be delimited without the appearance [reflected] in cognition. If the cow were of one form and the cognition of the cow of another form, then just as a horse-cognition of a different form does not delimit a cow of a different form, so too a cow-cognition of a different form would not delimit a cow of a different form. Therefore, there is no difference of form between the object and the cognition.
  It is replied: Now then, between the object and the cognition of the object, is there duality, or non-difference?
  [The Buddhist] says: Why [do you ask]? Because of the relation of the known and the knower.

children.text:
yathaiva tarhi bhavataḥ satyapyākārabhede jñānavijñeyayorgrāhyagrāhakabhāvaparikalpanādbheda evaṃ puruṣāntaḥkaraṇayorapīti / grāhyagrāhakabhāvāsiddherayuktamiti cet syādetat, yathā gotadvijñānayorgrāhyagrāhakabhāvo niścito naivaṃ puruṣāntaḥkaraṇayoḥ / tasmādvaiṣamyamiti / etadanupapannam / kasmāt ? mārgāntaragamanāt / prāguktaṃ yeṣāmākārabhedo nāsti teṣāmekatvam / idānīṃ tu rūpābhede 'pi grāhyagrāhakabhāvādevaṃ bruvato mārgāntaram / jñānamātrābhyupagamādaśākyīyamiti cet syānmatam, jñānamevāntarāsadviṣayabhūtānurañjitaṃ viṣayaviṣayirūpeṇa pratyavabhāsate / na tu kiṃcidbāhyaṃ kiṃcid grāhyarūpāpannamasti / tasmājjñānavijñeyayorgrāhyagrāhakabhedādbheda ityaśākyīyametat iti / tadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? siddhāntabhedāt / yeṣāṃ bāhyo viṣayo 'sti tatpakṣe 'yaṃ doṣaḥ / itareṣāṃ tu jñānamātrasya viṣayaviṣayibhāvaṃ pratiṣetsyāma iti /
  āha, evamapi viṣayānavasthāprasaṃgaḥ / viṣayiṇo viṣayatvapratijñānāt / yadi viṣayiṇo 'pyadhyavasāyasya viṣayabhāvaḥ pratijñāyate, tena puruṣasyāpi viṣayiṇo 'nyo viṣayīti prāptam, tasyāpyanya ityanavasthāḥ / atha mā bhūdayaṃ doṣa iti puruṣo niścayarūpatvānna viṣayo na tarhyadhyavasāyādapi niśceturarthāntaraṃ kalpayitavyamiti /
  ucyate- cetanātvātpuruṣe tadanupapattiḥ / indriyāṇi tāvadgrahaṇamātrarūpatvādapratyayānīti pratyayavadantastāvatkaraṇaṃ parikalpyate / anaḥkaraṇamapyupāttaviṣayendriyavṛttyupanipātāttadrūpāpattāvapi satyāmacetanatvātsvayamupalabdhumasamarthameva viṣayamityato bhoktāraṃ cetanaṃ puruṣamapekṣate / puruṣasya tu cetanatvād draṣṭrantaramaśakyaṃ kalpayitum / tasmānnānavasthāprasaṃgaḥ /
  āha, puruṣasyādhyavasāyakartṛtvaprasaṃgaḥ, caitanyāt / yadyacetanā buddhistena tasyā adhyavasāyo vṛttirghaṭādivanna prāpnoti / ataḥ puruṣasyādhyavasāyaḥ prāptaḥ / tataśca buddhyabhāva iti /
  ucyate- na, kaivalyādapratibandhaprasaṃgāt / anāmiśrarūpaṃ puruṣatattvamiti etadupariṣṭādvakṣyāmaḥ / sa yadi vyavasāyātmakaḥ syāt, apratibandhena diṅniścayādiṣu suptamattamūrcchitānāṃ ca vyavasāyaḥ syāt / dṛṣṭastvevamavasthasya vyavasāyapratibandhaḥ / tasmānna puruṣasya vyavasāyaha / yasya punarantaḥkaraṇaṃ vyavasāyakaṃ tasyaivaṃ doṣo nāsti / kasmāt ? traiguṇyāt / sattvādisaṃsthānaviśeṣo hi buddhiḥ, karaṇāntarapratiṣedhāt / tatra yadādhyavasāyalakṣaṇaṃ sattvaṃ guṇābhāvātpradhānabhūtena tamasā tiraskṛtaśakti bhavati tadādhyavasāyapratibandhaḥ /
  āha, kathaṃ punaretad gamyate sarvamidamacetanamiti ?
  ucyate- prakṛtivikārabhūtatvāt / iha yatprakṛtivikārabhūtaṃ tadacetanam / tadyathā tantupaṭādayaḥ prakṛtivikārabhūtaṃ tasmādacetanam / ākāśe darśanānnaikānta iti cenna, asiddhatvāt / na hyākāśasyātmapakṣe prakṛtivikāratvābhāvaḥ siddhaḥ / tasmādyuktametatprakṛtivikārabhūtatvādacetanaṃ sarvam / ata eva ca cetanasyāprakṛtivikārabhūtatvaṃ parasparavaidharmyāt / tasmānnānyasya paramārthasya bhoktṛtvamācetanyādupapadyate, na cet sūktaṃ bhoktṛbhāvādasti puruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Just as, for you, there is a difference between knowledge and the knowable through the postulation of the apprehended-apprehender relation even when there is no difference of form — so too between <s>Puruṣa</s> and the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>).
  If [you say] this is improper because the apprehended-apprehender relation is not established — [the argument would be:] just as the apprehended-apprehender relation of a cow and the cognition of a cow is certain, the same is not so for <s>Puruṣa</s> and the inner organ. Therefore there is an asymmetry.
  And this is untenable. Why? Because of resorting to a different path. Previously it was said that where there is no difference of form, there is identity. But now, even when there is no difference of form, you speak of difference through the apprehended-apprehender relation — this is a different path.
  If [you say] this cannot be avoided because only cognition is accepted [i.e., the Yogācāra position] — [the argument would be:] cognition itself, internally colored by a non-existent object, appears in the form of object and subject. But there is nothing external, nothing that has the nature of an apprehended object. Therefore, the difference of knowledge and knowable through the apprehended-apprehender distinction — this is [only] the Śākya [Buddhist] position.
  And that too is improper. Why? Because of the difference of philosophical standpoints. In the position of those for whom there is an external object, this defect [arises]. But for the others [i.e., Yogācāras], we shall refute the subject-object relation of mere cognition.
  [The objector] says: Even so, there follows the consequence of an infinite regress regarding the object. Because the subject is declared to be an object [of a higher subject]. If it is asserted that the subject — namely, determination — also has the nature of an object, then it follows that there is another subject beyond <s>Puruṣa</s> who is [also] a subject, and another beyond that — and so on without end. Or if, to avoid this defect, <s>Puruṣa</s> is not an object because he is of the nature of certainty, then neither should one postulate anything different from determination as [the source of] certainty.
  It is replied: Because of consciousness (<s>cetanatva</s>), this is untenable in the case of <s>Puruṣa</s>. First, the senses, being merely of the nature of grasping, do not produce cognitions — hence the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is postulated as that which produces cognitions. But even the inner organ, although it assumes the form [of objects] through the impact of the sensory activities that have taken up objects, is non-conscious and therefore incapable of apprehending the object by itself — hence it requires a conscious enjoyer, <s>Puruṣa</s>. But because <s>Puruṣa</s> is conscious, it is impossible to postulate another seer. Therefore, there is no consequence of an infinite regress.
  [The objector] says: There follows the consequence that <s>Puruṣa</s> is the agent of determination, because of consciousness. If <s>buddhi</s> is non-conscious, then its determination — its activity — does not obtain, like a pot and the like. Therefore, determination pertains to <s>Puruṣa</s>. And consequently, <s>buddhi</s> would not exist.
  It is replied: No, because [<s>Puruṣa</s>'s] isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) would imply the consequence of unimpeded [determination]. We shall explain below that the <s>Puruṣa</s>-principle is of an unmixed nature. If he were of the nature of determination, then there would be unimpeded determination regarding the ascertainment of directions, etc., and there would be determination even for those who are asleep, intoxicated, or unconscious. But an impediment to determination is observed in such states. Therefore, determination does not belong to <s>Puruṣa</s>. For the one whose inner organ is determinative, there is no such defect. Why? Because of the three <s>guṇa</s>s. For <s>buddhi</s> is a particular configuration of <s>sattva</s> and the other [<s>guṇa</s>s], from the exclusion of other instruments. When the <s>sattva</s> that is characterized by determination has its power obscured by <s>tamas</s> — which has become predominant due to the absence of [the other] <s>guṇa</s>s — then there is an impediment to determination.
  [The objector] asks: How is it known that all this [manifest world] is non-conscious?
  It is replied: Because it is a transformation of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). Here, whatever is a transformation of <s>Prakṛti</s>, that is non-conscious — just as thread, cloth, and the like, being transformations of <s>Prakṛti</s>, are non-conscious. If [you say] this is not conclusive because of the observation of space (<s>ākāśa</s>) — no, because that is not established. For the non-status of space as a transformation of <s>Prakṛti</s> is not established from the standpoint of the self (<s>ātman</s>). Therefore, it is proper: everything is non-conscious because of being a transformation of <s>Prakṛti</s>. And precisely for this reason, the conscious [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is not a transformation of <s>Prakṛti</s>, because of the mutual difference [between conscious and non-conscious]. Therefore, the nature of an enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) is not tenable for anything else in the ultimate sense, due to non-consciousness. Thus it is well said: <s>Puruṣa</s> exists because of [the necessity of] an enjoyer.
And because of activity for the sake of <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 17 //

children.text:
iha pravṛttimatāṃ nimittamantareṇa nivṛttirnopapadyate / pradhānamapi ca pravṛttimad, vyaktadarśanāt / tasmādyasya kaivalyaṃ pradhānapravṛttihetuḥ sa puruṣaḥ / pradhānānabhyupagamādubhayāprasiddhiriti cet syādetat, pradhānaṃ cetanavadasmākamaprasiddham / yāvattasya kaivalyārthaṃ pravṛttirbhavatā puruṣāstitve liṅgamapadiśyate tadidamasiddhaṃ pradipādyata iti / etaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? pūrvaṃ tatpratipādanāt / prākpradhānamapratipādyaivamācakṣāṇaḥ satyamevaṃ paryanuyogārhaḥ syāt, sādhitaṃ tu pradhānaṃ parimāṇādibhirityato na kiṃcidetat /
  sarvācāryavipratipatteḥ puruṣārthasiddhiriti cet syānmatam, yadi puruṣasya sattvameva syāttena taṃ pratyācāryāṇāṃ na dharmavivādaḥ syāt / asti cāsau / tathā hi keṣāṃcinnirguṇaḥ, keṣāṃcitparavān / ataḥ sarveṣāṃ vibhuḥ, parimito 'nyeṣāṃ, tathaiko naika iti / tasmādbhrāntimātraṃ puruṣakalpaneti / etadanupapannam / kasmāt ? sarvapadārthābhāvaprasaṃgāt / rūpādiṣvapi vipratipatteḥ / keṣāṃcitkṣaṇikāḥ, keṣāṃcitkālāntarāvasthāyinaḥ, tathāśritāḥ, svatantrā ityādi / tathā śrotādīni bhautikāni, āhaṃkārikāṇi, pauruṣāṇīti vipratipattiḥ / evaṃ sarvapadārthābhāvaḥ syāt / tasmādasti puruṣaḥ / tatra yuktaṃ sarvapramāṇānupalabdhernāsti puruṣa iti etadayuktam / yadapyuktam "śūnyakamādhyātmikaṃ paśyeti" tasya paścātpratiṣedhaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ / yatpunaretaduktaṃ "asti karmāsti vipākaḥ kārakastu nopalabhyata" iti satyametat / na hi puruṣaskandhānāṃ nikṣepe pratisaṃdhāne 'nyatra vā kāraka iti naḥ pakṣaḥ / tasmācchreyo 'rthibhiḥ sarvāgamatarkaviruddhāṃ nairātmyavādaparikalpanābhrāntimasamañjasāmapohya puruṣasattvaparijñānādeva jananamaraṇādisarvopadravapratipakṣabhūtaṃ paramamṛtaṃ dhruvaṃ sthānamavāptavyamiti // 17 //
children.translated_text: Here, for things that are in activity, cessation is not possible without a purpose. And <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter) too is in activity, as evidenced by the manifest [world]. Therefore, the <s>puruṣa</s> (person) is that for whose <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) <s>pradhāna</s>'s activity is the purpose. If one objects that since <s>pradhāna</s> is not accepted [by the opponent], there is non-establishment on both sides — one might say: <s>pradhāna</s>, like a conscious entity, is not established for us. Insofar as you point to its activity for the sake of <s>kaivalya</s> as a mark for proving <s>puruṣa</s>'s existence, that very thing is being presented as unestablished. But this is unjustified. Why? Because it was established earlier. If one were to say this before establishing <s>pradhāna</s>, one would indeed be open to this objection; but <s>pradhāna</s> has been proved through [the arguments of] finitude and the rest — therefore this amounts to nothing. If one objects that the aim of <s>puruṣa</s> is established from the disagreement of all teachers — one might say: if <s>puruṣa</s> truly existed, there would be no dispute among the teachers regarding its properties. But there is [such dispute]. For some hold it is without qualities, for some it is dependent on a higher [being]; for all it is all-pervading, for others it is limited; likewise some say it is one, others that it is many. Therefore the conception of <s>puruṣa</s> is mere delusion. But this is untenable. Why? Because the consequence would be the non-existence of all entities. For there is disagreement regarding forms and the like too. For some they are momentary, for others they persist over time; likewise some hold they are dependent, others that they are independent — and so forth. Similarly regarding hearing and the other [sense organs] — some say they are elemental, others that they derive from <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and others that they belong to <s>puruṣa</s>. Thus all entities would be non-existent [by this logic]. Therefore <s>puruṣa</s> exists. As for the position that <s>puruṣa</s> does not exist because it is not apprehended by any means of valid knowledge — this is unjustified. As for the statement 'one sees the inner domain as void,' we shall state its refutation later. As for the further statement 'there is action, there is [its] result, but no agent is found' — this is true [in a sense]. For our position is not that there is an agent in the depositing of the <s>skandha</s>s (aggregates) of <s>puruṣa</s>, in their reconnection, or elsewhere. Therefore, those who seek the highest good should [abandon] the fabrication of the <s>nairātmyavāda</s> (doctrine of no-self) which contradicts all scripture and reasoning,
<s>Kārikā</s> 18

children.text:
āha, gṛhṇīmahe tāvadastyayamātmeti / idānīmaneko 'thaika iti vicāryam / kutaḥ saṃśaya iti cet, sambandhināmubhayathā dṛṣṭatvāt / iha kasyacidanekasyānekena sambandha upalabhyate / tadyathā śrotrādinā śarīrasya / kasyacidekasyānekena / tadyathākāśasya ghaṭādinā / ayamapi cātmā kāryakāraṇasambandhītyataḥ saṃśayaḥ kiṃ śrotrādivadanekaḥ, ākāśavadeko veti ? kiṃ cānyat / ācāryavipratipatteḥ / aupaniṣadāḥ khalu eka ātmeti pratipannāḥ / kāṇādākṣapādārhataprabhṛtayaḥ punareka iti / yathā caikānekatvaṃ pratyātmano vipratipattirevaṃ sākṣitvaudāsīnyadraṣṭṛtvākartṛtveṣu / tasmādvaktavyaṃ kathamete dharmāḥ puruṣe 'vatiṣṭhanta iti ?
  ucyate- yattāvaduktaṃ sambandhitvādātmapadārthe sandehaḥ kimaneko 'thaika iti, atra brūmaḥ- bahavaḥ puruṣā iti pratijñā / kasmāt ?
children.translated_text: One says: we accept, then, that this self exists. Now it must be examined whether it is many or one. If one asks whence the doubt — it is because related things are observed in both ways. Here, a certain multiple [thing] is observed to be related to multiple [things] — for example, the body to hearing and the other [sense organs]. And a certain single [thing] is observed to be related to multiple [things] — for example, space to pots and the like. And this self too is related through the relation of effect and cause — hence the doubt: is it many like the sense organs of hearing and so forth, or one like space? Moreover, because of the disagreement among teachers. The <s>Aupaniṣada</s>s (Vedāntins) indeed hold that the self is one. But the <s>Kāṇāda</s>s (Vaiśeṣikas), <s>Ākṣapāda</s>s (Naiyāyikas), <s>Jaina</s>s, and others [hold that it is] many. And just as there is disagreement regarding the self's oneness or multiplicity, so too regarding its being a witness, its indifference, its being a seer, and its non-agency. Therefore it must be explained: how do these properties subsist in <s>puruṣa</s>? It is replied: as for what was said — there is doubt regarding the self as an entity because it is related [to things], whether it is many or one — to this we say: the thesis is that <s>puruṣa</s>s are many. Why?
Because of the specific allotment of birth, death, and the instruments [to each individual].

) vakṣyati / janma ca maraṇaṃ ca karaṇāni ca janmamaraṇakaraṇāni / teṣāṃ pratipuruṣaṃ niyamaḥ /etasmālliṅgādātmano bahutvamavasīyate / etaduktaṃ bhavati- janmalakṣaṇaṃ ca maraṇalakṣaṇaṃ ca kāryakāraṇasyāvasthāntaram / parasparavirodhinī tamaḥprakāśavat / tatra yadyeka ātmā syāt tena yathaikaṃ dravyaṃ tamaḥprakāśāvekapradeśopanipātinau na śaknotyanubhavitumasambhavāt, evamayaṃ janmamaraṇe api na śaknuyādupabhoktum / asti cāyaṃ kenacitkāryakaraṇena janmopabhogaḥ kenacinmaraṇopabhogaḥ / tena manyāmahe nānā ātmānaḥ, yeṣāṃ virodhidharmopabhogasāmarthyamiti / tathā karaṇānāṃ prakāśātiśayo viṣayagrahaṇalakṣaṇāśuddhyatiśayaścāṣṭāviṃśatidhāśaktiḥ, tayoḥ parasparavirodhādekenātmanā yugapadupabhogo nopapadyate / na hi śakyamekenātmanā prakāśātiśayo viṣayagrahaṇalakṣaṇo 'śuddhyatiśayaścāśaktilakṣaṇo virodhitvādyugapadupabhoktum / asti cāyaṃ karaṇanimittaḥ pratipuruṣaṃ niyamaḥ / tena manyāmahe nānā ātmāna iti /
  kiṃ cānyat /
children.translated_text: ). Birth and death and the instruments — these are <s>janmamaraṇakaraṇa</s>. Their allotment is specific to each <s>puruṣa</s>. From this inferential mark, the multiplicity of selves is ascertained. What is meant is this: the state characterized by birth and the state characterized by death are different conditions of the causal complex. They are mutually contradictory, like darkness and light. If there were a single self, then just as a single substance cannot simultaneously experience darkness and light falling on the same spot — since it is impossible — so too this [single self] would be unable to experience birth and death. But there is, for one [person], the experience of birth through a certain causal instrument, and for another, the experience of death. Therefore we hold that selves are many — those who have the capacity to experience contradictory properties. Similarly, the instruments have a twenty-eight-fold capacity consisting of the excess of illumination characterized by the apprehension of objects, and the excess of impurity characterized by incapacity. Since these two are mutually contradictory, their simultaneous experience by a single self is not tenable. For it is not possible for a single self to simultaneously experience the excess of illumination characterized by the apprehension of objects and the excess of impurity characterized by incapacity, because they are contradictory. And there is this specific allotment per individual occasioned by the instruments. Therefore we hold that selves are many.

<s>Janma</s> (birth) means the connection of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) — which resides in the subtle body beginning with <s>mahat</s> — with an external body, in accordance with its accumulated impressions. <s>Maraṇa</s> (death) means the abandonment of the previous body by the <s>liṅga</s> when the fruition of previously performed action is complete and the enjoyment of the present result has arrived. The instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>) are of thirteen kinds, as will be stated (
And because of the non-simultaneous activity [of <s>pradhāna</s>], the multiplicity of <s>puruṣa</s>s is established.

kasmāt ? ayugapatpravṛtteḥ pradhānasyetiśeṣaḥ, yasya pravṛttirupapadyate /
  kasya pravṛttirupapadyate ?
  pradhānasya /
  kathamiti ?
  ucyate- yadyeka ātmā syāttenaikapuruṣādhikāranibaddhaṃ pradhānam / śaktaścāsau yugapadanekāni śarīrāṇi upabhoktumityato yāvadbhiḥ śarīrairapacitāsu kālamātrāsvasminbhavaparivarte bhavitavyaṃ sarveṣāmutpattiṃ prati yugapatpravarteta / dṛṣṭā tu pradhānasyāyugapaccharīrabhāvena pravṛttiḥ / tasmādayugapatpravṛtteśca nānā ātmāna iti /
  anye punarāhuḥ- bahiṣkaraṇāmevāyugapatpravṛtteḥ / katham ? yadyeka ātmā syāttena tatsaṃskāropanibaddhānyeva sarvāṇi karaṇānītyataḥ pratipaṇḍitamavasthitaiḥ karaṇairyugapadviṣayāngṛhṇīyāt / bādhiryādyupaghāte vā sati piṇḍāntarasambandhinā karaṇenāsya śabdādikaraṇamapratiṣiddhaṃ syāt / na tu tathā bhavati / tasmātkaraṇānāmayugapatpravṛtternānā ātmāna iti / tadayuktam / kasmāt ? pūrveṇāviśeṣāt / karaṇānāṃ pratiniyamādityanenāyamupasaṃgṛhīto 'rthaḥ / tasmādyathoktamevāstu /
  kiṃ cānyat /
children.translated_text: Why? Because of the non-simultaneous activity — of <s>pradhāna</s>, this is the remainder [of the sentence] — whose activity is tenable. Whose activity is tenable? <s>Pradhāna</s>'s. How? It is replied: if the self were one, then <s>pradhāna</s> would be bound to the jurisdiction of a single <s>puruṣa</s>. And since that [single <s>puruṣa</s>] would be capable of enjoying multiple bodies simultaneously, <s>pradhāna</s> should proceed simultaneously toward the origination of all, in whatever time-portions of this cycle of existence bodies are to be produced. But the activity of <s>pradhāna</s> is observed to be non-simultaneous, proceeding through different bodies [at different times]. Therefore, because of the non-simultaneous activity [of <s>pradhāna</s>], selves are many. Others however say: because of the non-simultaneous activity of the external instruments. How? If the self were one, then since all instruments would be bound by its dispositions, the instruments, standing ready for each knower, would simultaneously apprehend objects. Or in the event of deafness or similar impairment, the apprehension of sounds and the like through an instrument belonging to another body would not be precluded for it. But this is not the case. Therefore, because of the non-simultaneous activity of the instruments, selves are many. But this is unjustified. Why? Because there is no distinction from the previous [argument]. This meaning is already encompassed by [the argument] 'because of the specific allotment of instruments.' Therefore let it remain as stated.
And indeed because of the contrariety [of the self's nature] to the three <s>guṇa</s>s and the rest. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 18)

children.text: iha triguṇamaviveki viṣayaḥ sāmānyamacetanaṃ prasavadharmītyete dharmāḥ pratipiṇḍamupalabhyante / yathā caite tathā tatpratiyogino nairguṇyādayaḥ puruṣadharmāḥ / tatra yathaiva guṇasvabhāvaviparītasvabhāvasyopalambhādekasmātpiṇḍādekapuruṣasiddhiḥ evaṃ pratipiṇḍaṃ guṇasvabhāvaviparītasvabhāvasyopalambhātpuruṣanānātvamavaseyam / tasmādavasthitametannānātmāna iti // 18 //
children.translated_text: Here, the properties — having three <s>guṇa</s>s, being non-discriminating, being an object, being common, being non-conscious, and being productive — are observed in each individual body. And just as these [properties exist], so too their contraries — being without <s>guṇa</s>s and so forth — are the properties of <s>puruṣa</s>. Therein, just as from the observation of a nature contrary to the nature of the <s>guṇa</s>s in a single body, the existence of a single <s>puruṣa</s> is established from that single body — so too, from the observation in each body of a nature contrary to the nature of the <s>guṇa</s>s, the multiplicity of <s>puruṣa</s>s should be ascertained. Therefore it stands firm that selves are many.
<s>Kārikā</s> 19

children.translated_text: One says: the multiplicity of the self has been established. Now, from what reason is the understanding of witness-hood, isolation, neutrality, seer-ship, and non-agency [of <s>puruṣa</s> derived]? It is replied:
And from that contrariety, the witness-hood of this <s>puruṣa</s> is established,
[as well as its] isolation, neutrality, seer-ship, and non-agency. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 19)
