tasmādityanena hetusāmānyamācaṣṭe / caśabdo 'vadhāraṇe / viparyāsāditi sāmānyena hetumupāttaṃ viśeṣe 'vasthāpayati / siddhaṃ sākṣitvamasya puruṣasyetyevamādinā sādhyadharmanirdeśaṃ karoti / tatra sākṣitvamityanena guṇānāṃ pravṛttāvastvātantryaṃ khyāpayati, pradhānasya tadarthanibandhanatvātpravṛtteḥ /
  adhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ kathamiti ?
  ucyate- yathā hi kriyāsākṣiṇi kasmiṃścidavasthite kartā tadicchānuvidhāyī kāryaṃ nirvartayati, na svatantraḥ, evaṃ pradhānamapi / pravṛttinivṛttyoryathā puruṣasyārthaḥ sidhyati tathā mahadahaṅkāratanmātrendriyabhūtadevamanuṣyatiryaksthāvarabhāvena vyūhate, na yadṛcchātaḥ / tasmātpuruṣastadarthaparatantratvātpradhānapravṛttinivṛttyoḥ sākṣī / kaivalyamityanena saṃsargadharmatvamātmano nivartayati, na yathā sattvādīnāṃ paraspareṇa prakāśādidharmāpekṣāṇāṃ saṃsargaḥ, evaṃ puruṣasya tairbhavati / mādhyasthyamityanenātiśayanihrāsānupapatteḥ puruṣasya guṇaiḥ saha bādhānugrahānupapattiṃ svakāryapravṛttau cāpakṣapātaṃ darśayati / draṣṭṛtvamityanenodāsīnasya kāryakāraṇapiṇḍavyūhasamakālaṃ caitanyaśaktisadbhāvātsukhaduḥkhamohasvabhāvānāṃ guṇaceṣṭānāmanivṛttārthānāṃ sannidhānamātrādupalabdhimātraṃ pratijānāti / akartṛbhāvaścetyanena saptavidhamakartṛtvamāśrayati / na hyayaṃ viṣayeṣu bāhyāntaḥkaraṇasānnidhye 'dhyavasāyaṃ kurute / na ca sattvādīnāṃ prakāśapravṛttiniyamalakṣaṇairdharmairitaretaropakāreṇa pravartamānānāṃ svena caitanyalakṣaṇena dharmeṇāṅgabhāvaṃ pratipadyate, nāpyaṅgibhāvam / evaṃ saha guṇaiḥ kāryaṃ na kurute strīkumāravat / sthitaprayogaṃ na kurute rathaśakaṭayantraprerakavat / na svātmano mṛtpiṇḍavat / na parataḥ kumbhakāravat / nāpyadeśānmāyākāravat / nobhayato mātṛpitṛvat / tadevamanena sūtreṇācāryaḥ puruṣasyādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ nairguṇyamaudāsīnyaṃ bhoktṛtvamakartṛtvaṃ ca sādhyatāmāpādya triguṇayādiviparyayaṃ sādhanatvenopanyati / taiḥ pañcabhistriguṇādiviparītaiḥ karmabhiḥ pañcānāmeṣāṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ pravṛttiravagantavyā /
  yasmādayaṃ sukhādibhyo 'rthāntarabhūtaḥ tasmādayaṃ tatkriyāsākṣī / tatra nairguṇyātsākṣitvam /
  āha, tadasiddheḥ / nairguṇyāsiddheḥ / yadyasya sukhādidharmatvamātmanaḥ prasiddhaṃ syādata etadyujjate vaktum / tattvasiddham / tasmādayuktametat / viśeṣānabhidhānāditarātsiddhirapīti cet syānmatam, ātmaguṇāḥ sukhādayo na śabdaguṇā ityatrāpi bhavatā viśeṣo nābhidhīyate / tasmādetadapyasiddham / etadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? ahaṃkāreṇaikavākyatve bhinnādhikaraṇatvaṃ syāt / dṛṣṭaṃ tu sukhito 'haṃ duḥkhito 'hamiti / tasmātsukhaduḥkhayoḥ śabdādyātmabhāvo na yuktaḥ /
  ucyate- na, gaurādiṣvanekāntāt / tadyathā gauraḥ kṛṣṇo 'hamiti śarīradharmerātmano bhinnādhikaraṇatvamahaṅkāreṇa evaṃ sukhaduḥkhayorapi syāt / na cātmaguṇatvaṃ syāditi /
  āha, pṛthagupalabdherayuktam / yadyapi gaurādīnāmavibhaktamahaṃkāreṇa grahaṇaṃ tathāpi pṛthagayaṃ prāgetānātmano gṛhītvā paścādavibhaktāngṛhṇanśaktnoti vyavasthāpayitumuṣyaite na punaramuṣyeti / na tvevaṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ pṛthagupalabdhiḥ / tasmādasadetaditi /
  ucyate- naivamutpadyate / kasmāt ? mārgāntaragamanāt / ahaṃkāreṇāvibhaktagrahaṇādātmaguṇatvamiti prāgapadiṣṭam / idānīṃ tu satyapi tasminpṛthaggrahaṇādabhāvaṃ bruvato mārgāntaragamanamanaikāntikasya cāparihāraḥ / kiṃ cānyat, saṃśayāvyatirekāt / yata eva gaurādayaḥ pṛthagupalabhyante na sukhādayo eva saṃśayaḥ / na ca yata eva saṃśayastata eva nirṇayo yuktaḥ / tasmādyuktametad gaurādivadahaṅkāreṇāpyabhinnagrahaṇācchabdādyātmabhūtāḥ sukhādayaḥ / kiṃ cānyat / svabhāvānavadhāraṇādanupādānaprasaṃgāt / sukhādyātmakāḥ śabdādaya iti cet syānmataṃ, yathāgniḥ pākajanimittamupādīyate 'tha caiṣāṃ pārthivatvamevaṃ śabdādayo 'pi sukhādinimittatvenopādīyeran atha caiṣāmātmaguṇatvameva syāditi / tadapyanupapannam / kasmāt ? sāmānādhikaraṇyadarśanāt / yathā nimittasyāgnerna pākajaiḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ pakvo 'gniḥ pacyate 'gniriti evaṃ śabdādīnāṃ nimittatvānna sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ syāt / sukhaśabdo duḥkha iti dṛṣṭaṃ tu / tasmānna teṣāṃ nimittārthenopādānamiti /
  āha, evamapi sukhādīnāṃ śabdādyātmabhāvo na yuktaḥ / kasmāt ? vipratipatteḥ / yathā hi śabdāḥ śabdātmakā eti sarvaiḥ śabdarūpeṇa gṛhyante, evaṃ sukhātmako 'yamiti sarvaistadrūpeṇa gṛhyate / dṛṣṭā tu vipratipattiḥ / tasmādātmaguṇā iti /
  ucyate- na, saṃskāraviśeṣanimittatvāt / tadyathā pittādisāmarthānmādhuryādiṣu vipratipattiḥ / na caiṣāmaśabdādiguṇatvasaṃskāraviśeṣayogātsukhādiṣu vipratipattiḥ / na caiṣāmaśabdādiguṇatvamiti / kiṃ cānyat / nimittatve 'pi tatprasaṃgāt / nimittavādino 'pyetatsamānam / na hi nimittanaimittikayorvipratipattirasti / tadyathā pradīpaprakāśayoḥ / tataśca vipratipatternimittatvamapi śabdādīnāmakalpanīyaṃ syāt / yaśca dvayordoṣo na tamekaścodyata iti / ātmaguṇākāṃkṣitvādadoṣa iti cet syānmatam nimittapradhānatvādanyaparipākavaśena sukhaduḥkhenotpādayatyātmanaḥ / tanmayatve tu nirākāṃkṣatvātpradhānasya vyavasthābhedo na yukta iti / tacca naivam / kasmāt ? uktatvāt / tanmayatve 'pi guṇabhāvānmādhuryādiṣu vipratipattirityādāvevoktametat / tasmāttanmayatve prādhānyamiti cāniścitābhidhānametat /
  āha, evamapyayuktametat / kasmāt ? atītānāgateṣvapi tu dṛṣṭeḥ / tasmātsukhādīnāṃ śabdādyātmabhāvo na yukta iti /
  ucyate- na, smṛtinimittatvād buddheḥ / ayamatītānāgateṣvapi śabdādiṣu smārtasukhaduḥkhayogo bhavati / tatsaṃparkāttu puruṣeṇa tathānubhūyate / puruṣaguṇatve tu pākajavannimittādutpannānāṃ sukhādīnāṃ viśeṣabhāvāttīvramandatānupapattiḥ syāt / tasmātsukhaduḥkhayoḥ śabdādyātmabhāvo na yuktaḥ / kiṃcānyat / anirmokṣaprasaṃgāt / dravyasya guṇairaviprayogātsukhaduḥkhayorātmaguṇatve satyātmanastābhyāmanirmokṣaprasaṃgaḥ / tasmāttayorātmaguṇatvamayuktamiti / śyāmādivattadvinivṛttiriti cet syānmatam, yathā śyāmaguṇatve satyaṇoragnisambandhāttadvinivṛttiḥ, śabdādiguṇatve cākāśasyāśabdakasyāvasthānamevamātmano 'pi / etadayuktam / kasmāt ? viśeṣopādānaprasaṃgāt / sādhyatvācca, yathā hyaṇuḥ śyāmatāṃ parityajya rūpaviśeṣameva raktalakṣaṇamupādatte, na rūpavattāṃ tyajati, evamātmāpi bāhyanimittasāmarthyātsukhāntaraṃ duḥkhād duḥkhāntaramupādadīta / na te atyantaṃ jahyāt / tathā ākāśaṃ śabdalakṣaṇaṃ kasyāṃcidavasthāyāmaśabdakaṃ bhavatītyasmānprati sādhyo 'yamarthaḥ / bheryādiśabdāstu tadguṇa eveti pratipādayiṣyāmaḥ tasmātsukhaduḥkhayoḥ śabdādyātmabhāvo 'yuktaḥ / evamanāmiśrarūpa ātmā / tataścecchādveṣaprayatnadharmajñānasaṃskārāṇāmanekasvabhāvānāṃ parasparavirodhināṃ ca tadguṇatvamanupapannam / tasmādyuktametannirguṇa ātmā nairguṇyācca sākṣimātra iti kevalo viviktatvāt /
  tasmādayaṃ guṇebhyaḥ pṛthagbhūtaḥ tasmātkevalaḥ na taiḥ saha saṃsargeṇa vartate /
  āha, kaḥ punarasyātmano guṇebhyaḥ pṛthagbhāvo 'bhipreta iti ?
  ucyate- tadupakāranirapekṣāṇāṃ sattvādīnāṃ svakāryasāmarthyapṛthagbhāvaḥ / na hi sattvādayaḥ prakāśādibhirdharmairitaretaropakāreṇa vartamānāḥ puruṣakṛtamupakāramapekṣante / prakāśādidharmasannidhānamātrādeva tu pravartante / tathā ca vārṣagaṇāḥ paṭhanti "pradhānapravṛttirapratyayā puruṣeṇāparigṛhyamāṇādisarge vartante" iti / yasmādguṇāstadupakāranirapekṣāḥ pravartante tasmādasāvapi tatsaṃsarga nānubhavati / dṛṣṭā tu loke 'pyekakāryatvāpṛthakpṛthagbhāvaparikalpanā / tadyathā ime bhrātaraḥ pṛthak, eṣāṃ naikaṃ kāryam / na pṛthagime yeṣāmekamiti /
  madhyastho viṣayitvāt / yasmādayaṃ puruṣo viṣayī tasmānmadhyasthaḥ / kiṃ kāraṇam ? viṣayāṇāṃ hyatulyabalatvāt, nyūnātiśayopapatteśca paraspareṇa bādhānugrahāvutpannau / viṣayī cāyam / tasmānnāsti nyūnatādyupapattiḥ / tataścetanābhāvaḥ / na cāmiśrarūpatvātsaṅgadveṣau guṇaviṣayau, ato madhyasthaḥ ?
  draṣṭṛtvaṃ caitanyāt / prakṛtivikārabhūtatvāt sattvādibhyaścaitanyamapoddhṛtya puruṣe vyavasthāpanīyam / na cācetanānāṃ draṣṭṛtvamupapadyate ityataḥ puruṣa eva caitanyād dṛṣṭā nānyattattvāntaram /
  akartṛbhāvaḥ, aprasavadharmitvāt / prasavārtho dharmaḥ prasavadharmaḥ so 'syāstīti prasavadharmī /
  kaḥ punarasau prasavārtho dharma iti ?
  ucyate- praspandanapariṇāmau / niṣkriyatvādakarteti yāvat / tadidamaprasavadharmitvādakarteti / kathamasya niṣkriyatvamiti cet ? caitanyāt / acetanānāṃ hi kṣīrādīnāṃ kriyāvattvamupalabdhaṃ, cetanasya na kasyacidityato niṣkriyaḥ puruṣaḥ / kiṃca anāmiśrarūpatvāt / anāmiśrarūpaṃ hi kriyādimatkṣīrādi / anāmiśrarūpaścāyam / tasmānniṣkriyaḥ / vibhutvāditi cet syādetat, yathā vibhutve sati pradhānasya sakriyatvamevaṃ puruṣasya iti vibhutve sakriyatvena bhavitavyamiti / tacca naivam / kasmāt ? dharmadvayasahitasya sāhacaryopalabdheḥ / tadvibhutvamācetanyānekarūpatvasahitaṃ kriyāvati dṛṣṭaṃ, na kevalam / na tu tathā puruṣe / tasmādviṣamametat / evaṃ niṣkriyaḥ puruṣaḥ niṣkriyatvācca pradhānātkāryakāraṇaṃ na kurute / kasmāt ? kriyāvataḥ kumbhakārasya mṛtpiṇḍātkāryaniṣpattisāmarthyadarśanāt / syādetat / utpāditasyānyena sthitiṃ kurute, dhātrīkumāravat / sthitasya vā prayogaṃ rathaśakaṭayantraprerakavaditi / etadapyanupapannaṃ, pūrvasmādeva hetoḥ athāpi syātsvataḥ puruṣaḥ kāryakaraṇaṃ kuruta iti tadapyayuktam / cetanācetanayoratyantabhedātprakṛtivikārabhāvānupapatteḥ / atha matamubhayata iti, tadapi naiva saṃbhavati, ubhayadoṣaprasaṃgāt / syātpunaretat avyapadiśya yoniṃ puruṣo 'bhidhyānamātreṇa kāryakaraṇaṃ kurute ityasadetat / kasmāt ? anutpattāvabhidhyānānupapatteḥ / īśvarakāraṇapratiṣedhe 'bhihitaṃ prāk pradhānavipariṇāmādbuddhimato buddhirnāsti / na ca buddhimantareṇābhidhyānamupapadyate, tadvṛttibhūtatvāt tathā buddhimatpūrvakasṛṣṭipratiṣedhaḥ kṛtaḥ / sa ihāpi yojyaḥ, adhyavasāyakartṛtvaṃ ca prākpratiṣiddham / evaṃ saptavidhenākartṛtvenākartā puruṣaḥ / uktaṃ ca
nādhyavasāyaṃ kurute puruṣo naivaṃ sthitiṃ prayogaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> does not perform <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination), nor does he engage in such a state or activity,

children.text: na svātmano na parato na vyapadeśānna cobhayataḥ //
children.translated_text: neither from his own self, nor from another, nor from designation, nor from both.

By the word 'therefore' he states the general reason. The particle 'ca' is used in the sense of emphasis. By 'from the inversion' he takes the reason stated generally and applies it to a specific case. By 'it is established that this <s>puruṣa</s> is a witness' and so forth, he makes the specification of the properties to be proved. There, by 'witness-hood' he declares that the <s>guṇas</s> are not independent in their operation, since the activity of <s>pradhāna</s> is dependent upon [<s>puruṣa</s>'s] purpose.
  How [is <s>puruṣa</s>'s] sovereignty [established]?
  [Reply:] Just as when some witness of an action is present, the agent, conforming to that one's wish, accomplishes the work — not independently — so too <s>pradhāna</s>. It arranges itself in the form of <s>mahat</s> (the great one), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties), <s>bhūtas</s> (gross elements), gods, humans, animals, and plants in such a way that <s>puruṣa</s>'s purpose is fulfilled through activity and cessation — not by chance. Therefore, <s>puruṣa</s> is the witness of <s>pradhāna</s>'s activity and cessation, since [<s>pradhāna</s>] is dependent on his purpose. By 'isolation' (<s>kaivalya</s>) he negates the property of being in contact with the self — not as <s>sattva</s> and the others have contact with each other through the mutual dependence of their properties like illumination and so forth, so does <s>puruṣa</s> have [contact] with them. By 'neutrality' (<s>mādhyasthya</s>), since increase and decrease are inapplicable, he shows that <s>puruṣa</s> cannot be helped or harmed by the <s>guṇas</s>, and that [<s>puruṣa</s>] is impartial in the operation of their own functions. By 'seer-hood' (<s>draṣṭṛtva</s>) he asserts that the indifferent [<s>puruṣa</s>], simultaneously with the arrangement of the mass of effects and causes, has mere perception through the mere presence [of the <s>guṇas</s>'] activities — whose nature is pleasure, pain, and delusion — which have not yet fulfilled their purpose, due to the existence of the power of consciousness. And by 'non-agency' (<s>akartṛbhāva</s>) he resorts to seven kinds of non-agency. For this [<s>puruṣa</s>] does not make a determination regarding objects in the presence of the external and internal instruments. Nor does it assume the role of a subordinate with respect to <s>sattva</s> and the others operating through mutual assistance by means of their properties of illumination, activity, and restraint, with its own property of consciousness — nor does it assume the role of the principal. Thus it does not produce an effect together with the <s>guṇas</s>, like a woman and child. It does not direct an established process, like a driver of a chariot, cart, or machine. It does not [create] from itself, like a lump of clay. It does not [create] from another, like a potter. It does not [create] by mere will, like a magician. It does not [create] from both, like a mother and father. Thus, by this <s>sūtra</s>, the teacher, having established as properties to be proved <s>puruṣa</s>'s sovereignty, freedom from <s>guṇas</s>, indifference, experiencer-hood, and non-agency, presents the inversion from the three <s>guṇas</s> and the rest as the means of proof. Through those five properties — inverse to the three <s>guṇas</s> and the rest — the operation of these five [properties] should be understood as applicable.
  Since this [<s>puruṣa</s>] is different from pleasure and the like, therefore it is a witness of their activities. There, witness-hood follows from freedom from <s>guṇas</s>.
  [Objection:] Because that is unestablished — because freedom from <s>guṇas</s> is unestablished. If the quality of pleasure and the like being properties of the self were well-established, then it would be proper to say this. [But] that is [in fact] established. Therefore this is untenable. If one says that since the specific [nature] is not stated, the establishment could also come from the other [side] — [we reply:] you too do not state the specific difference in [your claim that] pleasure and the like are qualities of the self, not qualities of sound [and the like]. Therefore that too is unestablished. That too is untenable. Why? Because if [pleasure etc.] were in the same sentence with the ego, they would have a different substrate. But it is observed: 'I am happy,' 'I am unhappy.' Therefore the identification of pleasure and pain with sound and the like is not proper.
  [Reply:] No, because it is inconclusive in cases like 'fair-complexioned' and the like. Just as 'I am fair, I am dark' — [here] properties of the body are [attributed to] the self through different substrates being [united] by the ego — so too it could be for pleasure and pain. And they would not be qualities of the self.
  [Objection:] This is untenable because of separate perception. Even though fair-complexion and the like are grasped undifferentiatedly by the ego, still, having first perceived these separately from the self, one subsequently grasping them undifferentiatedly can establish 'these belong to this, not to that.' But there is no such separate perception of pleasure and pain. Therefore that is false.
  [Reply:] That does not follow. Why? Because of going to a different path. It was previously stated that [pleasure etc. are] qualities of the self because the ego grasps them undifferentiatedly. But now, by asserting non-existence even while that [argument] stands, on the basis of separate perception, you are going to a different path — and the inconclusiveness is not resolved. Moreover, because the doubt is not eliminated. Since fair-complexion and the like are separately perceived but pleasure and the like are not — precisely that is the doubt. And it is not proper that from the very source of doubt comes the resolution. Therefore it is proper that, like fair-complexion and the like, through the undifferentiated grasping by the ego, pleasure and the like belong to sound and the like. Furthermore, because of the consequence of non-adoption due to the indeterminacy of [their] nature. If it is thought that sound and the like have pleasure etc. as their nature — just as fire is adopted as the cause of cooking, yet [the products] are earthy — so too sound and the like could be adopted as the cause of pleasure and the like, yet [pleasure etc.] could still be qualities of the self — that too is untenable. Why? Because coordination is observed. Just as there is no coordination between the cause, fire, and the products of cooking — 'Cooked fire, fire is being cooked' — so too there should be no coordination between sound and the like and [pleasure etc.] if they were merely causes. But it is observed: 'Pleasant sound, painful [sound].' Therefore they are not adopted in the sense of being causes.
  [Objection:] Even so, the identification of pleasure and the like with sound and the like is not proper. Why? Because of disagreement. Just as sounds are grasped by all as having the nature of sound, so too [if pleasure were the nature of something,] it would be grasped by all as 'this has the nature of pleasure.' But disagreement is observed. Therefore they are qualities of the self.
  [Reply:] No, because it is due to particular dispositions. Just as there is disagreement regarding sweetness and the like due to the influence of bile and so forth, [so too for pleasure etc.]. There is disagreement regarding pleasure and the like not because they are qualities of the self, but due to the connection with particular dispositions — and they are not non-qualities of sound and the like. Moreover, because the same consequence applies even if they are causes. This is equally [problematic] for the proponent of the cause-theory. For there is no disagreement between cause and effect — for example, between a lamp and its light. Therefore, from disagreement, even the causal nature of sound and the like should not be postulated. And a defect that is common to both [positions] cannot be objected to by one alone. If it is thought that there is no defect because [pleasure etc.] seek to be qualities of the self — since they are primarily causes, through the influence of another's transformation, they produce pleasure and pain for the self; but if they were of that nature [i.e., inherent in sound etc.], since there would be no seeking, the distinct determination of <s>pradhāna</s> would not be proper — that is not so. Why? Because this was already addressed. Even if they are of that nature, disagreement regarding sweetness and the like arises from the <s>guṇa</s>-status — this was stated at the outset. Therefore, that their being of that nature implies primacy — this is an unfounded assertion.
  [Objection:] Even so, this is untenable. Why? Because of observation in past and future [objects] as well. Therefore, the identification of pleasure and the like with sound and the like is not proper.
  [Reply:] No, because it is due to <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), which has memory as its cause. This connection of remembered pleasure and pain with past and future sounds and the like occurs [through memory]. But it is experienced as such by <s>puruṣa</s> through contact with that. If pleasure and pain were qualities of <s>puruṣa</s>, like things produced by cooking that arise from a cause, the intense and mild gradations of pleasure and the like would be inexplicable due to their [supposed] specific nature. Therefore, the identification of pleasure and pain with sound and the like is untenable. Moreover, because of the consequence of non-liberation. Since a substance is never separated from its qualities, if pleasure and pain were qualities of the self, the consequence would be that the self could never be liberated from them. Therefore, their being qualities of the self is untenable. If it is thought that their cessation occurs like dark-complexion and the like — just as, despite dark-complexion being a quality [of the atom], it ceases through the atom's contact with fire, and just as space exists in a soundless state despite sound being its quality — so too for the self — this is untenable. Why? Because of the consequence of adopting a particular [quality]. And because it is what needs to be proved. Just as an atom, abandoning dark color, adopts a particular form characterized as red, but does not abandon the property of having form — so too the self, by the power of an external cause, would adopt another pleasure or another pain from pain, but would not completely abandon them. Likewise, that space, whose nature is sound, exists in some state as soundless — that is precisely what needs to be proved against us. But we will demonstrate that the sounds of drums and the like are indeed its qualities. Therefore, the identification of pleasure and pain with sound and the like is untenable. Thus the self has an unmixed nature. And from that, it is untenable that desire, aversion, effort, <s>dharma</s> (merit), knowledge, and <s>saṃskāra</s> (impressions) — which are of manifold nature and mutually contradictory — are its qualities. Therefore it is proper: the self is without <s>guṇas</s>, and because of freedom from <s>guṇas</s>, it is merely a witness — therefore it is isolated, because it is distinct.
  Therefore, since this [<s>puruṣa</s>] is different from the <s>guṇas</s>, it is isolated — it does not exist in contact with them.
  [Objection:] What kind of distinctness of the self from the <s>guṇas</s> is intended?
  [Reply:] The distinctness is in the capacity of <s>sattva</s> and the others to perform their own functions without requiring his assistance. For <s>sattva</s> and the others, operating through mutual assistance by means of their properties of illumination, activity, and restraint, do not require assistance produced by <s>puruṣa</s>. Rather, they operate merely from the presence of the properties of illumination and the rest. And thus the followers of <s>Vārṣagaṇa</s> recite: 'The activity of <s>pradhāna</s> is without cognition; they operate in creation without being apprehended by <s>puruṣa</s>.' Since the <s>guṇas</s> operate without requiring his assistance, therefore he too does not experience contact with them. And in the world too, the attribution of separateness and non-separateness is based on having a common function. For example: 'These brothers are separate — they have no common function'; 'These are not separate — they have a common function.'
  [<s>Puruṣa</s> is] neutral because of being a subject. Since this <s>puruṣa</s> is a subject, therefore it is neutral. For what reason? Because the objects, being of unequal strength, give rise to harm and benefit with respect to each other due to the possibility of deficiency and excess. But this one is a subject. Therefore, the possibility of deficiency and the like does not apply. And from that, there is absence of partiality. And since it has an unmixed nature, attachment and aversion, which pertain to the <s>guṇas</s>, do not [apply]. Therefore it is neutral.
  Seer-hood is from consciousness. Since [everything else] belongs to the modifications of <s>prakṛti</s>, consciousness must be extracted from <s>sattva</s> and the like and established in <s>puruṣa</s>. And since seer-hood is not possible for non-conscious things, therefore <s>puruṣa</s> alone is the seer through consciousness — no other principle.
  Non-agency is because of not having the property of production. The property that has the purpose of production is the 'production-property'; one who has that is 'having the property of production.'
  What, then, is that property having the purpose of production?
  [Reply:] Vibration and transformation. [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is a non-agent because of inactivity — that is the meaning. Thus, because of not having the property of production, [<s>puruṣa</s> is] a non-agent. How is its inactivity [established]? From consciousness. For the activity of non-conscious things like milk and the like is observed, but not of any conscious thing — therefore <s>puruṣa</s> is inactive. Moreover, because of having an unmixed nature. For it is milk and the like, which have a mixed nature, that possess activity and the rest. And this [<s>puruṣa</s>] has an unmixed nature. Therefore it is inactive. If it is thought: just as <s>pradhāna</s>, despite being all-pervading, has activity, so too <s>puruṣa</s> — that all-pervasiveness should entail activity — that is not so. Why? Because activity is observed [only] in conjunction with two [other] properties. That all-pervasiveness is observed in what possesses activity [only] when accompanied by non-consciousness and manifold nature — not alone. But it is not so in <s>puruṣa</s>. Therefore, this is a false analogy. Thus <s>puruṣa</s> is inactive, and because of inactivity, it does not produce cause and effect from <s>pradhāna</s>. Why? Because we observe the capacity for producing an effect from a lump of clay only in an active agent like a potter. One might think: it maintains what has been produced by another, like a nurse and a child. Or it directs what is established, like a driver of a chariot, cart, or machine. That too is untenable, for the same reason as before. Or one might think: <s>puruṣa</s> produces cause and effect from itself — that too is untenable, because of the absolute difference between the conscious and the non-conscious, and the impossibility of the relationship of <s>prakṛti</s> and modification [between them]. If it is thought [it produces] from both — that too is impossible, because the defects of both would follow. One might further think that <s>puruṣa</s> produces cause and effect merely by meditation, without designating the source — that is false. Why? Because meditation is impossible without [prior] origination. It was stated earlier, in the refutation of God as cause: prior to the transformation of <s>pradhāna</s>, there is no <s>buddhi</s> for a conscious being. And without <s>buddhi</s>, meditation is impossible, since it is a function of that. Likewise, the refutation of creation preceded by a conscious being was made. That applies here too. And the agency of determination was refuted earlier. Thus, through seven kinds of non-agency, <s>puruṣa</s> is a non-agent. And it is said:
That is established.
Therefore, from this very contrast, the <s>sākṣitva</s> (witness-nature) of this <s>Puruṣa</s> is proven,
as well as <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation), <s>mādhyasthya</s> (neutrality), <s>draṣṭṛtva</s> (seer-hood), and <s>akartṛbhāva</s> (non-agency). Thus.
<s>Kārikā</s> 20

children.text: yataścetanāśaktisambandhātpuruṣa eva draṣṭā nānyattattvāntaraṃ, guṇāśca kartāro, na puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Since it is only <s>Puruṣa</s> who is the seer, by virtue of the connection with the power of consciousness, and not any other principle; and the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents) are the agents, not <s>Puruṣa</s> —
Therefore, from the conjunction with that [<s>Puruṣa</s>], the non-conscious <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) appears as if conscious;
and since the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents) are the agents, the indifferent one [<s>Puruṣa</s>] appears as if he were the agent. // <s>ISk</s> 20 //

children.text: puruṣasamparkād hi grahaṇadhāraṇavijñānavacanohāpohakriyā yathānyāyābhiniveśānāṃ karaṇadharmāṇāṃ pratyayarūpāṇāmivopalabdheścetanāśakteścādhyavasāyavṛttimanurudhyamānāyāstadbhāvasanniveśināṃ sattvādīnāṃ vyāpāravatāmabhisambandhād vyāpārāviṣṭāyā ivopalabdhiḥ / yatastatrāyamanekakālapravṛttamithyāpratyayābhyāsavāsanāpekṣo bhavabījaheturjñānaviśeṣaḥ prāṇabhṛtāmavabhāsate / śrotramupalabhyate tvakcakṣurjihvā ghrāṇamityādi / tathā puruṣaḥ karmaṇāṃ kartā, puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoriti / tasmātkaraṇasya grahaṇarūpatā puruṣasya ca kartṛrūpatā, sambandhyantarasamparkādanyagatānyatropalabhyamānā bhaktyādhyavasātavyā, na paramārthataḥ / uktaṃ ca

children.translated_text: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), presided over by consciousness, is conceived as if conscious itself;
and the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), situated among agents, is perceived as if he were an agent.

For, from contact with <s>Puruṣa</s>, since the functions of the instruments — grasping, retention, cognition, speech, acceptance, rejection, and activity — which are in the form of cognitions, are apprehended as if following their proper course, and since the power of consciousness, conforming to the operation of <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination), is connected with <s>sattva</s> and the other [<s>guṇas</s>] which are established in its nature and are possessed of activity, there arises an apprehension as if [consciousness itself] were pervaded by activity. Because therein this particular knowledge, which depends on the habitual impressions of false cognitions practiced over many lifetimes and which is the seed-cause of existence, manifests in living beings — [such cognitions as]: 'the ear perceives,' 'the skin, eye, tongue, nose [perceive],' and so forth. Likewise: '<s>Puruṣa</s> is the agent of actions,' '<s>Puruṣa</s> [experiences] pleasure and pain.' Therefore, the grasping-nature of the instrument and the agent-nature of <s>Puruṣa</s> — being apprehended in one through their presence in the other due to contact with a relatum — should be understood figuratively, not in the ultimate sense. And it has been said:

children.text:
āha, saṃyogātpararūpatāpattāvatiprasaṃgaḥ, aviśeṣāt / yadi cetanasaṃyogād buddhyādīnāṃ pratyayavadupacāraḥ vyāpitvādasya ghaṭādibhirapi saṃyogo na pratiṣidhyata ityataḥ prāptasteṣāmapi pratyayavadupacāraḥ / atha saṃyogāviśeṣātkaraṇānāmeva pratyayavadupacāro na ghaṭādīnāṃ, viśeṣastarhi vaktavya iti /
  ucyate- tadaprasaṃgaḥ / śaktyapekṣatvāt sphaṭikādivat / yathopadhānasaṃyogaviśeṣe satyākāśasphaṭikayoḥ sphāṭikamevopadhanasarūpaṃ pratyavabhāsate śaktito nākāśam, evaṃ puruṣasaṃyogāviśeṣe buddhighaṭayoḥ śaktito buddhireva cetanārūpāpannevopalabhyate, na ghaṭaḥ /
  āha, puruṣasya vikāryatvaprasaṃgaḥ, rūpāntaropādanāt / yadi tarhi karaṇasambandhātpuruṣaḥ kartṛtvopacāraṃ viṣayasarūpatāṃ ca pratipadyate, prāptamasyāpi sphaṭikavadrūpāntaropādānādvikāryatvam / atha nāsya viṣayarūpāpattiḥ, na tarhi karaṇasvarūpaḥ puruṣa iti /
  ucyate- na, bhaktito 'bhyupagamāt / buddhirupāttaviṣayendriyavṛttyupanipātāttādrūpyaṃ pratipadyate / buddhirūpaṃ tu sannidhānamātrācchaktiviśeṣayogātphalabhoktṛtvācca rājani bhṛtyajayaparājayopacāravatpuruṣa upacaryate / na tvasau buddhisaṃparkāttadrūpo bhavati / ata evāsya satyāṃ cetanāśaktau vyavasāyakartṛtvaṃ pratiṣidhyate, mā bhūt viṣayarūpāpattau satyāmanekasvabhāvatvādikāryatvaprasaṃgaḥ / tasmādviṣayasamparkādapyavikāryaḥ puruṣaḥ, na hyasya nityatvātkiṃcidanugrahāya nāpaghātāya / āha ca

children.translated_text: Just as a handful [of mustard seeds and the like] when scattered — on the point of a needle, mustard seeds and such
do not remain due to [the point's] subtle nature — so too, the pairs of opposites [do not remain] in the omniscient one.

[Objection:] From conjunction there would be the unwanted consequence of assuming the nature of the other, due to the absence of a distinguishing principle. If, from conjunction with the conscious, the <s>buddhi</s> and other [evolutes] are figuratively spoken of as if they were cognitions due to [<s>Puruṣa</s>'s] pervasiveness, then conjunction with pots and the like too cannot be denied, and therefore the figurative attribution of cognition to them would also follow. Or if, despite the non-distinction in conjunction, only the instruments are figuratively spoken of as having cognition and not pots and the like, then a distinguishing reason must be stated. [Reply:] There is no such unwanted consequence, because [the figurative attribution] depends on capacity, as in the case of a crystal and the like. Just as, when there is a particular conjunction with a colored substrate, it is only the crystal that reflects the form of the substrate due to its capacity, and not space — so too, despite there being no distinction in the conjunction of <s>Puruṣa</s> with <s>buddhi</s> and a pot, it is only <s>buddhi</s> that is apprehended as having assumed the form of consciousness due to its capacity, not the pot. [Objection:] There would be the unwanted consequence of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s being subject to modification, since he would assume another form. If, from contact with the instruments, <s>Puruṣa</s> acquires the figurative attribution of agency and assumes the form of the object, then, like a crystal, the unwanted consequence of his being subject to modification through assuming another form would follow. Or if there is no assumption of the object's form by him, then <s>Puruṣa</s> does not have the nature of the instrument [and the analogy fails]. [Reply:] No, because [this is] accepted only figuratively. <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) assumes such a form from the incidence of sense-activity that has grasped the object. But the form of <s>Puruṣa</s> is figuratively attributed merely from proximity, from possessing a particular capacity, and from being the enjoyer of results — just as victory and defeat of servants are figuratively attributed to the king. He does not actually become of that form through contact with <s>buddhi</s>. For this very reason, though he possesses the power of consciousness, his being the agent of determination is denied, lest — if the assumption of the object's form were real — there would be the unwanted consequence of his having multiple natures and being a product. Therefore, <s>Puruṣa</s> is unmodifiable even from contact with objects, for nothing whatsoever can benefit or harm him due to his eternality. And it has been said:

children.text: iti / cetanāśaktiyogāttu draṣṭṛtvamasya svābhāvikam / evaṃ cedyayuktaṃ

children.translated_text: What effect do rain and sunshine have on the sky? Their effect is on leather.
If the Self is like leather, he is non-eternal; if he is like space, he is equivalent to non-existence.
Thus. But <s>draṣṭṛtva</s> (seer-hood) is his natural attribute, from the connection with the power of consciousness. If this is so, [the following objection is] not proper:

children.text:
iti tadayuktam / kiṃ kāraṇam ? yasmādavikāryarūpasyākāśasya sannidhānamātrānmeghapayorajodhūmaprabhṛtibhirabhinnadeśatvādatyantaśuddhasyāpi malinamiva rūpamupalakṣyate, na ca vikāryatvam, evamanātmano 'pi syāt / tadyuktametatpuruṣasaṃyogātkaraṇasya pratyayopacāraḥ, puruṣasya ca guṇasaṃyogātkartṛtvopacāra iti /
  āha, ayuktametat / kasmāt ? saṃyogānupapatteḥ / puruṣasya hi guṇānāṃ ca saṃyogaḥ parikalpyamāno 'nyatarakarmajo vā parikalpyate yathā sthāṇuśyenayoḥ, ubhayakarmajo yathā meṣayoḥ, saṃyogajo vā dvyaṅgulākāśayoḥ, svābhāviko vā yathāgnyuṣṇayoḥ, śaktinimitto vā yathā cakṣurūpayoḥ, yogyatālakṣaṇo vā yathā matsyodakayoriti ? tanna tāvadanyatarakarmaja ubhyakarmajaśca saṃyoga eṣāmupapadyate / kasmāt ? vibhutvāt / na svābhāvikaḥ anirmokṣaprasaṃgāt / yathāgneḥ svābhāvikādauṣṇyānmokṣo na bhavati evamātmanaḥ svābhāvikatvādguṇasaṃyogādanirmokṣaprasaṃgaḥ syāt / śaktinimittaśca / kim ? anirmokṣaprasaṃgādeva, sa na bhavatītyanuvartate / svasvāmiśaktinimitte hi saṃyoge parikalpyamāne śaktyoḥ satatāvasthānādanirmokṣa eva prasajyeta / yogyatālakṣaṇaḥ śaktimātrarūpatvādasaṃvedyo 'tastadasiddhiḥ / kiṃca prayojanāntarānupapatteḥ / pravṛttyanuguṇaṃ hi yogyamityucyate / tasyā eva tu pravṛtte puruṣārthamapohya nimittāntaraṃ śakyaṃ kalpayitum / ākasmikatve ca niyamadvaitānupapattiḥ / tasmādayuktaṃ puruṣasya guṇānāṃ ca yogyatālakṣaṇaḥ sambandhaḥ / na yādṛcchikaḥ / mokṣakāraṇaniyamānupapatteḥ / saṃyogakāraṇapratidvandvaṃ kaivalyakāraṇam / yadi ca yādṛcchiko guṇapuruṣasaṃyogaḥ syāttasyājñānānnivṛttirnāstīti tadarthasyābhyutthānasyānarthakyaṃ prāptaṃ viśeṣānupapatteśca kāraṇāntaraṃ kalpayitum / ata etadapyayuktamiti / na vaiṣayikaḥ, anirmokṣaprasaṃgāt / satatameva hi puruṣasya viṣayitvamavyāvṛttaṃ guṇānāṃ ca viṣayatvamityanirmokṣaprasaṃga eva syāt / etāvāṃśca saṃyogaḥ parikalpyamānaḥ parikalpyeta / sarvathā ca nopapadyate / tasmāttatsaṃyogādityayuktamabhidhātumiti /
  ucyate- saṃyogānityatvādiha caupakārikaparikalpanādadoṣaḥ / ihānekavidhaḥ saṃyogaḥ / tadyathā prāptipūrvikā prāptiḥ / yathodāhṛtaṃ anyataraja ubhayakarmajaḥ saṃyoga ityādi / yatrāsau na saṃbhavati tatra sannidhimātrasāmānyād bhaktyā kalpyate / tadyathākāśasya gavādibhiḥ / pradeśairiti cenna abhāvāt / te 'pi hi niravayavatvādākāśasya bhaktyā kalpyante, mā bhūtkṛtakatvānityatvadoṣaprasaṃgaḥ / tasmātpradeśopacārātkāryamapyupacaritam / anyastu śāstrīyaḥ saṃyogo 'rthanimittaḥ / tatrānekasaṃyogopapatteriha puruṣāntaḥkaraṇayorabhinnadeśatvātsannidhimātrasāmānyādbhāktaṃ saṃyogaṃ parikalpyaivamucyata ityadoṣaḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: That [objection] is not proper. Why? Because just as space, which is of an unmodifiable nature, even though extremely pure, appears as if tainted merely from proximity with clouds, rain, dust, smoke, and the like — due to their sharing the same location — yet is not subject to modification, so too it would be the same for the non-self [i.e., <s>Puruṣa</s> who is not the body]. Therefore this is established: from the conjunction with <s>Puruṣa</s>, there is figurative attribution of cognition to the instrument; and from the conjunction of <s>Puruṣa</s> with the <s>guṇas</s>, there is figurative attribution of agency [to <s>Puruṣa</s>]. [Objection:] This is not proper. Why? Because conjunction is impossible. For the conjunction of <s>Puruṣa</s> and the <s>guṇas</s>, when conceived, is conceived either as produced by the action of one of the two, as [the conjunction] of a post and a falcon; or produced by the action of both, as of two rams; or produced by [another] conjunction, as of two atoms and space; or as natural, as of fire and heat; or as caused by capacity, as of the eye and form; or as characterized by fitness, as of fish and water. Now, conjunction produced by the action of one or by the action of both is impossible for these [<s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>guṇas</s>]. Why? Because [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is all-pervading. Nor is it natural, because there would be the unwanted consequence of non-liberation. Just as there is no liberation from fire's natural heat, so too from <s>Ātman</s>'s natural conjunction with the <s>guṇas</s>, there would be the unwanted consequence of non-liberation. And [conjunction] caused by capacity — what [about it]? Because there would be the unwanted consequence of non-liberation as well — that too does not obtain. For if conjunction is conceived as caused by the capacity of master and servant, there would be the consequence of non-liberation, since the capacities persist forever. [Conjunction] characterized by fitness, being merely of the nature of capacity, is unknowable, and therefore it is unestablished. Moreover, because no other purpose is possible — for what is fit is said to be so in conformity with activity, yet once that very activity has proceeded, one can, setting aside the purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s>, postulate another cause. And if it were accidental, the fixed duality [of <s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s>] would be impossible to account for. Therefore, conjunction between <s>Puruṣa</s> and the <s>guṇas</s> characterized by fitness is not proper. Nor is it accidental — because a fixed cause of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) would be impossible to account for. The cause of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) is the counterpart of the cause of conjunction. If the conjunction of <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> were accidental, there would be no cessation of it through knowledge, and thus the purposelessness of the effort [toward liberation] would follow, and due to the impossibility of accounting for a distinguishing factor, one cannot posit another cause. Therefore this too is not proper. Nor is it [conjunction] of the object-possessor type, because there would be the unwanted consequence of non-liberation. For <s>Puruṣa</s>'s being an object-possessor is perpetual and unceasing, and the <s>guṇas</s>' being objects [is likewise perpetual], so there would indeed be the consequence of non-liberation. And this is the extent of conjunction that can be conceived. In every way it is impossible. Therefore, to state 'from the conjunction with that' is not proper. [Reply:] There is no fault here, since conjunction is not [taken in a] literal [sense] but is conceived figuratively. Here conjunction is of many kinds. Namely: contact preceded by [spatial] reaching — as exemplified [above]: conjunction produced by the action of one, produced by the action of both, and so forth. Where that [literal conjunction] is not possible, it is figuratively conceived merely from proximity, by analogy with [spatial] nearness. As, for example, [the conjunction] of space with cows and the like. And if [one objects] 'by parts,' [we say] no, because [parts] do not exist. For those [parts] too, since space is partless, are figuratively conceived — lest the faults of being produced and non-eternal should follow. Therefore, from the figurative attribution of parts, even the effect is figuratively attributed. But there is another conjunction, a doctrinal one, caused by purpose. Among the many possible kinds of conjunction there, since <s>Puruṣa</s> and the internal organ share the same location, a figurative conjunction is conceived merely from proximity, by analogy with nearness — thus it is stated, and there is no fault. // 20 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 21

children.text:
āha, vijñātaṃ saṃyogadvayam / ayaṃ tvanyo 'rthanimittaḥ śāstrīyaḥ saṃyogo bhavatā paribhāṣyate / tatra vaktavyaṃ kimartho 'sāviti ?
  ucyate

children.translated_text: For the purpose of the seeing of <s>Puruṣa</s> —

[Objection:] The twofold [nature of] conjunction is understood. But this other conjunction — doctrinal and caused by purpose — is being defined by you. With respect to that, it must be stated: what is its purpose? [Reply:]

children.text: dṛṣṭirdarśanam / arthaśabdo nimittavacanaḥ / darśanamartho 'syāsau darśanārthaḥ / darśananimitto darśanahetuḥ darśanakāraṇa ityarthaḥ / etaduktaṃ bhavati- sannidhānāviśeṣe sati ātmana ākāśādeśca yasmāddṛkchaktiyuktaḥ puruṣaḥ tasmātkāryakāraṇatāmāpannena pradhānena saha bhoktṛtvena saṃbadhyate, nācaitanyādākāśādaya iti / athavā arthaśabdaḥ phalavacanaḥ / yathā tṛptyarthā bhujikriyā tṛptyau satyāṃ nivartate prāptyarthā gamikriyā prāptau satyām, evaṃ puruṣasya pradhānena darśanārthaḥ saṃyogaḥ darśane sati nivartate / tathā ca vakṣyati dṛṣṭā mayetiyupekṣaka eko dṛṣṭāhamityuparataiketi (

children.translated_text: <s>ISk</s> 66

). [Objection:] Even so, there would be the unwanted consequence of cessation simultaneous with the apprehension of sound and the like. Why? Because even in that state it is possible to say '<s>Prakṛti</s> has been seen.' [Reply:] Although this is so, nevertheless, just as the conjunction is for the purpose of the seeing of <s>Puruṣa</s>,

<s>Dṛṣṭi</s> (sight) is <s>darśana</s> (seeing). The word <s>artha</s> means 'cause.' <s>Darśana</s> (seeing) is the <s>artha</s> (purpose) of this — that is <s>darśanārtha</s> (having seeing as its purpose). [It means:] having seeing as its motive, having seeing as its cause, having seeing as its reason — this is the meaning. What is stated here is this: given that there is no distinction in proximity between <s>Ātman</s> (Self) and space and the like, since <s>Puruṣa</s> is endowed with the power of seeing, therefore he is connected as enjoyer with <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primordial Nature) which has entered into the relation of effect and cause, whereas space and the like are not [so connected] because they lack consciousness. Alternatively, the word <s>artha</s> means 'result.' Just as the act of eating is for the purpose of satisfaction and ceases when satisfaction is attained, and the act of going is for the purpose of reaching and [ceases] when reaching is attained, so the conjunction of <s>Puruṣa</s> with <s>Pradhāna</s> is for the purpose of seeing and ceases when seeing is attained. And thus it will be stated [later]: 'the one [says] "I have been seen" and is indifferent; the other [says] "I have seen her" and desists' (
so [it is] for the <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) of <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primordial Nature).

children.text:
kaivalyamiti vivekaparicchinnaṃ sattvādibhirasaṃsargadharmitvamātmanaḥ, so 'rtho 'sya so 'yaṃ kaivalyārthaḥ / satyapi hi darśanāviśeṣe pradhānaṃ puruṣasya kaivalyārthaṃ pravartate / yadāsya buddhistamaso 'ṅgitvādye guṇāḥ kāryarūpāpannāḥ śiraḥpāṇyādaya ādhyātmikā, bāhyāśca gavādayaḥ, kāraṇarūpāpannāścālocanakriyāsaṃkalpābhimānādhyavasāyalakṣaṇāḥ, so 'hamityaviśiṣṭapratyayopasaṃhāraṃ karoti tadā pravartata eva / yadā tvanye guṇāḥ prakṛtibhūtā vikārabhūtāḥ kāryabhūtāḥ kāraṇabhūtā acetanāḥ parārthā anyo 'haṃ na prakṛtirna vikṛtirna kāryaṃ na kāraṇaṃ nācetanaḥ svārtha iti bhinnapratyayopasaṃhāraṃ karoti tadā nivartate / so 'yaṃ puruṣasya dṛkchaktinimittaḥ pradhānasya ca kaivalyāvadhiparicchinnaḥ puruṣārthaḥ /
  satyapi pāribhāṣikatve
children.translated_text: <s>Kaivalya</s> (isolation) means the nature of being free from association with <s>sattva</s> and the other [<s>guṇas</s>] of the Self, as discriminated by discernment — that is its purpose, and this is <s>kaivalyārtha</s> (having isolation as its purpose). For even though there is no distinction in seeing, <s>Pradhāna</s> operates for the sake of the <s>kaivalya</s> of <s>Puruṣa</s>. When his <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), because <s>tamas</s> (darkness) predominates, makes an undifferentiated cognitive synthesis [thinking] 'I am that' — [conflating <s>Puruṣa</s>] with the <s>guṇas</s> that have assumed the form of effects, such as the head, hands, and other bodily [parts] which are <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self), and external [objects] such as cows and the like, and [the <s>guṇas</s>] that have assumed the form of causes, characterized as illumination, activity, conception, self-identification, and determination — then [<s>Pradhāna</s>] continues to operate. But when [<s>buddhi</s>] makes a differentiated cognitive synthesis [thinking]: 'the other <s>guṇas</s> are [in the state of] <s>prakṛti</s> (primal nature), modifications, effects, causes, non-conscious, and serving another's purpose; I am other — neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor modification, neither effect nor cause, not non-conscious, serving my own purpose' — then [<s>Pradhāna</s>] ceases. This purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is occasioned by the power of seeing of <s>Puruṣa</s> and is delimited by [the attainment of] <s>kaivalya</s> of <s>Pradhāna</s>. Even though [the conjunction] is figurative,
the conjunction of both is like [that of] a lame person and a blind person.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati / prāgapi kāryakāraṇasambandhātpuruṣe caitvanyamavasthitam / tadyathā agnerdahanaṃ paraśośchedanamasati dāhye chedye na vyajyate / tatsannidhānasamakālameva tu vyajyate / ityataḥ pradhānamapekṣate / tathā pradhānamapyantareṇa puruṣopakāraṃ svakādasarmarthamaniṣpannakāryasamaṃ cetitamanarthakama syādityataḥ puruṣamapekṣate / tatra ubhayoritaretarāpekṣā taṃ saṃyogamadhikārabandhamāhurācāryāḥ / paṅgvandhadṛṣṭāntastu nāntarīyakamātrapradarśanārtham / yathā paṅgurnāntareṇāndhaṃ dṛkchaktyā viśiṣṭenārthenārthavānbhavati andhaśca nāntareṇa paṅguṃ viśiṣṭenārthena, evaṃ pradhānaṃ nāntareṇa puruṣaṃ kṛtamapi kāryaṃ draṣṭuṃ śaktamanavadhikaṃ ca pravartamānaṃ viśeṣābhāvānnaiva nivartate / tathā puruṣaḥ satyapi cetanatve nāntareṇa pradhānamupalabhyābhāvādupalabdhā bhavediti pradhānamapekṣate / tasmāditaretarāpekṣayā saṃyogatve kalpyamāne yaduktaṃ
vinā sargeṇa bandho hi puruṣasya na yujyate /
children.translated_text: Without creation, the bondage of <s>Puruṣa</s> is indeed not possible;
creation is for the sake of his liberation alone — ah, the eloquence of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>!

What is stated here is this: even prior to the relation of effect and cause, consciousness is established in <s>Puruṣa</s>. Just as fire's burning and an axe's cutting are not manifested when there is nothing to be burned or cut, but are manifested simultaneously with the proximity of [those objects] — therefore [<s>Puruṣa</s>] requires <s>Pradhāna</s>. Likewise, <s>Pradhāna</s> too, without the assistance of <s>Puruṣa</s>, being incapable of its own function and equal to [something whose] effect has not been accomplished, and purposeless without being cognized — therefore it requires <s>Puruṣa</s>. Therein, the mutual dependence of both — that conjunction the teachers call the bond of [mutual] domain. The analogy of the lame and the blind is merely to illustrate the indispensability [of each to the other]. Just as the lame person without the blind person, who is distinguished by the power of sight, does not become purposeful, and the blind person without the lame person [who is distinguished by] a particular capacity [does not become purposeful] — so <s>Pradhāna</s>, without <s>Puruṣa</s>, even though it has accomplished its effect, is unable to see [the effect] and, continuing to operate without limit, never ceases due to the absence of a distinguishing [factor of cessation]. Likewise, <s>Puruṣa</s>, even though possessing consciousness, without <s>Pradhāna</s>, due to the absence of anything to apprehend, would not become an apprehender — therefore he requires <s>Pradhāna</s>. Therefore, when conjunction is conceived as consisting in mutual dependence, what was said —

children.text: iti tadayuktam / kasmāt ? na hyasau vinā sargeṇa na yujyata iti / āha ca

children.translated_text: The mutual dependence of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, consisting in the relation of the seen and the seer,
is called bondage by those who know the truth of the <s>śāstra</s> (doctrine).
— that is not proper. Why? Because it is not the case that [bondage] is not possible without creation. And it has been said:
Thus, even without creation, since the soul is bound by the <s>guṇas</s>,
therefore let the fancy of [that] fancy come to naught.
Thus conjunction is established.
From that [conjunction] arises creation. // <s>ISk</s> 21 //

children.text: pradhānapuruṣayorhi bhoktṛbhogyabhāvāpekṣanimitto 'yaṃ tattvasargo mahadādiḥ, bhāvasargaśca dharmādiḥ, bhūtasargaśca brāhmādiḥ pravartate / sā cāpekṣā puruṣānantyānna nivartata ityato 'rthavatīnāṃ hi prakṛtīnāṃ tadaparisamāpterna nivṛtirasti // 21 //
children.translated_text: For from the mutual dependence of <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primordial Nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> as enjoyer and enjoyed, this creation of principles — beginning with <s>Mahat</s> (the Great One) — proceeds, as well as the creation of dispositions beginning with <s>dharma</s> (virtue), and the creation of beings beginning with the <s>Brāhma</s> (pertaining to <s>Brahmā</s>). And that mutual dependence does not cease due to the infinitude of <s>Puruṣas</s>; therefore, for <s>Prakṛtis</s> (natures) that are purposeful, since that [purpose] is never fully accomplished, there is no cessation. // 21 //

children.text: // iti śrīyuktidīpikāyāṃ saptatipaddhatau pañcamamāhnikaṃ dvitīyaṃ ca prakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: // Thus ends the fifth lesson and the second section in the <s>Yuktidīpikā</s> following the Seventy [<s>Kārikās</s>]. //
<s>Kārikā</s> 22

children.text: evaṃ kāraṇāntarapratiṣedhātprakṛteḥ puruṣārtho 'yaṃ vyaktabhāvena vipariṇāma iti sthitam / tatredānīṃ vipratipattirācāryāṇām / kecidāhuḥ pradhānādanirdeśyasvarūpaṃ tattvāntaramutpadyate / tato mahāniti / patañjalipañcādhikaraṇavārṣagaṇānāṃ tu pradhānānmahānutpadyata iti / tadanyeṣāṃ purāṇetihāsapraṇetḥṇāṃ mahato 'haṃkāro vidyata iti pakṣaḥ- mahato 'smipratyayakartṛtvābhyupagamāt / ahaṃkārātpañca tanmātrāṇīti sarve / mahataḥ ṣaḍaviśeṣāḥ sṛjyante pañca tanmātrāṇyahaṃkāraśceti vindhyavāsimatam / tathā ahaṃkārādindriyāṇīti sarve / bhautikānīndriyāṇīti pañcādhikaraṇamatam / ekarūpāṇi tanmātrāṇītyanye / ekottarāṇīti vārṣagaṇyaḥ / indriyāṇi saṃskāraviśeṣayogātparigṛhītarūpāṇīti kecit / paricchinnaparimāṇānītyapare / vibhūnīti vindhyavāsimatam / adhikaraṇamapi kecittrayodaśavidhamāhuḥ / ekādaśakamiti vindhyavāsī / tathānyeṣāṃ mahati sarvārthopalbdhiḥ, manasi vindhyavāsinaḥ / saṃkalpābhimānādhyavasāyanānātvamanyeṣām, ekatvaṃ vindhyavāsinaḥ / tathā karaṇaṃ nirlikhitasvarūpaṃ śūnyagrāmanadīkalpam, prākṛtavaikṛtikāni tu jñānāni prerakāṅgasaṃgṛhītāni pradhānādāgacchanti ceti pañcādhikaraṇaḥ, na tu tathetyanye / kāraṇānāṃ mahatī svabhāvātivṛttiḥ pradhānāt, svalpā ca svata iti vārṣagaṇyaḥ / sarvā svata iti patañjaliḥ / sarvā parata iti pañcādhikaraṇaḥ / buddhiḥ kṣaṇiketi ca kālāntarāvasthāyinītyapare / evamanekaniścayeṣvācāryeṣu ye tāvatpradhānamahatorantarāle tattvāntaramicchanti tatpratikṣepāyācāryaḥ svamatamupanyasyati /
children.translated_text: Thus, since other causes have been refuted, it is established that this transformation of <s>prakṛti</s> (primal nature) into the form of the manifest is for the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>. Now regarding this there is disagreement among the teachers. Some say: from <s>pradhāna</s> an additional category of indescribable nature arises, and from that comes <s>mahat</s> (the great principle). But according to <s>Patañjali</s>, the <s>Pañcādhikaraṇa</s>s, and the <s>Vārṣagaṇa</s>s, <s>mahat</s> arises from <s>pradhāna</s>. For certain others — the authors of the <s>Purāṇa</s>s and <s>Itihāsa</s>s — the position is that <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) comes from <s>mahat</s>, because <s>mahat</s> is accepted as the agent of the 'I'-cognition. That from <s>ahaṅkāra</s> come the five <s>tanmātra</s>s (subtle elements) — all agree on this. That six non-specific [products] are created from <s>mahat</s> — five <s>tanmātra</s>s and <s>ahaṅkāra</s> — this is the view of <s>Vindhyavāsin</s>. Similarly, that the sense organs come from <s>ahaṅkāra</s> — all agree. That the sense organs are elemental — this is the view of the <s>Pañcādhikaraṇa</s>. That the <s>tanmātra</s>s are of uniform nature — some [say]. That they are successively increasing — the <s>Vārṣagaṇa</s>s [say]. That the sense organs have specific forms due to the conjunction with particular dispositions — some [say]. That they are of limited measure — others. That they are all-pervading — this is <s>Vindhyavāsin</s>'s view. Regarding the substrate, some say it is of thirteen kinds. <s>Vindhyavāsin</s> [says] it is eleven-fold. Likewise, for others the apprehension of all objects [resides] in <s>mahat</s>; for <s>Vindhyavāsin</s>, in <s>manas</s> (mind). Others [hold] that conceptualization, self-assertion, and determination are diverse; <s>Vindhyavāsin</s> [holds] they are one. Similarly, [according to] the <s>Pañcādhikaraṇa</s>, the instrument has a delineated essential nature, like an empty village or river; but the natural and modified cognitions, gathered together with the impelling component, come from <s>pradhāna</s> — but others disagree. The great transcendence of the nature of the causes comes from <s>pradhāna</s>, and a small [portion comes] from themselves — [says] the <s>Vārṣagaṇa</s>. All comes from themselves — [says] <s>Patañjali</s>. All comes from another — [says] the <s>Pañcādhikaraṇa</s>. And <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is momentary — [say some]; it persists over time — [say] others. Thus, among the teachers who hold diverse views, the master presents his own position for the purpose of refuting those who posit an additional category between <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>mahat</s>.
From <s>prakṛti</s> (primal nature) [comes] <s>mahat</s> (the great principle);

children.text:
prakṛtermahānutpadyate / mahānbuddhirmatirbrahmāpūrtiḥ khyātirīśvaro vikhara iti paryāyāḥ / sa tu deśamahattvātkālamahattvācca mahān / sarvotpādyebhyo mahāparimāṇayuktatvānmahān /
  anyasya tu pakṣe naivāhaṃkāro vidyata iti pratiṣedhavivakṣayedamāha /
children.translated_text: From <s>prakṛti</s>, <s>mahat</s> arises. <s>Mahat</s> has synonyms: <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>mati</s> (understanding), <s>brahma</s>, <s>āpūrti</s> (fulfillment), <s>khyāti</s> (discernment), <s>īśvara</s>, and <s>vikhara</s>. It is 'great' because of its greatness in spatial extent and temporal extent; it is 'great' because it possesses the greatest measure among all products. With the intention of denying [the view] that <s>ahaṅkāra</s> does not exist according to another position, he says:
From that [comes] <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (the ego-principle);

children.text:
tasmānmahato 'haṃkāra utpadyate /
  yaḥ punarāha, mahataḥ ṣaḍaviśeṣāḥ sṛjyante pañca tanmātrāṇyahaṃkāraśceti tannirāsārthamāha
children.translated_text: From that <s>mahat</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> arises. For the purpose of refuting the one who says that six non-specific [products] are created from <s>mahat</s> — five <s>tanmātra</s>s and <s>ahaṅkāra</s> — he says:
From that [comes] the group of sixteen.

children.text: tasmādahaṃkārātṣoḍaśako gaṇa utpadyate, pañca tanmātrāṇi ekādaśendriyāṇi ca / anenaiva ca bhautikendriyavādī pratikṣipto boddhavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: From that <s>ahaṅkāra</s> arises the group of sixteen: five <s>tanmātra</s>s (subtle elements) and eleven <s>indriya</s>s (sense organs). And by this, the proponent of elemental sense organs should be understood as refuted.
From those sixteen, from the five [<s>tanmātra</s>s, come] the five gross elements. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 22)

children.text: tasmādapi ṣoḍaśakādgaṇādyaḥ pañcako gaṇastataḥ pañca mahābhūtānyutpadyante / pūrvapadalopenātra mahābhūtānīti vaktavye bhūtānītyucyate / bhūtasaṃjñā hi tanmātrāṇāṃ na pṛthivyādīnāmatra tu sāṃkhyācāryāṇāmavipratipattiḥ bhūtakauṭasthyavādinastu mīmāṃsakā ārhatāśca / tatpratikṣepeṇedamucyata iti // 22 //
children.translated_text: From that group of sixteen, the group of five — from those, the five <s>mahābhūta</s>s (gross elements) arise. Here, by the elision of the first part [of the compound], where '<s>mahābhūta</s>s' should be said, '<s>bhūta</s>s' is said instead. For the designation '<s>bhūta</s>' belongs to the <s>tanmātra</s>s, not to earth and the rest — on this there is no disagreement among the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers. But the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>s and <s>Jaina</s>s advocate the immutability of the elements. This is stated in refutation of that.
<s>Kārikā</s> 23

children.text: āha, uktaṃ pradhānādbuddhirutpadyata iti / tatra vaktavyaṃ kiṃlakṣaṇā punarbuddhirityucyate
children.translated_text: One says: it has been stated that <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) arises from <s>pradhāna</s>. In that regard, it must be stated: what is the definition of <s>buddhi</s>? It is replied:
<s>Adhyavasāya</s> (ascertainment) is <s>buddhi</s> (intellect).

children.text:
ko 'yamadhyavasāyaḥ ? gaurevāyaṃ, puruṣa evāyamiti yaḥ pratyayo niścayo 'rthagrahaṇaṃ so 'dhyavasāyaḥ /
  atra kṣaṇikavādyāha yadyarthagrahaṇaṃ buddhiḥ, anityā / kasmāt ? hetvapekṣaṇāt / arthagrahaṇaṃ hīndriyādiviṣayasannidhānamāvaraṇādyabhāvaṃ cāpekṣate / na ca nityasya kāraṇāpekṣopapadyate / tasmādanityā buddhiḥ / abhivyakteradoṣa iti cetsyādetannendriyasannidhānādibhirarthagrahaṇaṃ janyate kiṃ tarhyabhivyajyata iti / tacca naivam / dvidhā doṣāt / sā hyabhivyaktiḥ svarūpalābho vā syāt grahaṇapratibandhavyudāso vā / kiṃ cātaḥ ? tadyadi tāvatsvarūpalābhaḥ kriyate 'rthagrahaṇamiti prāptam / arthagrahaṇapratibandhasyāndhakārasya vyudāsastadapyayuktam / vipratiṣedhāt / grahaṇaṃ ca syāttatpratibandhaśceti vipratiṣiddham / kiṃca bhedāt / vyaṅgyaṃ hi ghaṭādi candrārkauṣadhimaṇiratnapradīpabhedānna bhidyate / asti buddhīnāmarthabhedād bhedaḥ / vṛttibhedādadoṣo mṛdvaditi cet syānmatam , yathā mṛddravyasya ghaṭādisaṃsthānavṛttibhede 'pyabheda evaṃ buddheriti / tadapyayuktam / ananyatvāt / yadā buddhiranyā vṛttibhyaḥ, prāptastadbhede buddhibhedaḥ / kiṃca dṛṣṭāntāsiddheḥ / sādhyaṃ caitat kiṃ tadeva mṛddravyaṃ ghaṭādivṛttibhedamanubhavati āhosvitpratyayāntaravaśādanyaccānyaccotpadyate iti ? avayavabhedācca / upetya vānuvṛttiṃ brūmaḥ- na hi tadekaṃ mṛddravyam, kiṃ tarhi bahavo mṛtparamāṇavo 'nekadeśāvacchinnavṛttaya iti / kiṃ cānyat / nivṛttivibhaktigrahaṇāt / taddhi mṛddravyaṃ saṃsthānamapekṣyāpi gṛhyate, na tvarthagrahaṇamanapekṣya buddhergrahaṇamasti / tasmādviṣamo dṛṣṭāntaḥ / parimāṇādadoṣa iti cet syānmatam sattvādīnāmaṅgāṅgibhāvaniyamāttena tenārthagrahaṇātmanā vipariṇāmo vṛttiriti / etaccāyuktam / ubhayakalpane doṣaprasaṃgāt / yadi dharmāntaropādānaparityāgau vyaktavyaktī, dattottara eṣa pakṣaḥ / atha nāśotpādau tena dharmadharmiṇorananyatvāddharmāṇāṃ nāśotpādādbuddherapi nāśotpādaprasaṃgaḥ / tadanabhyupagame vānyatvamiti doṣaḥ / āha ca

children.translated_text: What has ceased and arisen [anew], being non-different, is impermanent — or else it is permanent;
but there is no permanence for [the collection of] things that have ceased and arisen, and for things that have not ceased, simultaneously.

What is this <s>adhyavasāya</s>? The cognition, the certainty, the grasping of an object [expressed as] 'this is indeed a cow' or 'this is indeed a person' — that is <s>adhyavasāya</s>. Here, the proponent of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikavādin</s>) says: if <s>buddhi</s> is the grasping of an object, it is impermanent. Why? Because it depends on causes. For the grasping of an object depends on the proximity of sense organs and their objects, and on the absence of obstructions and the like. And it is not tenable for something permanent to depend on causes. Therefore <s>buddhi</s> is impermanent. If one objects that there is no fault because of manifestation — one might say: it is not that the grasping of an object is produced by the proximity of sense organs and the like; rather, it is manifested. But this is not so, because of a twofold fault. For that manifestation would either be the attainment of its essential nature, or the removal of the obstruction to apprehension. What follows? If the attainment of its essential nature is effected, then we have arrived at [the position that] it is the grasping of an object [i.e., it is produced]. If it is the removal of the obstruction of darkness to the apprehension of the object, that too is unjustified, because of contradiction. For apprehension would exist and also its obstruction — this is contradictory. Moreover, because of differentiation. For what is to be manifested — such as a pot — is not differentiated by the differences of moon, sun, herb, gem, jewel, and lamp [that illumine it]. But there is differentiation in <s>buddhi</s>s due to the differentiation of objects. If one says there is no fault because of the differentiation of activity, as with clay — one might hold: just as, despite the differentiation of the activities [taking the form] of pot and the like, there is non-difference in the substance of clay — so too with <s>buddhi</s>. But this too is unjustified, because of non-difference [between buddhi and its activity]. When <s>buddhi</s> is different from its activities, then differentiation of <s>buddhi</s> is warranted when they are differentiated. Moreover, because the example is unestablished. For this is what needs to be proved: does that very same clay-substance undergo the differentiation of activities as pot and the like, or does something different and different arise due to a different cognition? And because of the differentiation of parts. Or, granting [your premise], we say there is persistence — but that is not a single clay-substance; rather, there are many clay-atoms with activities delimited by many locations. Moreover, because [clay] is grasped independently of the cessation of a particular [form]. For that clay-substance is grasped even independently of [any particular] configuration, but there is no grasping of <s>buddhi</s> independently of grasping an object. Therefore the example is dissimilar.

children.text:

children.translated_text: ). But this too does not refute [our position]. Why? Because of figurative usage. True, [activity and its possessor] are non-different, since no distinction between activity and its possessor is apprehended. Nevertheless, even when the operation has ceased — as in the case of an axe and the like — the essential nature of that which possesses activity does not cease. Therefore, figuratively positing a distinction, conventional usage proceeds regarding different effects. If one says that otherness too would follow from this — that is unjustified, because of invariability. Just as when an army, a row, a coil, or an earring configuration ceases, there is no cessation of its components, and there is differentiation of effects, yet there is no otherness — so too it would be with activity and its possessor. Therefore it is justified that because the dependence on causes pertains to activity [and not to <s>buddhi</s> itself], <s>buddhi</s> is not [momentarily] impermanent. By this, the alternative of manifestation has been addressed — that too pertains to activity, and therefore [we have also stated] 'because of differentiation due to the differentiation of sense organs and the like.' That too has been addressed by this very [argument]: differentiation of activity is not differentiation [of <s>buddhi</s> itself]. Moreover, because of inconclusiveness. Just as the differentiation of reflections from the differentiation of water and the like [does not entail that] what is to be manifested [i.e., the face] is not [itself manifested] — so too it would be elsewhere. If one says there is no fault because a different substance arises — one might hold that from the conjunction of water with the face, a different substance in the form of a reflection arises, but the face itself is not differentiated. But this is wrong. Why? Because it is untenable to posit both [face and water] as causes. For the face cannot be said to be the material cause, because it is distant; and [if it were the cause], there would be the consequence of perception even when the face is removed, as in the case of color produced by baking. As for what was said — 'there is no fault because of the differentiation of activity, as with clay' — let that be so. As for what was said about non-difference and the unestablished nature of the example — the non-difference of activity [and its possessor] has just now been addressed. And in the refutation of momentary destruction it was said: there is no arising of earth and the rest now in one way and now in another. As for the statement 'the clay-substance is not one' — cognition is the means of valid knowledge there. What is the object of a single cognition is one; if [you say] cognition of clay's multiplicity is experienced — [then show us] that [cognition]. As for the statement 'the essential nature of the clay-substance is ascertained independently of configuration, but the essential nature of <s>buddhi</s> is not grasped independently of grasping an object' —
Just as in the external and other states, the mind-continuum has modifications,
yet exists as a mere seed — so too let <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) be understood.

As for what was said — 'because of the fixed rule of the subsidiary-principal relation among <s>sattva</s> and the rest' — that is unjustified, precisely because impermanence is thereby established. Since things that are equal cannot have the relation of principal and subsidiary, [and] since the subsidiary-principal relation of <s>sattva</s> and the rest is accepted, increase and decrease must be accepted. And from that, it follows that <s>buddhi</s> is impermanent, because it is non-different from them. If one holds that it is permanent while remaining in that state — then it follows that <s>buddhi</s> is not constituted by <s>sattva</s> and the rest. And then there would be a contradiction with [the thesis that] there is non-discrimination between cause and effect. Therefore <s>buddhi</s> is impermanent. It is replied: as for what was said — '<s>buddhi</s> is impermanent because it depends on causes' — that is unjustified. Why? Because it proves what is already established. Who here has a dispute about whether <s>buddhi</s> is impermanent or permanent? Rather, by the statement 'the manifest is caused, impermanent,' this [impermanence] is already [accepted]. Therefore this [conclusion] is already encompassed by what is desired. If one says that momentariness follows from this very [reasoning] — one might further say: dependence on causes is indeed conditioned nature (<s>saṃskṛtatva</s>). And what is conditioned is momentary — like a lamp. Therefore, even though impermanence is [accepted], when no specific [type of impermanence] is stated, momentariness alone of <s>buddhi</s> is established by this reason. Why? Because there would be the consequence of contradicting what follows. For if this is so, then what is said subsequently for the purpose of establishing momentariness — 'because the grasping of each object is different, therefore impermanent' and so forth — would be purposeless. Therefore, since the earlier and later [statements] would be contradictory, this entire section would deserve neither study nor refutation. However, the [opponent's] preferred [concept of] <s>buddhi</s> is in this [context] — and without even considering the fault of irrelevant subsequent rebuttal, this [argument] is individually also unviable, because it pertains to activity. For the operation of <s>buddhi</s> — which is fully produced from its own cause — called 'grasping of an object,' which depends on the proximity of sense organs and the like, is not <s>buddhi</s> [itself]. If one says that the consequence is averted because of the non-difference [of activity and buddhi] — if one holds this, then because of the non-difference of activity and that which has the activity, even with this supposition, this consequence is not averted. And thus it is stated: 'The characteristic activity of each of the three [<s>guṇa</s>s]' (

yathā bāhyārthākāravaccittasantatiratha ca suptamūrchitavirodhasamāpannānāmartharūpādṛte bījamātrāstītyupagamyate sā citi kāpi vāvastheti vacanāt, na ca gṛhyate tathā buddhirapīti kasmānna parikalpyate ? yatpunaretaduktam yadi dharmāntaropādānaparityāgau vyaktavyaktī dattottara eṣa pakṣa iti / taditaratra tulyam / asmābhirapi tarhyasatkāryapratyākhyāne dattottara eṣa pakṣo vyaktitarna kriyate iti / nāśotpādau tu aniṣṭāveveti na parihāraṃ pratyādaraḥ kriyate / yadapyuktaṃ naṣṭādutpannāccānaṣṭamanutpannaṃ cānyannāstīti tadayuktam, anabhyupagamāt / nāśotpādau kaḥ pratijānīte yaṃ pratyetadarthavatsyāt ? kiṃ ca tvatpakṣaprāpteḥ / bhavata eva naṣṭotpannebhyaḥ skandhebhyo nānyā santatiratha ca nāsti doṣaḥ / kayāpi yuktayā syādetadanyaivāsāviti tataścaikā santatiriti hīnam / yadapyuktaṃ guṇavṛddhikṣaye 'nityatvamiti tadanupapannam / kasmāt ? rūpāntarāpyāyanāt / sattvaṃ hi prakarṣamanubhavadrajastamasī ca nyūnatāṃ dharmādirūpāṃ buddherāpyāyanti, nārthāntaraṃ kurvanti no khalvapyabhāvam, evaṃ rahastamo vā prakarṣamanubhavatsattvaṃ ca nyūnatādharmādirūpaṃ buddherāpyāyanti, nārthāntaraṃ kurvanti nābhāvam / evaṃ guṇavṛddhikṣaye 'pi rūpāntarāpyāyanānnāsti kṣayo buddheḥ / tatra yaduktaṃ hetvapekṣaṇādanityā buddhiriti etadayuktam /yatpunaretaduktaṃ pratyakṣagrahaṇānyatvātpratikṣaṇaṃ dīpāditailadhārāsu śabdabhedācca kṣaṇiketi, atra brūmaḥ- grahaṇānyatve coktaṃ vṛttibhedo na vṛttimadbhedaḥ / kiṃ cānyat / bhinnārthagrahaṇaikatvāt / upetya vā brūmaḥ- yadi pratyarthamanyadanyadgrahaṇaṃ kalpyate, vikalpabādhasamuccayasaṃśayadvitvātiśayanivāraṇeṣu, tathā kalmāṣaṃ śabalaṃ citramityanekārtharūpamekaṃ grahaṇaṃ na syāt / dṛṣṭaṃ tat / tasmānnāyaṃ kṣaṇikatve hetuḥ / evamavasthitamidaṃ- adhyavasāyo buddhirna kṣaṇiketi /
  buddhestu triguṇātmakatvāttasya guṇasya prakarṣe tattadrūpāntaramutpadyata iti /
  āha, kasya guṇasya prakarṣe buddheḥ kiṃ lakṣaṇaṃ rūpāntaramupajāyate ?

children.translated_text:
Just as the mental continuum (<s>cittasantati</s>) has the form of external objects, and yet for those who are asleep, unconscious, or in the attainment of cessation, it is accepted that only a seed [of consciousness] exists apart from the form of objects — and [the Buddhist] says 'it abides in some state of <s>citi</s> (awareness)' — and yet it is not apprehended; so too, why is <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) not postulated [similarly]? As for what was further said — 'if the acquisition and relinquishment of different properties are the manifest and unmanifest, this position has been answered' — this applies equally to the other side. For we too could say that in the refutation of <s>asatkārya</s> (non-pre-existence of the effect), 'this position has been answered' — yet the [refutation] is not rendered void. Destruction and production, however, are simply undesirable — hence no attention is paid to the objection. As for what was said — 'there is nothing other than the destroyed and the produced, nothing undestroyed and unproduced' — this is improper, because it is not accepted. Who maintains destruction and production, for whom this would be meaningful? Moreover, because your own position is reached: For you yourselves, there is no continuum apart from the destroyed and produced aggregates (<s>skandha</s>s) — and yet there is no defect. Through some reasoning, this [continuum] is said to be different [from the aggregates], and yet it is a single continuum — this is deficient.
  As for what was said — 'non-eternality from the increase and decrease of <s>guṇa</s>s' — this is untenable. Why? Because of the nourishment by a different form. For when <s>sattva</s>, experiencing predominance, and <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> [experiencing] diminution, nourish <s>buddhi</s> with the form of <s>dharma</s> and the like, they do not make it into something different, nor do they cause its non-existence. Likewise, when <s>rajas</s> or <s>tamas</s>, experiencing predominance, and <s>sattva</s> [experiencing] diminution, nourish <s>buddhi</s> with the form of <s>adharma</s> and the like, they do not make it into something different, nor cause its non-existence. Thus, even in the increase and decrease of <s>guṇa</s>s, because of the nourishment by a different form, there is no destruction of <s>buddhi</s>. Therefore, what was said — that <s>buddhi</s> is non-eternal because of dependence on a cause — this is improper.
  As for what was further said — that [<s>buddhi</s>] is momentary because of the difference of apprehension at each perception, as in the stream of oil in a lamp, and because of the difference of sounds — to this we say: Regarding the difference of apprehension, it was already stated that the difference is of the activity (<s>vṛtti</s>), not of the possessor of the activity (<s>vṛttimat</s>). Moreover, because of the unity of apprehension of diverse objects. Or we say, granting [your premise]: If a different apprehension is postulated for each object, then in cases of conceptual reversal, contradiction, conjunction, doubt, duality, and gradation, as well as [cognitions like] 'mottled,' 'variegated,' 'multicolored' — there would be no single apprehension having the form of multiple objects. But that [single apprehension] is observed. Therefore, this is not a reason for momentariness. Thus it is established: <s>buddhi</s> as determination is not momentary.
  But since <s>buddhi</s> is of the nature of the three <s>guṇa</s>s, when each <s>guṇa</s> predominates, a corresponding different form arises.
  [The objector] asks: When which <s>guṇa</s> predominates, what characteristic form arises in <s>buddhi</s>?
  It is replied:
