children.translated_text:
Detachment (<s>virāga</s>), however, is the clarity of <s>buddhi</s> that arises from the practice of knowledge and serves as the antidote to attachment (<s>rāga</s>). It has four states, characterized by effort (<s>yatamāna</s>), discrimination (<s>vyatireka</s>), single-sense mastery (<s>ekendriya</s>), and complete mastery (<s>vaśīkāra</s>). Of these, the effort and enthusiasm toward the ripening of the impurities (<s>kaṣāya</s>) characterized by the craving of the senses for objects is called '<s>yatamāna</s>' (the striving state). For the ascetic (<s>yati</s>) who is striving is established in this step. When the impurities of some senses have ripened, that is called '<s>vyatireka</s>' (the discriminating state). For then the ascetic's senses that have ripened are distinguished from those that have not yet ripened — that is the meaning. When all senses have fully ripened and the impurity remains only in the form of mere intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>), that is called '<s>ekendriya</s>' (the single-sense state). For the ascetic whose craving of all senses for objects has ceased, the one remaining sense — characterized as <s>manas</s> (mind) — then becomes fully ripened. The ripening even of [the impurity] remaining only as mere intention is called '<s>vaśīkāra</s>' (complete mastery). For this ascetic, whose craving for objects — [which was like] a mirage — has been uprooted at its very root of intention, is the master of the activity and cessation of the senses and the inner organ. Single-pointed, delighting in the One, having transcended the stage of ignorance, he becomes proximate to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
  Thus, having understood the four-staged step of detachment, the ascetic should strive for its practice. The means for this is what has been taught for the renunciation of objects both seen and heard of, combined with what will be stated in [the section on] contentments (<s>tuṣṭi</s>s) — making these one, progressively making each higher stage of reality (<s>tattvabhūmi</s>) the object of knowledge, one should remain equanimous in the preceding stage of reality.
  Mastery (<s>aiśvarya</s>) is characterized by non-obstruction, and it is eightfold: <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute), <s>mahimā</s> (becoming great), <s>laghimā</s> (becoming light), <s>garimā</s> (becoming heavy), <s>prāpti</s> (obtaining), <s>prākāmya</s> (irresistible will), <s>īśitva</s> (supremacy), <s>vaśitva</s> (subjugation), and <s>yatrakāmāvasāyitva</s> (fulfillment of desire). Of these, <s>aṇimā</s>, <s>mahimā</s>, <s>laghimā</s>, and <s>garimā</s> pertain to the elements. But <s>prāpti</s> and the rest pertain to <s>buddhi</s>. Thus, this is the fourfold <s>sāttvika</s> form of <s>mahat</s> (the great principle).
  [The objector] asks: What, then, is the form when another <s>guṇa</s> [predominates]?
  It is replied:

Here, by saying 'this form,' even though there is a distinction between <s>dharma</s> and the rest, the singular designation '<s>buddhi</s>' is used with the intention of non-differentiation. What is meant is this: when, having brought <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> under control, the <s>sattva</s> present in <s>buddhi</s> becomes predominant, then it has the form of <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>virāga</s> (detachment), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (mastery). Of these, <s>dharma</s> is said to be a <s>sattva</s>-constituent of the state of <s>buddhi</s>, accomplished in the disposition through the performance of actions prescribed by <s>śruti</s> (revelation) and <s>smṛti</s> (tradition). And it is of two kinds: the first is that which brings about the enjoyment of the desired body, senses, and objects in the stations of <s>Brahmā</s> and the like, and which serves as a limb of knowledge, etc.; the other is that which is accomplished through the performance of activities like the offering of the <s>agnihotra</s>, etc., and which is accomplished through <s>yama</s>s (restraints) and <s>niyama</s>s (observances). Of these, the five <s>yama</s>s are: non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), truthfulness (<s>satya</s>), non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), non-covetousness (<s>akalkatā</s>), and celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>). The five <s>niyama</s>s are: non-anger (<s>akrodha</s>), service of the teacher (<s>guruśuśrūṣā</s>), purity (<s>śauca</s>), moderation in food (<s>āhāralāghava</s>), and vigilance (<s>apramāda</s>). Through the unbroken performance of these, the <s>dharma</s> of <s>sattva</s> attains the state of disposition through effort in such excellent advancement, which serves to nourish the forms of knowledge and the rest. This is the first step, which serves as a staircase to both worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). When the ascetic is established here, he becomes fit for the practice of the remaining steps. Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is of two kinds: that characterized by the apprehension of sound and other [objects], and that characterized by the apprehension of the difference between the <s>guṇa</s>s and <s>Puruṣa</s>. Of these, that characterized by the apprehension of sound, etc. has the form of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and testimony (<s>āgama</s>). And that characterized by the apprehension of the difference between the <s>guṇa</s>s and <s>Puruṣa</s> is of two kinds: unprecedented and born of practice. Of the unprecedented kind: reflection (<s>ūha</s>), verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>), study (<s>adhyayana</s>) — and [the rest falls under] the section on attainments (<s>siddhi</s>).
The <s>tāmasika</s> (dark) [form] is the opposite of this. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 23 //

children.text: etat asmāddharmādeḥ sattvarūpādiviparyastaṃ tāmasaṃ tamaḥprakarṣopajanitamityarthaḥ / atra śāstracoditānuṣṭhānādāśayaniṣpannasattvāvayavo dharma ityuktam / śāstracoditasya nityasya ca karmaṇo 'nuṣṭhānād buddhyavasthastamo 'vayava āśayatāṃ pratipanno 'dharmaḥ / sa cāpi dvividhaḥ- aniṣṭaśarīrendriyaviṣayopabhoganirvartakaḥ, khyātivārakaśca / yathā ca jñānaṃ dvividhaṃ śabdādyupalabdhilakṣaṇaṃ guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhilakṣaṇaṃ caivamajñānamapi viparyayeṇa vācyam / yathā ca caturavasthaṃ vairāgyaṃ tathā yatamānādikaścaturavastho rāgaḥ yathā cāṣṭaguṇamaiśvaryamaṇimādi tathāṣṭaguṇamanaiśvaryamevametattāmasaṃ mahato rūpam / yaccaitadadharmādinimittabhūtamutkṛṣṭaṃ tamorūpaṃ tadrajasā sahāvirodhādekatāmivāpannamaśuddhirityācāryaiḥ paṭhyate / sattvarūpaṃ tu prakāśa iti / anayoścābhidhānādyaḥ pañcādhikaraṇapakṣaḥ prākṛtavaikṛtānāṃ jñānānāṃ pradhānavacchuṣkanadīsthānīyāntaḥkaraṇe bāhye ca prerakajñānāṃśakakṛta upanipātaḥ tathā sāttvikasthityātmakakṛtamapratyayasyāvasthānamiti tatpratikṣiptaṃ bhavati / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ ? yasmādaśuddhireva prakāśamalamatipravṛttaṃ nivartayituṃ prakarṣāpannānyābhūtā ca pravartayitum / ityevamaṣṭarūpā buddhirvyākhyātā // 23 //
children.translated_text: This means: the <s>tāmasika</s> [form], the opposite of this <s>dharma</s> and the rest — the <s>sāttvika</s> forms, etc. — is produced by the predominance of <s>tamas</s>. Here it was stated that <s>dharma</s> is a <s>sattva</s>-constituent of the state of <s>buddhi</s>, accomplished in the disposition through the performance of what is enjoined by scripture. [Correspondingly,] <s>adharma</s> (vice) is a <s>tamas</s>-constituent of the state of <s>buddhi</s>, attaining the state of disposition from the non-performance of obligatory actions and from performance of actions enjoined by scripture [i.e., prohibited acts]. And it too is of two kinds: that which brings about the enjoyment of undesired bodies, senses, and objects, and that which obstructs discriminative knowledge (<s>khyāti</s>). And just as knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is of two kinds — characterized by the apprehension of sound, etc. and by the apprehension of the difference between <s>guṇa</s>s and <s>Puruṣa</s> — so too ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) is to be stated conversely. And just as detachment (<s>vairāgya</s>) has four stages, so too attachment (<s>rāga</s>) has four stages beginning with <s>yatamāna</s> (the striving state). And just as mastery (<s>aiśvarya</s>) has eight qualities beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), so too powerlessness (<s>anaiśvarya</s>) has eight qualities. Thus, this is the <s>tāmasika</s> form of <s>mahat</s> (the great principle). And that predominant <s>tamas</s>-form which is the cause of <s>adharma</s> and the rest, having as it were become one with <s>rajas</s> due to their non-opposition, is called 'impurity' (<s>aśuddhi</s>) by the teachers. The <s>sattva</s>-form, however, is called 'illumination' (<s>prakāśa</s>). And by the statement of these two, the five-substrate theory — [namely, that] the impact of prompting cognitions upon the inner organ, which stands like a dry riverbed, and the external [cognitions] that are portions of natural and derivative cognitions, and the persistence of non-cognition due to the sustaining nature of <s>sattva</s> — is refuted. What is the reason? Because impurity alone has the power to arrest illumination when it is excessively active, and when predominant, to set non-cognition in motion. Thus <s>buddhi</s> with its eightfold form has been explained. // 23 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 24

children.text:
yastvasāvanantaramukto 'haṅkārastaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ /
  āha, yadyevaṃ tasmādidameva tāvaducyatāṃ kimasyāhaṅkārasya lakṣaṇamiti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
Now, the <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle) that was mentioned next after [<s>mahat</s>] — we shall explain it.
  [The objector] says: If so, then let this first be stated: What is the definition of this <s>ahaṃkāra</s>?
  It is replied:
<s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle) is self-conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>).

children.text:
kartuḥ svātmapratyavamarśātmako yo 'yamahamiti pratyaya utpadyate sa khalvahaṃkāraḥ, mahatastattvāntaram / kasmāt ? tasya sarvaviṣayādhyavasāyarūpatvāt, asya tu svātmapratyavamarśāt / na tvarthāntaram / kasmāt ? prakṛtivikārayorananyatvābhyupagamāt na hi naḥ prakṛterarthāntarabhūto vikāra iti prāgvistareṇa pratipāditam / sa ca mūrtipratyayābhyāṃ mahataḥ sthūlataraḥ / kasmāt ? avibhāgāt, vibhāganiṣpatteḥ kālādivat / triguṇasya ca mahato vikāratvādasāvapi triguṇaḥ / kasmāt ? prakṛtirūpasya vikāre dṛṣṭatvāt tantupaṭavat / tadbhāvasanniviṣṭāstu ye sattvādayasya ācāryairvaikārikataijasabhūtādiśabdenākhyāyante / tathā ca śāstramāha "etasmāddhi mahata ātmana ime traya ātmānaḥ sṛjyante vaikārikataijasabhūtādayo 'haṃkāralakṣaṇāḥ / ahamityevaiṣāṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ bhavati / guṇapravṛttau ca punarviśeṣalakṣaṇamiti" /
  āha, kā punarguṇapravṛttiryasyāmasmipratyayaikarūpasyāhaṅkārasya viśeṣapratipattirbhavatīti ?
  ucyate- yo 'yaṃ
children.translated_text:
That cognition which arises as 'I' — being of the nature of the agent's self-reflection (<s>svātmapratyavamarśa</s>) — that is <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, a category (<s>tattva</s>) different from <s>mahat</s> (the great principle). Why? Because [<s>mahat</s>] has the form of determination regarding all objects, while this [<s>ahaṃkāra</s>] is self-reflection. Yet it is not a completely different thing. Why? Because we accept the non-otherness of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and its transformation — for it has been extensively demonstrated earlier that a transformation is not something entirely different from its source. And it is grosser than <s>mahat</s> in both form and cognition. Why? Because of non-differentiation [becoming] differentiation — just as time and the like. And since it is a transformation of the three-<s>guṇa</s>-possessing <s>mahat</s>, it too possesses the three <s>guṇa</s>s. Why? Because the nature of the source is seen in the transformation — like thread and cloth. And the <s>sattva</s> and the other [<s>guṇa</s>s] that are situated in its states are designated by the teachers with the terms <s>vaikārika</s> (modified), <s>taijasa</s> (luminous), and <s>bhūtādi</s> (elemental). And thus the scripture says: 'From this great self, these three selves are created — the <s>vaikārika</s>, <s>taijasa</s>, and <s>bhūtādi</s>, characterized as <s>ahaṃkāra</s>. Their common characteristic is the [notion] "I." And in the activity of the <s>guṇa</s>s, there is a specific characteristic.'
  [The objector] asks: What, then, is the activity of the <s>guṇa</s>s in which the specific characteristic of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> — which has a single form as the 'I'-cognition — is apprehended?
  It is replied: That which —
Therefore, a twofold creation proceeds from it.

children.text:
dvividha indriyalakṣanastanmātralakṣaṇaśca / sā guṇavṛttirityucyate / kasmāt ? tatkāryatvāt / guṇapravṛttikāryo hi sargaḥ / dṛśyate ca khalu loke kāryakāraṇamupacaryamāṇam / tadyathā śālīnbhuṅkta iti /
  āha, prāguktamahaṃkārātṣoḍaśako gaṇa utpadyate / idānīṃ punarucyate tasmāddvividhaḥ pravartate sargaḥ / tadidaṃ pūrvottaravyāghātādayuktamiti /
  ucyate- na, sāmānyena vivakṣitatvāt /
  abhedavivakṣāyāṃ hi kṛtvā kāryakāraṇalakṣaṇamevamasmābhirupadiṣṭaṃ dvividhaḥ sarga iti / bhedavivakṣāyāṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text:
[It is] twofold: characterized by the senses (<s>indriya</s>) and characterized by the subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>). This is called the activity of the <s>guṇa</s>s. Why? Because it is the effect of that [activity]. For creation is the effect of the activity of the <s>guṇa</s>s. And indeed, it is observed in the world that the effect is figuratively identified with its cause. For example, 'he eats rice' [where 'rice' refers to cooked food, not the plant].
  [The objector] says: Previously it was said that a group of sixteen arises from <s>ahaṃkāra</s>. Now again it is said: 'from it, a twofold creation proceeds.' This is improper because of the contradiction between the earlier and later [statements].
  It is replied: No, because [the latter] is intended in a general sense.
  For, having intended non-differentiation, the cause-effect relationship has been taught by us thus: 'the creation is twofold.' But when differentiation is intended,
[The creation is] of the senses, [which is] elevenfold, and of the subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>), which is fivefold. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 24 //

children.text:
indriyāṇāmayamaindriyaḥ ekādaśa parimāṇamasya ekādaśakaḥ / evaṃ tanmātreṣu vaktavyam / tanmātrāṇāṃ śabdasparśādīnāmayaṃ tānmātraḥ sargaḥ / pañcakaśca pañca parimāṇamasyeti pañcakaḥ / asya tu ṣoḍaśakasya vikārasya saṃjñālakṣaṇaprayojanānyuttaratra vakṣyati / eṣā guṇapravṛttirvyākhyātā / yasyāmasmipratyayasya viśeṣagrahaṇaṃ bhavati- śabde 'haṃ sparśe 'haṃ rūpe 'haṃ rase 'haṃ gandhe 'hamiti /
  āha, ahaṅkāre sattvādīnāṃ saṃjñāntarāvacanam, ānarthakyāt / yadidamahaṃkāre sattvādīnāṃ saṃjñāntaramārabhyate vaikārikastaijaso bhūtādiriti, tanna vaktavyam / kasmāt ? ānarthakyāt / na hi tattvāntarasanniveśināṃ sattvādīnāṃ saṃjñāntarābhidhāne kiṃcitprayojanamastīti, saṃjñābhūyastvāt / athāyaṃ nirbandhastattvāntaram, saṃjñābhūyastvaṃ prāpnoti / prayojanābhidhānaṃ vā / viśiṣṭayatnānāmanākasmikatvāt / athavā prayojanaṃ vaktavyam- evamarthamahaṅkāre saṃjñāntarābhidhānamiti / kasmāt ? na hi viśiṣṭayatnānāmākasmikatvamupapadyata iti /
  ucyate- na, kāryaviśeṣahetutvāt / mahadādilakṣaṇānāṃ hi guṇānāmanekarūpastattvārambha iti hi na saṃjñāntaramārabhyate / ahaṃkārastu sattvatamobahulayorindriyatanmātraparvaṇoḥ prakṛtiḥ tadarthamācāryāṇāṃ yatnaviśeṣaḥ / dharmādiviśeṣābhyupāmānmahati prasaṃga iti cet na viśeṣitatvāt / tattvāntarārambha iti viśeṣitam, na tu dharmādayastattvāntaramato na mahati prasaṃgaḥ / viśeṣānabhidhānādayuktamiti cet syādetat, kaḥ punaratra viśeṣo yena dharmādi na tattvāntaram, tattvāntaraṃ tu śrotrādīti ? etacca naivam kutaḥ ? vṛttimātre tadupacārāt / vṛttimātre hi mahato dharmādyupacāraḥ / tathā ca tantrāntare 'pyuktam "prakāśavṛttirdharma" iti / vṛttiniṣpāditastu saṃsthānaviśeṣo vṛttimatastattvāntaramityanayorviśeṣaḥ / tasmādyuktametat kāryaviśeṣahetutvamiti // 24 //
children.translated_text:
This creation pertaining to the <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties) is the <s>aindriya</s> (sense-related); eleven is its measure, hence it is 'the group of eleven.' The same should be stated regarding the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). The creation pertaining to the <s>tanmātras</s> — sound, touch, and the like — is the <s>tānmātra</s> (subtle-element-related); and it is 'the group of five' since five is its measure. The names, characteristics, and purposes of this sixteen-fold modification will be stated later. This operation of the <s>guṇas</s> has been explained — in which the specific apprehension of the 'I'-notion occurs: 'I am in sound, I am in touch, I am in form, I am in taste, I am in smell.'
  [Objection:] The alternative names for <s>sattva</s> and the others in <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) are unnecessary, because they are purposeless. The alternative names that are introduced for <s>sattva</s> and the others in <s>ahaṃkāra</s> — <s>vaikārika</s>, <s>taijasa</s>, <s>bhūtādi</s> — should not be stated. Why? Because they are purposeless. For there is no purpose in stating alternative names for <s>sattva</s> and the others that are situated in another principle — since there would be a proliferation of names. If the insistence is that [each is] a different principle, then a proliferation of names follows. Or [one could say:] the purpose should be stated — for distinguished efforts are not without cause. Or rather, the purpose should be stated as follows: 'It is for this purpose that alternative names are stated for <s>ahaṃkāra</s>.' Why? For it is not possible that distinguished efforts are without cause.
  [Reply:] No, because [the names serve as] the cause of specific effects. For the <s>guṇas</s> characterized as <s>mahat</s> and the like, since the origination of principles is manifold, no alternative names are introduced. But <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is the source of the two stages — that of the <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties), which are <s>sattva</s>-predominant, and that of the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), which are <s>tamas</s>-predominant — and for that purpose, the teachers make a special effort. If it is objected that the same consequence would follow for <s>mahat</s>, since [it too has] specific [modifications such as] <s>dharma</s> and the like — no, because of the qualification. It is qualified as 'origination of a different principle'; but <s>dharma</s> and the like are not different principles, therefore the consequence does not apply to <s>mahat</s>. If it is said that this is untenable because the specific difference is not stated — [that is,] what is the specific difference by which <s>dharma</s> and the like are not different principles, but the ear and the like are? — that is not so. Why? Because the designation [of <s>dharma</s> etc.] applies only to a function. For <s>dharma</s> and the like are merely attributed to <s>mahat</s> as functions. As stated in other systems too: '<s>Dharma</s> is the function of illumination.' But a specific configuration produced by a function, [being distinct] from the possessor of the function, is a different principle — this is the distinction between them. Therefore it is proper that [the names serve as] the cause of specific effects. // 24 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 25

children.text:
āha, yadyevamidaṃ tarhi vaktavyamuṣya kāryaviśeṣasyaivaṃ saṃjñakādahaṃkārātpravṛttiriti /
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] If so, then it should be stated that this specific effect proceeds from the <s>ahaṃkāra</s> having such-and-such a name.
  [Reply:]
The <s>sāttvika</s> (sattva-predominant) group of eleven proceeds from the <s>vaikṛta</s> (modified) <s>ahaṃkāra</s>;

children.text:
sarga ityanuvartate / ekādaśendriyāṇi sattvabahulāni vaikṛtādahaṃkārātpravartante niṣpadyanta ityarthaḥ / ekādaśābhidhānādeva cendriyapratītiḥ, pūrvasūtre tatsāmānādhikaraṇyāt / ato na punarindriyagrahaṇam /
  āha, tanmātrasargaḥ punaḥ kiṃguṇaḥ, kasmāccāhaṅkārātpravartate iti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
'Creation' carries over [from the previous verse]. The eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties), being <s>sattva</s>-predominant, proceed from — that is, are produced from — the <s>vaikṛta</s> (modified) <s>ahaṃkāra</s>. Since the mention of 'eleven' already conveys the understanding of <s>indriyas</s>, through the co-reference with the previous <s>sūtra</s>, therefore there is no need to mention '<s>indriyas</s>' again.
  [Objection:] What quality characterizes the creation of the <s>tanmātras</s>, and why does it proceed from <s>ahaṃkāra</s>?
  [Reply:]
The <s>tānmātra</s> (subtle-element-related) creation from <s>bhūtādi</s> — that is <s>tāmasa</s> (tamas-predominant);

children.text:
bhūtāderbhūtādisaṃjñakāttamaḥpradhānāttānmātraḥ sargaḥ / tānmātrastu tamobahulo bhūtādisaṃjñakādahaṅkārātpravartate / tatra punastanmātragrahaṇātsaṃkhyā śasyata iti nocyate /
  āha, prakṛtiviśeṣanirdeśānarthakyam / prāguktaṃ sattvādīnāmahaṅkārāvasthitānāṃ vaikārikādyāḥ saṃjñā ucyante / tadyadi sattvaṃ vaikārikaśabdenocyate vaikārikāṇi caindriya ekādaśakaḥ sargaḥ pravartata ityukte gamyata etat sāttviko 'sau, bhūtādestānmātra ityukte gamyata etat tāmasa iti / kasmāt ? na hyasti sambhavo yatsattvāttamobahulaḥ sargaḥ syāttamasaśca sattvabahula iti /
  ucyate- na, aprasiddhatvajñāpanāt / yasyaivārthasya jñāpanārthamevamiha kriyate, kathaṃ gamyate sattvaṃ vaikārikaśabdenocyate, tamo bhūtādiśabdena, rajastaijasaśabdena ? aprasiddhārthā hi tāntrikī paribhāṣeyamanirṇītā na gamyata iti /
  āha, taijasasaṃjñānarthakyamiti /
  ucyate na,
children.translated_text:
The <s>tānmātra</s> creation proceeds from the <s>bhūtādi</s> — the one designated as <s>bhūtādi</s>, which is <s>tamas</s>-predominant — that is, the <s>tānmātra</s> creation, being <s>tamas</s>-predominant, proceeds from the <s>ahaṃkāra</s> designated as <s>bhūtādi</s>. And the number [five] is not stated again there because of the mention of <s>tanmātra</s> [carrying over].
  [Objection:] The specification of the particular source is purposeless. It was previously stated that alternative names are given for <s>sattva</s> and the others in the state of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> — <s>vaikārika</s> and so forth. If <s>sattva</s> is denoted by the word <s>vaikārika</s>, then when it is said 'the <s>aindriya</s> group of eleven proceeds from <s>vaikārika</s>,' it is already understood that it is <s>sāttvika</s>; and when it is said 'the <s>tānmātra</s> from <s>bhūtādi</s>,' it is already understood that it is <s>tāmasa</s>. Why? For it is not possible that a <s>tamas</s>-predominant creation would arise from <s>sattva</s>, or a <s>sattva</s>-predominant one from <s>tamas</s>.
  [Reply:] No, because it makes known what is not well-known. For the very meaning that is intended to be conveyed is done so here — how is it already understood that <s>sattva</s> is denoted by the word <s>vaikārika</s>, <s>tamas</s> by the word <s>bhūtādi</s>, and <s>rajas</s> by the word <s>taijasa</s>? For this technical terminology, whose meaning is not well-established, has not been settled and is not understood.
  [Objection:] The name <s>taijasa</s> is also purposeless.
  [Reply:] No,
both [proceed] from <s>taijasa</s>. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 25 //

children.text: ubhayatra tatsāmarthyāt / syādetadevaṃ yadyasya kāryasāmarthyameva na syāt / asmāttu taijasādubhayamapyetattanmātrendriyasaṃjñakaṃ pravartata ityanuvartate / katham ? yadā hi vaikāriko 'haṅkāra indriyabhāvena pravartate tadā niṣkriyatvāttaijasaṃ pravartakatvenākāṃkṣati, bhūtādi bhedakatvena / kasmāt ? tenaiva tadbhedāt / tadyathāgnināgnau prakṣipto 'gnireva bhavati, āpo vāpsu prakṣiptā āpa eva bhavanti, evaṃ sattvameva sattve tu bhedaṃ janayati guṇāntarasaṃsargamapekṣate / bhūtādilakṣaṇasya tu tamasaḥ saṃsargād bhidyamānaṃ taijasena ca rajasā kriyātmakenānugṛhītamekādaśendriyabhāvamapekṣate / tathā bhūtādilakṣaṇaṃ tamo 'haṅkārāttanmātrabhāvena pravartamānaṃ pravṛttyarthaṃ taijasamākāṃkṣati, vaikārikaṃ bhedatvena / kasmāt ? tenaiva tasya bhedāditi yojyam / śāsraṃ caivamāha- "tadetasminvaikārike strakṣyamāṇa eṣa bhūtādistaijasenopaṣṭabdha evaṃ vaikārikamabhidhāvati / tathaiva tasminbhūtādau srakṣyamāṇe eṣa bhūtādistaijasenoṣṭabdha etaṃ bhūtādimabhibhavati /" ityanena nyāyena taijasādubhayaniṣpattiriti vyākhyāto 'haṅkāraḥ // 25 //
children.translated_text: Because of its capacity in both [cases]. This would be so if it had no capacity for producing effects. But from this <s>taijasa</s>, both — designated as <s>tanmātras</s> and <s>indriyas</s> — proceed; 'creation' carries over. How? For when the <s>vaikārika</s> (modified) <s>ahaṃkāra</s> proceeds in the form of <s>indriyas</s>, being inactive [on its own], it requires the <s>taijasa</s> as the activator, and the <s>bhūtādi</s> as the differentiator. Why? Because differentiation of that [<s>sattva</s>] occurs precisely through that [<s>tamas</s>]. Just as fire thrown into fire becomes fire itself, and water poured into water becomes water itself, so too <s>sattva</s> [by itself] in <s>sattva</s> would produce [only sameness] — but to produce differentiation, it requires the conjunction of another <s>guṇa</s>. When [<s>sattva</s>] is differentiated through conjunction with <s>tamas</s> characterized as <s>bhūtādi</s>, and supported by the <s>taijasa</s> <s>rajas</s> whose nature is activity, it assumes the form of the eleven <s>indriyas</s>. Likewise, <s>tamas</s> characterized as <s>bhūtādi</s>, proceeding from <s>ahaṃkāra</s> in the form of <s>tanmātras</s>, requires the <s>taijasa</s> for the purpose of activity, and the <s>vaikārika</s> for differentiation. Why? Because differentiation of that [<s>tamas</s>] occurs precisely through that [<s>sattva</s>] — this should be connected. And the scripture says thus: 'When this <s>vaikārika</s> is about to create, this <s>bhūtādi</s>, supported by the <s>taijasa</s>, approaches the <s>vaikārika</s>. Likewise, when this <s>bhūtādi</s> is about to create, this <s>bhūtādi</s>, supported by the <s>taijasa</s>, overpowers this <s>bhūtādi</s>.' By this reasoning, the production of both from the <s>taijasa</s> is explained — thus <s>ahaṃkāra</s> has been explained. // 25 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 26

children.text:
āha, prāgapadiṣṭa aindriya ekādaśakaḥ pravartate vaikṛtādahaṃkārāditi, tatsāmānyābhidhānānna pratipadyāmahe / tasmādvaktavyaṃ kānīndriyāṇi bhavato 'bhipretāni ?
  ucyate- dvividhānīndriyāṇi, buddhīndriyāṇi, karmendriyāṇi ca / tatra
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] It was previously stated that 'the <s>aindriya</s> group of eleven proceeds from the <s>vaikṛta</s> <s>ahaṃkāra</s>' — but since that was stated only in general terms, we do not understand it. Therefore it should be stated: what <s>indriyas</s> are intended by you?
  [Reply:] The <s>indriyas</s> are of two kinds: <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (cognitive sense faculties) and <s>karmendriyas</s> (action faculties). Among these:
The <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (cognitive sense faculties) are called ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose.

children.text:
karṇau tvakcakṣuṣī ca rasanaṃ ca nāsikā ca karṇatvakcakṣūrasananāsikāḥ / ākhyānamākhyā pratyāyanamityarthaḥ / etaiḥ śabdairākhyā yeṣāṃ tānīmāni karṇatvakcakṣūrasananāsikākhyāni / adhiṣṭhānabhedāddvivacanena vigrahaḥ kriyate / etāni buddhīndriyāṇi pratyavagantavyāni / buddherindriyāṇi buddhīndriyāṇi /
  kiṃ punaretāni buddheriti ?
  ucyate- śabdādiviṣayapratipattau dvāram / kasmāt ? abahirvṛttitvāt / antaḥkaraṇasya nāsti bahirvṛttirityato nālametatsākṣācchabdādīnarthānpratipattum / tasmācchrotrādilakṣaṇaṃ sākṣād bāhyaviṣayaprakāśanasamarthaṃ kāraṇāntaramapekṣate / tatpraṇālikayā tasya viṣayagrahaṇam / tasmādyuktamuktaṃ buddherbāhyaviṣayapratipattau dvārabhūtatvādbuddhīndriyāṇīti /
  āha, karmendriyāṇi punaḥ kānīti ?
children.translated_text:
The ears, skin, eyes, tongue, and nose are [collectively called] 'ear-skin-eye-tongue-nose.' '<s>Ākhyā</s>' means name, that is, designation. Those whose names are by these words — these are called 'named as ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose.' The compound is analyzed with dual number due to the difference of substrata. These should be understood as <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (cognitive sense faculties). They are 'faculties of <s>buddhi</s>' (cognition), hence <s>buddhīndriyas</s>.
  What, then, [is their relation] to <s>buddhi</s>?
  [Reply:] They are the doors for the apprehension of objects such as sound and the like. Why? Because [<s>buddhi</s>] does not have external operation. Since the internal organ does not have external operation, it is unable to directly apprehend objects such as sound and the like. Therefore, it requires another instrument — characterized as the ear and the like — that is capable of directly illuminating external objects. Through the channel of those [sense faculties], [<s>buddhi</s>] grasps the objects. Therefore it is proper to say that they are <s>buddhīndriyas</s>, since they serve as doors for <s>buddhi</s>'s apprehension of external objects.
  [Objection:] What, then, are the <s>karmendriyas</s> (action faculties)?
Voice, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are said to be the <s>karmendriyas</s> (action faculties). // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 26 //

children.text:
vākca pāṇī ca pādau pāyuścopasthaśca vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthāḥ / etāni karmendriyāṇyāhurācakṣate / karmārthānīndriyāṇi karmendriyāṇi / kiṃ punaḥ karma ? vacanādi vakṣyamāṇam / etadvikurvat iti karmendriyāṇi /
  āha, kathametadupalabhyate adhiṣṭhānādarthāntarabhūtānīndriyāṇi, na punaradhiṣṭhānamātramiti ?
  ucyate- adhiṣṭhānādindriyapṛthaktvam, śaktiviśeṣopalambhāt / yathā śarīrāsambhavino viṣayavyavasāyalakṣaṇasya śaktiviśeṣasyopalambhādarthāntaraṃ buddhiranumīyate, evamadhiṣṭhānāsambhavino viṣayagrahaṇalakṣaṇasya śaktiviśeṣasyopalambhādarthāntaramindriyamiti /
  āha, na, asambhavāsiddheḥ / adhiṣṭhānamātrasya viṣayagrahaṇaṃ na sambhavati, arthāntarasya ca sambhavati ityetadubhayamapi cāprasiddhamiti /
  ucyate- naitadaprasiddham / tulyajātīyeṣu tadanupapatteḥ / yasmād bhautikeṣvanyeṣu ghaṭādiṣu viṣayagrahaṇasāmarthyāsambhavaḥ āhaṃkāravikāravattatsāmarthyāpratiṣedhānnendriyāṇāṃ nastatpratiṣedho 'numātavya iti / etaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? śaktibhedāpatteḥ / vaikārikaṃ sattvamāhaṅkārikaṃ prakāśarūpaṃ, tacchaktiviśeṣādindriyāṇi utpadyante / bhūtādilakṣaṇasya tamasaḥ sāmarthyāt tanmātrāṇi parasya, pṛthivyādīnāmekarūpatvāt / tasmādayamasamaḥ samādhiriti / etena bhautikatvaṃ pratyuktam /
  āha, kathamavagamyate bahūnīndriyāṇi, na punarekamevendriyaṃ manovatsarvārthamanekādhiṣṭhānaṃ syāditi ?
  ucyate- na, yugapatpravṛttyapravṛttiprasaṃgāt / yadyekamevendriyaṃ manovatsarvārthamanekādhiṣṭhānaṃ syādekaviṣayapratipattau vā sarvaviṣayapratipattiḥ / dṛṣṭastu grahaṇabhedastasmānnaikamindriyamiti / bhautikairanugrahopaghātadarśanādindriyāṇāṃ bhautikatvamiti cet syānmatam, iha bhautikānāṃ ghaṭādīnāṃ bhautikairmṛddaṇḍacakrasūtrodakamudgarādibhiranugrahopaghāto dṛṣṭaḥ / yadi ca bhautikānīndriyāṇi na syuḥ naiṣāṃ bhautikairañjanādibhiranugrahaḥ kriyate, upaghātaśca rajaḥprabhṛtibhiriti / etaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? anekāntāt / tadyathā bhautikairvadanādibhirantaḥkaraṇasya grahaṇadhāraṇasmṛtilakṣaṇo 'nugrahaḥ kriyate, upaghātaścopalādibhiḥ / na cāsya bhautikatvam / evamindriyasyāpi syāt / vaiśeṣikaguṇavyañjakatvādvikārapratītiriti cet atha matam- pṛthivyādivaiśeṣiko gandho ghrāṇenābhivyajyate / audako rase rasanena ca / āgneyaṃ rūpaṃ vīkṣaṇena / vāyavīyaḥ sparśastvacā /ākāśīyaḥ śabdaḥ śrotreṇa / yena ca yasya vaiśeṣikaguṇābhivyaktistasya tadvikāratvaṃ dṛṣṭam / tadyathā pradīpasya rūpābhivyañjakatve sati taijasatvamiti / etaccānupapannam / kasmāt ? aniṣṭaprasaṃgāt / vaiśeṣikaguṇavyañjakānāṃ tadvikāramicchataḥ prāptamapāṃ gandhābhivyaktihetutvāt pārthivattvam / athaitadaniṣṭaṃ, na tarhyaikāntiko heturiti / tatra yaduktaṃ vaiśeṣikaguṇābhivyañjakatvād bhautikānīndriyāṇīti etadayuktam // 26 //
children.translated_text:
Voice, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are [collectively called] 'voice-hands-feet-anus-genitals.' These are said to be — that is, declared to be — <s>karmendriyas</s> (action faculties). Faculties whose purpose is action are <s>karmendriyas</s>. What, then, is action? Speaking and the like, which will be stated later. They are <s>karmendriyas</s> because they transform this [action].
  [Objection:] How is it known that the <s>indriyas</s> are something different from the substrata [i.e., the physical organs], and not merely the substrata themselves?
  [Reply:] The <s>indriyas</s> are distinct from the substrata, because of the observation of a specific capacity. Just as <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is inferred as something different [from the body] because of the observation of a specific capacity — namely, the determination of objects, which cannot belong to the body — so too the <s>indriya</s> is [inferred as] something different because of the observation of a specific capacity — namely, the grasping of objects, which cannot belong to the substratum.
  [Objection:] No, because the impossibility is not established. That the substratum alone cannot grasp objects, and that something different can — both of these are not established.
  [Reply:] That is not unestablished — because of the impossibility [of grasping] in things of the same class. Since other material things such as pots and the like do not have the capacity to grasp objects, but since the capacity is not denied for <s>indriyas</s>, being modifications of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> — therefore their denial of that capacity should not be inferred. This too is untenable. Why? Because of the occurrence of a difference in capacity. <s>Sattva</s> pertaining to <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, being of the <s>vaikārika</s> (modified) kind, has the nature of illumination — from its specific capacity, the <s>indriyas</s> are produced. From the capacity of <s>tamas</s> characterized as <s>bhūtādi</s>, the <s>tanmātras</s> [are produced]; but earth and the like have a uniform nature [without such specific capacity]. Therefore this is an unequal comparison. By this, the [theory of the <s>indriyas</s> being] material is refuted.
  [Objection:] How is it known that there are many <s>indriyas</s>, and not just a single <s>indriya</s> that, like the mind, grasps all objects and has multiple substrata?
  [Reply:] No, because there would be the consequence of simultaneous operation and non-operation. If there were a single <s>indriya</s> that, like the mind, grasps all objects and has multiple substrata, then upon apprehending one object, all objects would be apprehended. But differentiated grasping is observed — therefore there is not a single <s>indriya</s>. If it is thought that the <s>indriyas</s> are material because of the observation of benefit and harm by material things — [the argument being that] here, the benefit and harm of material things like pots and the like by material things like clay, sticks, wheels, threads, water, hammers, and so forth is observed; and if the <s>indriyas</s> were not material, then benefit would not be done to them by material things like collyrium, nor harm by dust and the like — this too is untenable. Why? Because it is inconclusive. For example, the internal organ, though not material, receives benefit through material things like the face and the like — namely, grasping, retention, and memory — and harm through stones and the like. Yet it is not material. So too it could be for the <s>indriyas</s>. If it is thought that materiality is inferred because [the <s>indriyas</s>] manifest the specific qualities [of each element] — [the argument being that] the specific quality of earth, smell, is manifested by the nose; the specific quality of water, taste, by the tongue; the specific quality of fire, form, by the eyes; the specific quality of air, touch, by the skin; the specific quality of space, sound, by the ear — and whatever manifests the specific quality of something is observed to be a modification of that, just as the lamp, by manifesting form, is known to be fiery — this too is untenable. Why? Because of an undesired consequence. For one who holds that whatever manifests a specific quality is a modification of that — since water is a cause of manifesting smell, it would follow that water is earthy. If that is undesired, then the reason is not invariable. Therefore, what was stated — that the <s>indriyas</s> are material because they manifest specific qualities — that is untenable. // 26 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 27

children.text:
āha, ekādaśendriyāṇi ahaṅkārādutpadyanta iti prāgapadiṣṭam / idānīṃ buddhīndriyakarmendriyāṇi daśāpadiśyante / tadidaṃ padārthanyūnamiti /
  ucyate- syādetadevam, yadyetāvadindriyaparva syāt / kiṃ tarhīti-
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] It was previously stated that eleven <s>indriyas</s> are produced from <s>ahaṃkāra</s>. Now, ten — five <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (cognitive sense faculties) and five <s>karmendriyas</s> (action faculties) — are enumerated. This is one category short.
  [Reply:] This would be so if the <s>indriya</s> group consisted of only this many. What then?
Here, the mind (<s>manas</s>) is the deliberative [faculty];

children.text:
atrendriyaparvaṇi mano bhavadbhiḥ pratyavagantavyam / tatra saṃkalpakamiti lakṣaṇamācakṣmahe / saṃkalpo 'bhilāṣa icchātṛṣṇetyādyanarthāntaram / saṃkalpayatīti saṃkalpakam / etanmanaso lakṣaṇam /
  tasmādasya pratyakṣato 'nupalabhyamānasyāstitvamavasīyate / kasmāt ? vyastasamastānāmindriyāntarāṇāṃ tadasambhavāt / apohya hi manaḥ saṃkalpaṃ vyastānāmindriyāntarāṇāṃ bhavānparikalpayet samastānāṃ vā ? kiṃ cātaḥ ? tanna tāvadvyasthānāmindriyāṇāṃ saṃkalpo bhavati / kiṃ kāraṇam ? aniyataviṣayatvāt / niyato hi śrotrādīnāṃ śabdādirviṣayaḥ / aniyataviṣayaśca saṃkalpaḥ / kiṃca trikālaviṣayatvāt / vartamānaviṣayā śrotrādivṛttiḥ trikālaviṣayaśca saṃkalpaḥ / tasmānna vyastānāṃ nāpi samastānām / badhirādiṣu tadabhāvaprasaṃgāt / yadi samastendriyavṛttiḥ saṃkalpaḥ syātprāṇādivaditi cet syānmatam, yathā samastendriyavṛttiḥ prāṇādiḥ, na cānyataravaikalye tadabhāvaḥ, evaṃ samastendriyavṛttiḥ saṃkalpaḥ syānna cānyataravaikalye tadabhāvaḥ syāditi / etaccānupapannam / viśeṣitatvāt / nirviṣayā prāṇādivṛttiḥ / śabdādiviṣayastu saṃkalpa iti viśeṣitam / tasmādvyastasamastānāmindriyāṇāṃ saṃkalpānupapattermanaso liṅgametadastitve iti siddham /
  āha, tadavadhāraṇīyam, indriyadvaividhyāt / dviprakārāṇi hīndriyāṇi purastādupadiṣṭāni / tatra mano 'pyavadhāraṇīyaṃ kiṃ buddhīndriyamatha karmendriyamiti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
Here, in the section on the sense organs, <s>manas</s> (mind) is to be understood by you. In that regard, we state its definition as '<s>saṃkalpaka</s>' (that which forms intentions). <s>Saṃkalpa</s> (intention), desire, wish, craving — these are synonymous. That which forms intentions is <s>saṃkalpaka</s>. This is the definition of <s>manas</s>.
  Therefore, the existence of this [<s>manas</s>], though not apprehended through direct perception, is ascertained. Why? Because it is impossible for the other sense organs, whether taken individually or collectively, [to perform <s>saṃkalpa</s>]. For setting aside <s>manas</s>, would you attribute <s>saṃkalpa</s> (intention) to the other sense organs taken individually, or to them taken collectively? What follows from this? First, <s>saṃkalpa</s> does not belong to the individual sense organs. What is the reason? Because their objects are not unrestricted. For the object of hearing and the rest is restricted to sound and so forth. But <s>saṃkalpa</s> has unrestricted objects. Moreover, because [<s>saṃkalpa</s>] has objects in all three times. The operation of hearing and the rest has only present objects, whereas <s>saṃkalpa</s> has objects in all three times. Therefore it belongs neither to the individual [organs] nor to the collective [organs] — because in the case of deaf persons and the like, there would be the unwanted consequence of its absence. If one objects that <s>saṃkalpa</s> is a function of all the sense organs collectively, like <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the rest — one might think: just as <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest are functions of all the sense organs collectively, and yet the absence of one does not entail their absence, so too <s>saṃkalpa</s> would be a function of all sense organs collectively and would not be absent when one is lacking. But this too is untenable. Because [<s>saṃkalpa</s>] is differentiated [from <s>prāṇa</s>]. The function of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest is without a [specific sensory] object, whereas <s>saṃkalpa</s> is differentiated by having sound and the like as its objects. Therefore, since <s>saṃkalpa</s> is impossible for the sense organs whether taken individually or collectively, this is the inferential mark for the existence of <s>manas</s> — this is established.
  One says: this must be determined, since the sense organs are of two kinds. For the sense organs have been previously taught as being of two kinds. In that regard, <s>manas</s> too must be determined — is it a cognitive organ (<s>buddhīndriya</s>) or an action organ (<s>karmendriya</s>)?
  It is replied:
That [<s>manas</s>] is called a sense organ in both ways.

children.text:
hyarthe caḥ paṭhitaḥ / taddhīndriyamubhayathetyarthaḥ / mano na kevalaṃ buddhīndriyamapi tu karmendriyamapi /
  niyamahetvabhāvādayuktamiti cet syātpunaretat, ko 'tra niyamahetuḥ yadindriyatvāviśeṣe manasa evobhayapracāratvamabhyupagamyate, nānyeṣāmiti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
The particle 'hi' is used in the sense of 'ca' (and). The meaning is: that [<s>manas</s>] is a cognitive organ in both ways. <s>Manas</s> is not merely a cognitive organ (<s>buddhīndriya</s>) but also an action organ (<s>karmendriya</s>).
  If one objects that this is unjustified because there is no reason for the restriction — one might further say: what reason for restriction is there here, such that when there is no distinction in being a sense organ, only <s>manas</s> is acknowledged to operate in both ways, and not the others?
  It is replied:
Being internal and having objects in all three times, it therefore operates in both ways. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 27)

children.text: trikālaviṣayatvāt / iha yasyāntastriṣu ca kāleṣu karaṇasya vṛttistadubhayapracāram, tadyathā buddhiḥ / sākṣāt viṣayānabhisandhānādatītānāgatavartamānaviṣayatvācca mano 'ntastrikālaviṣayam / tasmādubhayapracāraṃ taditi siddham // 27 //
children.translated_text: Because it has objects in all three times. Here, whichever instrument has its operation internally and in all three times, that operates in both ways — just as <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) does. Because it does not directly engage with objects, and because it has past, future, and present objects, <s>manas</s> is internal and has objects in all three times. Therefore, it is established that it operates in both ways. (27)
End of the sixth lesson in the <s>Yuktidīpikā</s>, a commentary following the path of the <s>Sāṃkhyasaptati</s>.
<s>Kārikā</s> 28

children.text:
samadhigataṃ karaṇaparva / tasyedānīṃ vyastasamastavṛttayo vaktavyāḥ / sati cobhayābhidhāne vyastavṛttireva tāvaducyate, na samastavṛttiḥ / kiṃ kāraṇam ? prakaraṇaśeṣabhūtatvāt / śrotrādīnāṃ hi sadbhāvaprakaraṇamidamanukrāntam / sa caiṣāṃ sadbhāvaḥ śaktiviśeṣopālambhādityuktam / idānīmasau śaktiviśeṣo 'smākaṃ vyastavṛttirityucyate / tasmāttadanukramaṇaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ /
  āha, yadyevaṃ tasmāducyatāṃ tasya karaṇasya kasminnarthe vṛttiḥ, kiṃ lakṣaṇaṃ veti ?
  ucyate- yaduktaṃ tasya kasminnarthe vṛttirityatra brūmaḥ
children.translated_text:
The section on the instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>) has been completed. Now their individual and collective functions are to be stated. And when both are to be described, the individual function is stated first, not the collective function. What is the reason? Because it is the remainder of the topic at hand. For this topic of establishing the existence of hearing and the rest has been undertaken. And it has been said that their existence is [established] through the apprehension of specific capacities. Now that specific capacity is what we call the individual function. Therefore, we shall follow that order.
  One says: if so, then let it be stated — in what domain does that instrument operate, and what is its defining characteristic?
  It is replied: to the question 'in what domain does it operate,' we say:
The function of the five [cognitive organs] with respect to form and the rest is held to be mere apprehension.

  yatpunaretaduktaṃ kiṃlakṣaṇeti atra brūmaḥ- ālocanamātramiṣyate / ālocanaṃ grahaṇamityanarthāntaram / mātraśabdo viśeṣanivṛttyarthaḥ / tadyathā bhaikṣamātramasmingrāme labhyata ityukte nānyo viśeṣa iti jñāyate / chandromātramadhīte māṇavaka ityukte nānyadadhīta iti / evamālocanamātramindriyāṇāmiṣyate vṛttirityukte nānyo viśeṣa iti gamyate / tena kiṃ siddhaṃ bhavati ? yaduktamanyairācāryaiḥ sāmānyajñānamindriyāṇāṃ viśeṣajñānaṃ buddheriti tatpratiṣiddhaṃ bhavati /
  āha, kaḥ punarasmindarśane doṣo yata etatpratiṣidyata iti ?
  ucyate- sāmānyaviśeṣayoritaretarāpekṣatve satyekasminnavirodhādanyataraparikalpanānarthakyam / yadi khalvindriyasya sāmānyajñānaṃ na syāttena viśeṣāpekṣaṃ sāmānyaṃ sāmānyāpekṣaśca viśeṣa iti yatra sāmānyajñānaṃ tatra viśeṣajñānamapi na pratiṣidhyata ityubhayamapīndriyasya syāt / tataścāntaḥkaraṇaparikalpanānarthakyam / viśeṣavato vāntaḥkaraṇasya kaḥ sāmānyena virodha ityubhayasyāpi tatra sambhavādindriyānarthakyam / tasmādapratyayamindriyamiti / indriyasya cetpratyayaḥ syādyathā pratyayavato 'ntaḥkaraṇasyāniyataviṣayatvam, evamasyāpi syāt na tu tadasti / tasmādapratyayamindriyamiti / kiṃca kālātivṛttiprasaṃgāt / indriyasya cetpratyayaḥ syādyathā pratyayavato 'ntaḥkaraṇasya trikālaviṣayatvamevamasyāpi syāt / na tu tadasti / tasmādapratyayamindriyamiti / kiṃ cānyat smṛtyadarśanāt / indriyasya cetpratyayaḥ syādyathā pratyayavato 'ntaḥkaraṇasyādirūpopapattirevamatrāpi syāt / na tu tadasti / tasmādapratyayamindriyaṃ siddhamiti /
  ucyate- na kāraṇāntaraprasaṃgāt / yadi pradīpavadindriyaṃ prakāśakaṃ syāttena yathā tatprakāśiteṣu ghaṭādiṣvartheṣu karaṇāntaramārgaṇamevamatrāpi syāt / na caitadiṣṭam / ato na pradīpavadindriyaṃ prakāśakamiti / antaḥkaraṇasadbhāvādayuktamiti cet syānmatam- asti kāraṇāntaraṃ buddhilakṣaṇaṃ yadindriyeṇa pradīpavatprakāśitamarthaṃ gṛhṇāti / tasmātparavādānuvādo 'yaṃ kriyate, na pratiṣedha iti / tacca naivam / kasmāt ? pradīpendriyayoranyatarānupādānaprasaṃgāt / indriyamapi prakāśakam, pradīpo 'pi / tatrānyatarasyānupādānaṃ prasaktam / kasmāt ? na hyekārthakāriṇo yugapatkaraṇe sāmarthyamastīti / kiṃ cānyat / antaḥkaraṇahāneḥ / indriyeṇa pradīpavatprakāśitānbāhyānarthānsākṣādantaḥkaraṇaṃ gṛhṇātīti vadato 'ntaḥkaraṇameva hīyate / tasmādayuktamantaḥkaraṇasya sāmarthyam / puruṣasyeti cenna karaṇānarthakyaprasaṃgāt / sākṣādviṣayagrahaṇasamarthaṃ puruṣamicchataḥ karaṇānarthakyaṃ prasajyate / tasmādyuktametat grāhakamindriyaṃ na tu pradīpavatprakāśakamiti /

  ucyate- viṣayasamparkāttādrūpyāpattirindriyavṛttigrahaṇaṃ, tathā viṣayendriyavṛttyanukāreṇa niścayo gaurayaṃ śuklo dhāvatītyevamādiḥ pratyayaḥ / tathā viṣayasamparkāgame śrotrādivṛtteḥ tādrūpyāgamo vartamānakālatā, grahaṇasyānubhavāttu saṃskārādhānaṃ tatpūrvikā ca smṛtiriti trikālaviṣayā pratyayasyetyayamanayorviśeṣaḥ / bāhyastu prakāśo na viṣayarūpāpannaḥ / saṃskārāttu ghaṭādīnāṃ vyavadhānarūpaṃ pārthivaṃ chāyālakṣaṇaṃ vyañjakatvāya kalpate, cakṣuṣo 'nugrahāya / ubhayorvā cakṣurviṣayayorityapare / tasmādupapannametat prakāśakaṃ pradīpādi, grāhakaṃ śrotrādi, vyavasāyakamantaḥkaraṇamiti /
  atha karmendriyāṇāṃ kā vṛttirityucyate- naiyāyikāstvevamāhuḥ- ghrāṇarasanacakṣustvakcchrotrāṇīndriyāṇi bhūtebhyaḥ / bhūtebhya ityanena svaviṣayopalabdhilakṣaṇaṃ hīndriyāṇāṃ bhūtaprakṛtitve sati nirvahati (?) nānyathā / tāni punarindriyakāraṇāni pṛthivyaptejovāyurākāśamiti bhūtāni / ebhyaḥ pañcabhyo yathāsaṃkhyaṃ ghrāṇarasanacakṣustvakcchrotrāṇi pañcendriyāṇi bhavanti / bhūtaprakṛtitvamiti bhūtasvabhāvaṃ vyākhyāyamānaṃ pañcasvapi sambhavati / bhūtakāraṇatvaṃ tvanyeṣu caturṣu tathaiva / śrotre tu kathaṃcitkarṇaśaṣkulyavacchinnanabhobhāgābhiprāyeṇa vyavahārataḥ samarthanīyam / evaṃ bhautikānīndriyāṇi svasvaviṣayamadhigantumutsahanta iti tallakṣaṇatvameṣāṃ sidhyatīti, ato bhūtebhya ityuktam / etattu sāṃkhyācāryāṇāṃ neṣṭam / evaṃ hi sāṃkhyavṛddhā āhuḥ- āhaṅkārikāṇīndriyāṇi arthaṃ sādhayitumarhanti nānyathā / tathā hi kārakaṃ kārakatvādeva prāpyakāri bhavati / bhautikāni cendriyāṇi kathaṃ prāpyakārīṇi duravartini viṣaye bhaveyuḥ ? āhaṃkārikāṇāṃ tu teṣāṃ vyāpakatvāt / viṣayākārapariṇāmātmikā vṛttirvṛttimato 'nanyā satī sambhavatyeveti suvacaṃ prāpyakāritvam api ca mahadaṇuguṇagrahaṇamāhaṅkāritve teṣāṃ kalpate, na bhautikatve / bhautikatve hi yatparimāṇaṃ karaṇaṃ tatparimāṇaṃ grāhyaṃ gṛhṇīyāt /
  āha, atha karmendriyāṇāṃ kā vṛttiriti ?

children.translated_text:
With respect to form and the rest — that is, with respect to sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, each differentiated by its own subdivisions — the operation of the five [organs], namely hearing, skin, eye, tongue, and nose, characterized respectively as audition, tactile sensation, vision, gustation, and olfaction, is called their function. Here, in the enumeration of the instruments, since the organ of hearing was mentioned first, there is no purpose in transgressing the order of enumerating its objects, so it should be read as 'of the five with respect to sound and the rest.' The earlier [reading 'form and the rest'] is a scribal error.
  As for the question 'what is its defining characteristic,' we say: it is held to be mere apprehension. Apprehension and grasping are synonymous. The word 'mere' (<s>mātra</s>) serves to exclude any further specification. Just as when it is said 'only alms are obtained in this village,' it is understood that there is no other distinction; or when it is said 'the student studies only the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedic meters),' [it is understood] he studies nothing else — so when it is said 'the function of the sense organs is held to be mere apprehension,' it is understood that there is no further specification. What is thereby established? That which is stated by other teachers — namely, that general cognition belongs to the sense organs and particular cognition to <s>buddhi</s> — is thereby refuted.
  One says: what fault is there in this [other] view, that it should be refuted?
  It is replied: since the general and the particular are mutually dependent, when both are possible in one [faculty] without contradiction, the postulation of the other is purposeless. For if the sense organ did not have general cognition — given that the general depends on the particular and the particular depends on the general — where there is general cognition, particular cognition too is not precluded, so both would belong to the sense organ. Then the postulation of an internal organ would be purposeless. Or if the internal organ possesses particulars, what conflict is there with [it also possessing] the general? Since both would be possible there, the sense organ would be purposeless. Therefore, the sense organ is without determinate cognition (<s>apratyaya</s>). If the sense organ had determinate cognition, then just as the internal organ, which has determinate cognition, has unrestricted objects, so too would the sense organ — but this is not the case. Therefore, the sense organ is without determinate cognition. Moreover, because there would be the unwanted consequence of temporal transgression. If the sense organ had determinate cognition, then just as the internal organ, which has determinate cognition, has objects in all three times, so too would the sense organ — but this is not the case. Therefore, the sense organ is without determinate cognition. Furthermore, because memory is not observed [in sense organs]. If the sense organ had determinate cognition, then just as the internal organ, which has determinate cognition, has the capacity for producing impressions and the like, so too would the sense organ — but this is not the case. Therefore, it is established that the sense organ is without determinate cognition.
  It is replied: no, because there would be the unwanted consequence of [requiring] another instrument. If the sense organ were illuminating like a lamp, then just as when a lamp illuminates objects such as pots, another instrument must be sought [to grasp them], so too here. But this is not desired. Therefore, the sense organ does not merely illuminate like a lamp. If one objects that this is unjustified because of the existence of the internal organ — one might think: there is another instrument, namely <s>buddhi</s>, which grasps the object illuminated by the sense organ as by a lamp; therefore this is a restatement of the opponent's view, not a refutation. But that is not so. Why? Because there would be the unwanted consequence of dispensing with one or the other of lamp and sense organ. The sense organ too would illuminate, and the lamp too [would illuminate]. Then one of them becomes dispensable. Why? Because two instruments that serve the same purpose do not have the capacity to operate simultaneously. Moreover, because the internal organ would be undermined. For one who says that the internal organ directly grasps external objects illuminated by the sense organ as by a lamp, the internal organ itself is undermined. Therefore, the capacity of the internal organ is unjustified [on that view]. And if one says [the grasper is] <s>puruṣa</s> (the self) — no, because there would be the unwanted consequence of the instruments being purposeless. For one who holds that <s>puruṣa</s> is capable of directly grasping objects, the instruments become purposeless. Therefore, it is justified that the sense organ is a grasper, not merely an illuminator like a lamp.
  One says: granted that the function of the sense organ is mere grasping, without determinate cognition. But what is the distinction between grasping, determinate cognition, and illumination?
  It is replied: the conformity to the nature [of the object] arising from contact with the object — that is the grasping that constitutes the function of the sense organ. Likewise, the determination following the pattern of the sense organ's engagement with the object, such as 'this is a cow,' 'this is white,' 'it is running' — that is determinate cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>). And when contact with the object ceases, the cessation of the conformity of the function of hearing and the rest [to the object constitutes] the present-time nature [of grasping]; from the experience of grasping, however, there arises the depositing of impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and memory preceded by that — thus determinate cognition has objects in all three times. This is the distinction between them. External illumination, however, does not take on the form of the object. Rather, from the constitution [of things], the earthy form of obstruction in the nature of shadow belonging to pots and the like serves as a revealer, for the benefit of the eye. Or, according to others, [it serves] both objects of the eye. Therefore, it is well-established that lamps and the like are illuminators, hearing and the rest are graspers, and the internal organ is the determiner.
  Now, what is the function of the action organs? It is said: the <s>Naiyāyika</s>s say thus — 'nose, tongue, eye, skin, and ear are sense organs arising from the elements.' By saying 'from the elements,' the defining characteristic of sense organs as apprehending their own respective objects is consistent only when the sense organs have an elemental nature, not otherwise. Those elemental causes of the sense organs are: earth, water, fire, air, and space — these are the elements. From these five, in corresponding order, arise the five sense organs: nose, tongue, eye, skin, and ear. The elemental nature, when explained as having the nature of elements, applies to all five. But being caused by the elements [applies] in the same way to the other four. For the ear, however, it must be justified somehow through conventional usage, with the intention of [referring to] the portion of space enclosed by the ear cavity. Thus, since the elemental sense organs are capable of apprehending their own respective objects, their defining characteristic is established — hence it is said 'from the elements.' But this is not accepted by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers. For the elder <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers say thus: the sense organs, being products of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), are capable of accomplishing their objects, not otherwise. For an instrument, by virtue of being an instrument, operates by reaching [its object]. If the sense organs were elemental, how could they operate by reaching a distant object? But for those [organs] that are products of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, because of their pervasive nature — since their function, consisting in transformation into the form of the object, being non-different from the possessor of the function, is quite possible — the claim that they operate by reaching [their object] is easily stated. Moreover, the grasping of both great and minute qualities is tenable if they are products of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, not if they are elemental. For if they were elemental, the instrument of a certain size would grasp only an object of that same size.
  One says: what then is the function of the action organs?
  It is replied:
Speech, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure are [the functions] of the five [action organs]. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 28)

children.text: vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthānāṃ tu vacanādānaviharaṇotsargānandalakṣaṇā yathākramaṃ vṛttayaḥ pratyavagantavyāḥ / tatrocyate 'neneti vacanam / tasmādya evārthapratyāyanasamartho varṇasamudāyaḥ padavākyaślokagranthalakṣaṇaḥ sa vāgindriyasyārtho nānyaḥ / ādīyate 'nenetyādānam / āṅabhividhyarthe prayujyate / tataśca yadeva prakṣālanaparimārjanopasparśanādhyayanapraharaṇaśilpavyāyāmādi kṛtsnaṃ grahaṇaṃ sa indriyārthā nānyaḥ / viśiṣṭaṃ haraṇaṃ viharaṇam / ataśca yadeva samaviṣamanimnonnatacaṅkramaṇaparivartananāṭyavyāyāmādiḥ sa indriyārtho nānyaḥ / evamutkṛṣṭaḥ sarga utsargaḥ / nānyaḥ / ataśca ya evāśitapītavipariṇāmasya samyakstrotomārgānusāriṇo visargaḥ sa indriyārtho nānyaḥ / evamabhivyāpyānandamānandaḥ / tataśca ya evāsādhāraṇaprītinayanābhiniṣpattilakṣaṇaḥ sa indriyārtho nānyaḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: The functions of <s>vāc</s> (speech organ), <s>pāṇi</s> (hands), <s>pāda</s> (feet), <s>pāyu</s> (organ of excretion), and <s>upastha</s> (organ of generation) are to be understood respectively as characterized by speech, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure. Among these: that by which one speaks is speech (<s>vacana</s>). Therefore, whatever assemblage of phonemes — in the form of words, sentences, verses, and texts — is capable of conveying meaning, that alone is the object of the speech organ, nothing else. That by which one takes is grasping (<s>ādāna</s>). The prefix 'ā' is used in the sense of 'towards' or 'completely.' Therefore, whatever constitutes the entire range of taking — washing, wiping, touching, studying, striking, craftsmanship, exercise, and the like — that alone is the object of this sense organ, nothing else. Distinguished movement is locomotion (<s>viharaṇa</s>). Therefore, whatever constitutes walking on even and uneven, low and high [ground], turning around, dance, exercise, and the like — that alone is the object of this sense organ, nothing else. Similarly, excellent emission is excretion (<s>utsarga</s>). Therefore, whatever constitutes the proper discharge of what has been eaten and drunk, following the channels of the body — that alone is the object of this sense organ, nothing else. Likewise, pervading bliss is pleasure (<s>ānanda</s>). Therefore, whatever is characterized by the production of incomparable delight and [sexual] satisfaction — that alone is the object of this sense organ, nothing else. (28)
<s>Kārikā</s> 29

āha, prāgantaḥkaraṇavṛttinirdeśaḥ, sargakramānugamātpūrvaṃ buddhyahaṃkāramanasāṃ vṛttinirdeśaḥ kartavyaḥ / kiṃ kāraṇam ? evaṃ hi sargakramo 'nugato bhavati / kramabhede vā prayojanaṃ vaktavyamiti /

children.text:
) / tasmātsargakrameṇa vinā tannirdeśaḥ prāgācāryeṇa kriyate iti /
  āha, tadasambhavaḥ, śāstre prāgabhimānābhidhānāt / śāstraṃ hyevamāha- kā nu bhoḥ saṃjñā māturudare 'vasthitaṃ kumāraṃ pratyabhinirviśata iti ? asmītyeṣā māhātmī saṃviditi / tathā kāryakāraṇavyūhasamakālaṃ māhātmyaśarīro 'smīti pratibuddhyate / pravṛttāścaiva hyavyaktā bhavantyasmītyasmitāmātrāḥ / pramāṇaṃ ca śāstram / tasmātprāgantaḥkaraṇanirdeśaḥ kartavyaḥ /
  ucyate- tannimittārthena vivakṣitatvāt / satyametat kāryakāraṇavyūhaniṣpattisamakālamasmītyeṣā māhātmī saṃvit pratyupadhīyate / śabdādiviṣayastvantaḥkaraṇapratyayaḥ śrotrādinimitta iti / etatpūrvaśabdena vivakṣitam / na ca nimittamatikramya naimittikābhidhānaṃ nyāyyam /
  athavā naiva vayamidaṃ praṣṭavyā yathā prāgantaḥkaraṇavṛttinirdeśaḥ kartavya iti / kiṃ kāraṇam ? yasmāt
children.translated_text: ). Therefore, without the order of creation, the teacher gives this exposition earlier. One objects: that is impossible, because self-assertion is mentioned earlier in the scripture. For the scripture says: 'What designation, pray, is applicable to a child situated in the mother's womb?' 'I am' — this is the majestic awareness. Likewise, simultaneously with the formation of the causal complex, one awakens [with the thought] 'I am, possessing a body of greatness.' And indeed the unmanifest [entities] come into being, being mere 'I-am-ness' of the nature of 'I exist.' And scripture is the authority. Therefore the exposition of the inner organ should be given first. It is replied: because it is intended for the purpose of [explaining] its cause. True, simultaneously with the formation of the causal complex, this majestic awareness 'I am' is established. But the cognition of the inner organ, whose objects are sound and the like, is caused by the ear and the other [sense organs]. This is what is intended by the word 'prior.' And it is not proper to state the caused without [first] going beyond the cause.

One says: previously, the specification of the function of the internal organ [should come first]. Following the order of creation, the specification of the functions of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), and <s>manas</s> (mind) should be stated first. What is the reason? For in this way the order of creation would be followed. Or if there is a deviation from the order, the purpose must be stated.
  It is replied: no, because [the internal organ's function] is preceded by the function of the sense organs. For the determinate cognition of the internal organ is set in motion by the function of the sense organs. And thus it will be stated: 'Whether in the seen or likewise in the unseen, the function of the three is preceded by that [i.e., the function of the sense organs]' —
The characteristic activity of each of the three [<s>guṇa</s>s is specific].

children.text: svalakṣaṇameva svālakṣaṇyam / svārthe taddhitavṛttiḥ, anyabhāvastu kālaśabdavyavāyāditi / yathā buddhyahaṃkāramanasāṃ hi saukṣmyānna śakyaṃ svarūpamabhidhātumityato vṛttireva lakṣaṇabhāvenopadiśyate / śrotrādīnāmapi ca saukṣmyāllakṣaṇamapadeṣṭumaśakyamiti vṛttirevocyate, na lakṣaṇam / tadeva caiṣā lakṣaṇaṃ bhavati / yacchabdālocanasamarthaṃ tacchrotram / evamitareṣvapi vaktavyam / buddhyahaṃkāramanasāṃ ca lakṣaṇamadhyavasāyādyuktam / tadeva vṛttitvenācakṣāṇaḥ śrotrādīnāmeva cābhidadhānaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cāpyācakṣāṇo vṛttivṛttimatorananyatvaṃ jñāpayati / anyathā tu yathādhyavasāyādi lakṣaṇamevaṃ rūpādiṣu pañcānāmalocanamātraṃ lakṣaṇamityucyate, na tu vṛttiriti / śrotrādivad buddhyādīnāmapi vyavasāyādayo vṛttirityucyate, na tu lakṣaṇam / tasmādanyathā nirdeśo jñāpakaṃ vṛttivṛttimatoranyatvasyeti vyākhyātā karaṇavṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: The characteristic peculiarity is indeed '<s>svālakṣaṇya</s>' (specific individuality). The <s>taddhita</s> suffix has reflexive meaning; but the difference [from the base] is due to the intervention of a temporal word. Since, due to their subtlety, the essential nature of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), and <s>manas</s> (mind) cannot be stated directly, their activity is taught as their defining characteristic. And since the defining characteristic of the ear and the other [sense organs] too cannot be stated due to their subtlety, their activity is stated, not their defining characteristic. Yet that very [activity] becomes their defining characteristic. That which is capable of apprehending sounds is the ear — and so on for the others. And the defining characteristic of <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> was stated as ascertainment and so forth. By stating that very [characteristic] as activity, and by stating it as the defining characteristic of the ear and the rest, he indicates the non-difference of activity and the possessor of activity. Otherwise, just as ascertainment and so forth are the defining characteristic [of the inner organs], so for the five [sense organs] regarding form and the rest, mere apprehension would be stated as the defining characteristic, not as activity. And ascertainment and the like for <s>buddhi</s> and the rest would be stated as activity, not as the defining characteristic. Therefore the alternative manner of exposition is an indicator of the otherness of activity and its possessor — thus the activity of the instruments has been explained.
This [activity] is non-common (specific to each instrument).
