seti pūrvakṛtāṃ vṛttimabhisambadhnāti / eṣeti sarvanāmnā pratyākṛṣṭāṃ tāmeva pratyakṣaṃ prati nirdiśati / bhavatīti vakṣyamāṇena dharmāntareṇāsyāstadvattānubhāvitaṃ khyāpayati / asāmānyeti dharmamācaṣṭe / sāmānyā sādhāraṇetyarthaḥ / na sāmānyāsāmānyā / pratikaraṇaṃ niyatetyuktaṃ bhavati / yā hīyamanukrāntā karaṇaparvaṇo 'dhyavasayādikā vṛttiriyaṃ vyastānāṃ karaṇānāṃ pratisvaṃ niyatā / tataścaiṣāṃ buddhyādīnāṃ kāryaviśeṣanimittabhāvasaṃsūcitasya svarūpasyāsaṃkaraḥ siddhaḥ /
  āha, sāmānyaviśeṣayoritaretarāpekṣatvādasāmānyābhidhānena sāmānyasyāpyabhidhānādadhyavasāyādikā karaṇānāmasāmānyā vṛttirityukte 'rthādāpannameṣāṃ sāmānyāpi vṛttirastīti / tasmādasāvapi vaktavyeti /
  ucyate-
children.translated_text: The word 'sā' (this) connects with the activity previously mentioned. The demonstrative pronoun 'eṣā' (this very) directly points to it as perceptible. 'Bhavatī' (is) indicates, through another property to be stated, its possession of that quality. 'Asāmānyā' (non-common) states the property. '<s>Sāmānyā</s>' means 'shared'; 'not shared' is '<s>asāmānyā</s>.' What is stated is that [each activity] is restricted to each instrument. For the activity of ascertainment and so forth which has been described for the stages of the instruments — this, when the instruments are taken separately, is restricted to each one individually. And thereby the non-confusion of the essential natures of <s>buddhi</s> and the rest — which are indicated by their being the basis of specific effects — is established. One objects: since the common and the specific are mutually dependent, by stating the non-common, the common too is [implicitly] stated. When it is said that the non-common activity of the instruments is ascertainment and so forth, it is implicitly understood that they also have a common activity. Therefore that too should be stated. It is replied:
The common activity of the instruments is the five breaths beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 29)

children.text:
sāmānyā cāsau karaṇavṛttiḥ sāmānyakaraṇavṛttiḥ / prāṇaścādyo yeṣāṃ te prāṇādyāḥ, prāṇāpānasamānodānavyānāḥ pañca samastakaraṇavṛttiḥ pratyavagantavyeti / taiḥ sarvaiḥ sahitaḥ prāṇa iti vedānteṣvapi /
  āha, ayuktametat / kasmāt ? dharmiṇo dharmyantaravṛttibhāvānupapatteḥ / vṛttirityayaṃ śabdo vyāpāramācaṣṭe / na ca dharmāntaraṃ dharmāntarasya vyāpāro bhavitumarhatīti /
  ucyate- na kārye kāraṇopacārāt / satyametat / dharmī dharmyantarasya vṛttitvenāśakyaḥ parikalpayitum / kiṃ tu sāmānyakaraṇavṛttyā preryamāṇo vāyustatpravaṇatvāttatkāryatāṃ pratipadyate / tatra prāṇādikārye vāyau prāṇopacāraṃ kṛtvā evamucyate- prāṇādyā vāyavaḥ pañca /
  tatpreraṇāsiddherayuktamiti cet syādetat, kathametadavagamyate 'rthāntarapreritasya vāyoriyaṃ kriyā bhavati na punaḥ svatantrasyeti ?
  ucyate- na svataḥ, tadvyatiriktatvānupapatteḥ / iheyamakasmādbhinnā kriyāvāyoḥ svato vā syāt, karaṇavṛttivyatiriktatvādvā / kiṃ cātaḥ ? tatra tāvatsvata upapadyate / kasmāt ? sarvatra prasaṃgāt svābhāvike hi vāyordiksaṃcāre 'bhyupagamyamāne sarvatra tatsaṃbhavaḥ syāt / tataśca tiryakpātādivṛttirhanyeta, na cānyataḥ / kasmāt ? adarśanāt / na hi pṛthivyādīnāṃ vāyupreraṇasāmarthyaṃ kvacidupalabdham / bhastrādiṣu dṛṣṭamiti cenna, anyanimittatvāt / atrāpi caitravyāpāra upalabhyate ityavaśyamanyannimittamupalabhyate ityabhyupagantavyam / ātmeti cenna, kriyāpratiṣedhāt / upapāditametatpūrvamātmā niṣkriya iti / na ca niṣkriyasya preraṇamupapadyate / na ca nirnimittā svabhāvabhedānāmanākasmikatvāt / tasmādyattannimittaṃ sā samastakaraṇavṛttiḥ /
  sa cāyaṃ vāyureka eva sthānasaṃcāraviśeṣānnānākhyo bhavati / yathaiko devadattaḥ pācako lāvaka iti kvacit / tadayuktam / kasmāt ? yugapatparasparātiśayavirodhāt / pūrvasmātpūrvasmāduttara uttaro vāyurbalīyāniti hyabhyupagamaḥ / tadetadekasyaikasminkāle nopapadyate / tasmādupapannaṃ prāṇādyā vāyavaḥ pañca /
  kiṃ punareṣāṃ prāṇādīnāṃ lakṣaṇamiti ?
  ucyate- dvividhāḥ prāṇādayaḥ / antarvṛttayo bahirvṛttayaśca / tatra mukhanāsikābhyāṃ pragamanātpraṇateśca prāṇaḥ / yo 'yaṃ mukhanāsikābhyāṃ sañcarati so 'ntarvṛttirvāyuḥ prāṇa ityabhidhīyate / yā kācitpraṇatirnāma bhūteṣu tadyathā praṇateyaṃ senā, praṇato 'yaṃ vṛkṣaḥ, praṇato 'yaṃ dharme, praṇato 'yamarthe, praṇato 'yaṃ kāme, praṇato 'yaṃ vidyāyām / tadviparīteṣu vā bāhyaprāṇavṛttireṣā / prāṇiviṣaya evaiṣā bhavati / sa khalvayamatrābhivyakto bhavati / tadyathā mahatā vā duḥkhenābhiplutasya mahatā vā bandhunā viyuktasya, sahitasya vā saurabheyasya, nipānāvatīrṇasya vā mahiṣasyāvagateḥ /
  apakramaṇāccāpānaḥ / yo 'yaṃ rasaṃ dhātūn śukraṃ mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vātārtavagarbhāṃścākarṣannadhogacchannayamantarvṛttirvāyurapāna ityabhidhīyate / yaccāpi kiṃcidapakramaṇaṃ nāma bhūteṣu tadyathā apakrānto 'yaṃ dharmādibhyastadviparītebhyo vā iti bāhyā khalvapānavṛttireṣā / apānaviṣaya evaiṣa bhavati / balavattaraścāyaṃ prāṇodvāyoḥ kasmāt ? eṣā hyetaṃ prāṇamūrdhvaṃ vartamānamarvāgeva sanniyacchati arvāgeva sanniruṇaddhi / eṣo 'trābhivyakto bhavati / tadyathā upakūpamupaśvabhraṃ vā parivartamānasyā__śatapadīṃ laṅghayataḥ /
  hṛdyavasthānātsaha bhāvācca samānaḥ / yastvayaṃ prāṇāpānayormadhye hṛdyavatiṣṭhate sa samāno vāyurantarvṛttiḥ yaścāpi kaścitsaha bhāvo nāma bhūteṣu dvandvārāmatā / tadyathā saha dāsye, saha yakṣye, saha tapaścariṣyāmi saha bhāryāputrairbandhubhiḥ suhṛdbhiśca vartiṣya bāhyā samānavṛttireṣā / samānaviṣaya evaiṣa bhavati iti / balavattaraḥ khalvayaṃ prāṇāpānābhyām / eṣa hyetau prāṇāpānau ūrdhvamarvākca vartamānau madhya eva sanniyacchati, madhya eva sanniruṇaddhi, sa caiṣau 'trābhivyakto bhavati / tadyathā srutasārasya vā sārameyasya, anaḍuho voḍhabhārasya, dharmābhitaptāyā vā eḍakāyā ardhārdhakāyaṃ śakaśaketi / prāṇānte sarvaprāṇināṃ prāṇāpānāvutsṛjyordhvamadhaśca muktayoktrau hayāviva viṣamaṃ saṃcārayan śarīraṃ sa parāsyati /
  mūrdhārohaṇadātmotkarṣaṇāccodānaḥ / yastvayaṃ prāṇāpānasamānānāṃ sthānānyatikramya rasaṃ dhātūṃścādāya mūrdhānamārohati tataśca pratihato nivṛttaḥ sthānakaraṇānupradānaviśeṣādvarṇapadavākyaślokagranthalakṣaṇasya śabdasyābhivyaktinimittaṃ bhavati ayamantarvṛttirvāyurudāna ityucyate / yaścāpi kaścidātmotkarṣo nāma bhūteṣu tadyathā hīnādasmi śreyān, sadṛśena vā sadṛśaḥ, sadṛśādasmi śreyān, śreyasā vā sadṛśaḥ, śreyaso vā śreyān / etasmiṃstathā rūpābhimāno vā prāptavidyastu / tadyathā bahvantaraviśeṣādalpāntaraviśeṣo 'smyaguṇavato vā guṇavānasmīti bāhyodānavṛttireṣā / udānaviṣaya evaiṣa bhavati / balavattaraḥ khalvayaṃ pūrvabhyaḥ / katham ? eṣa hyetānprāṇādīnūrdhvamavāṅmadhye ca vartamānānūrdhvamevonnayati, ūrdhvamevotkarṣati / sa caiṣo 'trābhivyakto bhavati śītodakena vā paryukṣitasya prāsamasiṃ vikośaṃ codyatamabhipaśyataḥ /
  śarīravyāpteratyantāvinābhāvācca vyānaḥ / yastvayamālomanakhāccharīraṃ vyāpya rasādīnāṃ dhātūnāṃ pṛthivyādināṃ vyūhaṃ marmaṇāṃ ca praspandanaṃ prāṇādīnāṃ ca sthitiṃ karoti so 'ntarvṛttirvyānaḥ / yaścāpi kaścidatyantāvinābhāvo nāma bhūteṣu tadyathā pativratā bhartāraṃ mṛtamapyanugacchati bhavāntare 'pyayameva bhartā syāt tathā dharmādibhistadviparītaiśceti bāhyo vyānaviṣaya evaiṣa prabhavati / balavattamaścāyaṃ sarvebhyaḥ / katham ? anena hi vyāpte śarīradaṇḍake tadvaśīkṛtānāṃ prāṇādīnāṃ samā sthitirbhavati / sa eṣo 'ntakāle prāṇabhṛtāmavinābhāvena vartamāno 'bhivyajyate / tadyathā hā tarhi pādau haimau śītībhūtau gulphe jaṅghe urū kaṭirudaramuraḥkaṇṭhe 'sya khuraghuro vartate hū(?) ityavaiṣo bāhyo vyāna iti / evamete prāṇādyāḥ sthānakāryaviśeṣasūcitāḥ pañca vāyavo vyākhyātāḥ teṣāṃ prerikā sāmānyakaraṇavṛttiḥ /
  eṣā ca tantrāntareṣu prayatna ityucyate / sa ca dharmādisaṃskārabhāvanāvaśādanuparato jīvanam / āha ca

children.translated_text: The activity within all the instruments collectively, like a lamp,
non-manifest, having the form of action, constituting life, and sustaining the body —

Common, and it is the activity of the instruments — hence '<s>sāmānyakaraṇavṛtti</s>' (common instrumental activity). Those whose first is <s>prāṇa</s> are '<s>prāṇādya</s>' — [namely] <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>samāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>vyāna</s> — the five should be understood as the activity of all the instruments collectively. Together with all of them, <s>prāṇa</s> [is mentioned] even in the <s>Vedānta</s>s. One objects: this is unjustified. Why? Because it is untenable for a property to serve as the activity of another property. The word 'activity' designates operation. And one property cannot serve as the operation of another property. It is replied: no, because of figurative attribution of the cause to the effect. True. A property cannot be posited as the activity of another property. But the wind, being impelled by the common instrumental activity and being inclined toward that, attains the status of its effect. Therefore, making the figurative attribution of <s>prāṇa</s> to the wind which is the effect of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, it is said: 'The five breaths beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>.' If one objects that this is unjustified because the impelling [by the instruments] is not established — how is it known that this action of the wind occurs when impelled by something else, and not independently? It is replied: not from itself, because the absence of that [specific action] apart [from the instrumental activity] is untenable. Here, this diverse action of the wind would either be from itself, or from being different from the activity of the instruments. What follows? It is not from itself. Why? Because there would be a consequence [of it occurring] everywhere. For if the wind's movement in [various] directions were accepted as natural, it would occur everywhere. And thereby the activity of transverse motion and the like would be destroyed. Nor from another [material cause]. Why? Because it is not observed. For the capacity of earth and the rest to impel the wind is never observed anywhere. If one says it is observed in bellows and the like — no, because it has a different cause. Here too the operation of a conscious agent is observed; therefore it must necessarily be accepted that there is another cause. If one says [the cause is] the self — no, because of the refutation of [its] activity. It was established earlier that the self is without activity. And it is not tenable for something without activity to impel. And [the activity of wind] is not without a cause, because things that differ in nature are not uncaused. Therefore whatever is that cause —

children.text: sā yāvadaniruddhā tu hanti vāyuṃ rajo 'dhikā /
children.translated_text: as long as that [activity], predominating in <s>rajas</s>, is unsuppressed, it drives the wind;
and by virtue of the unobstructed [operation of] <s>dharma</s> and the rest, a person lives that long.

children.text: atra ca sāmānyakaraṇavṛttigrahaṇasāmarthyātprāṇādyāḥ pañca vāyavaḥ / buddhīndriyāṇi ṣaṣṭham / karmendriyāṇi saptamam / pūraṣṭamam / pūrityahaṃkārāvasthāsaṃvidhamadhikurute / yasmādāha- tatra

children.translated_text: Because the awareness residing in <s>ahaṅkāra</s> fills the effect with the cause,
therefore it is called '<s>pūri</s>' (filling) — the eighth manifestation for the experiencer.

And here, by the force of the phrase 'common instrumental activity,' the five breaths beginning with <s>prāṇa</s> [constitute the first common activity]. The <s>buddhīndriya</s>s (cognitive sense organs) are the sixth. The <s>karmendriya</s>s (active sense organs) are the seventh. <s>Pūri</s> is the eighth. '<s>Pūri</s>' refers to the state of awareness belonging to <s>ahaṅkāra</s>. For it is said: therein —

children.text:
sā cāhaṅkāragatā saṃvid buddhigataiva puruṣeṇopalabhyate /
  yasmādvakṣyati-
  ete pradīpakalpāḥ parasparavilakṣaṇā guṇaviśeṣāḥ /
  kṛtsnaṃ puruṣasyārthaṃ prakāśya buddhau prayacchanti // (

children.translated_text: <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 36
). 'Because <s>buddhi</s> accomplishes all experience for <s>puruṣa</s>' (
<s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 37

children.text: pracyuto mahato yastu na prāpto jñānalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: That which has fallen from <s>mahat</s> but has not attained the character of knowledge —
that activity, being the source of knowledge, is the source [of action], like an egg of a hen.

And that awareness residing in <s>ahaṅkāra</s> is apprehended by <s>puruṣa</s> [only] as residing in <s>buddhi</s>. For he will state: 'These <s>guṇa</s>-modifications, which are mutually distinct and like lamps, having illuminated the entire purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>, present it to <s>buddhi</s>' (

children.text: tāsāṃ lakṣaṇaviṣayasatattvaguṇasamanvayā bhavanti / tatra lakṣaṇaṃ tāvat vyavasāyādapracyavanaṃ dhṛtiḥ / phalamanabhisandhāya śāstrokteṣu kāryeṣvavaśyakartavyatābījabhāvaḥ śraddhā / dṛṣṭānuśravikaphalābhilāṣadvārako hi buddherābhogaḥ sukhā / vettumicchā vividiṣā / tannivṛttiravividiṣā / tatra yadāyaṃ jantuḥ śubhāśubheṣu kāryeṣu vṛttyanusārī jijñāsurajijñāsurvā śarīraṃ parityajati tāmeva karmayonimupapadyate / tasyāmupapannastāmeva bhāvayati / etattāvallakṣanasatattvam / āha ca
vāci karmaṇi saṃkalpe pratijñāṃ yo na rakṣati /
children.translated_text: One who does not protect one's commitment in speech, action, and thought,
who is devoted to that and pledged to that — this indeed is the characteristic of <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness).

Their characteristics, domains, reality, and correlation with <s>guṇas</s> are [as follows]. First, as to their characteristics: non-deviation from determination is <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness). The seed-state of the sense of obligatory duty in actions prescribed by scripture, without regard to results, is <s>śraddhā</s> (faith). The inclination of the intellect directed toward desire for seen and heard fruits is <s>sukhā</s> (desire for happiness). The wish to know is <s>vividiṣā</s> (desire to know). Its cessation is <s>avividiṣā</s> (absence of desire to know). Among these, when this being, following [a particular] function in auspicious or inauspicious actions, desirous of knowing or not desirous of knowing, abandons the body, it is reborn in that very <s>karmayoni</s> (source of action). Having been born in it, it cultivates that very [disposition]. This is so far the reality of their characteristics. And it is said:
Freedom from envy, celibacy, performing sacrifices, causing others to sacrifice, austerity,

children.text: dānaṃ parigrahaḥ śaucaṃ śraddhāyāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ smṛtam //
children.translated_text: charity, acceptance, purity — these are remembered as the characteristics of <s>śraddhā</s> (faith).

children.text: sukhārthī yastu seveta vidyāṃ karma tapāṃsi vā /
children.translated_text: One who, desiring happiness, resorts to learning, action, or austerities,

children.text: prāyaścittaparo nityaṃ sukhāyāṃ sa tu vartate //
children.translated_text: who is always devoted to expiation — that one abides in <s>sukhā</s> (desire for happiness).
Duality and unity, distinctness, permanence, consciousness and non-consciousness, subtlety,
the doctrine of pre-existent effect and the doctrine of non-pre-existent effect — these are to be investigated by <s>vividiṣā</s> (desire to know).
Like one who has drunk poison, or one asleep, or one intoxicated — <s>avividiṣā</s> (absence of desire to know) is always the source for those who are [merely] meditating;
it is called the natural course that destroys the [subtle] body and its instruments.

children.text: viṣayasatattvaṃ punaḥ sarvaviṣayiṇī dhṛtiḥ / āśramaviṣayiṇī śraddhā / dṛṣṭānuśravikaviṣayiṇī sukhā / vyaktaviṣayiṇī vividiṣā / avyaktaviṣayiṇyavividiṣā / guṇasamanvayastu rajastamobahulā dhṛtiḥ / sattvarajobahulā śraddhā / sattvatamobahulā sukhā / rajobahulā vividiṣā / tamobahulāvividiṣā iti / uktaṃ ca

children.translated_text: The characteristics, domains, reality, and threefold <s>guṇa</s>-correlation of the five

children.text: yonīnāṃ yo vidyādyativṛṣabhaṃ taṃ tvahaṃ manye //
children.translated_text: <s>yonis</s> (sources) — whoever knows this, I consider him the best among the great ones.

As for the reality of their domains: <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness) pertains to all objects. <s>Śraddhā</s> (faith) pertains to the <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life). <s>Sukhā</s> (desire for happiness) pertains to seen and heard [objects]. <s>Vividiṣā</s> (desire to know) pertains to the manifest. <s>Avividiṣā</s> (absence of desire to know) pertains to the unmanifest. As for the correlation with <s>guṇas</s>: <s>dhṛti</s> is <s>rajas</s>- and <s>tamas</s>-predominant. <s>Śraddhā</s> is <s>sattva</s>- and <s>rajas</s>-predominant. <s>Sukhā</s> is <s>sattva</s>- and <s>tamas</s>-predominant. <s>Vividiṣā</s> is <s>rajas</s>-predominant. <s>Avividiṣā</s> is <s>tamas</s>-predominant. And it is said:

children.text:
ityuktāḥ prāṇādayo yonayaśca /
  etad dvayamadhigamya samyaṅmārgānugamanaṃ kuryāt / rajastamodharmādisādhanabhāvavinivṛttitastvatra prāṇānāmantarvṛttiranupādhikatvādanivartyā / bahirvṛttistu mārgāmārgaviṣayatayā prayoktavyā / kathamityucyate- prāṇaviṣayā tāvatpraṇatirdharmādiviṣaya evāparoddhavyā / tato hyasya sattvavṛddhiḥ, sattvavṛddheścottarottarabuddhirūpādhigamaḥ / apānaviṣayastvapakramaṇaṃ dharmādiviṣaya evāparoddhavyamevaṃ hyasya khyātiviṣayākārasya tamaso nirhrāsaḥ / tataścottarottarabuddhirūpādhigamaḥ / tathā samānaviṣayaṃ sāhacaryasattvadharmānuguṇaṃ kuryāt / yasmācchāstramāha- sattvārāmaḥ sattvamithunaśca sadā syāditi / ātmotkarṣa tūdānaviṣayam / avidyāparvaṇo 'ntyaṃ rūpaṃ vivarjya tatpratipakṣairnivartayet / atyantāvinābhāvaṃ ca vyānaviṣayaṃ jñānaviṣaya eva bhāvayet / yonīnāṃ catasṛṇāṃ dharmatābījatāmevādadyāt / avividiṣāmapi aniṣṭaphalahetuṣu bhāvayet / so 'yaṃ dharmādiṣu pravaṇastatpratipakṣāpakrāntaḥ sattvārāmo vinivṛttābhimāno jñānaniṣṭhaḥ saviśuddhayoniracireṇa parama brahmopapadyata iti / āha ca

children.translated_text: The wise one, having established the external activity of <s>prāṇa</s> on the correct path,
free from the impurity of disturbance, surely attains the immortal abode.

Thus the <s>prāṇas</s> and the <s>yonis</s> (sources) have been explained.
  Having understood these two, one should follow the correct path. Here, the cessation of the internal activity of the <s>prāṇas</s> through the removal of the means such as <s>rajas</s>, <s>tamas</s>, <s>dharma</s> and the rest [is not possible], since their internal function, being unconditioned, cannot be stopped. But the external function, being subject to the right and wrong paths, should be directed. How? It is said: First, regarding the domain of <s>prāṇa</s>: reverence should be directed only toward the domain of <s>dharma</s> and the like. For from that comes increase of <s>sattva</s>, and from the increase of <s>sattva</s>, progressive attainment of the forms of <s>buddhi</s>. The domain of <s>apāna</s> — namely, departure — should be directed only toward the domain of <s>dharma</s> and the like; for thus there is diminution of <s>tamas</s>, which has the form of the object of <s>khyāti</s> (discrimination). And from that, progressive attainment of the forms of <s>buddhi</s>. Likewise, the domain of <s>samāna</s> — namely, companionship — should be made consonant with <s>sattva</s>-<s>dharma</s>. Since the scripture says: 'One should always be a companion of <s>sattva</s> and paired with <s>sattva</s>.' Self-elevation, moreover, is the domain of <s>udāna</s>; abandoning the final form of the stage of ignorance, one should reverse it with its antidotes. And the domain of <s>vyāna</s> — absolute inseparability — should be cultivated in the domain of knowledge alone. And of the four <s>yonis</s>, one should adopt only the seed-state of <s>dharma</s>. <s>Avividiṣā</s> too should be cultivated regarding the causes of undesirable fruits. This [person], inclined toward <s>dharma</s> and the rest, departed from their opposites, a companion of <s>sattva</s>, with pride eliminated, established in knowledge, with purified <s>yonis</s>, before long attains the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. And it is said:
Having established the <s>dharma</s>-causality and the like of the five <s>yonis</s>,
[knowing] 'this is fully ripened' — one should not go again downward to that [state] once cultivated.
Thus the individual and collective activity of the instruments has been explained. // 29 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 30

children.text:
āha, yeyamekaikasmin rūpādāvarthe karaṇacatuṣṭayasya vṛttiḥ sā kiṃ yugapat āhosvit krameṇeti ? kutaḥ saṃśaya iti cet ubhayathā dṛṣṭatvāt / ihaikārthaviṣayāṇāṃ yugapadapi vṛttirdṛṣṭā / tadyathā candramaṇḍale cakṣuṣāṃ manaso vā / kramaśaśca tadyathā ghaṭe madhūdakapayasām / ekārthaviṣayaṃ ca karaṇacatuṣṭayam / ato naḥ saṃśayaḥ kiṃ cakṣurmanovadyugapadasya vṛttiḥ, āhosvinmadhvādivatkrameṇeti ?
  ucyate- yathādarśanamapi tāvaducyatām / kimatra yuktaṃ bhavān manyate ? sa cetsapyagupadekṣyasi ko nirbandhastadeva pratipadyāmahe iti /
  yadyavaṃ tasmādidamasmaddarśanam
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] Does this activity of the fourfold instruments with respect to each object such as form and the like occur simultaneously or sequentially? If asked 'whence the doubt?' — because it is observed both ways. Here, the simultaneous operation of things pertaining to a single object is observed — for example, [multiple] eyes [seeing] the disc of the moon, or [multiple functions of] the mind. And sequential [operation] too — for example, honey, water, and milk [being poured] into a pot. And the fourfold instruments pertain to a single object. Therefore our doubt is: does their operation occur simultaneously, like the eyes and mind, or sequentially, like honey and the like?
  [Reply:] First state your own view. What do you think is proper here? If you too would see [it the same way], what is the point of insistence? We shall accept that very [view].
  If so, then this is our view:
The operation of the fourfold [instruments] is simultaneous;

children.text:
tuśabdo 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ yugapadevetyarthaḥ / buddhyahaṃkāramanasāṃ hi buddhīndriyāṇāṃ ca samānadeśatvam / tatra na śakyata etadvaktuṃ sati śaktisadbhāve viṣayasambandhe ca kasyacittatra vṛttiḥ kasyacinneti / kiṃ cānyat / meghastanitādiṣu kramānupalabdheḥ / yadi hi krameṇa śrotrādīnāmantaḥkaraṇasya ca bāhye 'rthe vṛttiḥ syādapi tarhi meghastanitakṛṣṇasarpālocanādiṣvapyupalabhyate kramaḥ / na tūpalabhyate / tasmādyugapadeva bāhye 'rthe catuṣṭayavṛttiriti /
  ucyate- yaduktaṃ śrotrādīnāmantaḥkaraṇasya cābhinnakālaṃ vṛttirityatra brūmaḥ, ayuktametat / kiṃ kāraṇam ? yasmādasmākaṃ
children.translated_text:
The particle 'tu' is for emphasis — 'simultaneously only' is the meaning. For <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), and <s>manas</s> (mind), together with the <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (cognitive sense faculties), occupy the same location. Given this, when there is the existence of capacity and connection with the object, it cannot be said that some operate there and others do not. Moreover, because in [cases like] thunder from clouds, no sequence is perceived. For if the operation of the ear and the other [senses] and the internal organ with respect to an external object were sequential, then even in [cases like] thunder from clouds, the sight of a black serpent, and so forth, a sequence would be perceived. But it is not perceived. Therefore the operation of the fourfold [instruments] with respect to an external object is simultaneous.
  [Reply:] As for the statement that the operation of the ear and the other [senses] and the internal organ occurs at the same time — to this we say: that is untenable. For what reason? Because in our view:
and the operation of that [fourfold group] is also declared to be sequential.

children.text:
tasyeti catuṣṭayamapi sambadhyate / caśabdo 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ / kramaśa evetyarthaḥ / kramaśa eva hi bāhyāntaḥkaraṇavṛttyorekārthanipātaḥ /
  yattūktaṃ samānadeśānāṃ śaktisambandhasadbhāve vṛttyabhāvānupapattiriti, atra brūmaḥ- cakṣurādivadetatsyāt / tadyathā cakṣustvacoḥ samānadeśatve śaktiviṣayasambandhopapattau rajodhūmātapādigataḥ sparśa evopalabhyate, na rūpam / evamihāpi syāt / tasmāt
children.translated_text:
'Of that' connects with the fourfold [group] as well. The particle 'ca' is for emphasis — 'sequentially only' is the meaning. For the occurrence of the external and internal organ-functions upon a single object is sequential only.
  As for the objection that when things occupying the same location have capacity and connection, it is untenable that they would not operate — to this we say: it would be like the eye and skin. Just as when the eye and skin occupy the same location, with both capacity and object-connection being present, only touch — of dust, smoke, heat, and the like — is perceived, not form. So too it would be here. Therefore:
in the seen, and likewise in the unseen,

children.text: kramaśa eva catuṣṭayasya vṛttiḥ / adṛṣṭagrahaṇena punaratrātīnāgatavyavahitaviṣayagrahaṇam / tatrātītaṃ dvividham, dṛṣṭaviṣayadṛṣṭaviṣayaṃ ca / atrāpi dṛṣṭaviṣayaṃ pratyabhijñānamityabhipretam, adṛṣṭaviṣayaṃ smṛtiḥ / sā tu liṅgāgamābhyāmakasmādvā bhavati / tathā ca vṛṣagaṇavīreṇāpyuktaṃ bhavati ___ anāgatavyavahitaviṣayajñānaṃ tu liṅgagāgamābhyām / āha ca

children.translated_text: From the contact of the object and the sense faculty, perceptual knowledge is said [to arise];
that very [knowledge], when it has become supersensory, through repeated impression, is memory.

the operation of the fourfold [instruments] is sequential only. By the word 'unseen,' moreover, here the grasping of past, future, and hidden objects [is indicated]. Among these, the past is of two kinds: having a previously-seen object and having an unseen object. Here, that which has a previously-seen object is intended as recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>); that which has an unseen object is memory (<s>smṛti</s>). And that [memory] arises from inference, from scripture, or spontaneously. And thus it has been stated by <s>Vṛṣagaṇavīra</s> as well: ___ The knowledge of future and hidden objects is through inference and scripture. And it is said:
That very knowledge, dependent on repeated impression, at a later time,
when it arises in the very same [context] together with the sense faculty, is called recognition.

children.text:
tatra duṣṭe kramaḥ prati nāsti sandehaḥ /
  yatpunaretaduktaṃ dṛṣṭe meghastanitakṛṣṭasarpālocanādau kramānupalabdheryugapaccatuṣṭayasya vṛttirityatra brūmaḥ- etadapyayuktam / kiṃ kāraṇam ? yasmāt
children.translated_text:
Among these, regarding the unseen, there is no doubt about the sequence.
  As for the objection that in seen [cases] such as thunder from clouds, sight of a black serpent, and so forth, the operation of the fourfold [instruments] is simultaneous because no sequence is perceived — to this we say: that too is untenable. For what reason? Because:
the operation of the three [internal organs] is preceded by that [external sense faculty]. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 30 //

children.text:
na tāvad buddhyahaṃkāramanasāṃ sākṣād bāhyārthagrahaṇasāmarthyamasti, antaḥkaraṇānupapattiprasaṃgāt, śrotrādivaiyarthyaprasaṃgāt, dvāridvārabhāvavyāghātaprasaṅgācca / tasmātpūrvaṃ śrotrādīnāmarthasambandho 'sti meghastanitādāvapyavaśyametadabhyupagantavyam / paścāttu tadvṛttyupanipātādantaḥkaraṇasyetyasti kramo 'trāpi / tatra yaduktaṃ meghastanitādiṣu kramānanugate yugapaccatuṣṭayasya vṛttirityetadayuktam /
  anyaistvanyathānvayo darśitaḥ / tadyathā catuṣṭayasya mano 'haṃkārabuddhīnāmantaḥkaraṇānāṃ bāhyenaikena karaṇena śrotreṇa vā cakṣuṣā vā saha catuṣṭayasyetyarthaḥ / asya dṛṣṭe vartamāne yugapadvṛttiḥ pūrvācāryairnirdiṣṭā / ācāryeṇa tu krameṇetyarthaḥ / adṛṣṭe 'tītādāvapi kramaśaśca krameṇaiva, yatastrayasyāntaḥkaraṇasya tatpūrvikā bāhyendriyapūrvikā vṛttiḥ / yadā yathānubhavastathā saṃskāraḥ, yathā ca saṃskārastathā smṛtirityevaṃ vṛttirbāhyendriyapūrviketi // 30 //
children.translated_text:
First of all, <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> do not have the capacity to directly grasp external objects — because otherwise the existence of the internal organ would be unjustified; because the ear and other [external senses] would become purposeless; and because the relationship of door and door-keeper would be contradicted. Therefore, the contact of the ear and the other [senses] with the object comes first — this must necessarily be accepted even in [cases such as] thunder from clouds. Only afterwards, through the occurrence of their [the external senses'] function, does the internal organ [operate] — thus there is sequence here too. Therefore, the claim that the operation of the fourfold [instruments] is simultaneous in [cases like] thunder from clouds where no sequence is perceived — that is untenable.
  Others, however, have shown a different interpretation. Namely: of the fourfold — mind, ego, and intellect — the three internal organs together with one external instrument, the ear or the eye — 'of the fourfold' means this. In the seen, i.e., the present, the simultaneous operation of this [fourfold group] is declared by the earlier teachers. But by the [present] teacher, [it is] sequential — this is the meaning. In the unseen — past and the like — also 'sequentially,' meaning: by sequence only, since the operation of the three — the internal organ — is preceded by that, i.e., preceded by the external sense faculty. When the impression is as the experience, and the memory is as the impression — thus the operation is preceded by the external sense faculty. // 30 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 31
