children.translated_text: the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> alone is the motive — no instrument is made to act by any [other]. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 31 //

children.text:
yasya karaṇasya yā vṛttirapadiṣṭā tadyathā śrotrasya śabdagrahaṇam, cakṣuṣo rūpagrahaṇam ityādi / tāmeva pratipadyante- svaviṣayajidhṛkṣayāvalambanta ityarthaḥ / parasparasyākūtaṃ parasparākūtam / ākūtamabhiprāyo 'bhisandhirityarthaḥ / parasparākūtaṃ hetuḥ pratipatterasyāḥ, seyaṃ parasparākūtahetukī / parasparākūtaṃ pratipatteḥ kāraṇamiti kṛtvā tācchabdyaṃ labhate / tadyathā dadhitrapusaṃ jvaraḥ / etaduktaṃ bhavati yadā cakṣuṣāmradāḍimādi rūpamupalabdhaṃ bhavati tadā rasanendriyamupāttaviṣayasya cakṣuṣo vṛttiṃ saṃvedya svaviṣayajighṛkṣayautsuktavadvikāramāpadyate, rasanasya vṛtiṃ saṃvedya pādau viharaṇamārabhete hastāvādānaṃ, tāvadyāvadasau viṣayo rasanendriyayogyatāṃ nītaḥ / tato rasanaṃ svaviṣaye pravartate / evamitareṣvapi vaktavyam /
  āha, yadyevaṃ tena tarhīndriyāntaravṛttisaṃvedane 'kṣapratyayavatvaprasaṃgaḥ / yadi tarhīndriyāntareṇendriyāntarasya vṛttiḥ saṃvedyate, prāptamasya pratyayavattvam / athāpratyayamindriyaṃ parasparākūtasaṃvedanaṃ, tarhi na vācyamiti / kiṃ ca parasparadvāridvārabhāvaprasaṃgaśca / indriyāntaraṃ cedindriyāntarasya vṛttiṃ saṃvedya svārthamākāṃkṣet, prāptamasya dvāritvamitarasya ca dvāratvam / tadayuktamindriyāṇāṃ parasparākūtasaṃvedanamiti /
  ucyate- na, upacārāt / prāgevopadiṣṭamasmābhirapratyayamindriyamiti / kiṃ tarhi svaviṣayasya paṭoḥ sahacāriṇamarthamindriyāntaraviṣayatāmāpannaṃ saṃspṛśya svabhāvata indriyāntaraṃ svaviṣayaṃ prati sākāṃkṣaṃ bhavati, tatsannidhau vikriyādarśanāt / tatra saṃvedanamupacaryaivamucyate ityadoṣaḥ / kiṃ cānyat / bhautikāvayavapratyayavivṛttivattadvivṛtteḥ / yathā buddheḥ prasādamanantaraṃ bhautikānāmavayavānāṃ mukhanayanādīnāṃ prasādo bhavati, na caiṣāṃ pratyayavattvam, evamihāpi syāt / na ca pratyayavattvam / etena dvāridvārabhāvaḥ pratyuktaḥ /
  mano 'dhiṣṭhānasāmarthyādvā / athavā parasparaviṣayamākūtaṃ parasparākūtam, yathā jalaviṣayaḥ puruṣaḥ jalapuruṣaḥ / ākūtamicchā saṃkalpaḥ mana ityarthaḥ / sa heturasyāḥ seyaṃ parasparākūtahetukī tām / etaduktaṃ bhavati, yathā kiṃcidindriyaṃ viṣaye pravṛttaṃ bhavati tadā taddvāreṇa samastamarthamupalabhya tatsahacāriṇamarthāntaramākāṃkṣadindriyāntaraṃ vṛttyā pratitiṣṭhate / tenākāṃkṣāvatā manasādhiṣṭhitāmindriyaṃ vikriyāmāpadyate / tathā ca tantrāntare 'pyuktaṃ- "yasya yasyendriyasya viṣayaṃ manodhyāyatyabhisampattyarthena tasya tasyautsukyaṃ pravṛttiśca bhavatīti /" etaduktaṃ svāṃ svāṃ pratipadyante parasparākūtahetukīṃ vṛttiriti /
  kimindriyaṃ manovṛttyādhiṣṭhāya svaviṣaye pravartayati yathā paraśvādīṃścaitra iti ?
  netyucyate / kiṃ tarhi svaviṣayasaṃkalpānugṛhītasya manasaḥ saṃsparśātsvayamevendriyaṃ svaviṣayaṃ pratipadyate / kasmāt ? prayogaśaktyasiddheḥ / na hi yathā caitrasya paraśvādiprayogaśaktiḥ siddhā evaṃ manasa indriyaprayogaśaktiḥ / tasmādayuktamindriyasya manaḥ prerakamiti / raja iti cetsyānmatam, rajaso hīndriyāntaraprayogasāmarthyaṃ vidyate / tasmādayuktamuktaṃ prayogaśaktyasiddhernendriyāṇāṃ manaḥprayojakamiti / etaccāyuktam ? kasmāt ? aviśeṣāt / indriyāntare 'pi hi tarhi rajo 'stītyata ātmabhūtenaivāsya nimittena pravṛttirapratiṣiddhā, kiṃ manasā parikalpiteneti ? kiṃ cānyat, karaṇāntarānupapatteḥ / caitro hi paraśvādīnāṃ prayogaṃ karaṇāntareṇa karoti / na tu manasaḥ karaṇāntaramastītyasamānam / pāṇivaditi cenna caitravyāpārāpekṣatvāt / tadapi hi caitravyāpārāpekṣaṃ pravartate na svataḥ / kiṃca tadvyatirekeṇa pravṛttyupalabdheḥ / yasya hi prayojakāntarāpekṣā pravṛttiḥ na tasya kadācidapi svatantrasya bhavati / asti tu saṃkalpavyatirekeṇa meghastanitādiṣvindriyasya pravṛttiḥ / tasmānnendriyāntarasya manaḥ kārakam / na cetkārakaṃ yathā maulānāṃ guṇānāmevamihāpi puruṣārtha evaṃ heturna kena citkāryate karaṇamiti siddham // 31 //
children.translated_text:
The function that has been described for each instrument — for instance, the hearing of sound by the ear, the grasping of form by the eye, and so on — that very [function] they engage in; that is, they rest upon it through the desire to grasp their own object — this is the meaning. The intention of one another (<s>parasparākūta</s>) — '<s>ākūta</s>' means purpose, intention, aim. The mutual intention is the cause of this engagement, and that [engagement] is 'caused by mutual intention' (<s>parasparākūtahetukī</s>). Because the mutual intention is the cause of the engagement, [the engagement] receives the designation [of being caused by it]. For example: 'yogurt-cucumber is fever' [i.e., yogurt-cucumber causes fever]. What is meant is this: when the eye perceives the form of a mango, pomegranate, etc., then the organ of taste, having become aware of the activity of the eye that has grasped its object, undergoes a modification as if eager through the desire to grasp its own object; [then] having become aware of the activity of the tongue, the feet begin locomotion and the hands begin grasping, until that object is brought into proximity suitable for the organ of taste. Then the tongue engages in its own object. The same should be said regarding the others as well.
  [Objection:] If so, then there would be the consequence of sense organs having [further] sense-cognition in their awareness of the activity of other sense organs. If, then, one sense organ becomes aware of the activity of another sense organ, it follows that it has the character of requiring [further] cognition. And if the sense organ is without [further] cognition [in its] awareness of mutual intention, then nothing needs to be said. Furthermore, there would be the consequence of their being mutually door-and-doorway. If one sense organ, having become aware of the activity of another sense organ, desires its own object, it follows that it becomes a doorway, and the other becomes a door. Therefore, the mutual awareness of intention among sense organs is untenable.
  [Reply:] No, because it is figurative (<s>upacāra</s>). We have already previously taught that the sense organ is without [further] cognition. Rather, by touching an object that accompanies its own object — one that has come to be the object of another sense organ — the other sense organ naturally becomes desirous toward its own object, because modification is observed in the presence of that [object]. The [term] 'awareness' there is said figuratively — hence there is no fault. Moreover, because its unfolding is like the cognition-dependent unfolding of material components. Just as, following the serenity of the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), there comes serenity of the material components — the face, eyes, etc. — yet these do not have the character of requiring [further] cognition; so here too it would be the same. And there is no [character of requiring further] cognition. By this, the door-and-doorway [objection] is answered.
  Or [alternatively], by the power of the mind (<s>manas</s>) as the presiding [factor]. Or alternatively, '<s>parasparākūta</s>' means 'intention directed toward mutual objects,' like 'a water-person' [meaning 'a person in water']. '<s>Ākūta</s>' means desire, volition — i.e., the mind — that is the meaning. That is the cause of this [engagement], and that [engagement] is 'caused by mutual intention.' What is meant is this: when any sense organ is engaged toward an object, then through its channel, having perceived the entire object, another sense organ, desiring an accompanying different object, becomes established in its activity. That desiring [organ] is presided over by the mind, and [so] the sense organ undergoes modification. And in another treatise (<s>tantra</s>) too it is said: 'Whichever sense organ's object the mind contemplates for the purpose of approaching, that [sense organ] develops eagerness and activity.' This is what is meant by: 'They engage in their own [functions], caused by mutual intention.'
  [Question:] Does the mind, having presided over the sense organ, set it in motion toward its own object, as <s>Caitra</s> [drives] dogs and the like?
  [Reply:] No, it is said. Rather, by the mere contact of the mind — which has been assisted by the volition regarding its own object — the sense organ itself engages toward its own object. Why? Because the power of application (<s>prayogaśakti</s>) is not established [for the mind]. For just as <s>Caitra</s>'s power of application over dogs and the like is established, the mind's power of application over the senses is not similarly established. Therefore, it is not correct that the mind is the impeller of the sense organs. If one says 'because of <s>rajas</s> (activity)' — that might be the view, since <s>rajas</s> indeed has the capacity for the application of other sense organs. Therefore, [one might say] the objection is wrong that 'because the power of application is not established, the mind is not the activator of the senses.' But this too is incorrect. Why? Because of non-distinction. For in other sense organs too, <s>rajas</s> exists; therefore, activity through its own inherent cause is not obstructed — why then postulate the mind? Moreover, because of the inapplicability of another instrument. For <s>Caitra</s> applies dogs and the like through another instrument. But the mind has no other instrument — hence the analogy fails. [If one says] 'like the hand' — no, because [the hand too] depends on <s>Caitra</s>'s effort. For that too operates depending on <s>Caitra</s>'s effort, not by itself. Furthermore, because activity is observed without that [mind]. For that whose activity depends on another impeller never has activity independently. But there is activity of the sense organ without volition, as in [the involuntary response to] thunder-claps, etc. Therefore, the mind is not the agent of another sense organ. If it is not an agent, then — just as with the original <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) — here too, the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is the cause; [the instrument] is not made to act by anything — this is established. // 31 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 32.

children.text:
āha, karaṇaṃ pratyācāryavipratipatteḥ / tadavadhāraṇaṃ karttavyam / ācāryāṇāṃ karaṇaṃ prati vipratipattiḥ / ekādaśavidhamiti vārṣagaṇāḥ / daśavidhamiti tāntrikāḥ pañcādikaraṇaprabhṛtayaḥ / dvādaśavidhamiti patañjaliḥ / tasmādbhavataḥ katividhaṃ karaṇamabhipretamiti vaktavyametat /
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] Because of the disagreement among teachers regarding the instruments, their determination must be made. There is disagreement among teachers regarding the instruments: 'Eleven-fold' — [say] the <s>Vārṣagaṇas</s>. 'Ten-fold' — [say] the <s>Tāntrikas</s>, beginning with the <s>Pañcādhikaraṇa</s> [school] and others. 'Twelve-fold' — [says] <s>Patañjali</s>. Therefore, it must be stated: how many-fold is the instrument according to you?
  It is replied:
The instrument is thirteen-fold; it accomplishes the bringing, holding, and illuminating [of objects].

children.text:
pañca karmendriyāṇi pañca buddhīndriyāṇi mano 'haṅkāro buddhiścetyetatsarvaṃ puruṣārthopayogikaraṇam / kasmāt ? apuruṣārthopayogitve tattvāntarānupapattiprasaṃgāt / yadi yathā vārṣagaṇā āhuḥ- liṅgamātre mahānasaṃvedyaḥ kāryakāraṇarūpeṇa viśiṣṭāviśiṣṭalakṣaṇena, tathā syāttattvāntaram / tanna syāt, anarthakatvāt /
  āha, satyam, pradhānalakṣaṇānāṃ guṇānāṃ vaiṣamyamātrarūpatve 'pi tattvāntaramasau bhaviṣyatīti / kasmāt ? sāmyādvaiṣamyamupākhyāntaramiti /
  etaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? tattvānavasthāprasaṃgāt / evaṃ hi parikalpyamāne pradhānamahatoryadantarālaṃ tadapi ca kriyārūpatvādakriyāvata upākhyāntaramiti tattvāntarānavasthāprasaṃgaḥ / abhyupagame vā mahatastattvāntarāṇāṃ ca kriyākālavirodhaḥ / tasmāttattvāntarānupapattiranavasthā vā, trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇamityanyataravadavaśyamabhyupagantavyam / tatra cāsmatpratijñātameva nirdoṣaṃ lakṣyate / tasmādupapannametat trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇamiti /
  āha, karaṇamiti kriyākārakasambandhagarbho 'yaṃ nirdeśaḥ / katham ? yena tatkaraṇamiti / tatra vaktavyam kā kriyā, kiṃ ca tatkriyate yadapekṣya buddhyādīnāṃ karaṇatvamiti ?
  ucyate- yaduktaṃ kā kriyetyatra brūmaḥ- tannirvartakamihābhipretāt na daṇḍādivat, kiṃ tarhi tadāharaṇadhāraṇaprakāśakaram / tatrāharaṇaṃ karmendriyāṇi kurvanti, viṣayārjanasamarthatvāt / dhāraṇaṃ buddhīndriyāṇi kurvanti, viṣayasannidhāne sati śrotrādivṛttestadrūpāpatteḥ / prakāśamantaḥkaraṇaṃ karoti, niścayasāmarthyāt /
  apara āha- āharaṇaṃ karmendriyāṇi kurvanti / dhāraṇaṃ mano 'haṃkāraśca / prakāśanaṃ buddhīndriyāṇi buddhiśceti / etadabhisandhāya buddhyādīnāṃ karaṇatvamucyata iti /
  yattūktaṃ kiṃ kāryamiti, ucyate-
children.translated_text:
The five action-organs (<s>karmendriya</s>), the five cognitive organs (<s>buddhīndriya</s>), the mind (<s>manas</s>), ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), and intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) — all this is the instrument useful for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the self). Why? Because if it were not useful for <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose, there would be the consequence of the non-establishment of [any] further category. If, as the <s>Vārṣagaṇas</s> say, '<s>mahat</s> (the great one) is not perceptible in the mere subtle body (<s>liṅgamātra</s>), being characterized as both differentiated and undifferentiated in the form of cause and effect' — then it would be a [separate] category. But that would not be [valid], because it would be purposeless.
  [Objection:] True, but even though the nature of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) — which have the characteristics of <s>Pradhāna</s> — is merely disproportion, it will be a [separate] category. Why? Because disproportion from equilibrium is a different designation.
  This too is incorrect. Why? Because there would be an infinite regress of categories. For when conceived in this way, that which is between <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>mahat</s> — that too, being of the nature of activity, would be a different designation from the inactive — hence an infinite regress of categories. Or, upon accepting [this], there would be a contradiction in the time of activity of <s>mahat</s> and those [intermediate] categories. Therefore, either the non-establishment of further categories [follows], or an infinite regress — one or the other must necessarily be accepted: that the instrument is thirteen-fold. And in this, what we have proposed is seen to be faultless. Therefore, this is established: the instrument is thirteen-fold.
  [Objection:] The term '<s>karaṇa</s>' (instrument) is a designation containing the relationship of action and agent. How? 'That by which [something is done] is the instrument.' There it must be stated: what is the action, and what is it that is done, with reference to which <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and the rest have the status of instruments?
  [Reply:] As to what was asked 'what is the action?' — we say: what is meant here is 'that which accomplishes it' — not like a stick etc. [which is an inert tool], but rather: it accomplishes the bringing, holding, and illuminating [of objects]. Therein, the action-organs (<s>karmendriya</s>) accomplish the bringing, because they are capable of procuring objects. The cognitive organs (<s>buddhīndriya</s>) accomplish the holding, because when an object is present, the functions of the ear and others take on the form of that [object]. The internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) accomplishes the illumination, because of its capacity for determination.
  Another [teacher] says: The action-organs accomplish the bringing. The mind and ego accomplish the holding. The cognitive organs and the intellect accomplish the illumination. With reference to this, the instrumental character of <s>buddhi</s> and the rest is stated.
  As to what was asked 'what is the effect?' — it is replied:
And the effect of that [instrument] is tenfold —

children.text: daśadheti pañca viśeṣāḥ pañcāviśeṣāḥ / tadapyata eva kāryaśabdaṃ labhate /
children.translated_text: 'Tenfold' means: five specific (<s>viśeṣa</s>) [objects] and five non-specific (<s>aviśeṣa</s>) [objects]. And that receives the designation 'effect' for this very reason:
the to-be-brought, the to-be-held, and the to-be-illuminated. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 32 //

children.text: taddhyāhartavyaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ prakāśayitavyaṃ ca / ataḥ kāryamityucyate, na nirvartyatvāt // 32 //
children.translated_text: For that indeed is to be brought, to be held, and to be illuminated. Therefore it is called 'effect' — not because it is 'produced.' // 32 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 33 [actually 13].

children.text:
etasmiṃstrayodaśavidhe tu karaṇe trayodaśaṃ kataraditi ?
  ucyate- buddhirahaṃkāro manaśca / tasmāt /
children.translated_text:
In this thirteen-fold instrument, which is the thirteenth?
  It is replied: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), and <s>manas</s> (mind). Therefore:
The internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is threefold.

children.text: kasmāt ? viṣayānabhisandhānāt / śrotrādipraṇālikayā ca viṣayasaṃpratipatteḥ / aviśeṣābhidhānād buddhyādipratipattirayukteti cetsyānmatam, aviśeṣeṇedamuktamācāryeṇa antaḥkaraṇaṃ trividhamiti / tatra kathamidamavagamyate buddhyahaṃkāramanasāṃ grahaṇābhipretaṃ, na punaranyeṣāmiti ? ucyate- na, prathamasaṃkhyāvyatikramahetvanupapatteḥ / buddhyādisaṃkhyāṃ hi vyatikramamāṇasya pratipattau nāsti hetuḥ / tasmātteṣāmeva grahaṇam / yathā vasantāya kapiñjalānālabhata iti / śrotrasyāntaḥkaraṇatvaprasaṃgādayuktamiti cet syādetat- buddhimahaṃkāraṃ coktvā tata āha buddhīndriyāṇi karṇatvakcakṣūrasananāsikākhyānīti (
children.translated_text:
Why? Because they do not engage directly with objects. And because the apprehension of objects [occurs] through the channel of the ear and other [sense organs]. [Objection:] If one thinks — 'Because of the general statement, the identification of <s>buddhi</s> and the rest is incorrect' — that might be the view, since the teacher stated without specification: 'The internal organ is threefold.' How then is it understood that the inclusion of <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> is intended, and not of others?
  [Reply:] No, because there is no reason for exceeding the initial enumeration. For one who would exceed the enumeration beginning with <s>buddhi</s> and the rest has no reason for that understanding. Therefore, it is [only] their inclusion. Just as [in the rule]: 'One should sacrifice <s>kapiñjalas</s> (partridges) to Spring.' [Objection:] If one thinks there would be the consequence of the ear being an internal organ — this might be [the objection]: having stated <s>buddhi</s> and <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, [the teacher] then says: 'The cognitive organs are called ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose' (
<s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 26

children.text: ) / tasmācchrotramantaḥkaraṇaṃ prasajyata iti / etadanupapannam / kasmāt ? manasaḥ pṛthagabhidhānāt / ata evedamācāryeṇāpekṣya manaso 'ntaḥkaraṇatvaṃ pṛthaguktam- taccendriyamubhayathā samākhyātam, antastrikālaviṣayamiti (
children.translated_text: ). Therefore, the ear would [seemingly] be entailed as an internal organ. This is untenable. Why? Because of the separate mention of <s>manas</s>. It is precisely with this in view that the teacher separately stated the internal nature of the mind: 'That is called an organ in both ways — the internal [organ], whose object spans the three times' (
<s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 27
). Therefore, it is established that the internal organ is threefold — <s>buddhi</s> and the rest.
The external [organ] is tenfold.

children.text:
pañca buddhīndriyāṇi pañca karmendriyāṇītyetadbāhyaṃ daśaprakāramācāryairākhyāyate /
  āha, daśadhā bāhyamityasyānarthakyam, pariśeṣabuddheḥ / antaḥkaraṇaṃ trividhamityukte gamyata etatpariśeṣādeva daśadhā bāhyamiti / tasmāttadgrahaṇamanarthakamiti /
  ucyate- na, viṣayārthatvāt / trayasya viṣayākhyamityevaṃ vakṣyāmītyācārya ārabhate / akriyamāṇe tvasmin kintat trayasya viṣayākhyamiti na jñāyate /
  āha, evamapi viṣayagrahaṇātsiddherbāhyagrahaṇapārthakamiti /
  ucyate- vaktavyaṃ tāvadidamavaśyaṃ viṣayabhāvapratipattyartham / tatra śeṣe vā yathānyāsaṃ vocyamāne na kaścidviśeṣaḥ / athavā nedaṃ bāhyasaṃjñāpratipattyarthamārabhyate, kiṃ tarhi niyamārtham / katham ? daśadhā bāhyaṃ śabdādiviṣayagrahaṇabhūtameva trayasyāpi viṣayākhyaṃ yathā syāt, mā bhūdantaḥprāṇādibhūtam / athavā daśadhaiva bāhyam / bhedaviṣayaṃ bāhyamityarthaḥ / prāṇādibhūtasya tu bhedo nāstītyadoṣaḥ /
  tadetat
children.translated_text:
The five cognitive organs and the five action-organs — this is declared by the teachers as the external [instrument] of ten kinds.
  [Objection:] The statement 'tenfold external' is purposeless, because it can be understood by remainder. When 'the internal organ is threefold' is stated, it is understood merely by remainder that the external is tenfold. Therefore, that inclusion is purposeless.
  [Reply:] No, because it serves the purpose [of introducing] the object. The teacher begins [with this] because he will say: 'The object-designation of those three [is next].' If this [statement about the external] were not made, one would not know [the referent of] 'the object-designation of those three.'
  [Objection:] Even so, since it is established from the mention of 'object,' the inclusion of 'external' is redundant.
  [Reply:] This must necessarily be stated for the purpose of understanding the object-relation. In that case, whether the remainder is stated as-is or spoken [explicitly], there is no difference. Or alternatively, this is not undertaken for the purpose of understanding the designation 'external,' but rather for the purpose of restriction. How? 'The external is tenfold' — consisting only of the grasping of objects such as sound, etc. — this is so that the object-designation of those three may also apply [to the external]; it should not be [understood as] consisting of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the rest. Or alternatively, 'the external is tenfold only' — meaning: the external pertains to differentiated [objects]. The meaning is that there is no differentiation for that which consists of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest — hence there is no fault.
  That is to say:
The object-designation of those three [internal organs is as follows].

children.text:
buddhyahaṃkāramanolakṣaṇasya hi trayasyopāttaviṣayā buddhīndriyakarmendriyavṛttayaḥ samparkādviṣayarūpapratyavabhāsanimittatāmupagacchantyo viṣayākhyatāṃ labhante / tathā mano 'haṃkārāvapi buddheḥ / buddhistu niścayarūpatvātkaraṇāntaranirapekṣā sarvamarthaṃ pravṛttau prati niścayarūpeṇādhyastaṃ puruṣāyopasaṃharati /
  tatra śabdādisannidhāne vṛttīnāṃ tādrūpyāpattestadapagame ca tādrūpyāpagamāt prāpyakāri /
children.translated_text:
For the activities of the cognitive organs and action-organs, having taken up objects, through contact with the triad characterized as <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s>, come to be the cause of the manifestation of the object-form, and thus receive the designation 'object-related.' Similarly, <s>manas</s> and <s>ahaṃkāra</s> [are object-designations] also for <s>buddhi</s>. But <s>buddhi</s>, being of the nature of determination, independent of other instruments, presents all objects to <s>Puruṣa</s> in the form of determination superimposed [upon them] for the sake of activity.
  Because the functions [of the external organs], when the objects such as sound and the rest are present, take on the form of those [objects], and when those [objects] are absent, lose that form — [therefore the external organs] operate by contact (<s>prāpyakāri</s>).
The external [organs operate] in the present time only.
But because of the proximity of the sense-organ functions that have taken up objects, through the force of memory-cognition caused by the deposit of impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of that form —
the internal organ [operates across] the three times. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 33 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 34.

children.text:
āha, prākchabdādiṣu śrotrādīnāmālocanamātraṃ vṛttirityaviśeṣeṇoktam / tatra kiṃ tathaiva pratipattavyamathendriyāṇāṃ viṣayaviśeṣo 'stīti ? atha coktaṃ kāryaṃ ca tasya daśadhā viśeṣalakṣaṇamaviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ ca / tatra kena karaṇena kasya viṣayasya grahaṇamiti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] Previously it was said without specification that the function of the ear and the rest regarding sound and so on is mere apprehension. Regarding that — is it to be understood just in that way, or do the sense organs have [distinctions regarding] specific objects? And it was [also] said: 'Its effect is tenfold' — characterized as specific (<s>viśeṣa</s>) and non-specific (<s>aviśeṣa</s>). There, which instrument grasps which object?
  It is replied:
The cognitive organs (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>) — of those, five have specific and non-specific objects.

children.text:
teṣāṃ pūrvoktānāmindriyāṇāṃ yāni buddhīndriyāṇi pañca śrotrādīni tāni viśeṣāviśeṣaviṣayāṇi pratipattṛbhedena / tatra devānāṃ yāni indriyāṇi tāni dharmotkarṣādviśuddhānyaviśeṣānapi gṛhṇanti prāgeva viśeṣāt, yogināṃ ca saṃprāptaviśeṣāṇām / asmadādīnāṃ tu viśeṣāneva tamasā parivṛtatvāt /
  āha, kiṃ karmendriyāṇāmapi pratipattṛbhedādgrahaṇabhedo bhavati ?
  netyucyate / kiṃ tarhi sarveṣāmeva
children.translated_text: Of those previously mentioned sense organs, the five <s>buddhīndriya</s>s (cognitive sense organs) — hearing and the rest — have both specific (<s>viśeṣa</s>) and non-specific (<s>aviśeṣa</s>) objects, depending on the difference of the apprehending subjects. Among those, the sense organs of gods, being purified due to the excellence of <s>dharma</s>, apprehend even the non-specific [objects], let alone the specific ones; and so too [the organs] of <s>yogins</s> who have attained the [perception of] specific [subtle elements]. But for beings like us, [they apprehend] only the specific objects, because [our organs] are enveloped by <s>tamas</s> (darkness). One asks: is there also a differentiation in apprehension for the <s>karmendriya</s>s (active sense organs) due to the difference of subjects? It is replied: no. Rather, for all [beings alike] —
Speech has sound as its object.

children.text:
vāgindriyasya vāyvabhihateṣu vadanapradeśeṣu tālvādiṣu dhvanervarṇapadavākyaślokagranthabhāvena vikārāpādanaṃ sarvaprāṇināmaviśiṣṭam /
  āha, athetarāni karmendriyāṇi kathamiti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text: The vocal organ's production of modifications of sound — in the form of phonemes, words, sentences, verses, and texts — from the vibration [produced] in the parts of the mouth such as the palate and the rest, when struck by air, is the same for all living beings. One asks: and how about the remaining active sense organs? It is replied:
The remaining [active sense organs] also have the five [elements] as their objects. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 34)

children.text:
pāṇipādapāyūpasthāstu ādānaviharaṇotsargānandalakṣaṇaiḥ karmabhiḥ śabdasparśarasarūpagandhasamudāyarūpā mūrtīrvikurvantīti /
  āha, yadi pañcaviṣayāṇyevāviśeṣāṇīti niyamo 'bhyupagamyate tenaikakaraṇeṣvādānādikriyānupapattiprasaṃga iti /
  ucyate na, niyamapratiṣedhārthatvāt / svaviṣayaniyamo buddhīndriyavatkarmendriyāṇāmapi mā vijñāyītyato niyamapratiṣedhārthamidamārabhyate / tadarthameva cāpiśabdamācāryo 'dhijage / sambhāvanārthamapi ca pañcaviṣayāṇyetāni prāgeva tu catustriviṣayāṇīti /
  āha, kathametadavagamyate viśeṣāviśeṣaviṣayāṇīndriyāṇi, na punarasadviṣayāṇi iti ?
  ucyate- viśeṣāṇāmasattvāsiddheḥ / pratyakṣatastāvadviśeṣā upalabhyante / tasmādeṣāmasattvamaśakyaṃ pratijñātum / athāpi syātsādhyametatpratyakṣamevaitadanavadyam, bāhyavastuviṣayamayamṛgatṛṣṇikādivijñānavatpratyakṣābhāsam / etaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? vikalpānupapatteḥ / sarvamabhūtamabhyupagantavyam / yatra nāsti kiṃcid bhūtārthena pratyakṣaṃ yadapyekṣyetarat pratyakṣābhāsaṃ syāt / uktastvayaṃ vikalpaḥ / tasmādayuktaṃ jñānamātramidamiti / kiṃ cānyat / viparītadarśanaprasaṃgāt / mṛgatṛṣṇikāsvapnaviṣayairasadbhiḥ satāmasattvamicchatastadvadeva viparītadarśanaprasaṃgaḥ / tathā hi gandharvanagarādiṣu kadācittamevārthaṃ gāṃ paśyati, kaścidgajaṃ paśyati, kadācitpatākām / svapne caikamūrtipatitānāṃ gopuruṣāśvarāsabhanadīvṛkṣaprabhṛtīnāṃ darśanaṃ smaraṇe viparyayeṇa dṛṣṭam / tathā vātāyanena hastiyūthapraveśane___ / vicchinnānāṃ cāvayavānāṃ punaḥ sandhānaṃ ākāśagamanamanīśvarasyānimittaṃ rājyalābha iti / taditaratrāpi syāt / na tvasti / tasmādayuktaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇikāsvapnādivadasattvaṃ bhāvānām / arthakriyā ca na syāt / yathā svapne snātānuliptāśitapītavastrācchāditānāmaphalatvaṃ dṛṣṭam, evamihāpi syāt / śukravisargavaditi cet, syādetat- yathā dvayasamāptipūrvakaḥ śukravisargaḥ sa ca tadabhāve 'pi svapne bhavati, evamitaratsyāditi / tadayuktam, rāgādinimittatvāt / tathāhi jāgrato 'pi tat dvayasamāpattimantareṇa bhavati / tasmānmanorañjanānimittaṃ tat / pretavaditi cet syādiyaṃ mama sadbuddhiḥ, yathā pretānāmasadbhiḥpūyanadyādibhirarthakriyā, narakapālaiśca bādhanam / evamatrāpi syāditi / tadayuktam / asiddhatvāt / na hyetadasaditi siddham / kiṃca pratyakṣeṇa cāpratyakṣabādhanāt / iha pratyakṣaṃ balīya ityapratyakṣasya tena pratyākhyānamupapadyate / bhavantastvapratyakṣena pratyakṣaṃ pratyācakṣate / tasmādayuktaṃ narakalāpādivadasatāmarthakriyeti / svabhāvabhedāttadasattvamiti cet, syādetat- yadi paramārthato narakapālāḥ syusteṣāmapi duḥkhasambandhaḥ syāt, mūrtimattvāviśeṣāt / na
tu teṣāṃ bādhāsti / tasmād bhrāntirasāviti / etadayuktam / kasmāt ? karmaśaktivaicitryāt / pratyakṣameva tāvatkarmanimitto vāgbuddhisvabhāvāhāravihāraśaktibhedabhinno vicitraḥ saṃsāra upalabhyate / sa nipuṇamavekṣitumaśakyaḥ, gambhīratvāt / kiṃ punarapratyakṣakarmaṇāṃ vipākavaiśvarūpyamatarkagocaramasmadādibuddhayaḥ paricchetsyanti ? tasmānmanorathamātrametat / dharmādharmānupapattiśca syāt / yathā svapne brahmahatyāsurāpānāgamyagamanādīnāmaphalatvam, evamitaratrāpi syāt, asadaviśeṣāt / middhopaghātāttadviśeṣa iti cet na, aviśeṣāt / asattve tulye kvacidupaghātaḥ kvacinnetīcchāmātrametat / evaṃ cet nāsantaḥ pṛthivyādayaḥ / na cedasanto yuktamupadiṣṭaṃ buddhīndriyāṇi teṣāṃ pañca viśeṣāviśeṣaviṣayāṇīti // 34 //
children.translated_text: The hands, feet, anus, and reproductive organ — through actions characterized as grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure — modify material forms that consist of the aggregate of sound, touch, taste, form, and smell. One objects: if the restriction is accepted that [the active organs] have only five objects without distinction, then the consequence would be that actions such as grasping and the like cannot be performed by a single instrument. It is replied: no, because the purpose is to negate [such] restriction. The statement is made for the purpose of negating the restriction that the active sense organs, like the cognitive sense organs, should be known [as having only] their own specific objects. And for this purpose the master employed the particle 'api' (also). And [this is said] also for the purpose of indicating possibility — these have five objects; how much more so do they have four or three objects. One asks: how is it known that the sense organs have both specific and non-specific objects, and not objects that are non-existent? It is replied: because the non-existence of the specific [objects] is not established. For the specific [objects] are directly perceived. Therefore their non-existence cannot be asserted. If one further objects that this is what needs to be proved — perception itself is faultless, and [yet] this [perception], like the cognition of a mirage and the like, having external objects as its content, is a mere semblance of perception. But this is unjustified. Why? Because the alternative is untenable. Everything would have to be accepted as unreal. Where there is no true reality whatsoever, even that which is regarded as a semblance of perception would itself be a semblance. But this alternative has been stated [and refuted]. Therefore it is unjustified [to say] that this is mere cognition. Moreover, because of the consequence of inverted perception. For one who, on the basis of non-existent things like mirages and dream-objects, desires the non-existence of existing things — there would be the same consequence of inverted perception. For in the case of cities of the <s>gandharva</s>s and the like, sometimes that very object
Thus ends the seventh day's session in the glorious <s>Yuktidīpikā</s>.
<s>Kārikā</s> 35

children.text:
dvāridvārabhāvameṣāmidānīṃ vakṣyāmaḥ / tatra bāhyaṃ karaṇaṃ dvāram, antaḥkaraṇaṃ dvārīti /
  āha, karaṇāviśeṣādayuktam antaḥkaraṇasya hīndriyānāṃ ca karaṇatvamaviśiṣṭam / tatra ko heturantaḥkaraṇaṃ dvāri, dvārāṇīndriyāṇīti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text: We shall now explain the door-doorkeeper relationship among these [instruments]. There, the external instrument is the door, and the inner organ is the doorkeeper. One objects: this is unjustified because there is no distinction among the instruments. For the inner organ and the sense organs alike are instruments without distinction. What then is the reason [for saying] that the inner organ is the doorkeeper and the sense organs are the doors? It is replied:
<s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), together with the inner organ, encompasses every object;

children.text: tasmāt trividhaṃ karaṇaṃ dvāri dvārāṇi śeṣāṇi || 35 ||
children.translated_text: therefore the three-fold instrument is the doorkeeper, and the remaining [instruments] are the doors. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 35)

children.text:
sahāntaḥkaraṇena vartate yā sāntaḥkaraṇā buddhiḥ / ahaṃkāramanobhyāṃ sahitā buddhirityarthaḥ / atra cāntaḥkaraṇagrahaṇenaiva buddhergrahaṇe siddhe bhūyo buddhigrahaṇaṃ prādhānyakhyāpanārtham / bhavati hi pradhānasya sāmānye 'ntarbhūtasyāpi pṛthagupadeśaḥ / tadyathā
  jagāma taṃ vanoddeśaṃ vyāsaḥ saha maharṣibhiḥ /
  iti maharṣigrahaṇe vyāso 'pyantarbhūtaḥ prādhānyātpṛthagucyate, evaṃ sāntaḥkaraṇā buddhiḥ sarvaṃ viṣayamavagāhate, viśiṣṭānaviśiṣṭāṃśca śabdādīnsannikṛṣṭaviprakṛṣṭavyavahitānpramāṇabalena svavṛtte viṣayīkarotītyarthaḥ / etaduktaṃ bhavati aniyataviṣayo dvārī, niyataviṣayāṇi dvārāṇi / tadyathā prāsādasya pūrvottaradakṣiṇapaścimānāṃ svadiṅniyamo na pūrvamuttaraṃ dakṣiṇaṃ paścimaṃ vā kadācidbhavati, tathetarāṇyapi dvārīṇi / tatrāniyatāḥ sarvadigavasthitairdvāraiḥ pravartanta evamihāpi śrotrādīni svaviṣayaniyatāni / sāntaḥkaraṇā tu buddhiḥ sarvaṃ viṣayamavagāhate yasmāt tasmādaniyataviṣayatvādupapannamettrividhaṃ karaṇaṃ dvāri, dvārāṇi śeṣāṇīti // 35 //
children.translated_text: That which operates together with the inner organ is '<s>sāntaḥkaraṇā</s>' (accompanied by the inner organ) — <s>buddhi</s>. The meaning is: <s>buddhi</s> accompanied by <s>ahaṅkāra</s> and <s>manas</s>. Here, although the mention of <s>buddhi</s> is already accomplished by the word 'inner organ,' the additional mention of <s>buddhi</s> is for the purpose of indicating its pre-eminence. For there is a separate mention of the principal even when it is included in the general [term]. For example: '<s>Vyāsa</s> went to that forest region together with the great sages' — although <s>Vyāsa</s> is included in the reference to 'great sages,' he is mentioned separately due to his pre-eminence. Similarly, <s>buddhi</s> together with the inner organ encompasses every object — it brings within its scope sounds and the other [objects], both specific and non-specific, whether proximate, remote, or obstructed, by the force of the means of valid knowledge, making them conform to its own activity. The meaning is: it takes them in through the operation upon objects, and assigns them to <s>buddhi</s>, making them its own content. What is stated is this: the doorkeeper has unrestricted objects, while the doors have restricted objects. Just as in a palace, the northern, eastern, southern, and western [doors] have their own directional restriction — the eastern never becomes the northern, southern, or western — so too the other doors [i.e., sense organs]. But [the inhabitants], unrestricted [in direction], enter through the doors situated in all directions. So here too, hearing and the rest are restricted to their own objects. But <s>buddhi</s> together with the inner organ encompasses every object — therefore, because of the unrestricted nature of its objects, it is fitting that the three-fold instrument is the doorkeeper, and the remaining [instruments] are the doors.
<s>Kārikā</s> 36
These [instruments], which are like lamps, mutually distinct, and are modifications of the <s>guṇa</s>s,
having illuminated the entire purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>, present it to <s>buddhi</s>. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 36)

children.text: ete ityanena trayamabhisambadhnāti śrotrādīnāmanyatamaṃ mano 'haṃkāraśca / pradīpakalpā ityanena prakāśasāmyaṃ karaṇaparvaṇa ācaṣṭe, yathā pradīpaḥ prakāśaka evaṃ karaṇamapi, tadvyāpāre sati viṣayāvirbhāvānupapatteḥ / parasparavilakṣaṇa ityanena vyastavṛttiṃ pūrvoktāmākarṣati / tayā hyeṣāṃ vailakṣaṇyamanumīyate, ālocanasaṃkalpābhimānabhedāt / guṇaviśeṣā ityanena sattvādīnāṃ puruṣavijñānamuddiśya tadbhāvena pariṇāmaṃ khyāpayati / kṛtsnaṃ puruṣasyārthamiti viśeṣāviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ āhāryadhāryaprakāśyatayā yathāsambhavaṃ prakāśya svavṛttyanuguṇaṃ kṛtvā viṣayavyāpāreṇānubhūya buddhāvādhatte, atadviṣayatāmāpādayatītyarthaḥ / kadācittu buddhireva bāhyakaraṇasaṃkalpābhimānagṛhītam / sarvathā tvayaṃ śāstrārtho yena vā tena karaṇena viṣayamupāttaṃ buddhiradhyavasyati / tayā cādhyavasāyarūpāpannayā cetanāśaktiranugṛhyate na karaṇāntarasya puruṣeṇa samabandho 'sti / tataśca dvāriṇāṃ bahutvāttaddarśanaviśeṣasvātantryasamuccayāntaḥkaraṇapuruṣakartṛtvadoṣāṇāmaprasaṃgaḥ // 36 //
children.translated_text: By the word 'these,' he connects the three: one or another of hearing and the rest, <s>manas</s>, and <s>ahaṅkāra</s>. By 'like lamps,' he states the similarity to light of the stages of the instruments — just as a lamp illuminates, so too does the instrument, since without its operation the manifestation of the object would be untenable. By 'mutually distinct,' he draws in the separate activity mentioned before. For their distinctness is inferred through that [separate activity], due to the difference of apprehension, conceptualization, and self-assertion. By '<s>guṇaviśeṣa</s>s' (modifications of the <s>guṇa</s>s), he indicates the transformation of <s>sattva</s> and the rest into that form, directed toward the cognition of <s>puruṣa</s>. 'The entire purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>' — the effect characterized as both specific and non-specific — having illuminated it in the manner of being brought, held, and made manifest, as appropriate, and having made it conform to its own activity, and having experienced it through the operation upon objects, it deposits it in <s>buddhi</s>. The meaning is: it causes [<s>buddhi</s>] to have that as its object. Sometimes, however, <s>buddhi</s> itself [apprehends] what has been grasped by the external instruments, conceptualization, and self-assertion. In all cases, however, this is the import of the <s>śāstra</s>: <s>buddhi</s> ascertains the object apprehended by whichever instrument. And by [<s>buddhi</s>] which has taken on the form of ascertainment, the power of consciousness is favored — there is no direct connection of any other instrument with <s>puruṣa</s>. Therefore, because of the multiplicity of the doorkeepers, the faults of attributing to each doorkeeper independent perception, combined [perception], and agency of the inner organ and <s>puruṣa</s> do not arise.
<s>Kārikā</s> 37

children.text:
āha, kaḥ punaratra heturyena dvāritvāviśeṣe satyahaṃkāramanasī buddhau viṣayādhānaṃ kuruto na punaranayoḥ sākṣātpuruṣeṇa sambandha iti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text: One asks: what then is the reason why, despite there being no distinction in doorkeeper-status, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> and <s>manas</s> deposit objects in <s>buddhi</s>, and these two do not have a direct connection with <s>puruṣa</s>? It is replied:

children.text: sarva pratyupabhogaṃ yasmāt puruṣasya sādhayati buddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Because <s>buddhi</s> accomplishes all experience for <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text:
ahaṃkāramanasorhi, nāsti niścayarūpatā, saṃkalpābhimānamātrarūpatvāt / aniścitaviṣayayā ca karaṇavṛttyā puruṣasya samandho 'narthakaḥ syāt / svayaṃ vā niśceturasya kartṛtvaṃ syāt / tataścāmiśraniścayakāraṇatvādayamapyāmiśrarūpaḥ syāt / sarvaṃ caitaduktottaraṃ niścayarūpā hi buddhiḥ / atastadvṛttyupanipātī viṣayaḥ sannidhānamātrātpuruṣeṇa saṃcetito nāsyaudāsīnyaṃ bādhitumutsahate, no khalvapyānarthakyamanuṣajyate / etaduktaṃ sarvaṃ pratyupabhogaṃ yasmātpuruṣasya sādhayati buddhiriti /
  āha, evamapi śabdādilakṣaṇo viṣayaḥ prakṛtaḥ, sa ca buddhyā sarvaḥ pratipādyate / tatra viṣayāntaramapyasti pradhānapuruṣāntaralakṣaṇam / tathā cāhuḥ / "upabhogasya śabdādyupalabdhirādiḥ guṇapuruṣopalabdhirantaḥ" / tasmāttatpratipattyarthaṃ karaṇāntaraṃ vaktavyamiti /
  ucyate- na vaktavyam / kiṃ kāraṇam / yasmāt
children.translated_text: For <s>ahaṅkāra</s> and <s>manas</s> do not have the nature of determination — since they are merely of the nature of conceptualization and self-assertion. And the connection of <s>puruṣa</s> with an instrumental activity whose object is undetermined would be purposeless. Or he would himself have the agency of determining — and from that, since he would be the cause of a mixed determination, he too would be of a mixed nature. And all this has been answered: for <s>buddhi</s> has the nature of determination. Therefore the object that falls upon its activity, being merely proximate to <s>puruṣa</s>, is cognized [by him], and is not able to obstruct his indifference, nor is purposelessness incurred. This is what is meant by: 'because <s>buddhi</s> accomplishes all experience for <s>puruṣa</s>.' One objects: if so, the object under discussion is characterized as sounds and the like, and all of that is presented by <s>buddhi</s>. But there is also another object characterized as [the distinction between] <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>. As they say: 'The beginning of experience is the apprehension of sounds and the like; the end is the apprehension of the <s>guṇa</s>s and <s>puruṣa</s>.' Therefore, for the apprehension of that [distinction], another instrument must be stated. It is replied: it need not be stated. For what reason? Because —

children.text: saiva ca viśinaṣṭi punaḥ pradhānapuruṣāntaraṃ sūkṣmam || 37 ||
children.translated_text: that very [<s>buddhi</s>] also discriminates the subtle difference between <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 37)

children.text: yato yasmātkāraṇāt sā buddhireva hi kāṣṭhāpannena tamasābhibhūtatvāddharmādīnāṃ sattvadharmāṇāṃ prakṛtibhūtānvikārabhūtānparatantrānupakāryānupakārakānacetanānsaṃsargadharmiṇaśca guṇānātmatvenādhyavasya puruṣāyopaharati / sa ca mithyājñānābhyāsavāsanānurañjitaṃ buddhipratyayamanurudhyamāno darśitaviṣayatvāttathaiva pratipadyate / yadā tu dharmādyabhyāsāttamorūpāgame satyuttarottarāṇāṃ sattvadharmāṇamutkarṣastadā vinivṛttamithyāpratyayā vṛttiḥ / na prakṛtivikārabhūtaḥ svatantro 'nupakāryo 'nupakārakaścetano 'saṃsargadharmā ca / tato viparītāśca guṇā iti śuddhādhyavasāyaṃ karoti / puruṣaśca paropahṛtapravṛttitvāttathaiva pratipadyate / tadetad guṇānāṃ puruṣasya cāntaraṃ dvayorapi niścayasvabhāvatvādasmātpūrvoktadharmabhede 'pi sati sūkṣmaṃ gambhīraṃ durjñeyam / ataśca sūkṣmaṃ yad buddhimātramavalambya tadaviśiṣṭāyāścetanāśakaktergrāhyagrāhaka_____ // 37 //
children.translated_text: Because — for the reason that — that <s>buddhi</s> itself, when <s>tamas</s> has reached its culmination, being dominated [by it], ascertains the <s>guṇa</s>s — which are properties of <s>sattva</s> such as <s>dharma</s> and the rest, which belong to <s>prakṛti</s> and its modifications, which are dependent, helpful and to-be-helped, non-conscious, and subject to conjunction — as the self, and presents them to <s>puruṣa</s>. And he, <s>puruṣa</s>, conforming to the cognition of <s>buddhi</s> which is colored by the latent impression of the habitual practice of false knowledge, and having been shown [this] object, understands it in just that way. But when, through the practice of <s>dharma</s> and the rest, the form of <s>tamas</s> retreats and there is a progressive increase in the properties of <s>sattva</s> — then the activity whose false cognition has been eliminated [ascertains]: 'This is not a product of <s>prakṛti</s>, not dependent, not to-be-helped-or-helping, but conscious and not subject to conjunction. And the <s>guṇa</s>s are contrary [to this].' Thus it produces a pure ascertainment. And <s>puruṣa</s>, whose activity is directed by another, understands it in just that way. This difference between the <s>guṇa</s>s and <s>puruṣa</s> — because the nature of both is [apprehended through] determination — even when the previously stated difference of properties exists, is subtle, profound, and hard to know. And therefore, being subtle and depending on <s>buddhi</s> alone, [it is grasped] by the undifferentiated power of consciousness through [the relation of] grasped and grasper.
<s>Kārikā</s> 38

children.text:
vyākhyātaṃ karaṇaparva / kāryaparvedānīṃ vaktavyam / tasya ca purastāduddeśaḥ kṛtaḥ- kāryaṃ ca tasya daśadhā pañca viśeṣā iti / sāmprataṃ tu nirdeśaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ /
  āha, yadyevaṃ tasmādidameva tāvaducyatāṃ ke viśeṣāḥ, ke 'viśeṣā iti /
  ucyate-
children.translated_text: The stage of the instruments has been explained. Now the stage of the effects must be stated. Its enumeration was given earlier: 'And its effect is tenfold — five specific [and five non-specific].' Now we shall give the exposition. One says: if so, then let this first be stated — what are the specific, and what are the non-specific? It is replied:
The <s>tanmātra</s>s (subtle elements) are the non-specific.

children.text:
yāni tanmātrāṇi pañcāhaṃkārādutpadyante iti prāgapadiṣṭam / te khalvaviśeṣāḥ / kāni punastanmātrāṇītyucyate śabdatanmātraṃ, sparśatanmātraṃ, rūpatanmātraṃ, rasatanmātraṃ, gandhatanmātramiti /
  kathaṃ punastanmātrāṇīti ?
  ucyate- tulyajātīyaviśeṣānupapatteḥ / anye śabdajātyabhede 'pi /
  sati viśeṣā udātānudāttasvaritānunāsikādayastatra na santi tasmācchabdatanmātram / evaṃ sparśatanmātre mṛdukaṭhinādayaḥ / evaṃ rūpatanmātre śuklakṛṣṇādayaḥ / evaṃ rasatanmātre madhurāmlādayaḥ / evaṃ gandhatanmātre surabhyādayaḥ / tasmāttasya tasya guṇasya sāmānyamevātra, na viśeṣa iti tanmātrāsvete 'viśeṣāḥ /
  āha, atha ke punarviśeṣā iti ?
  ucyate- yāni khalu
children.translated_text:
It was previously stated that the five <s>tanmātra</s>s (subtle elements) arise from <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle). They are indeed the non-specifics (<s>aviśeṣa</s>). What, then, are the <s>tanmātra</s>s? It is said: the <s>tanmātra</s> of sound, the <s>tanmātra</s> of touch, the <s>tanmātra</s> of form, the <s>tanmātra</s> of taste, and the <s>tanmātra</s> of smell.
  How are they '<s>tanmātra</s>s' (mere-thats)?
  It is replied: Because specific varieties of the same class are not possible. Others [say]: even though there is no difference in the class of sound,
  the specificities such as raised (<s>udātta</s>), low (<s>anudātta</s>), circumflex (<s>svarita</s>), nasal (<s>anunāsika</s>), etc. exist there [in gross sound] but do not exist here [in the <s>tanmātra</s>]. Therefore it is a <s>śabdatanmātra</s> (sound-<s>tanmātra</s>). Likewise, in the touch-<s>tanmātra</s>, [specific qualities like] soft, hard, etc. [are absent]. Likewise, in the form-<s>tanmātra</s>, white, black, etc. [are absent]. Likewise, in the taste-<s>tanmātra</s>, sweet, sour, etc. [are absent]. Likewise, in the smell-<s>tanmātra</s>, fragrant, etc. [are absent]. Therefore, only the generic quality of each sense-quality is present here, not the specific — hence these are the non-specifics (<s>aviśeṣa</s>) among the <s>tanmātra</s>s.
  [The objector] asks: What, then, are the specifics (<s>viśeṣa</s>)?
  It is replied: Those which indeed —
From those [<s>tanmātra</s>s], the five gross elements (<s>bhūta</s>s) arise, from the five,
they are produced.
These are called the specifics (<s>viśeṣa</s>s).

children.text: tatra śabdatanmātrādākāśam, sparśatanmātrādvāyuḥ, rūpatanmātrāttejaḥ, rasatanmātrādāpaḥ, gandhatanmātrātpṛthivī / tebhyo bhūtānītyetāvati vaktavye pañca pañcabhya iti grahaṇaṃ samasaṃkhyākatastadutpattijñāpanārtham / tenaikaikasmāttanmātrādekaikasya viśeṣasyotpattiḥ siddhā / tataśca yadanyeṣāmācāryāṇāmabhipretam ekalakṣaṇebhyastanmātrebhyaḥ parasparānupraveśādekottarā viśeṣāḥ sṛjyanta iti tatpratiṣiddhaṃ bhavati / kintarhi antareṇāpi tanmātrānupraveśamekottarebhyo bhūtebhya ekottarāṇāṃ bhūtaviśeṣāṇāmutpattiḥ / tatra śabdaguṇācchabdatanmātrādākāśamekaguṇam, śabdasparśaguṇātsparśatanmātrāddviguṇo vāyuḥ, śabdasparśarūpaguṇādrūpatanmātrāttriguṇaṃ tejaḥ, śabdasparśarūparasaguṇādrasatanmātrāccaturguṇā āpaḥ, śabdasparśarūparasagandhād gandhatanmātrātpañcaguṇā pṛthivī / atra ca vāyoḥ śītaḥ sparśa apāṃ ca, tejasa uṣṇaḥ, anuṣṇāśītaḥ pṛthivyāḥ / rūpaṃ ca śuklaṃ bhāsvaraṃ ca tejaso 'pāṃ ca, kṛṣṇaṃ pṛthivyāḥ / raso madhuro 'pām, sādhāraṇaḥ pṛthivyāḥ / gandhastu pārthiva eva tadavayavānupraveśādbhūtāntareṣūpalabhyate / ityete pṛthivyādīnāṃ dharmāḥ / anye ca parasparānugrāhakāḥ / ke punasta ityāha-
ākāro gaurāṃ raukṣyaṃ varaṇaṃ sthairyameva ca /
children.translated_text: Shape, heaviness, roughness, covering, firmness,
stability, division, forbearance, dark-shadedness, and being the object of all enjoyment —

Of these, from the sound-<s>tanmātra</s> [arises] space (<s>ākāśa</s>), from the touch-<s>tanmātra</s> wind (<s>vāyu</s>), from the form-<s>tanmātra</s> fire (<s>tejas</s>), from the taste-<s>tanmātra</s> water (<s>āpas</s>), from the smell-<s>tanmātra</s> earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>). Where it would suffice to say 'from them the elements arise,' the phrase 'five from the five' is used for the purpose of indicating that each arises from its corresponding [<s>tanmātra</s>] in equal number. Thereby, the production of each specific from each individual <s>tanmātra</s> is established. And consequently, the view held by other teachers — that the specifics are created with successive additional [qualities] through mutual interpenetration of the single-charactered <s>tanmātra</s>s — is refuted. Rather, even without the interpenetration of <s>tanmātra</s>s, the production of elements with successive additional qualities occurs from the elements with successive additional [qualities]. Thus: from the sound-<s>tanmātra</s> with the quality of sound, space (<s>ākāśa</s>) has one quality; from the touch-<s>tanmātra</s> with the qualities of sound and touch, wind (<s>vāyu</s>) has two qualities; from the form-<s>tanmātra</s> with the qualities of sound, touch, and form, fire (<s>tejas</s>) has three qualities; from the taste-<s>tanmātra</s> with the qualities of sound, touch, form, and taste, water (<s>āpas</s>) has four qualities; from the smell-<s>tanmātra</s> with sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) has five qualities. And here: the touch of wind is cold, and of water too; of fire it is hot; of earth it is neither hot nor cold. The form of fire is white and luminous, and of water too; of earth it is dark. The taste of water is sweet; of earth it is common [i.e., varied]. Smell, however, belongs only to earth; it is perceived in other elements due to the penetration of earth-particles. These are the properties of earth and the rest. And there are others that mutually assist one another. What are they? He says:
these are the properties of earth. The others, distinguished from these,
are the pervasive [properties] of water, fire, wind, and space — know them!

children.text: snehaḥ saukṣmyaṃ prabhā śauklyaṃ mārdavaṃ gauravaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: Moistness, subtlety, luster, whiteness, softness, heaviness,
coolness, nourishment, purity, and continuity — these are the qualities of water.

children.text: ūrdhvagaṃ pāvakaṃ dagdhṛ pācakaṃ laghu bhāsvaram /
children.translated_text: Upward-moving, purifying, burning, cooking, light, luminous,
destructive, vigorous, bright — [fire is] different in character from the previous two.
Lateral movement, purity, propelling, impelling, strength,
roughness, shadowlessness, coldness — these are the various properties of wind.
All-pervading movement, non-arrangement, and extension — these three
are known as the properties of space, which are contrary to the properties of the preceding [elements].

children.text: saṃhatānāṃ tu yatkāryaṃ sāmānyaṃ te gavādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The common effect of these [elements] when combined is [the production of things like] cows and the like.
From the properties of each element [come] the specific [characteristics] — there is no doubt about this.

children.text:
tatrākārādidharmaiḥ pṛthivyā lokasya copakriyate bhūtāntarāṇāṃ ca / tatrākārāttāvat gavādīnāṃ ghaṭādīnāṃ cākāranirvṛttiḥ gauravādeṣāmavasthānam / raukṣyādapāṃ saṃgraho vaiśadyaṃ ca bhūtānām / varaṇādanabhipretānāṃ chādanam / sthairyādvṛttiḥ prajānāṃ bhūtāntarāṇāṃ ca / sthitermātrādisannidhānādyanugrahaḥ / bhedādghaṭādiniṣpattiḥ / vyūhaścāvayavānām / kṣānterupabhogabhogyatā / kṛṣṇacchāyatvādrātrisampacchāyākāryaprasiddhiśca / sarvopabhogyatvātsarvabhūtānugrahaḥ / evaṃ snehādibhirlokasyopakāraḥ kriyate bhūtāntarāṇāṃ ca / snehādrūpasaṃpadvāyupratīkāro 'gniśamanaṃ saṃgrahaśca pṛthivyāḥ / saukṣmyādanupraveśaḥ / śauklyāccandrādvinirvṛttiḥ / mārdavātsnānāvagāhanamekakriyā kaṭhinānām cāvanāmanam / gauravātsantānācca bhūtānugrahārthaṃ srotastvam / śaityāduṣṇapratīkāraḥ / rakṣātaḥ prajāsu ghoraśamanam / pavitratvāddharmopacayaḥ śaucavidhiralakṣyopaghātaśca / santānāddravyasaṃghātaḥ / tathordhvagatyādibhirdharmamātraistejasāṃ lokasya copakriyate bhūtāntarāṇāṃ ca / ūrdhvagateḥ pākaprakāśasiddhiḥ / pāvakatvād dravyaśaucaṃ ca / dāhakatvātkṣārotpattiḥ / śītapratīkāro nabhasaścoṣṇatvaṃ śabdaniṣpattyartham / pācakatvātsvedya svedanamannapaktiḥ pṛthivyavayavānāṃ kriyāyogyatā, tathā bāhyāntarapariṇāmaḥ, rasalohitamāṃsasnāyvasthimajjāśukrāṇāṃ lāghavāddāhyātikramaḥ / bhāsvaratvāddravyāntaraprakāśanam / pradhvaṃsitvāddagdhapakvānāmupabhogaḥ / taijasaḥ prajāpālanam / tathā tiryakpātādibhirdharmairvāyunā lokasya copakāraḥ kriyate bhūtāntarāṇāṃ ca / tiryakpātāddṛṣṭivikṣepo gandhasaṃvahanaṃ ca / pavitratvātpūtidravyapavanam / ākṣepanodanābhyāmutkarṣaḥ prathamaṃ dharmāmbhasaḥ / vyūhaśca śarīre rasādīnāṃ dhātūnāṃ ca / agneścopadhmānamabhidhātaścākāśasya / balātsamīkaraṇaṃ sarveṣām / raukṣyādviśoṣaṇam / acchāyatvādahorātraprasiddhiḥ /
śaityāduṣṇapratīkāraḥ / tathā sarvatogatyādibhirdharmairnabhasā lokasyopakāraḥ kriyate bhūtāntarāṇāṃ ca / sarvatogateḥ samantāttulyadeśaśravaṇanāmekaśrutitvam / avyūhaviṣkambhābhyāṃ sarveṣāmavakāśatādānamityuktāḥ pṛthivyādayaḥ / ete viśeṣā ityucyanta iti /
  āha, kathaṃ punarete viśeṣā ityucyante ?
  yasmāt
children.translated_text:
Of these, earth benefits the world and the other elements through its properties of shape, etc. Through shape, the formation of cows, pots, and the like. Through heaviness, their stability. Through roughness, the absorption and clarity of waters and elements. Through covering, the concealment of undesired things. Through firmness, the sustenance of beings and other elements. Through stability, the support provided by the proximity of a mother, etc. Through division, the production of pots and the like. And the arrangement of parts. Through forbearance, the capacity for enjoyment and being enjoyed. Through dark-shadedness, the establishment of night, shade, and shadow-effects. Through being the object of all enjoyment, the benefit of all beings.
  Thus, through moistness and the rest, water benefits the world and the other elements. Through moistness, the excellence of form, counteraction of wind, quenching of fire, and binding of earth. Through subtlety, penetration. Through whiteness, production from the moon. Through softness, bathing and immersion as a single action, and the bending of hard things. Through heaviness and continuity, becoming streams for the benefit of beings. Through coolness, counteraction of heat. Through nourishment, the pacification of what is terrible among creatures. Through purity, the accumulation of <s>dharma</s>, the rite of purification, and the destruction of unseen impurities. Through continuity, the binding of substances.
  Likewise, through upward movement and the rest, fire benefits the world and other elements through its properties alone. Through upward movement, the accomplishment of cooking and illumination. Through purifying nature, the purification of substances. Through burning capacity, the production of alkali. The counteraction of cold and the heating of space for the purpose of producing sound. Through cooking capacity, the sweating of what should be sweated, the cooking of food, the fitness of earth-particles for activity, and likewise the internal and external transformation of chyle, blood, flesh, sinew, bone, marrow, and semen. Through lightness, the surpassing of what should be burned. Through luminosity, the illumination of other substances. Through destructiveness, the enjoyment of what is burned and cooked. Fire protects beings.
  Likewise, through lateral movement and the rest, wind benefits the world and other elements through its properties. Through lateral movement, the dispersal of vision and the carrying of smells. Through purity, the purification of foul substances. Through propelling and impelling, the initial elevation of the waters of <s>dharma</s>. And the arrangement of sap and other bodily constituents in the body. And the fanning of fire and the filling of space. Through strength, the equalization of all. Through roughness, desiccation. Through shadowlessness, the establishment of day and night. Through coolness, the counteraction of heat.
  Likewise, through all-pervading movement and the rest, space benefits the world and other elements through its properties. Through all-pervading movement, the equal hearing in all directions — having a single tone. Through non-arrangement and extension, the providing of room for all. Thus earth and the rest have been described. They are called 'specifics' (<s>viśeṣa</s>).
  [The objector] asks: How are these called specifics?
  Because —
[They are] peaceful, violent, and deluding. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 38 //

children.text: tatra śāntāstāvat svasaṃskāraviśeṣayogāttatsannidhau prasādādidharmotpatteḥ / ghorāstu śeṣādidharmanimittatvāt / mūḍhāśca varaṇādidharmahetutvāt / tanmātrāṇi punaraśāntaghoramūḍhāni ato 'viśeṣā ityucyante / tadete yathā vyākhyātā aviśeṣā viśeṣāḥ puruṣārthasiddhyarthaṃ bahudhā vyavatiṣṭhante / kasmāt ? na hyeteṣāmekadhāvasthāne puruṣārthaḥ siddhyatīti // 38 //
children.translated_text: Of these, 'peaceful' — because of the connection with a specific disposition, in its proximity properties such as clarity arise. 'Violent' — because of the connection with a specific disposition, in its proximity properties such as burning arise. 'Deluding' — because of the connection with a specific disposition, in its proximity properties such as heaviness arise. And the gross elements have these three [natures] together.
<s>Kārikā</s> 39

children.text:
āha, atisāmānyoktamidamityato na pratipadyāmahe / tasmādvaktavyaṃ kathaṃ viśeṣaṇāmavasthānamiti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text: [The objector] says: What has been stated is too general, and therefore we do not understand it. Therefore, it should be stated: how are the specifics (<s>viśeṣa</s>s) qualified? It is replied:

children.text: sūkṣmā mātāpitṛjāḥ saha prabhūtaistridhā viśeṣāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: [There are] subtle (<s>sūkṣma</s>), born of mother and father (<s>mātāpitṛja</s>), together with the gross (<s>prabhūta</s>) — the specifics (<s>viśeṣa</s>s) should be threefold.

children.text:
tatra sūkṣmā nāma ceṣṭāśritaṃ prāṇāṣṭakaṃ saṃsarati / mātṛpitṛjāstu dvividhāḥ / jarāyujā aṇḍajāśca / teṣāṃ kośopahṛtāḥ kośāḥ lomarudhiramāṃsāsthisnāyuśukralakṣaṇaḥ / tatra lomarudhiramāṃsānāṃ mātṛtaḥ sambhavaḥ / asthisnāyuśukrāṇāṃ pitṛtaḥ / tatraivāśitapītādhyāsā daṣṭau kośānapare vyācakṣate /
  kathaṃ punareṣāṃ kośatvam ?
  āveṣṭanasāmarthyāt / yathā kośakāraḥ kośenāveṣṭito 'svatantraḥ, evaṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ saprāṇametairāveṣṭitamasvatantraṃ tattatkarmopacinoti /
  prabhūtāstūdbhijjāḥ svedajāśca tadetaistrividhairdaivamānavatairyagyonalakṣaṇastrividho bhūtasarga ārabhyate / tatra devānāṃ caturvidhaṃ śarīraṃ pradhānānugrahāt, yathā paramarṣerviriñcasya ca / tatsiddhibhyo yathā brahmaṇaḥ putrāṇāṃ tatputraputrāṇāṃ ca / mātāpitṛto yathāditeḥ kaśyapasya ca putrāṇām / kevalādvā yathā pitṛto mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ vaśiṣṭhasya / manuṣyāṇāṃ tu jarāyujam / dharmaśaktiviśeṣāttu kasyacidanyathāpi bhavati / yathā droṇakṛpakṛpīdhṛṣṭadyumnādīnām / tiryagyonīnāmapi caturvidham

children.translated_text: The viviparous [body is that] of cows and the like; the oviparous, of birds;
the plant-born, of grasses and the like; and that of tiny creatures is called sweat-born.

Of these, the subtle [body] is that which transmigrates as the octad of vital breaths (<s>prāṇāṣṭaka</s>) dependent on activity. The mother-father-born, however, are of two kinds: viviparous (<s>jarāyuja</s>) and oviparous (<s>aṇḍaja</s>). Their sheaths (<s>kośa</s>) are characterized by hair, blood, flesh, bone, sinew, and semen. Of these, hair, blood, and flesh originate from the mother; bone, sinew, and semen from the father. Others explain the sheaths as consisting of what is eaten and drunk, overlying the two [parental contributions].
  How are they 'sheaths'?
  Because of [their] capacity for enveloping. Just as a silkworm, enveloped by its cocoon, is not independent, so too the subtle body, together with the vital breaths, enveloped by these [sheaths], is not independent and accumulates the various <s>karma</s>s.
  The gross (<s>prabhūta</s>) [specifics] are the plant-born (<s>udbhijja</s>) and sweat-born (<s>svedaja</s>). With these three kinds — divine, human, and animal — the threefold creation of beings is undertaken. Among the gods, the body is of four kinds, through the special grace of <s>pradhāna</s>: as in the case of the supreme <s>Ṛṣi</s> and <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>); through attainments, as in the case of the sons of <s>Brahmā</s> and their sons' sons; through mother and father, as in the case of the sons of <s>Aditi</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s>; or from one parent alone, as in the case of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> from <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> on the father's side. For humans, however, [the body is] viviparous. But through a special force of <s>dharma</s>, it may be otherwise for some — as in the case of <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Kṛpī</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, and others. For animals too, [the body] is of four kinds.

children.text:
evaṃ trividhā viśeṣā vyākhyātāḥ /
  tatra kecinniyatāḥ kecidaniyatā ityāha- ke punaratra niyatāḥ, ke vāniyatāḥ ?

children.translated_text: The subtle [bodies] among them are permanent; the mother-father-born ones cease. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 39 //

Thus the threefold specifics have been explained.
  Of these, some are permanent and some are not permanent. He says: Which, then, [are permanent and which are not]?

children.text:
sūkṣmā āsargapralayānnityāḥ mātṛpitṛjā nivartante / saha prabhūtairiti vartate / kecittu prabhūtagrahaṇena bāhyānāmeva viśeṣāṇāṃ grahaṇamicchanti / teṣāmudbhijjasvedajayoragrahaṇam / tasmādubhayathā prabhūtā ityetadanavadyam /
  āha, sūkṣmābhidhānamaprasiddhatvāt / mātāpitṛjāśca prabhūtāśca ityato yukta eṣāṃ parigrahaḥ / sūkṣmāstvaprasiddhā / tasmādvaktavyaṃ kathameṣāmutpattirastitvaṃ veti ?
  ucyate- pūrvasarge prakṛterupapannānāṃ prāṇināṃ sattvadharmotkarṣādantareṇa dvayasamāpattiṃ manasaivāpatyamanyadvā yathepsitaṃ prādurbabhūva / priyaṃ khalvapi cakṣuṣā nirīkṣya kṛtārthamātmānaṃ manyate / tasyāmapi kṣīṇāyāṃ vāksiddhirbabhūva / abhibhāṣya prāṇino yadicchanti tadāpādayanti / tadadyāpyanuvartate- yacchaṅkhī virutenāpatyaṃ bibharti / priyaṃ khalvapi sambhāṣya mahatīṃ prītimanubhavati / tasyāmupakṣīṇāyāṃ hastasiddhirbabhūva / saṃspṛśya pāṇimīpsitamarthamupapādayanti / tadetadadyāpyanuvartate- yatpriyaṃ cirādālokya pāṇau saṃspṛśya prītirbhavati / asyāmupakṣīṇāyāmāśleṣasiddhirbabhūva / āliṅganena prāṇina īpsitaṃ labhante / tadetadadyāpyanuvartate- yatpriyamāliṅgya nirvṛttirbhavati / tasyāmupakṣīṇāyāṃ dvandvasiddhirārabdhā / strīpuṃsau saṃdhṛṣyāpatyamutpādayetāṃ mamedaṃ mamedamiti ca parigrahāḥ pravṛttāḥ / etasminnevāvasare saṃsāro varṇyate /
  tatra cācāryāṇāṃ vipratipattiḥ / pañcādhikaraṇasya tāvadvaivartaṃ śarīraṃ mātāpitṛsaṃsargakāle karaṇāviṣṭaṃ śukraśoṇitamanupraviśati / tadanupraveśācca kalalādibhāvena vivardhate / vyūḍhāvayavaṃ tūpalabdhapratyayaṃ māturudarānnissṛtya yau dharmādharmau ṣaṭsiddhyupabhogakāle kṛtau tadvaśādavatiṣṭhate / yāvattatkṣayāccharīrapātastāvat / yadi dharmasaṃskṛtaṃ karaṇaṃ tato dyudeśaṃ sūkṣmaśarīreṇa prāpyate, tadviparyayāttu yātanāsthānaṃ tiryagyoniṃ vā, miśrībhāvena mānuṣyam / evamātivāhikaṃ sūkṣmaśarīramindriyāṇāṃ dhāraṇaprāpaṇasamarthaṃ nityaṃ bāhyenāpāyinā pariveṣṭyate parityajyate ca / patañjalestu sūkṣmaśarīraṃ yatsiddhikāle pūrvamindriyāṇi bījadeśaṃ nayati tatra tatkṛtāśayavaśāt dyudeśaṃ yātanāsthānaṃ vā karaṇāni vā prāpayya nivartate / tatra caivaṃ yuktāśayasya karmavaśādanyadutpadyate yadindriyāṇi bījadeśaṃ nayati tadapi nivartate, śarīrapāte cānyadutpadyate / evamanekāni śarīrāṇi / vindhyavāsinastu vibhutvādindriyāṇāṃ bījadeśe vṛttyā janma / tattyāgo maraṇam / tasmānnāsti sūkṣmaśarīram / tasmānnirviśeṣaḥ saṃsāra iti pakṣaḥ / eṣā sūkṣmaśarīrasyotpattiḥ // 39 //
children.translated_text:
The subtle [bodies] are permanent from creation to dissolution; the mother-father-born ones cease. 'Together with the gross ones' is to be supplied. Some, however, by the word 'gross' (<s>prabhūta</s>) wish to include only the external specifics. Their [view leads to] the non-inclusion of plant-born and sweat-born. Therefore, in both ways, 'gross' — this is unobjectionable.
  [The objector] says: The mention of the subtle [body] is [problematic] because it is not well-established. Mother-father-born and gross — these are fit for acceptance. But the subtle [bodies] are not well-established. Therefore, it should be stated: how does their production or existence [come about]?
  It is replied: In the first creation, among beings arising from <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), through the excellence of the <s>dharma</s> of <s>sattva</s>, without the union of a couple, offspring and other desired things were produced by mind alone. Indeed, even [now] one looks at a beloved with the eyes and considers oneself fulfilled. When that [power] was exhausted, the power of speech arose. By addressing beings, they brought about whatever they desired. This still continues — as when a conch-blower sustains offspring through its call. Indeed, by conversing with a beloved, one experiences great joy. When that [power] was diminished, the power of the hand arose. By touching with the hand, they brought about the desired object. This too still continues — as when, after looking at a beloved for a long time, there is joy from touching with the hand. When that [power] was diminished, the power of embrace arose. Through embrace, beings obtained what they desired. This too still continues — as when there is fulfillment from embracing a beloved. When that [power] was diminished, the power of coupling began. A man and a woman, joining together, would produce offspring, and possessiveness arose — 'this is mine, this is mine.' It is at this very juncture that <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) is described.
  There is disagreement among teachers on this matter. According to the five-substrate theory, the body which is a product of transformation enters the semen and blood at the time of the parents' union, infused with the [subtle] instrument. And through that entry, it grows in the form of an embryo (<s>kalala</s>), etc. When the limbs are developed and cognition is obtained, having emerged from the mother's womb, it abides under the influence of the <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> that were performed during the period of the six attainments and enjoyment — until bodily death from the exhaustion of those [karmas]. If the instrument is conditioned by <s>dharma</s>, then the celestial realm is reached with the subtle body; if the opposite, the place of torment or an animal birth; through a mixture, [one attains] humanity. Thus the transmigrating subtle body (<s>ātivāhika</s>), capable of carrying and conveying the senses, being permanent, is enveloped by an impermanent external [gross body] and released from it.
  According to <s>Patañjali</s>, however, the subtle body first conveys the senses to the seed-place at the time of attainment. There, under the influence of the dispositions (<s>āśaya</s>) created by it, having conveyed the instruments to the celestial realm or the place of torment, it withdraws. And there, for one with appropriate dispositions, through the force of <s>karma</s>, another [subtle body] arises which conveys the senses to the seed-place — that too withdraws; and at bodily death, another arises. Thus there are many bodies.
  According to <s>Vindhyavāsin</s>, however, birth is through the activity of the senses at the seed-place, due to the all-pervasive nature [of the self]. The abandonment of that is death. Therefore, there is no subtle body. Therefore, <s>saṃsāra</s> is without specifics — this is his position. This is the origin of the subtle body. // 39 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 40

children.text:
āha, evamanekaniścayeṣvācāryeṣu bhavataḥ kā pratipattiriti ?
  ucyate- yattāvatpatañjalirāha sūkṣmaśarīraṃ vinivartate punaścānyadutpadyate, tat sūkṣmāsteṣāṃ niyatā iti vacanādasmābhirnābhyupagamyate / tasmāt
children.translated_text:
[The objector] says: When there is disagreement among many teachers, what is your position?
  It is replied: First, as for what is —
Produced prior [to the gross body], unattached, permanent, [extending] from <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) to the subtle elements,
the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) transmigrates, without enjoyment, imbued with dispositions (<s>bhāva</s>s). // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 40 //

children.text: tatra pūrvotpannamityanena mahadādeḥ sūkṣmaparyantasya liṅgasyāsargapralayānnityatvamāha / asaktamityanena gūḍhasthirabījānupraveśamācaṣṭe / na hi liṅgaṃ kvacidvyāhanyate, kiṃ tarhi likṣādi bījamapyāviśati / badaragolamapi bhitvā praviśati / niyatamityanena pratipuruṣavyavasthāṃ pratijānāti / sādhāraṇo hi mahānprakṛtitvāditi vārṣagaṇānāṃ pakṣaḥ / mahadādītyanena prāṇāṣṭakaṃ parigṛhṇāti pūrvātmānaḥ prāṇādyāśca pañca vāyava iti / sūkṣmaparyantamiti tattvāntarapratiṣedhamāha, etāvadeva nāto 'nyaditi / saṃsaratīti gatimācaṣṭe, tataścāvibhutvād bījāveśatyāgau prakhyāto bhavataḥ / nirupabhogamiti śarīrāntarasyāvakāśaṃ karoti / sūkṣmaśarīrasya hyupabhogasāmarthye 'bhyupagamyamāne śarīrāntarasya niravakāśatvādanutpattiprasaṃgaḥ syāt / bhāvairadhivāsitamityanena bhāvāṣṭakaparigrahaṃ dyotayati / buddhirūpairiha dharmādibhiradhivāsitam / tatsāmarthyātsarvatrāpratihataṃ prāṇāṣṭakaṃ sūkṣmaśarīre 'vasthānagamanamātraphale vyavasthitam / dyutiryakpreteṣu saṃsaratīti tenaiva cārthasiddhau śarīrāntaraparikalpanānarthakyamato na bahūni śarīrāṇi // 40 //
children.translated_text: Here, by the word 'primordially produced' (<s>pūrvotpanna</s>), he states the permanence of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), from <s>Mahat</s> (the Great One) down to the subtle elements, due to its persistence through creation and dissolution. By the word 'unattached' (<s>asakta</s>), he indicates its entering into hidden, stable seeds — for the <s>liṅga</s> is never obstructed anywhere; rather, it enters even a seed as small as a louse-egg, and it penetrates even through a jujube fruit by splitting it open. By the word 'constant' (<s>niyata</s>), he asserts a fixed assignment to each <s>Puruṣa</s> (individual soul). For the view of the <s>Vārṣagaṇas</s> is that <s>Mahat</s> is shared, since it has the nature of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). By the expression 'beginning with <s>Mahat</s>,' he includes the group of eight — <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the rest — as the prior selves, along with the five winds beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>. By 'ending with the subtle' (<s>sūkṣmaparyanta</s>), he negates any additional principles, meaning 'this much only, nothing beyond this.' By 'transmigrates' (<s>saṃsarati</s>), he indicates movement, and from that, since it is non-pervasive, the entering into and departing from seeds becomes well-known. By 'without experience' (<s>nirupabhoga</s>), he makes room for another body; for if the capacity for experience were admitted for the subtle body itself, then due to there being no need for another body, the absurd consequence would follow that it would never arise. By 'perfumed by the dispositions' (<s>bhāvair adhivāsitam</s>), he indicates the inclusion of the eightfold <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions) — perfumed by <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and the rest, which are of the nature of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). By virtue of those, the group of eight beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>, unobstructed everywhere, is established in the subtle body with the sole function of abiding and moving. It transmigrates among gods, humans, and departed spirits. And since the purpose is accomplished by that alone, the postulation of another body would be purposeless — therefore there are not many bodies. // 40 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 41

children.text: yatpunaretaduktam- vibhutvādindriyāṇāṃ svātmanyavasthānaṃ vṛttilābho vṛttinirodhaśca saṃsāra iti, ayuktametat / kasmāt ? vibhutvāsiddheḥ / na hi vibhutvamindriyāṇāṃ kaścidabhyupagacchati / kiṃ kāraṇam ? satatopalabdhiprasaṃgāt / yugapadupalabdhiprasaṃgācca / kāryakaraṇapuruṣāṇāṃ hi vibhutve satatopalabdhiprasaṃgaḥ / viṣayāṇāṃ pratibandhābhāvātprasajyate / prātpyaviśeṣācca sarvaviśeṣāṇāṃ yugapadupalabdhiprasaṃgaḥ / vyavahitaviṣayagrahaṇaṃ ca / sarvatra sannidhānātsannikṛṣṭaviprakṛṣṭayoḥ pratyakṣānumānāgamānāṃ cāviśeṣaḥ prasajyate / vṛttiviśeṣāttadviśeṣa iti cet na, hetvabhāvāt / vibhūnāmihāsti vṛttiviśeṣa ityatra heturanuktaḥ / tasmānna karaṇānāṃ vibhutvamupapadyate / tasmāt
children.translated_text: Now, as to what was stated — that on account of the all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>) of the sense organs, their abiding in their own self, the attainment of function, and the cessation of function constitute <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) — this is untenable. Why? Because all-pervasiveness is not established. For no one accepts the all-pervasiveness of the sense organs. What is the reason? Because of the absurd consequence of perpetual perception. And because of the absurd consequence of simultaneous perception. For if the effect, the instrument, and <s>Puruṣa</s> were all-pervasive, the absurd consequence of perpetual perception would follow, since there would be no obstruction of objects. And because there would be no difference in contact, the absurd consequence of simultaneous perception of all particulars would follow. And there would be apprehension of screened objects. Because of presence everywhere, there would be no distinction between the proximate and the remote, and no distinction among <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), and <s>āgama</s> (testimony) — this absurd consequence would follow. If it is argued that there is such distinction due to a distinction of function — no, because of the absence of a reason. No reason has been given for why there should be a distinction of function among all-pervasive entities. Therefore, all-pervasiveness of the instruments is not tenable. Therefore —

children.text: citraṃ yathāśrayamṛte sthāṇvādibhyo vinā yathā cchāyā /
children.translated_text: Just as a painting without a support, or as a shadow without posts, persons, and the like,
So too, without the gross elements (<s>viśeṣas</s>), the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) does not stand unsupported. // <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 41 //

children.text:
yathā hi citrasya kuḍyamṛte 'vasthānaṃ nāsti, sthāṇupuruṣādibhyo vā vinā cchāyāyāḥ tadvadvinā viśeṣairna tiṣṭhati nirāśrayaṃ liṅgam / tasmādupapannametat saviśeṣaḥ saṃsāraḥ /

  āha, sūkṣmaśarīrayogātpūrveśvaratvaprasaṃgaḥ / tasmādayuktaṃ tannimittamasyāgrahaṇamiti /
  ucyate- na anekāntāt / tadyathā kṣudrajantūnāṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ laghimā ca, na caiṣāmīśvaratvamevaṃ sarvaprāṇināṃ syāt / atha matamagṛhyamāṇena sambandhāt sthūlasyāpi śarīrasyāgrahaṇaṃ pretāñjanasiddhamālyādivat / tadapyanupapannam / anekāntāt / tadyathā karaṇairagṛhyamāṇaiḥ śarīrasya sambandhaḥ / na cāgrahaṇam, piśācādibhirvā tathaitadapi syāt / kiṃca antaḥkaraṇānuvidhāne caiśvaryābhimānāt / yasya cādhyavasāyamanuvidadhatyaṇimādīni tasyaiśvaryamabhipretam / na tu yasya svabhāvasiddhāni / anyathā tu pipīlikādīnāmapyākāśagamanādaiśvaryaṃ syāt /
