  ucyate- na anabhyupagamāt / na dharmādharmanimittaṃ vaivartaṃ śarīram, kiṃ tarhi ādhikārikamityadoṣaḥ / na cānekaśarīratvamabhyupagamyate / tasmātpakṣāntaropālambho 'yam / kiṃ ca kṛtsnāśayapariṇāmāpratijñānāt / kṛtsnasyāśayasya pariṇāmaṃ jānannevamupālabhyaḥ syādekadeśastu no vipariṇāmī / tasmānna kiṃcidetat / nimittāvaśeṣādāśayaikadeśābhivyaktirayukteti cet, syānmatam- iha nimittānāmalpabahutvaviśeṣādāśayābhivyaktiviśeṣo dṛṣṭaḥ / tadyathā vāyvādikrodhādiṣu / prāyaṇakālaścāyaṃ phalābhivyaktau nimittam / aviśiṣṭaścāsau / tasmādāśayaikadeśapariṇāmo 'nupapanna iti / etaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? naimittikatvāt / pūrvakṛtasya karmaṇaḥ phalabhogaparisamāptiḥ, sāmpratasya ca phalopabhogārthavipariṇāmaḥ prāyaṇasya nimittam / na tu prāyaṇo vipariṇamasyeti / kiṃca śarīrāntarābhāvaśca / kṛtsnasyāśayasyābhivyaktimicchataḥ śarīrāntarābhāvo nimittāntarābhāvātprāpnoti / tatra kṛteneti cet na, kalalādyavasthānāśe tadasambhavāt / tatra kṛtābhyāṃ hi bījāveśaḥ karaṇasya niṣpādito yāvatkalalādyasthāyāmeva taccharīraṃ vinaṣṭamiti tatra kṛtāśayasyāsambhavāccharīrāntarānupapattiprasaṃgaḥ / kiṃ ca sthāvarāṇāṃ ca śarīrāntarāsambhavaḥ / āśayasya sthāvaraśarīrārambhe caritārthatvātsthāvaraśarīreṇa cāśayopādānasambhavāttasya saṃsārābhāvaḥ prāptaḥ / tasmādupapannametatpuruṣārthamādisargotpannaṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ saṃsarati / yāvacca sa puruṣārtho na parisamāpyate tāvattiṣṭhata iti // 41 //
children.translated_text:
For just as a painting has no stability without a wall, or a shadow without posts, persons, and the like, so too without the gross elements (<s>viśeṣas</s>), the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) does not stand unsupported. Therefore this is established: transmigration is accompanied by gross elements.
[Objection:] If transmigration is accompanied by gross elements, then the body should be perceived when it travels to the seed-place of transmigration. But this is not so. Therefore this is untenable.
[Reply:] No, because it has been specified. That body is specified as 'subtle' (<s>sūkṣma</s>). Therefore its non-apprehension is not without cause.
[Objection:] Due to the possession of a subtle body, the absurd consequence of lordship from the very beginning would follow. Therefore it is untenable that this is the reason for its non-apprehension.
[Reply:] No, because it is not invariable. For example, tiny creatures have subtle bodies and lightness, yet lordship does not belong to them — so it would be for all living beings. Now, if you think that due to the connection with what is not apprehended, even the gross body would not be apprehended — like objects seen through ghost-ointment, <s>siddha</s>-garlands, and the like — that too is untenable. Because it is not invariable. For example, the sense organs are not apprehended, yet the body connected with them is apprehended. Or, by the same logic, it should be the case with <s>piśācas</s> (demons) and the like as well. Moreover, regarding the conformity of the inner organ, it is due to the pride of lordship. The lordship intended is that of one whose <s>aṇimā</s> (power of becoming minute) and other powers follow his determination — not of one for whom they are innate. Otherwise, even ants would have lordship because of their ability to travel through space.
[Objection:] No, because of the absurd consequence of the impossibility of a body. If a subtle body arises, then the capacity for another body would be contradicted, since both have fulfilled their purpose. Therefore, it is untenable that transmigration is accompanied by gross elements.
[Reply:] No, because this is not accepted. The body that undergoes transformation is not due to <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), but rather it is for a specific purpose (<s>ādhikārika</s>) — so there is no fault. And multiple bodies are not accepted. Therefore this is an objection against another school's position. Moreover, because complete transformation of the entire repository (<s>āśaya</s>) is not asserted. Only one who knows the transformation of the entire repository could raise this objection — but only a part transforms, not the whole. Therefore this amounts to nothing. If it is argued that, due to the exhaustion of causes, the manifestation of only a part of the repository is untenable — one might think: here, due to differences of more or less among the causes, differences in the manifestation of the repository are observed, as in the case of wind and anger and so forth. And the time of death is a cause for the manifestation of the result. And that is undifferentiated. Therefore the transformation of only a part of the repository is untenable — this too is untenable. Why? Because it is caused. The completion of the fruition of previously performed <s>karma</s> (action), and the transformation for the experience of present results — these are the cause of death. But death itself does not cause the transformation. Moreover, regarding the absence of another body: for one who wishes for the manifestation of the entire repository, the absence of another body would follow from the absence of another cause. If it is argued that it is by what was done there — no, because that is impossible upon the destruction of the embryonic and other stages. For the entry of the seed into the instrument was accomplished by both of those, and as long as the body is destroyed while still in the embryonic stage, the repository created there cannot exist, and so the absurd consequence of the impossibility of another body would follow. Moreover, for stationary beings too, another body would be impossible. Since the repository has fulfilled its purpose in initiating a stationary body, and since a stationary body cannot take up a new repository, the absence of its transmigration would follow. Therefore it is established that the subtle body, produced at the first creation for the sake of <s>puruṣārtha</s> (the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>), transmigrates. And as long as that purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is not completed, so long does it persist. // 41 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 42

children.text:
āha, yadi puruṣārthā liṅgasyotpattirabhyupagamyate tatsamanantaramevānena puruṣārtho 'vasāyayitavyo na punardevamānuṣatiryagbhāvena punaḥ punarājañjavībhāvo 'nuṣṭhātavya iti /
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] If the arising of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) is accepted as being for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, then immediately upon that, the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> should be accomplished, and there should be no need for repeated straightforward progression through states of gods, humans, and animals.
[Reply:]
This, which is for the purpose of <s>puruṣārtha</s> (the goal of <s>Puruṣa</s>), through the connection of cause and effect,
by virtue of the versatility of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) persists like an actor (<s>naṭavat</s>). // <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 42 //

children.text: yadyapi puruṣārthasiddhyarthaṃ liṅgamutpadyate, tathāpi sattvarajastamasāṃ trayāṇāmapi prādhānyādrajastamobhyāmabhibhūte sattve tatpreritaṃ nimittanaimittikaśarīrendriyaviṣayopabhoganirvartakaṃ śṛṇoti / tadyathā agnihotraṃ juhuyātsvargakāmo, yamarājyamagniṣṭomenābhijayatīti / tatra phalecchayā yonīḥ prāṇādīṃśca sammukhīkṛtya kriyāmārabhate / guṇavṛttavaicitryācca prayatnavānapi manovāgdehairmalinamapi karma karoti / tataśca prakṛtervibhutvayogāttena tena nimittenopasthāpitaṃ devamanuṣyatiryakpretādiśarīramekasvabhāvamapi sannaṭavadvyavatiṣṭhate liṅgamākṛtiviśeṣopādānatyāgasāmyataḥ / vibhutvaṃ guṇānāṃ trayāṇāmapi sāmyāditaretarābhibhavo dṛṣṭaḥ / tasmādbhāvanimittaḥ saṃsāraḥ / tannimittānupādānānmokṣaḥ // 42 //
children.translated_text: Although the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) arises for the purpose of accomplishing <s>puruṣārtha</s> (the goal of <s>Puruṣa</s>), nevertheless, since all three — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — are predominant, when <s>sattva</s> is overpowered by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, impelled by them, it produces the experience of body, sense organs, and objects through the causal nexus of cause and effect. For example: 'One who desires heaven should offer the <s>agnihotra</s>' and 'One conquers the realm of <s>Yama</s> by the <s>agniṣṭoma</s>' sacrifice. There, out of desire for the result, having directed oneself toward wombs and vital breaths and the rest, one undertakes action. And due to the variety of the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), even one who makes effort performs impure <s>karma</s> (action) through mind, speech, and body. Therefore, by virtue of the versatility of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), being presented with various causes, the <s>liṅga</s>, though of a single nature, persists like an actor through the adoption and abandonment of different forms — taking on bodies of gods, humans, animals, departed spirits, and the like — by equality in assuming and discarding particular appearances. The versatility of the <s>guṇas</s> is that, starting from equilibrium, the mutual dominance of all three is observed. Therefore, transmigration is caused by the <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions). Liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) comes from the non-acquisition of those causes. // 42 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 43

children.text:
āha, bhāvā iti tatra bhavatābhidhīyate, na cāsya śabdasyārthaṃ pratipadyāmahe / tasmādvaktavyamidaṃ ke punaramī bhāvā iti ?
  ucyate- dharmādyā bhāvāḥ / dharmo jñānaṃ vairāgyamaiśvaryamadharmo 'jñānamavairāgyamanaiśvaryamityete bhāvāḥ /
  tatrācāryāṇāṃ vipratipattiḥ / pañcādhikaraṇasya tāvaddvividhaṃ jñānaṃ prākṛtikaṃ vaikṛtikaṃ ca / prākṛtikaṃ trividhaṃ- tattvasamakālaṃ sāṃsiddhikamābhiṣyandikaṃ ca / tatra tattvasamakālaṃ saṃhataśca mahāṃstattvātmanā mahati pratyayo bhavati / utpannakāryakāraṇasya tu sāṃsiddhikamābhiṣyandikaṃ ca bhavati / sāṃsiddhikaṃ yatsaṃhatavyūhasamakālaṃ niṣpadyate, yathā paramarṣerjñānam / ābhiṣyandikaṃ ca saṃsiddhakāryakaraṇasya kāraṇāntareṇotpadyate / vaikṛtaṃ tu dvividhaṃ svavaikṛtaṃ paravaikṛtaṃ ca / svavaikṛtaṃ tārakam / paravaikṛtaṃ siddhyantarāṇi / āha ca

children.translated_text: That which is simultaneous with the principles is the transformative one; the second, which is spontaneously flowing (<s>ābhiṣyandika</s>), arises from it;
The third is the derivative (<s>vaikṛta</s>) — this has been declared as the sixfold system (<s>ṣāṭkauśika</s>).

[Objection:] You say '<s>bhāvas</s>' (dispositions), but we do not understand the meaning of this word. Therefore, you should state: what are these <s>bhāvas</s>?
[Reply:] The <s>bhāvas</s> are those beginning with <s>dharma</s> (virtue): <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), <s>adharma</s> (vice), <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), <s>avairāgya</s> (attachment), and <s>anaiśvarya</s> (lack of sovereignty) — these are the <s>bhāvas</s>.
Among the teachers, there is disagreement on this matter. According to the <s>Pañcādhikaraṇa</s> school, knowledge is of two kinds: natural (<s>prākṛtika</s>) and derivative (<s>vaikṛtika</s>). The natural is of three kinds: simultaneous with the principles (<s>tattvasamakāla</s>), innate (<s>sāṃsiddhika</s>), and spontaneously flowing (<s>ābhiṣyandika</s>). Among these, 'simultaneous with the principles' means that when the aggregate exists, there arises in <s>Mahat</s> (the Great One) an awareness of <s>Mahat</s> as a principle. But for one whose effect-and-cause has arisen, there are the innate and the spontaneously flowing. The innate is that which is produced simultaneously with the arrangement of the aggregate — as the knowledge of the primordial sage (<s>paramarṣi</s>). The spontaneously flowing arises for one whose effect-and-instrument is accomplished, through another cause. The derivative is of two kinds: self-derivative (<s>svavaikṛta</s>) and other-derivative (<s>paravaikṛta</s>). The self-derivative is the liberating knowledge (<s>tāraka</s>). The other-derivative consists of the other <s>siddhis</s> (attainments). And it is said:
But here, since there is no distinction from arising together with the beings, he states the innate (<s>sāṃsiddhika</s>) without differentiation —

children.text: vaikṛtamapi ca dvividhaṃ svavaikṛtaṃ tatra tārakaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: The derivative (<s>vaikṛta</s>) too is of two kinds; among them, the self-derivative is the liberating (<s>tāraka</s>) knowledge.
The other-derivative, beginning with one's own liberating knowledge and so forth, is said to be sevenfold.

children.text:
iti yathā jñānamevaṃ dharmādayo 'pīti /
  vindhyavāsinastu nāsti tattvasamaṃ sāṃsiddhikaṃ ca / kiṃ tarhi siddhirūpameva / tatra paramarṣerapi sargasaṃghātavyūhottarakālameva jñānaṃ niṣpadyate yasmād gurumukhābhipratipatteḥ pratipatsyata ityapītyāha- siddhaṃ nimittaṃ naimittikasyānugrahaṃ kurute, nāpūrvamutpādayatīti / nimittanaimittikabhāvāccaivamupapadyate / tatra paramarṣeḥ paṭurūhaḥ anyeṣāṃ kliṣṭa ityayaṃ viśeṣaḥ / sarveṣāmeva tu tārakādyaviśiṣṭamācārya āha- trividhā bhāvāḥ sāṃsiddhikāḥ prākṛtikā vaikṛtikāśceti / tatra sāṃsiddhikagrahaṇāttattvasamakālaṃ pratyācaṣṭe, naiva tadastīti / katham ? yadi hi tathā syāttattvāntarānutpattisaṃghāto vyūhaścānarthakaḥ syāt / mahatyutpannaṃ jñānaṃ tatraivopalabdhamiti kaḥ saṃghātārthaḥ ? tathā carṣerūho nopapadyate, pratibandhābhāvāt / na hyasya kāryakāraṇavyūhasamakālajñānotpattau kaścitpratibandho 'sti / aparivṛtakhalatvādyataḥ kālāntaraṃ pratīkṣate / tasmādasya sahaiva kāryakāraṇābhyāṃ jñānamabhiniṣpadyate pradīpaprakāśādityataḥ sāṃsiddhikam / anyeṣāṃ tu sattvasyāpaṭutvātkālāntareṇa prakṛtyabhiṣyandād drāgiti bhavati / kṛṣṇasarpadarśanavat / tatprākṛtam / vaikṛtaṃ tu dvividhaṃ pūrvavat / yathā ca paramarṣerjñānaṃ sāṃsiddhikamevaṃ māhātmyaśarīrasyaiśvaryaṃ, bhṛgvādīnāṃ dharmaḥ, sanakādīnāṃ vairāgyam / adharmo yakṣarakṣaḥprabhṛtīnām / anaiśvaryaṃ ṣaṭsiddhikṣayakālotpannānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ tiraścāñca / rāgo 'jñānaṃ paramarṣivarjyānām / prākṛtāstu tadyathā vairāgyaṃ bhagavadāsureḥ / tasya hi paramarṣisambhāvanādutpanno dharmaḥ, aśuddhiṃ pratidvandvibhāvādapajagāma / tasyāmapahatāyāṃ prakṛteḥ śuddhisrotaḥ pravṛttaṃ yenānugṛhīto duḥkhatrayābhighātādutpannajijñāsaḥ pravrajitaḥ / tathā maheśvarasamparkānnandina aiśvaryam / nahuṣasyāgastyasamparkāddharma ityādi / vaikṛtāstu bhāvā asmadādīnām / evaṃ trividhabhāvaparigrahāttvācāryasya na sarvaṃ svataḥ patañjalivat, na sarvaṃ parataḥ pañcādhikaraṇavat
/ kintarhi mahatī svabhāvātivṛttiḥ prakṛtito 'lpā svato vikṛtitaḥ /
  evam
children.translated_text:
Just as knowledge is thus classified, so too are <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and the rest.
But <s>Vindhyavāsin</s> holds that there is no knowledge simultaneous with the principles, nor innate knowledge. What then? It is only of the nature of attainment (<s>siddhi</s>). According to him, even for the primordial sage, knowledge is produced only after the time of the arrangement of the aggregate of creation, because he will understand through reception from a teacher — thus he says: 'The accomplished one (<s>siddha</s>) bestows grace upon the caused, it does not produce something new.' And through the relation of cause and effect, this is tenable. There, for the primordial sage the process is swift, for others it is difficult — this is the distinction. But the <s>Ācārya</s> (teacher, i.e., <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>) states that for all, the liberating knowledge and the rest are undifferentiated. He says: 'The <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions) are threefold: innate (<s>sāṃsiddhika</s>), natural (<s>prākṛtika</s>), and derivative (<s>vaikṛtika</s>).' There, by the term 'innate,' he rejects what is simultaneous with the principles — that simply does not exist. How so? Because if it were so, the arising of further principles and the aggregate and arrangement would be purposeless. If knowledge arises in <s>Mahat</s> and is apprehended there itself, what purpose does the aggregate serve? Likewise, the process of the sage would be untenable, because there would be no obstruction. For there is no obstruction to the arising of knowledge simultaneously with the arrangement of effect and cause. Since the threshing floor has not been cleared, as it were, it awaits another time. Therefore, knowledge is produced for him simultaneously with effect and cause, like the light of a lamp — hence it is innate (<s>sāṃsiddhika</s>). But for others, due to the dullness of <s>sattva</s>, it arises after some time through the spontaneous overflow of <s>Prakṛti</s>, gradually — like the sight of a black serpent. That is natural (<s>prākṛtika</s>). The derivative is of two kinds, as before. And just as the knowledge of the primordial sage is innate, so too is the sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) of the cosmic body (<s>māhātmyaśarīra</s>), the <s>dharma</s> of <s>Bhṛgu</s> and others, and the <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) of <s>Sanaka</s> and others. <s>Adharma</s> (vice) belongs to <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and the like. Lack of sovereignty (<s>anaiśvarya</s>) belongs to humans and animals born at the time of the decay of the six attainments. Passion (<s>rāga</s>) and ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) belong to all except the primordial sage. The natural (<s>prākṛtika</s>) ones are, for example, the dispassion of the blessed <s>Āsuri</s>. For his <s>dharma</s> arose from association with the primordial sage, and his impurity departed through the opposition to it. When that was removed, the pure stream of <s>Prakṛti</s> flowed forth, by which, being graced, and having developed the desire to know from the affliction of the threefold suffering, he renounced. Likewise, the sovereignty of <s>Nandin</s> came from association with <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord). The <s>dharma</s> of <s>Nahuṣa</s> came from association with <s>Agastya</s> — and so forth. The derivative (<s>vaikṛtika</s>) dispositions belong to people like us. Thus, through the acceptance of the threefold dispositions, the <s>Ācārya</s>'s position is neither that everything is from oneself, like <s>Patañjali</s>'s, nor that everything is from another, like the <s>Pañcādhikaraṇa</s>'s. Rather, the great spontaneous occurrence is from <s>Prakṛti</s>, the small portion is from oneself, and the derivative is from transformation.
Thus —

children.text:
sāṃsiddhikāśca bhāvāḥ prākṛtikā vaikṛtāśca dharmādyāḥ /
  dṛṣṭāḥ karaṇāśrayiṇaḥ
children.translated_text:
The <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions) — innate (<s>sāṃsiddhika</s>), natural (<s>prākṛtika</s>), and derivative (<s>vaikṛtika</s>) — beginning with <s>dharma</s> (virtue),
are seen as residing in the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>),
and just as these are, so too
those residing in the effect (<s>kārya</s>), beginning with the embryo (<s>kalala</s>) and the rest. // <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 43 //

children.text: trividhā eveti kalalādigrahaṇena śarīrāṇyāha / teṣāmākṛtivaiśvarūpyaṃ caturdaśavidhe saṃsāre trividham / tatra sāṃsiddhikastāvat vaivarttānāṃ grahanakṣatratārādīnām / jātikṛtaśca viśeṣaḥ haṃsānāṃ śauklyam, tittiramayūrādīnāṃ citracchadatvamiti / prākṛtaṃ yathāmāhātmyaṃ śarīrābhimānāt tasya hyabhimāno bhavati- hantāhaṃ putrānsrakṣye ye me karma kariṣyanti / ye māṃ paraṃ ca jñāsyanti / sa yādṛksargamabhidhyāyati tādṛkpradhānādutpadyate / tadyathā maheśvarasya rudrakoṭisṛṣṭāviti / vaikṛtāstu kalalādyāḥ / yathā bhiṣagvede 'bhihitam- kṣīraṃ pītvā garbhiṇī gauraṃ putraṃ janayatīti / ete bhāvā vyākhyātāḥ / eṣāṃ vaiśvarūpyālliṅgasya gativiśeṣaḥ saṃsāro bhavatīti // 43 //
children.translated_text: 'Threefold indeed' — by the mention of <s>kalala</s> (embryonic matter) and the like, he speaks of the bodies. Their diversity of form in the fourteen-fold <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence) is threefold. Among these, the <s>sāṃsiddhika</s> (natural) [body belongs] to the revolving [celestial beings] such as planets, stars, and constellations. The <s>jātikṛta</s> (species-determined) distinction [includes] the whiteness of swans, and the multicolored plumage of partridges, peacocks, and the like. The <s>prākṛta</s> (primordial) [body arises] according to [one's] greatness, from the pride regarding the body — for one has this pride: 'I shall create sons who will perform rituals for me, who will know me and the supreme.' Whatever kind of creation he contemplates, that kind arises from <s>pradhāna</s> — for example, <s>Maheśvara</s>'s creation of ten million <s>Rudras</s>. The <s>vaikṛta</s> (modified) [bodies] are those beginning with <s>kalala</s> (embryonic matter). As stated in the medical scripture: 'A pregnant woman who drinks milk gives birth to a fair-complexioned son.' These dispositions have been explained. From their diversity, the particular course of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) — namely, <s>saṃsāra</s> — comes about. // 43 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 44

children.text:
āha, kasya punarbhāvasyānuṣṭhānātko gamanaviśeṣo liṅgasya niṣpadyata iti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] Through the practice of which disposition does which particular course of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) come about?
  [Reply:]
Through <s>dharma</s> (merit) there is movement upward;
<s>Dharma</s> has been described. Through its practice, birth occurs in the divine realm, which has eight varieties.
through <s>adharma</s> (demerit) there is movement downward.

children.text:
adharmo 'pyuktaḥ / tadanuṣṭhānāpañcavikalpāyāṃ tiryagbhūmāvutpattirbhavati /
  āha, ekabhūmiviśeṣānupapattiḥ, gativiśeṣāt / yadi bhāvānāṃ bhūmiviśeṣanimittatvaṃ niyamyate tenaikasyāṃ bhūmau hīnamadhyamotkṛṣṭatvaṃ jātyākṛtisvabhāvānugrahopaghātānāṃ na prāpnoti /
  ucyate- na tarhyanena bhūmiviśeṣo niyamyate, kiṃ tarhi ūrdhvaśabda utkṛṣṭavacanaḥ / dharmeṇa deveṣu mānaveṣu tiryakṣu cordhvagamanamutkṛṣṭaṃ janma bhavati / tathādharmādadhogamanamapakṛṣṭaṃ janma bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>Adharma</s> too has been described. Through its practice, birth occurs in the animal realm, which has five varieties.
  [Objection:] There is the impossibility of differentiation within a single realm, because of [the restriction to] particular courses. If it is determined that the dispositions are causes of particular realms only, then within a single realm, the inferior, middling, and superior grades of birth, form, nature, benefit, and harm would not be possible.
  [Reply:] This does not determine a particular realm. Rather, the word 'upward' means 'superior.' Through <s>dharma</s>, there is upward movement — that is, superior birth — among gods, humans, and animals alike. Likewise, through <s>adharma</s>, there is downward movement — that is, inferior birth.
and through knowledge, <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).

children.text:
caśabdo 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ / jñānenaivāpavargaḥ, na bhāvāntareṇeti / yaduktamanyairācāryaiḥ- vairāgyātpuruṣakaivalyaṃ jñānavairāgyābhyāṃ ceti tatpratiṣiddhaṃ bhavati /
  āha, yadi punarvairāgyātpuruṣakaivalyamabhyupagamyate ka evaṃ sati doṣaḥ syāt ?
  ucyate- na śakyamevaṃ pratipattum / kasmāt ? saṃsāranimittāpratipakṣatvāt / yadi rāganimittaḥ pradhānapuruṣasaṃyogaḥ syāt prāptamidaṃ tatpratipakṣeṇa vairāgyeṇa viyogo bhaviṣyatīti / na tvevam / kutaḥ ? saṃyogakṛte kāryakaraṇasarge niṣpatteḥ / kāryakaraṇavyūhottarakālaṃ hi rāgo bhavati / tasmānnāsau kāryakaraṇaniṣpatternimittamiti śakyamāśrayitum / yasya tu jñānānmokṣa iti pakṣaḥ, tasya pratipakṣādajñānādbandha iti prāptamasti, na cāsau prāgapi kāryakaraṇaniṣpatteḥ / tasmānna vairāgyānmokṣaḥ / ataeva na jñānavairāgyābhyāṃ mokṣo 'sti / ubhayanimittāsambhavāt / tasmātsūktaṃ jñānenaivāpavargaḥ /
children.translated_text:
The particle 'ca' is for emphasis — 'through knowledge alone is <s>apavarga</s> (liberation), not through anything else.' What was stated by other teachers — 'through <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) comes the isolation of <s>puruṣa</s>' and 'through both knowledge and dispassion' — that is refuted.
  [Objection:] If liberation through <s>vairāgya</s> were accepted, what defect would there be?
  [Reply:] It cannot be understood thus. Why? Because it is not the antidote to the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). If the conjunction of <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> were caused by attachment, then it would follow that separation would occur through its antidote, dispassion. But it is not so. Why? Because the conjunction is established in the production of the body and instruments. For attachment arises only after the arrangement of the body and instruments. Therefore, it cannot be held that [attachment] is the cause of the production of the body and instruments. But for one whose position is 'liberation comes from knowledge,' the converse follows — bondage comes from its antidote, ignorance — and that [ignorance] exists even prior to the production of the body and instruments. Therefore, liberation does not come from dispassion. For this very reason, liberation does not come from both knowledge and dispassion — because both cannot be the cause simultaneously. Therefore it is well said: 'Through knowledge alone is <s>apavarga</s>.'
From the opposite [of knowledge] comes bondage. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 44 //

children.text: jñānaviparyayo 'jñānam / tasmād bandhastrividho bhavati prakṛtibandho dakṣiṇābandho vaikārikabandhaśceti // 44 //
children.translated_text: The opposite of knowledge is ignorance. From that, bondage is threefold: <s>prakṛtibandha</s> (bondage to <s>prakṛti</s>), <s>dakṣiṇābandha</s> (bondage to merit), and <s>vaikārikabandha</s> (bondage to supernatural powers). // 44 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 45

[Objection:] From which disposition does <s>prakṛtibandha</s> (bondage to <s>prakṛti</s>) arise?
  [Reply:]
Through <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), dissolution into <s>prakṛti</s>;

children.text:
vairāgyādaṣṭasu prakṛtiṣu layaṃ gacchati, asāvucyate prakṛtibandha iti /
  āha, yadi vairāgyātprakṛtilayaḥ prāpto yadetatprakṛtau vairāgyamāñjasam / anyā prakṛtistriguṇā, kāraṇabhūtā, kāryabhūtā, kāryakāraṇabhūtā, akāryakāraṇabhūtā acetanā paratantrā ceti / anyaḥ puruṣo nirguṇo, na kāryaṃ, na kāraṇaṃ, na kāryakāraṇaṃ, tadviparītaḥ cetanaḥ svatantraśceti tato 'pi prakṛtau layaḥ tataścānirmokṣaprasaṃga iti /
  ucyate- viparyayāditi vartate / tadihābhisambhantsyāmaḥ / tataśca viparītaṃ yadeva vairāgyaṃ tuṣṭikāṇḍānupatitaṃ prakṛtyādiṣu paratvābhimānaḥ tata eva prakṛtilayo bhavati nānyasmāt / athavātrāpi yattatprakṛtāvanyatvajñānaṃ tata eva mokṣo na vairāgyāt / kutaḥ ? bhavabījāpratipakṣatvāditi hyuktam / āmbhasikasya ca mokṣaprasaṃgāt / tulyā hyasya nānātvasaṃvid, āsaṃgadoṣanivṛtteḥ / na caitadiṣṭam / tasmādyuktametat vairāgyātprakṛtilaya iti /
  āha, atha dakṣiṇābandhaḥ kutaḥ ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
Through <s>vairāgya</s>, one is dissolved into the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> — that is called <s>prakṛtibandha</s> (bondage to <s>prakṛti</s>).
  [Objection:] If dissolution into <s>prakṛti</s> is attained through <s>vairāgya</s>, then this <s>vairāgya</s> toward <s>prakṛti</s> is straightforward. <s>Prakṛti</s> is one thing — possessing three <s>guṇas</s>, being a cause, being an effect, being both cause and effect, being neither cause nor effect, non-conscious, and dependent. <s>Puruṣa</s> is another — free from <s>guṇas</s>, neither effect nor cause, nor both, the opposite of that, conscious, and independent. Yet even so, dissolution into <s>prakṛti</s> occurs — and from that, the consequence of non-liberation.
  [Reply:] 'From the opposite' carries over [from the previous verse]. We shall connect that here. Thus, it is precisely that dispassion which, being included in the category of <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment), involves the conceit of superiority toward <s>prakṛti</s> and the other [principles] — from that very [misguided dispassion] comes dissolution into <s>prakṛti</s>, not from anything else. Alternatively, here too, it is that knowledge of otherness from <s>prakṛti</s> alone [that leads to liberation] — not dispassion. Why? Because, as stated, it is not the antidote to the seed of existence. And because the consequence would be that even the aquatic [yogin] attains liberation — for his cognition of multiplicity is equal [to the true yogin's], [except that he merely] ceases the defect of attachment. And that is not desired. Therefore it is proper: 'Through <s>vairāgya</s>, dissolution into <s>prakṛti</s>.'
  [Objection:] Then from what comes <s>dakṣiṇābandha</s> (bondage to merit)?
  [Reply:]
Through <s>rājasa</s> (passion-born) attachment, <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) occurs;

children.text:
yo 'yaṃ dṛṣṭānuśravikaviṣayābhilāṣaḥ sa rāgaḥ / tatra dṛṣṭaviṣayarāgāttatprāptinirvartakaṃ karma karoti / tataśca tatropapadyate / ānuśravikaviṣayābhilāṣādagnihotrādiṣu pravartate / tataśca svargādiṣūpapattirbhavati / asau dakṣiṇābandhaḥ / dṛṣṭānuśravikaviṣayābhilāṣadvāreṇa tannirvartake karmaṇi pravartamāno guṇavṛttivaicitryādaniṣṭaphalanirvartakamapi karma karoti / evaṃ mānuṣye gatyantare yopapattiḥ sarvāsau rāgāt /
  āha, rājasaṃgrahaṇānarthakyam tatpūrvakatvādrāgasya / rajonimitta eva hi rāgaḥ / tatra saṃsāro rāgādityeva vaktavyam, rājasagrahaṇamanarthakamiti /
  ucyate- na, viṣayaviśeṣaṇatvāt / viṣaye yo rāgaḥ sa saṃsāraheturityasyārthasya jñāpanārthamidamucyate / anyathā yo yateḥ sāttviko yamaniyamadhyānādyanuṣṭhānānurāgaḥ pravacanarāgo vā so 'pi saṃsārāya syāt /
children.translated_text:
That which is desire for seen and traditionally-heard objects is attachment. Among these, from attachment to seen objects, one performs actions that bring about the attainment of those [objects]. And from that, one is reborn there. From desire for traditionally-heard objects, one engages in <s>agnihotra</s> and other [rituals]. And from that, birth in heaven and the like occurs. This is <s>dakṣiṇābandha</s> (bondage to merit). Through the channel of desire for seen and heard objects, while engaging in actions that bring them about, due to the variety of <s>guṇa</s>-operations, one also performs actions that bring about undesired results. Thus, whatever birth occurs in the human [realm] or in any other course — all of that is from attachment.
  [Objection:] The mention of '<s>rājasa</s>' is purposeless, since attachment is preceded by that [<s>rajas</s>]. For attachment is indeed caused by <s>rajas</s>. Therefore it should simply be said '<s>saṃsāra</s> comes from attachment' — the mention of '<s>rājasa</s>' is purposeless.
  [Reply:] No, because it qualifies the object. This is stated to convey the meaning that it is attachment to objects that causes <s>saṃsāra</s>. Otherwise, the <s>sāttvika</s> attachment of an ascetic to the practice of <s>yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, meditation, and the like, or attachment to scripture, would also lead to <s>saṃsāra</s>.
through supernatural powers (<s>aiśvarya</s>), non-obstruction;

children.text:
yadaṣṭaguṇamaiśvaryamaṇimādi prāgupadiṣṭaṃ tasmātsve sve viṣaye 'vighāta utpadyate / tadabhiratirvaikāriko bandhaḥ /
  āha, yadi tribhistribhirnimittairvairāgyādibhistrividho bandho nirvartyate yaduktamajñānād bandha iti tadayuktam / bhāvāntaraṃ hyajñānamataḥ phalāntareṇa bhavitavyamiti /
  ucyate- na, mūlakāraṇatvāt / jñānavarjitānāṃ hi bhāvānāṃ yatphalaṃ tatrājñānaṃ mūlam / tannimittatvātsarveṣām / na hi jñānivairāgyamalaṃ prakṛtilayāya / tathetarāṇi paramarṣyādāvadṛṣṭatvād vicitraṃ kāryamekasmātkāraṇādayuktamiti vairāgyādīnyasādhāraṇāni pṛthak kalpyante, sādhāraṇaṃ tvajñānamato na kaściddoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
The eightfold supernatural power beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), which was previously described — from that, non-obstruction arises in one's respective domain. Delight in that is <s>vaikārikabandha</s> (bondage to supernatural powers).
  [Objection:] If threefold bondage is produced by three causes — dispassion and the rest — then what was stated, 'from ignorance comes bondage,' is untenable. For ignorance is something different, and therefore there should be a different result.
  [Reply:] No, because [ignorance] is the root cause. For the result of dispositions devoid of knowledge has ignorance as its root. Since all [forms of bondage] are caused by that. For the dispassion of a knower is not sufficient for dissolution into <s>prakṛti</s>. Likewise for the others — since a diverse effect from a single cause was not observed in the case of the supreme sage and the like, dispassion and the rest are posited separately as uncommon [causes]; but ignorance is common — therefore there is no defect.
From the opposite, the reversal of that. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 45 //

children.text: anaiśvaryāttu aṇimāderaṣṭavidhādavighātaviparyayo vighāto bhavati / tadevametadaṣṭavidhaṃ dharmādividhānamupādāyāṣṭavidhaṃ naimittikamupapadyate / evameṣa tattvasargo bhāvasargaśca vyākhyātaḥ / etacca vyaktasya rūpaṃ pravṛttiśca parikalpyate / phalamidānīṃ vakṣyāmaḥ // 45 //
children.translated_text: From the absence of supernatural power — that is, the reversal of the eightfold non-obstruction beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> — obstruction occurs. Thus, based on the eightfold classification of <s>dharma</s> and the rest, the eightfold occasioned [creation] comes about. Thus, the elemental creation and the dispositional creation have been explained. And this is how the form and activity of the manifest are conceived. We shall now explain the fruit. // 45 //
Thus ends the eighth chapter and the third section of the <s>Yuktidīpikā</s>.
<s>Kārikā</s> 46

children.text:
āha, kiṃ punastatphalamiti ?
  ucyate- yaḥ khalu
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] What, then, is that fruit?
  [Reply:] That which indeed [is]:
This is the intellectual creation, called error, incapacity, contentment, and attainment;

children.text: tatphalamiti vākyaśeṣaḥ / eṣa iti vakṣyamāṇasya sammukhīkaraṇārthamucyate / pratyayasarga iti pratyayaḥ padārtho lakṣaṇamiti paryāyāḥ, pratyayānāṃ sargaḥ pratyayasargaḥ padārthasargo lakṣaṇasarga ityarthaḥ / athavā pratyayo buddhirniścayo 'dhyavasāya iti paryāyāḥ / tasya sargo 'yamataḥ pratyayasargaḥ pratyayakāryaṃ pratyayavyāpāra ityarthaḥ / athavā pratyayapūrvakaḥ sargaḥ pratyayasargaḥ / buddhipūrvaka ityuktaḥ / katham ? evaṃ hi śāstram- "mahadādiviśeṣāntaḥ sargo buddhipūrvakatvāt / utpannakāryakaraṇastu māhātmyaśarīra ekākinamātmānamavekṣyābhidadhyau hantāhaṃ putrānsrakṣye ye me karma kariṣyanti / ye māṃ paraṃ cāparaṃ ca jñāsyanti / tasyābhidhyāyataḥ pañca mukhyasrotaso devāḥ prādurbabhūvuḥ / teṣūtpanneṣu na tuṣṭiṃ lebhe / tato 'nye tiryaksrotaso 'ṣṭāviṃśatiḥ prajajñe / teṣvapyasya matirnaiva tasthe / athāpare navordhvasrotaso devāḥ prādurbabhūvuḥ / teṣvapyutpanneṣu naiva kṛtārthamātmānaṃ mene / tato 'nye 'ṣṭāvarvāksrotasa utpeduḥ / evaṃ tasmād brahmaṇo 'bhidhyānādutpannastasmātpratyayasargaḥ / sa viparyayākhyaḥ aśaktyākhyaḥ tuṣṭyākhyaḥ siddhyākhyaśceti /" tatrāśreyasaḥ śreyastvenābhidhānaṃ viparyayaḥ / vaikalyādasāmarthyamaśaktiḥ / cikīrṣitādūnena nirvṛtistuṣṭiḥ / yatheṣṭasya sādhanaṃ siddhiḥ / tadyathā dharmārthapravṛtto 'gniṣṭomādīnparityajya saṃkaraṃ kurvīta so 'sya viparyayaḥ / sādhanavaikalyādasāmarthyamaśaktiḥ / ādhānamātrasantoṣastuṣṭiḥ / kṛtsnasya kriyātiśeṣasyānuṣṭhānaṃ siddhiḥ / evamarthādiṣu yojyam / yaścāyaṃ caturvidhaḥ phalaviśeṣo viparyayādirākhyātaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That fruit' — this is the completion of the sentence. 'This' is said to bring the forthcoming [topic] to the fore. 'Intellectual creation' — '<s>pratyaya</s>' means category, characteristic — these are synonyms; the creation of <s>pratyayas</s> is the 'intellectual creation,' meaning the creation of categories or the creation of characteristics. Alternatively, '<s>pratyaya</s>' means <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), determination, ascertainment — these are synonyms. Its creation — therefore 'intellectual creation' means the product of intellect, the operation of intellect. Or alternatively, a creation preceded by <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition) is the 'intellectual creation' — meaning 'preceded by intellect.' How? For the scripture says thus: 'The creation from <s>mahat</s> to the specific [elements] is preceded by intellect. Having produced the body and instruments, the one with the great body, seeing himself alone, contemplated: "I shall create sons who will perform rituals for me, who will know me and the supreme and the lesser." From his contemplation, five principal-stream gods appeared. When they were produced, he was not satisfied. Then twenty-eight transverse-stream [beings] were born. Regarding them too, his mind was not settled. Then nine other upward-stream gods appeared. Even when they were produced, he did not consider himself fulfilled. Then eight other downward-stream [beings] arose." Thus from the contemplation of that <s>Brahmā</s>, the intellectual creation arose. It is called error, incapacity, contentment, and attainment.' Among these, designating the inauspicious as auspicious is <s>viparyaya</s> (error). Inability due to deficiency is <s>aśakti</s> (incapacity). Satisfaction with less than what is desired is <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment). The accomplishment of what is desired is <s>siddhi</s> (attainment). For example, one engaged in <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> (wealth) who abandons <s>agniṣṭoma</s> and other [proper rituals] and performs mixed [improper] rites — that is his error. Inability due to deficiency of means is incapacity. Contentment with mere initiation is contentment. The performance of the entirety of ritual obligations is attainment. The same should be applied to <s>artha</s> and the other [goals]. And this fourfold classification of fruits — error and the rest — has been declared.
From the conflict of the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s>, its divisions are fifty. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 46 //

children.text: guṇānāṃ vaiṣamyaṃ guṇavaiṣamyam / guṇavaiṣamyaṃ prādhānyaguṇabhāvayoga ityarthaḥ / guṇavaiṣamyādvimardo guṇavaiṣamyavimardaḥ, pratyayaparyāyeṇa sattvarajastamasāmitaretarabhāvaḥ / tannimittā eṣāṃ pratyayāṇāṃ pañcāśadbhedā bhavanti // 46 //
children.translated_text: The disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> is '<s>guṇavaiṣamya</s>.' The disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> means the state of predominance and subordination — this is the meaning. The conflict arising from the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> is the 'conflict of <s>guṇa</s>-disequilibrium' — in the sense of <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition), it is the mutual interaction of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. Caused by that, there are fifty divisions of these <s>pratyayas</s> (intellectual dispositions). // 46 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 47
How? It is said:
The divisions of <s>viparyaya</s> (error) are five;

children.text:
tamo moho mahāmohastāmisro 'ndhatāmisra iti / tatrāśreyasi pravṛttasya pratyayāvare śreyo 'bhimāne ādyo viparyayastama ityabhidhīyate / bhautikeṣvākāreṣu śiraḥpāṇyādiṣvātmagraho yo 'yaṃ vyūḍhoraskaḥ sitadaśanastāmrākṣaḥ pralambabāhuḥ so 'hamiti / tathā śravaṇasparśanarasanaghrāṇavacanādānaviharaṇotsargānandasaṃkalpābhimānādhyavasāyalakṣaṇāsu karaṇavṛttiṣvahaṃ śrotā draṣṭā cetyevamādirādyakālapravṛtto grahaḥ sarvasmādavaro moha ityucyate / kathaṃ punarayamavaraḥ ityucyate pūrvaṃ śarīrendriyavyatiriktamupalabdhumicchansaukṣmyāttattadanadhigame bhūtākāramabhūtaṃ pramāṇaṃ paraparikalpitaṃ vānumanyeta, svayaṃ vā parikalpayediti na mārgād dūrāpagatametat / ayaṃ tu pratyakṣādigatotpattisthitivināśeṣvanekarūpakeṣu kāryakaraṇeṣvahamiti abhimanyate, tasmātpūrvasyādavaraḥ / bāhye tu viṣaye mamedamityabhiniveśaḥ pūrvasmādavara ityucyate / pūrvaḥ śarīriṇo 'pratyakṣatvātkaraṇavṛttyaviśeṣād vātmavṛtteḥ kāryakaraṇe kuryādātmabuddhimiti śakyametad bhinnanimittākāradeśasvabhāvaprayojanānugrahopaghātotpattisthitivināśāṃśca mātṛpitṛputrabhrātṛputradāragohirāyavasanācchādanādīnayamakasmādātmatvena paśyati, tasmātpūrvasmādavaraḥ / krodhaścaturtho viparyayaḥ pūrvasmādavaraḥ tāmisra ityabhidhīyate / kathaṃ punarayaṃ pūrvasmādavara iti ? ucyate- pūrvo 'bhiniveśapratiṣedhamabhyanujānāti / yadāsya bāhyadravyaviyoge kaścitkuśalasaṃsṛṣṭa evaṃ bravīti saṃsārasya ___ buddhāvavasthāpya vimṛśyatāṃ yāvadayaṃ kālo yadi kaścitpriyeṇāviyuktapūrvaḥ / tasmādāgamāpāyiṣu bāhyeṣu dravyeṣu viduṣā nābhiniveśaḥ kārya iti, tadā pratyāha satyamevametaditi / sannikṛṣṭastu viyogakāla iti na buddhiravasthāpayituṃ śakyate / krodhāviṣṭastu svavikalpitagrāhaviparītabuddhiraśakyo daṇḍenāpinivartayitum / tasmātpūrvasmādavaraḥ / maraṇaviṣādaḥ pañcamo viparyayaḥ pūrvasmādavaro 'ndhatāmistra ityabhidhīyate / kathaṃ punarayaṃ pūrvasmādavara ityucyate- pūrvo 'bhiniveśātpratiṣidhyamānaḥ pratīkāramantato
jihvākṣinirīkṣato (?) nāpi tāvadārabhate / na tu brahmādau stambaparyante saṃsāre svanimittaniyatatamapātasya vināśasya kenacitpratīkāraḥ kṛtaḥ / tasmādaparihāryaṃ maraṇamanuśocatpūrvasmādavara iti / ete pañca viparyayabhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: <s>Tamas</s> (darkness), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom), and <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness). Among these, for one engaged in the non-good, the lowest error consisting in the conceit of well-being — the first error — is called <s>tamas</s>. The self-identification with material forms such as head, hands, and the like — 'I am this one with a broad chest, white teeth, copper eyes, and long arms' — [is tamas]. Similarly, with respect to the instrumental activities characterized as hearing, touching, tasting, smelling, speaking, grasping, locomotion, excretion, pleasure, conceptualization, self-assertion, and determination — the identification 'I am the hearer, I am the seer,' and so forth, which has been operating from the beginning — this, being lower than all [the rest], is called <s>moha</s> (delusion). How is this one lower? It is said: one who previously wished to apprehend [something] distinct from the body and sense organs, but failed to attain this or that due to subtlety, might assent to a false means of knowledge constructed by another as if it were real, or might construct one himself — this has not gone far from the path. But this one identifies as 'I' with the causal complex [of body and senses] which are perceived through direct perception and the rest as having manifold forms in origination, persistence, and destruction — therefore it is lower than the previous. The attachment to external objects as 'this is mine' is called lower than the previous [i.e., <s>mahāmoha</s>]. The earlier one [<s>tamas</s>] — since the embodied self is not directly perceptible, and since there is no distinction in instrumental activity, one might make an identification of self with the causal complex due to the self's [unperceivable] activity — this is possible. But this one — why does he see as his self things whose causes, forms, locations, natures, purposes, benefits, harms, origins, durations, and destructions are all different, such as mother, father, son, brother, grandson, wife, cattle, gold, food, and clothing? Therefore it is lower than the previous. Anger is the fourth error; it is lower than the previous and is called <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom). How?
And incapacity is due to the deficiency of the instruments. The varieties are twenty-eight.

children.text: bhavatītyanuvartate / tatra bāhyakaraṇavaikalyaṃ saha manasaikādaśaprakāram / saptadaśavidhaṃ buddhivaikalyam / ete 'śaktibhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Comes to be' continues [from the previous verse]. Among these, the deficiency of the external instruments together with <s>manas</s> is of eleven kinds. The deficiency of <s>buddhi</s> is of seventeen kinds. These are the varieties of incapacity.
Contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) is ninefold; attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) is eightfold. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 47)

children.text: evaṃ caturvidhasya pratyayasargasya guṇavaiṣamyavimardena pañcāśadbhedā bhavanti // 47 //
children.translated_text: Thus, through the friction of the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇa</s>s, the fourfold intellectual creation has fifty varieties.
<s>Kārikā</s> 48

children.text:
vistareṇa tu padārthaśatasahasramānantyaṃ vā lakṣaṇānām /
  kathamityucyate yasmāt-
children.translated_text: But in detail, there are a hundred thousand categories of characteristics, or an infinite [number]. How? It is said, because —
The varieties of <s>tamas</s> (darkness) are eightfold.

children.text: ya ete pañca viparyayabhedā vyākhyātāḥ teṣu tamaso 'ṣṭavidho bhedaḥ / katham ? paravijñānamāśritya pravṛttasyāṣṭāsu prakṛtiṣvaparāsu parābhimānagrahāt /
children.translated_text: Of these five varieties of error that have been explained, <s>tamas</s> has an eightfold division. How? Because one who has engaged [in error] relying on the knowledge of others identifies the eight inferior <s>prakṛti</s>s (primary principles) as the supreme.
And of <s>moha</s> (delusion),

children.text: kim ? aṣṭavidho bheda iti / caśabdātkāryakaraṇasāmarthye 'ṣṭavidhe 'ṇimādāvahamiti pratyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: what? An eightfold division — implied by the word 'and.' [This is] the cognition 'I am' with respect to the eight kinds of capacity of the causal complex, such as <s>aṇimā</s> (the power of becoming minute) and the rest.
<s>Mahāmoha</s> (great delusion) is tenfold.

children.text: mātṛpitṛbhrātṛsvasṛpatnīputraduhitṛgurumitropakārilakṣaṇe daśavidhe kuṭumbe yo 'yaṃ mametyabhiniveśaḥ / dṛṣṭānuśravikeṣu vā śabdādiṣvityapare / sa daśavidho mahāmohaḥ parisaṃkhyāyate /
children.translated_text: The attachment 'this is mine' regarding a family of ten kinds — characterized as mother, father, brother, sister, wife, son, daughter, teacher, friend, and benefactor. Or [according to] others, regarding sounds and the like, whether seen or heard of. This great delusion is enumerated as tenfold.
<s>Tāmisra</s> (gloom) is eighteenfold.

children.text: aṣṭavidhe kāryakaraṇasāmarthye daśavidhe ca kuṭumbe viṣayeṣu vā yaḥ pratihanyamānasyāveśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The violent emotion of one who is thwarted with respect to the eight kinds of capacity of the causal complex and the ten kinds of family or sense objects.
And <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness) is likewise. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 48)

children.text:
tatheti sāmānyātideśārthaḥ / andhatāmisro 'ṣṭādaśadhaiveti / katham ? asāvapyaṣṭavidhātkāryakaraṇasāmarthyāddaśavidhācca kuṭumbātpratyavasānasya viṣādaḥ /
  evamete pañca viparyayabhedāḥ svalakṣaṇato viṣayaviśeṣā lakṣitāḥ / tatrāpi cāṣṭāsu prakṛtiṣu sattvarajastamasāṃ saṃhataviviktapariṇatavyastasamastānāṃ paratvābhimānabhedādekaikā prakṛtiḥ pañcadaśabhedā / ata eva te 'ṣṭau pañcadaśa viṃśaṃ śataṃ ca bhavanti / yathā mokṣe pravṛttasya evaṃ dharmakāmeṣvapi / ekaḥ padārtho vistareṇa parisaṃkhyāyamāno 'nantabhedaḥ sampadyate / nidarśanamātrametadācāryeṇa kṛtam / evamaśaktyādiṣvapi lakṣaṇāntareṣu yojyam / seyamavidyā pañcaparvā saprapañcā vyākhyātā / tadanantaroddiṣṭānaśaktibhedānvakṣyāmaḥ // 48 //
children.translated_text: 'Likewise' serves the purpose of general extension. <s>Andhatāmisra</s> is also eighteenfold. How? It is the despair at death arising from the eightfold capacity of the causal complex and the tenfold family. Thus these five varieties of error have been characterized according to their specific objects and individual natures. And further, among the eight <s>prakṛti</s>s, due to the different [combinations of] <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — combined, separated, transformed, individual, and aggregate — each <s>prakṛti</s> has fifteen varieties due to the differences in the conceit of supremacy. Therefore those eight [times] fifteen become one hundred and twenty. Just as for one engaged in liberation, so too for one [engaged in] <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s>. A single category, when enumerated in detail, turns out to have infinite divisions. This is merely an illustration given by the master. The same should be applied to the other categories of incapacity and the like as well. This five-part ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) with its elaboration has been explained. We shall now explain the varieties of incapacity enumerated in connection with it.
<s>Kārikā</s> 49

children.text:
āha, ativyāsābhihitamidamiti nāsmākaṃ buddhāvavatiṣṭhate / tasmādviparyayoktaṃ bhedābhidhānaṃ parityajya vaktavyam kathamaśaktiraṣṭāviṃśatibhedeti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text: One says: this has been stated too elaborately and does not remain in our understanding. Therefore, setting aside the statement of varieties given under error, it should be stated: how is incapacity twenty-eight-fold? It is replied:
The eleven impairments of the sense organs, together with the impairments of <s>buddhi</s>, have been enumerated as incapacity.

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ vadhā indriyavadhāḥ / svasaṃskāraviṣayayogātprakarṣāpannena tamasā grahaṇarūpasya sattvasyābhibhavātsvaviṣayeṣvapravṛttayaḥ / tadyathā
children.translated_text: The impairments of the sense organs are '<s>indriyavadhā</s>s.' [These are] non-functioning with respect to their own objects, due to the suppression of <s>sattva</s>, whose nature is apprehension, by <s>tamas</s> which has reached its excess through the conjunction with its own dispositions and objects. Namely:
Deafness, blindness, loss of smell, muteness, numbness,
madness, skin disease, crippled hands, impotence, constipation, and lameness.

children.text:
tatra bādhiryaṃ śrotrasya, āndhyaṃ cakṣuṣaḥ, aghratvaṃ nāsikāyāḥ, mūkatā vācaḥ, jaḍatā rasanasya, unmādo manasaḥ, kauṣṭhyaṃ tvacaḥ, kauṇyaṃ pāṇeḥ, klaibyamupasthasya, udāvartaḥ pāyoḥ, paṅgutā pādayorityevamindriyavadhā ekādaśa /
  anye tu
children.translated_text: Among these: deafness is [the impairment] of the ear; blindness of the eye; loss of smell of the nose; muteness of speech; numbness of the tongue; madness of the mind; skin disease of the skin; crippled hands of the hand; impotence of the reproductive organ; constipation of the anus; lameness of the feet. Thus the impairments of the sense organs are eleven. Others however [say]:
The seventeen impairments of <s>buddhi</s> are the inversions of contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) and attainment (<s>siddhi</s>). (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 49)

children.text:
tatra tuṣṭayaḥ prakṛtyādyā vakṣyamāṇāḥ, tāsāṃ dvividho viparyayaḥ / avyutpannasya yogadharmeṇa tasyāṃ bhūmāvapravṛttiḥ, vyutpannasya cottarabhūmyaparijñānātpūrvasyāṃ bhūmāvakṣemarūpeṇa grahaṇam / ātmavido vā sarvāsu bhūmiṣu / teṣu yatpūrvaṃ tadaśaktibhāvābhipretam / yanmadhyamaṃ tadāpekṣikam / katham ? tanmātrabhūmyavastho hi yogyasmitādibhūmyanavajayāttuṣṭo mahābhūtātikramātsiddhaḥ / tathā vijitāsmitārūpo mahadādyavasthāpekṣayā tuṣṭaḥ, pūrvabhūmyapekṣayā siddhaḥ / evaṃ mahadavasthaḥ pradhānāpekṣayā pūrvāpekṣayā ca / pradhānāvasthaḥ puruṣāpekṣayā pūrvāpekṣayā ca / guṇapuruṣāntarajñastu siddha eva / tasmādavyutpannasyāmbhaḥprabhṛtiṣu navānambhaḥprabhṛtayo buddhivadhāḥ / tārakādiviparyayeṇāṣṭāvatārakādayaḥ / eṣā khalvaśaktiraṣṭāviṃśatibhedā /
  tuṣṭistu sannihitaviṣayasantoṣāccikīrṣitādarthādūnena nivṛttiḥ sāmānyata ekaiva, pratyarthamanantā, śatena tuṣṭaḥ sahasreṇeti / śāstre tu bāhyādhyātmikānāṃ sukhaduḥkhamohānāṃ prāptiṣvapagameṣu vācāvyavasthyalakṣaṇā upāyanavatvānnava tuṣṭayo bhavanti // 49 //
children.translated_text: Among these, the contentments beginning with <s>prakṛti</s> and the rest will be stated later. Their inversion is twofold: for one who is uninstructed, non-engagement in that stage due to the discipline of <s>yoga</s>; and for one who is instructed, clinging to the earlier stage in the form of complacency due to not having fully comprehended the higher stage. Or [it applies to] the knower of the self at all stages. Among these, what is first is intended as the state of incapacity; what is intermediate is relative. How? For one stationed at the level of the <s>tanmātra</s>s, being content because of not having conquered the levels of <s>yoga</s>, <s>asmitā</s>, and the like, is perfected through having transcended the gross elements. Similarly, one who has conquered the level of <s>asmitā</s>, compared to the level of <s>mahat</s> and the rest, is content, but compared to the previous level, is perfected. Similarly, one stationed at the level of <s>mahat</s>, compared to <s>pradhāna</s> and compared to the previous [level]. One stationed at the level of <s>pradhāna</s>, compared to <s>puruṣa</s> and compared to the previous [level]. But one who knows the difference between the <s>guṇa</s>s and <s>puruṣa</s> is simply perfected. Therefore, for one who is uninstructed, the nine [contentments] beginning with <s>ambhas</s> (waters) and the rest are the impairments of <s>buddhi</s>; through the inversion of <s>tāraka</s> (the saving [knowledge]) and the rest, the eight beginning with <s>tāraka</s> [are also impairments]. This indeed is the twenty-eight-fold incapacity. Contentment, generally speaking, is a single [thing] — the cessation from an object that is less than what is desired, due to satisfaction with what is at hand. But with reference to each object, it is infinite — 'content with a hundred, content with a thousand,' and so forth. But in the <s>śāstra</s>, contentments are nine in number because of their novelty as conventional designations regarding the attainments and departures of external and internal pleasures, pains, and delusions.
<s>Kārikā</s> 50
Of those [contentments] —
four are internal: they are called <s>prakṛti</s> (nature), <s>upādāna</s> (means), <s>kāla</s> (time), and <s>bhāgya</s> (fortune).

children.text:
ādhyātmikī iti śarīraśarīriṇorviśeṣamupalipsamānena yoginā yadanātmanyātmabuddhiravasthāpyate sā khalvādhyātmikī siddhiḥ tuṣṭiḥ santoṣaḥ kṣema ityarthaḥ /
  tāsāṃ prakṛtyākhyā / yadā vītāvītaiḥ pradhānamadhigamya tatpūrvakatvaṃ ca mahadādīnāṃ vikārāṇāmānantyācca pradhānātmanaḥ kṛtsnasya mahadādibhāvena vipariṇāmāsambhavādekadeśasyāprakṛtivikārabhūtasya bhoktṛtvamakartṛtvaṃ cādhyavasya saṅgadveṣanivṛttiṃ labhate, sādyā tuṣṭirambha ityabhidhīyate / kasmāt ? amitaṃ hi pradhānatattvaṃ bhāti jagadbījabhūtatvānmahadādibhāvapariṇāmena nyūnasyaikadeśasyātmana evāpūrāt / tadvyatirekeṇa cānyasyaikadeśasyobhayadharmiṇo bhoktṛbhūtasya sadbhāvātsaṃprakṣālane 'pi cāpasaṃhṛtam, vaiśvarūpyasyānucchedāt / tathā ca śāstramāha- ambha iti guṇaliṅgasannicayamevādhikurute / guṇāśca sattvarajastamāṃsi / liṅgaṃ ca mahadādi atra sannihitaṃ bhavati / tadidaṃ pradhānamamitaṃ bhātyamitamupalabhyata ityambhaḥ / sa khalvayaṃ yogī pradhānalakṣaṇāṃ bhūmimavajitya tanmahimnā ca tadaśūnyaṃ dṛṣṭvā vyatiriktasya padārthāntarasyābhāvaṃ manyamānastāmeva bhūmiṃ kaivalyamiti gṛhṇāti / bhinne ca dehe prakṛtau layaṃ gacchati, tataśca punarāvartate / tasyāṃ ca tuṣṭāvanye sapta mahadādikāraṇino 'varuddhā draṣṭavyāḥ / tatra yathā prādhānikasya puruṣe nāsti vijñānaṃ evamitareṣāmuttareṣu tattveṣu / mahatkāraṇinaḥ pradhāne 'smitākāraṇino mahati, tanmātrakāraṇino 'haṃkāre / tadekadeśāścaiṣāṃ bhoktāraḥ pūrvavat / atrāpi ca sattvādīnāṃ saṃhataviviktapariṇatavyastasamastānāṃ bhedādavidyāvacchedānantyamavaseyam /
  āha, tuṣṭyavidyayorabhedaḥ lakṣaṇaikatvāt / aṣṭāsu prakṛtiṣvātmabuddhistuṣṭiḥ / tadeva ca tama ityavidyākāṇḍe nirdiṣṭam / tasmātpadārthasaṃkara iti /
  ucyate- na, pratyayaviśeṣāt / tamaḥpradhānapuruṣopadeśe sati pratyayanirdidhārayiṣayā tayoḥ pradhānameva jyāyo na puruṣa ityabhiniviśeta / tuṣṭistu kiṃ paramityāśritya pravṛttaḥ pradhānajñānamātre santoṣātpadārthāntaraṃ vijñātumeva nādriyate / kiṃ ca prahāṇaviśeṣāt / nirūḍhamūlo hyanātmani ātmagraho jñānottarakālabhāvanayā prahātavyaḥ / tamobahulatvāttama ityabhidhīyate / pelavastu sattvabahulo darśanapraṇayastuṣṭiḥ / kiṃca tattvābhijayāt / vijitabhūmikasya hi yoginastanmāhātmyavaśīkṛtatvād bhūmyantare pravṛttistuṣṭiḥ / itarasya tvabhiniveśamātramevetyanayorviśeṣaḥ / tasmānna padārthasaṃkara iti vyākhyātā prakṛtyākhyā tuṣṭiḥ /
  yadā tu satyapi prakṛtisāmarthye nānapekṣya yathāsvamupādānaṃ bhāvānāmutpattiḥ sambhavati prakṛtyaviśeṣe sarvakālamutpattiprasaṃgāt, prakṛtikṛtyamevedaṃ viśvamityabhyupagacchatastadaviśeṣād goḥ puruṣādutpattiprasaṃgaḥ, puruṣasya vā mahiṣāt / kiṃ ca jātyabhedaprasaṃgāt / prakṛtikṛtyamidaṃ viśvamityabhyupagacchato jātibhedo na syāt, tadaviśeṣāt / dṛṣṭaṃ tūpādānājjātyanuvidhānaṃ bhāvānām / tasmāttadeva kāraṇatvena parikalpayituṃ nyāyyam / upādānaikadeśa eva ca kāryakāraṇavidhātmā bhoktetyetasmād darśanātsaṅgadveṣanivṛttiṃ labhate, sā dvitīyā tuṣṭiḥ salilamityabhidhīyate / kathaṃ punaretatsalilam ? satyupādāne vikāro līyata iti / tathā ca kṛtvā śāsramāha "salilaṃ salilamiti vaikārikopanipātamevādhikurute, sati tasmiṃllīyate jagaditi" / sa khalvayaṃ yogī pārthivānavajitya tanmahimnā jagadaśūnyaṃ dṛṣṭvā padārthāntarasyābhāvaṃ manyamānastāmeva bhūmiṃ kaivalyamiti gṛhṇāti / bhinne ca dehe pṛthivyādiṣu līyate / tataśca punarāvartate /
  yadā ca satyupādānasāmarthye na tāvataiva bhāvānāṃ prādurbhāvaḥ kiṃ tarhi sannihitasādhanānāmapi kālaṃ pratyapekṣā bhavati- kālaviśeṣādbījādaṅkuro jāyate, aṅkurānnālaṃ, nālātkāṇḍam, kāṇḍātprasava ityādi / anyathā tūpādānānāṃ sannidhānamātrātkṣaṇenaivāmīṣāmavasthāviśeṣāṇāmabhivyaktiḥ syāt / kiṃca kālaviparyayeṇotpattiprasaṃgāt / na caitadiṣṭam / kiṃ ca tadanabhidhānāt / dṛśyante ca prāṇināṃ kālānurūpāḥ svābhāvāhāravihāravyavasthāḥ / tasmādasāveva kāraṇam / tadekadeśaścāprakṛtivikārabhūto bhoktetyetasmāddarśanātsaṃgadveṣanivṛttiṃ labhate, sā tṛtīyā tuṣṭirogha ityabhidhīyate / kathaṃ punarayaṃ kāla ogha ityucyate ? salilaughavatsarvābhyāvahanāt / tadyathā salilaughastṛṇaṃ kāṣṭhamaśmānaṃ prāṇinaṃ vā svamūrtisaṃsṛṣṭaṃ sarvamevābhyāvahati, evamayaṃ kālo garbhādbālyaṃ, bālyātkaumāraṃ, kaumārādyauvanaṃ, yauvanātsthāviryam, sthāviryānmaraṇaṃ, tathā bījānmūlaṃ mūlādaṅkuramiti vahati / tathā cāha

children.translated_text: "The very first night that a person comes into being in the womb,
having set forth, he continues on that [path]; he goes and does not return."

<s>Ādhyātmikī</s> (pertaining to the self) means: when a <s>yogin</s> desiring to discern the distinction between the body and the embodied soul establishes the notion of self in what is not the self, that indeed is the <s>ādhyātmikī siddhi</s> (internal attainment), <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment), <s>santoṣa</s> (satisfaction), <s>kṣema</s> (security) — this is the meaning.
Among these, the one called <s>prakṛti</s> (nature) is as follows: when, through discriminating and non-discriminating [cognitions], one has apprehended <s>pradhāna</s> (the primal matter) and the fact that <s>mahat</s> (the great one) and the other <s>vikāras</s> (evolutes) are preceded by it, and because of the infinity of <s>pradhāna</s> in its essential nature, and because the complete transformation of the whole into the form of <s>mahat</s> and the rest is impossible, one ascertains that a portion which is not a modification of <s>prakṛti</s> is an experiencer and a non-agent, and thereby obtains the cessation of attachment and aversion — that first <s>tuṣṭi</s> is called <s>ambhas</s> (water). Why? Because the <s>pradhāna</s> principle appears limitless, being the seed of the world, through transformation into the state of <s>mahat</s> and the rest, due to the incompleteness of the self which is merely a portion; and because of the existence of another portion, possessing the properties of both, which is the experiencer, distinct from it; and even when washed away, it is not withdrawn, since its manifold nature is not destroyed. And thus the <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative text) says: "<s>Ambhas</s> refers precisely to the aggregate of <s>guṇa</s>-marks (<s>guṇaliṅga</s>). The <s>guṇas</s> are <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. And the <s>liṅga</s> (mark), namely <s>mahat</s> and the rest, is present here. This <s>pradhāna</s> appears limitless, is apprehended as limitless — hence <s>ambhas</s>." That <s>yogin</s>, having conquered the level characterized by <s>pradhāna</s>, and seeing through its greatness that [the world] is not empty of it, considering there to be no other category beyond it, grasps that very level as <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). And when the body breaks apart, he dissolves into <s>prakṛti</s>, and from there he returns again. And those who are content with that [level] — seven others, those whose cause is <s>mahat</s> and the rest, should be understood as included. There, just as the one whose [cause is] <s>pradhāna</s> has no knowledge regarding <s>puruṣa</s> (the self), so too the others regarding the higher <s>tattvas</s> (principles): the one whose cause is <s>mahat</s> [is absorbed] in <s>pradhāna</s>, the one whose cause is <s>asmitā</s> (ego) in <s>mahat</s>, the one whose cause is the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) in <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle). And the experiencers of these are portions of each, as before. Here too, from the differentiation of <s>sattva</s> and the rest — combined, separated, transformed, individual, and aggregate — the infinity of the divisions of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) should be understood.
[Objection:] There is no difference between <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), since their characteristics are identical. The notion of self in the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (material causes) is <s>tuṣṭi</s>; and that very thing has been designated as <s>tamas</s> (darkness) in the section on <s>avidyā</s>. Therefore there is a confusion of categories.
[Reply:] No, because of the difference in mental disposition. When there is instruction concerning <s>tamas</s>, <s>pradhāna</s>, and <s>puruṣa</s>, one who desires to fix his understanding clings to the view that <s>pradhāna</s> alone is superior, not <s>puruṣa</s>. But <s>tuṣṭi</s> is one who, having taken recourse to "what is the highest?", is satisfied with mere knowledge of <s>pradhāna</s> and does not even care to know any other category. Moreover, because of the difference in abandonment: the deeply rooted notion of self in what is not the self must be abandoned through contemplation in the period following knowledge. Because of the preponderance of <s>tamas</s>, it is called <s>tamas</s>. But the gentle one, predominant in <s>sattva</s>, who is inclined toward seeing — that is <s>tuṣṭi</s>. Furthermore, because of the conquest of <s>tattvas</s> (principles): for the <s>yogin</s> who has conquered [a particular] level, <s>tuṣṭi</s> is the inclination toward another level, being under the sway of its greatness. For the other, it is mere obstinate clinging — this is the distinction between the two. Therefore there is no confusion of categories — thus the <s>tuṣṭi</s> called <s>prakṛti</s> has been explained.
When, however, even though the capacity of <s>prakṛti</s> exists, the production of things is not possible without reference to their respective material causes (<s>upādāna</s>) — since if there were no distinction in <s>prakṛti</s>, production would follow at all times; and for one who accepts that this entire universe is merely the work of <s>prakṛti</s>, since there is no distinction in it, there would be the absurd consequence that a cow could be born from a man, or a man from a buffalo. Moreover, because there would be the absurd consequence of no distinction of species: for one who accepts that this universe is the work of <s>prakṛti</s>, there would be no differentiation of species, since there is no distinction in it. But it is observed that things follow their species according to their material cause. Therefore it is proper to conceive of that alone as the cause. And one who holds the view that an experiencer, who is a portion of the material cause itself, is of the nature of the cause-effect relation, and thereby obtains the cessation of attachment and aversion — that is the second <s>tuṣṭi</s>, called <s>salila</s> (water/fluid). But how is this called <s>salila</s>? Because when the material cause exists, the modification dissolves [back into it]. And thus, having done so, the <s>śāstra</s> says: "<s>Salila</s>, <s>salila</s> — this refers to the subsidence of modifications; when that [material cause] exists, the world dissolves into it." That <s>yogin</s>, having conquered the earthly [elements], seeing through their greatness that the world is not empty [of them], considering there to be no other category, grasps that very level as <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). And when the body breaks apart, he dissolves into earth and the other [elements]. And from there he returns again.
When, however, even though the capacity of the material cause exists, the manifestation of things does not occur by that alone, but rather there is dependence upon time even for those whose means are at hand — from a particular time a sprout is born from a seed, from the sprout a stem, from the stem a stalk, from the stalk a blossom, and so on. Otherwise, from the mere proximity of material causes, the manifestation of these particular stages would occur in a single instant. Moreover, because there would be the absurd consequence of production in reverse temporal order. And this is not desired. Furthermore, because of non-specification of that [time]. And living beings are observed to have natural patterns of food and activity conforming to time. Therefore that [time] alone is the cause. And one who holds the view that an experiencer is a portion of it, not being a modification of <s>prakṛti</s>, and thereby obtains the cessation of attachment and aversion — that is the third <s>tuṣṭi</s>, called <s>ogha</s> (flood). But how is this time called <s>ogha</s>? Because it carries everything along like a flood of water. Just as a flood of water carries along everything that is mixed with its own form — grass, wood, stone, or a living being — so too this time carries one from the womb to childhood, from childhood to youth, from youth to maturity, from maturity to old age, from old age to death; likewise from seed to root, from root to sprout, and so on. And thus it is said:

tasmādoghasāmānyādoghaḥ kālaḥ / sa khalvayaṃ yogī kālamavajitya padārthāntarābhāvaṃ manyamānastāmeva bhūmiṃ kaivalyamiti manyate / dehabhede ca kālamanupraviśati / tataśca punarāvartate /
  yadā tu satyapi kālasāmarthye bhāvānāmutpattiḥ bhāgyānapekṣate / kasmāt ? tatsannidhāne 'pyaprādurbhāvāt / satyapi sādhanasāmarthye kālaviśeṣe ca kasyacidutpattirbhavati kasyacinneti / tasmādasti kāraṇāntaraṃ yadapekṣya bhāvānāmutpattiranutpattiśca / kiṃ cābhyutthānānupapattiprasaṃgāt / kālamātrātphalaṃ bhavatītyetadicchataḥ śāstrokteṣu kriyāviśeṣeṣvabhiṣecanavratopavāsāgnihotrādiṣvabhyutthānaṃ na syāt / kasmāt ? ānarthakyāt / asti ca, tasmānna kālanimittā bhāvānāmutpattiḥ / kiṃ ca tadanuvidhānāt / dṛśyante khalvapi prakṛtyupādānakālāviśeṣe 'pi bhāgyaviśeṣātphalaviśeṣāḥ / tasmāttatsaṃkāra eva kāraṇam / tadekadeśaścāprakṛtivikārabhūto bhoktetyetasmāddarśanātsaṃgadveṣanivṛttiṃ labhate / sā caturthī tuṣṭirvṛṣṭirityabhidhīyate / kathaṃ punarvṛṣṭirityucyate / sarvasattvāpyāyanāt / yathā hi śīrṇānāmapi tṛṇalatādīnāṃ vṛṣṭiṃ prāpya punarāpyāyanaṃ bhavati, evameva sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ bhāgyavipariṇāmātpunarāpyāyanaṃ bhavati / tasmādvṛṣṭisāmyād bhāgyākhyā tuṣṭirvṛṣṭirityabhidhīyate / śāstramapyāha- "vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭiriti śriya evopanipātamadhikurute / sā hi vṛṣṭivatsarvamāpyāyatīti /" sa khalvayaṃ yogī bhāgyānyavajitya tanmahimnā jagadaśūnyaṃ dṛṣṭvā padārthāntarasyābhāvaṃ manyamānastāmeva bhūmiṃ kaivalyamiti gṛhṇāti / sa tasyāmeva dehabhede līyate / tataśca punarāvartata iti /
  āha, kālabhāgyayorapratipattiḥ, samākhyāparijñānāt / prakṛtyātmakasya tāvadyogino 'ṣṭau prakṛtayo viṣaya ityuktaṃ purastāt / upādānātmakasya ca pṛthivyādīni mahābhūtāni / kālabhāgyayostu na tathoktam / tasmādvaktavyaṃ kasya tattvasyaiṣā samākhyeti ?
  ucyate- na, uktatvāt / prāgevaitadapadiṣṭaṃ na kālo nāma kaścitpadārtho 'sti / kiṃ tarhi kriyāsu kālasaṃjñā / tāśca karaṇavṛttiriti / pratipāditam / na cānyā vṛttirvṛttimataḥ / tasmātkāraṇacaitanyapratijñaḥ kālātmaka iti / bhāgyasaṃjñā tu dharmādharmayoḥ / tau ca buddhidharmāviti prāgapadiṣṭam / tasmādbhāgyavādī buddhicaitanika iti /
  āha, na tuṣṭyantaratvāt / prakṛtitvānmahānpūrvaṃ prakṛtyākhyāyāṃ tuṣṭāvavaruddhaḥ / tasyedānīṃ tuṣṭyantaratvena parikalpanaṃ nātisamañjasamiti /
  ucyate- mahāṃstarhi pūrvatuṣṭiviṣayabhāvādapakṛṣyata iti / kāryakaraṇavṛttikriyārūpāṃ vṛttimaddyotyāṃ parikalpya tasyāṃ kālatvamayamāha / mahataśca rūpaṃ dharmādikaṃ mahato 'rthāntaraṃ bhāgyamiti bhāgyavān / athavā bāhya evāyaṃ kālaḥ karmakāraṇaṃ nirdiśyate / tatra cānye 'pi svamatiparikalpitapadārthāntarātmabhāvagrahā eveti sāṅkhyāḥ pravādinaḥ pratikṣiptā boddhavyā iti /
  apara āha, prakṛticaitanikaḥ pradhānabhāvāśādyupādānakālabhāgyavādino mahadahaṅkāratanmātravādina iti / tadetadapasiddhatvādayuktam / na hi mahadahaṅkāratanmātralakṣaṇāḥ prakṛtaya upādānakālabhāgyabhāvena prasiddhāḥ / tasmādidamapyayuktam / evametā ādhyātmikyaścatasrastuṣṭayaḥ /

Therefore, because of its similarity to a flood, time is called <s>ogha</s> (flood). That <s>yogin</s>, having conquered time, considering there to be no other category, regards that very level as <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). And at the dissolution of the body, he enters into time. And from there he returns again.
When, however, even though the capacity of time exists, the production of things depends upon <s>bhāgya</s> (fortune). Why? Because even in its presence, manifestation does not occur [for all]. Even when there is capacity of the means and a particular time, for some there is production and for some there is not. Therefore there exists another cause, with reference to which there is production and non-production of things. Moreover, because there would be the absurd consequence that exertion would be pointless: for one who desires that fruit comes from time alone, there would be no point in exerting oneself in the specific rites prescribed by the <s>śāstras</s> — <s>abhiṣecana</s> (consecration), <s>vrata</s> (vows), <s>upavāsa</s> (fasting), <s>agnihotra</s> (fire sacrifice), and so on. Why? Because they would be purposeless. But [exertion] does exist; therefore the production of things is not caused by time alone. Moreover, because of conformity to that [fortune]: even when there is no distinction in <s>prakṛti</s>, material cause, and time, differences in results are observed due to differences in fortune. Therefore that disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>) alone is the cause. And one who holds the view that an experiencer is a portion of it, not being a modification of <s>prakṛti</s>, and thereby obtains the cessation of attachment and aversion — that is the fourth <s>tuṣṭi</s>, called <s>vṛṣṭi</s> (rain). But how is it called <s>vṛṣṭi</s>? Because it nourishes all beings. Just as withered grasses and creepers, upon receiving rain, are nourished again, so too all living beings are nourished again through the transformation of fortune. Therefore, because of its similarity to rain, the <s>tuṣṭi</s> called <s>bhāgya</s> (fortune) is designated as <s>vṛṣṭi</s> (rain). The <s>śāstra</s> also says: "<s>Vṛṣṭi</s>, <s>vṛṣṭi</s> — this refers to the subsidence of <s>śrī</s> (prosperity). For she, like rain, nourishes everything." That <s>yogin</s>, having conquered the [realm of] fortune, seeing through its greatness that the world is not empty [of it], considering there to be no other category, grasps that very level as <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). At the dissolution of the body, he dissolves into that very [fortune]. And from there he returns again.
[Objection:] There is no apprehension of time and fortune [as separate categories], because of the knowledge of their designations. For the <s>yogin</s> whose [cause is] <s>prakṛti</s>, the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> have been stated previously as the objects. And for the one whose [cause is] the material cause, the great elements beginning with earth. But for time and fortune, nothing has been stated in that way. Therefore one must state: of which <s>tattva</s> (principle) is this designation?
[Reply:] No, because it has already been stated. It has been indicated earlier that there is no entity called "time." Rather, the designation "time" applies to actions, and these are the activity of the instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>) — this has been established. And the activity is not different from that which possesses the activity. Therefore, one who maintains that the cause is conscious, being of the nature of time [is subsumed under that]. And the designation <s>bhāgya</s> (fortune) belongs to <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit). And these are properties of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), as has been indicated before. Therefore, the proponent of fortune is one who holds consciousness to be [a property of] <s>buddhi</s>.
[Objection:] No, because it would be [identical with] another <s>tuṣṭi</s>. Since <s>mahat</s> (the great one) is a <s>prakṛti</s> (material cause), it has already been included in the <s>tuṣṭi</s> called <s>prakṛti</s>. To now conceive of it as a different <s>tuṣṭi</s> is not quite appropriate.
[Reply:] Then <s>mahat</s> is withdrawn from being an object of the former <s>tuṣṭi</s>. Having conceived of a function in the form of the activity of effects and instruments that is to be illuminated, he declares it to be time. And the form of <s>mahat</s>, consisting of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and so on, being something different from <s>mahat</s> [in its causal aspect], is fortune — thus one who holds fortune [as the cause]. Alternatively, this time is taught as an external cause of action. And there too, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teachers should be understood as having refuted others who cling to the notion of self in categories fabricated by their own intellect.
Another says: the one who holds consciousness to be [a property of] <s>prakṛti</s> [includes] those who advocate <s>pradhāna</s>, the nature of things, material cause, time, and fortune; [those who advocate] <s>mahat</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>tanmātras</s>. But this is untenable because it is refuted. For the <s>prakṛtis</s> characterized as <s>mahat</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and <s>tanmātras</s> are not known in the form of material cause, time, and fortune. Therefore this too is untenable. Thus these four internal (<s>ādhyātmikī</s>) <s>tuṣṭis</s> [have been explained].

children.translated_text: "One should not inflict upon another what is disagreeable to oneself;
this, in brief, is <s>dharma</s> (righteousness); one who acts otherwise is driven by desire."

The word "<s>ca</s>" (and) is used in the sense of emphasis. For a <s>yogin</s> who has not properly investigated the nature of the self, the cessation of the fault of attachment merely from seeing the defects of sense objects is the external <s>tuṣṭi</s>. In this regard, when one recognizes the fault in acquisition — since not everyone has noble birth, one who is in need must necessarily engage in the acquisition of sense objects. Because of their non-inherent nature, they remain only in certain places — this has been stated before. Moreover, because they have adversaries. Even without conceiving of the natural abiding of sense objects, when one is inclined toward acquisition through receiving gifts and so on, that too is improper. Why? Because there are adversaries. Even so, there is no one without adversaries in the acquisition of sense objects, and therefore one must necessarily strive against their obstruction. And if, while striving, one should destroy the adversary's obstruction, then through the practice of benefiting oneself by harming another, there would be conflict with the <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative teaching). For it is said:
And again it is said:
"Whatever wealth arises from injury to living beings,
that should be abandoned without regard, for it brings destruction in the next world."
"Therefore, knowing that [beings] made of <s>sattva</s> and the rest are merely aggregates, like a pot and the like,
up to <s>Brahmā</s>, [knowing] the impermanence of bodies,
the happiness that is truly proclaimed by the good as [fleeting as] a blazing firebrand of grass,
should not be brought down by the firmly established sufferings that arise in the next body."

children.text:
atha punarayaṃ pratyanīkairvihanyate, tato 'sya viṣayābhāvaḥ / sukhārthaṃ ca pravṛttasya bhūyiṣṭhaṃ duḥkhamevetyetasmāddarśanānmādhyasthyaṃ labhate, sā pañcamī tuṣṭiḥ sutāramityabhidhīyate / kathaṃ punaḥ sutāramityucyate ? sukhamanenopāyena taranti viṣayasaṃkaṭamiti sutāram /
  yadā tu yogī pūrvadoṣādhigame 'bhijātyā vā yatnārjitaviṣayatve sati rakṣādoṣamupanyasyati / katham ? bhoktṛbhogyabhāvāvyatirekāt sarvaprāṇisādhāraṇā viṣayāḥ, tasmātteṣāṃ rakṣā vidheyā / tasyāṃ ca pravartamāno yadi paramuparundhyāt tadā pūrvoktadoṣaḥ, athātmānaṃ, viṣayābhāvaḥ / rātrindivaṃ ca tadekāgramanasaḥ sukhārthaṃ pravṛtasya bhūyiṣṭhaṃ duḥkhamevetyetasmāddarśanānmādhyasthyaṃ labhate / sā ṣaṣṭhī tuṣṭiḥ supāramityabhidhīyate / kathaṃ punaḥ supāramityucyate ? sukhamanena pāraṃ viṣayārṇavasya prayāntīti /
  yadā tu sati pūrvadoṣe, sati vā grāmanagaranigamasanniveśādyupāyānuṣṭhānādvā kṛtaviṣayarakṣo yogī kṣayadoṣamupanyasyati / katham ?

children.translated_text: That substance by which embodied beings, through delusion, wish to ward off [suffering],
that very thing, because of its destructibility, becomes the cause of their dissatisfaction.

But when this [yogin] is overcome by adversaries, then he has no objects. And for one who has exerted himself for the sake of happiness, the predominant result is suffering alone — from this perception he attains equanimity. This is the fifth contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), called '<s>sutāram</s>' (good crossing). How is it called '<s>sutāram</s>'? Because by this means they easily cross over the difficulty of sense objects — hence '<s>sutāram</s>.'
  But when the <s>yogin</s>, upon perceiving the previous defects, or when, through noble birth or having acquired objects through effort, he presents the defect of protection: How? Because the objects of experience, by the inseparability of the enjoyer-enjoyed relation, are common to all beings — therefore their protection must be arranged. And in undertaking that [protection], if he obstructs another, then the previously stated defect [arises]; if [he obstructs] himself, [there is] the absence of objects. And for one who, day and night, with single-pointed mind, has exerted himself for the sake of happiness, the predominant result is suffering alone — from this perception he attains equanimity. This is the sixth contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), called '<s>supāram</s>' (good far shore). How is it called '<s>supāram</s>'? Because by this means they happily reach the far shore of the ocean of sense objects.
The sense objects of those who crave objects, obtained with effort and well-guarded,
perish even as they watch, like bubbles on water.
There is nothing in this world, movable or immovable,
whose destruction is not seen, either through perception or through inference.
Therefore, one who is attached to perishable things — sons, wife, home, and the like —
the wise one should deliberately turn away the notion of 'mine.'

children.text:
iti etasmāddarśanānmādhyasthyaṃ labhate, sā saptamī tuṣṭiḥ sunetramityucyate /
  kathaṃ punaḥ sunetramityucyate ?
  sukhamanenātmānaṃ kaivalyāvasthāṃ nayantīti sunetram /
  yadā tu satsu pūrvadoṣeṣu prasaṅgadoṣamupanyasyati / katham ? prāptaviṣayāṇāmindriyāṇāṃ tadabhilāṣānnivṛtistatsukham / viṣayajighṛkṣayā ca duḥkham / prāptirapyeṣāmanupaśāntaye tadupabhogakauśalāya ca / yasmādāha-

children.translated_text: When a sense-enjoyer continuously indulges in sense objects,
his intention for them increases all the more.

From this perception he attains equanimity. This is the seventh contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), called '<s>sunetram</s>' (good guide).
  How is it called '<s>sunetram</s>'?
  Because by this [means] they happily lead themselves to the state of <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) — hence '<s>sunetram</s>.'
  But when, the previous defects remaining, he presents the defect of attachment: How? The cessation of the craving of the senses that have obtained objects — that is happiness. And the desire to seize objects is suffering. Their attainment too is for non-pacification and for skill in enjoyment. As it is said:
Therefore, even as one might quench a submarine fire,
one cannot turn the senses away from objects through enjoyment.
Therefore, knowing that contact with objects is incapable of bringing cessation,
one should wander free from attachment regarding the senses.

children.text:
ityetasmād darśanānmādhyasthyaṃ labhate sāṣṭamī tuṣṭiḥ sumārīcamityucyate / kathaṃ sumārīcamityucyate ? arcateḥ pūjārthasya śobhanamarcitaṃ viṣayasaṃganivṛttasya yogino 'vasthānaṃ bhavati /
