  yadā tu pūrvadoṣeṣu hiṃsādoṣamupanyasyati / katham ? anupahatyānyabhūtāni viṣayabhogānupapatteḥ / upabhogo hi nāma manojñābhyavahāraḥ, strīsevā, hayagajanarādibhiryānamityevamādi / tatra manojñābhyavahāracikīrṣuṣā tadaṅgānāṃ go 'jāvibalīvardastrīpuruṣādīnāmavaśyamupaghātaḥ kāryaḥ / anupaghāte vā viṣayānupapattiprasaṃgaḥ / striyamāsevamānenānyāsāṃ strīṇāṃ mātṛpitṛbhrātṛprabhṛtīnāṃ ca, anyathā tadabhāvo hayādīnām / tasmādupabhogārthināvaśyamanyopaghātaḥ kāryo nihitadaṇḍena vā viṣayopabhogastyājya iti / āha ca
yathā yathā hi viṣayo vṛddhiṃ gṛhṇāti dehinām /
children.translated_text: For as sense objects increase for embodied beings,
the destruction of their limbs increases correspondingly.

From this perception he attains equanimity. This is the eighth contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), called '<s>sumārīcam</s>' (well-honored). How is it called '<s>sumārīcam</s>'? A noble (<s>śobhana</s>) honored (<s>arcita</s>) state of abiding becomes [the lot] of the <s>yogin</s> who has turned away from attachment to sense objects.
  But when, with the previous defects [remaining], he presents the defect of violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>): How? Because the enjoyment of sense objects is not possible without harming other beings. For enjoyment (<s>upabhoga</s>) consists of pleasant eating, the company of women, travel by horse, elephant, chariot, and the like. Of these, the desire for pleasant eating —
Therefore, not desiring the bodily suffering of other beings,
one should live with contentment alone, having abandoned all possessions.
For one who speaks truth, is tranquil, and desires nothing from any being,
the knowledge at the end of the darkness of [worldly] existence arises before long.

children.text:
ityetasmāddarśanānmādhyasthyaṃ labhate, sā navamī tuṣṭiruttamābhayamityapadiśyate / katham ? uttamaṃ hi prāṇināṃ sarvebhyo hiṃsābhayamiti tadapagamāduttamābhayamiti /
  āha, arjanarakṣaṇalakṣaṇayorapi tuṣṭyoḥ paropaghātadoṣāḥ, apadiṣṭo 'syāmapi ca / tatra kathamanayorviśeṣaḥ pratipattavya iti ?
  ucyate na, viṣayabhedāt / tatra yeṣāmarjanarakṣaṇe pratyādriyate viṣayī tadarthinā pratyanīkānāmavaśyamabhighāto 'nuṣṭhātavya ityādāvuktam / iha tu yeṣāmevārjanarakṣaṇe tadanupaghātenāśakyo viṣayopabhoga ityetadvivakṣitam / tasmādasaṃkīrṇametadityevamambhaḥprabhṛtayo nava viṣayebhyaḥ saṃgadveṣanivṛttihetavo vyākhyātāḥ / te jñānavirahitānāṃ yogināṃ tuṣṭiśabdavācyatāṃ labhante / jñānināṃ tu vairāgyaparvasaṃjñitā svāsu svāsu tattvabhūmiṣu siddhā eveti // 50 //
children.translated_text:
From this perception he attains equanimity. This is the ninth contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), designated as '<s>uttamābhayam</s>' (supreme fearlessness). How? The supreme [fear] of all beings is the fear of violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>); from the removal of that, [it is called] 'supreme fearlessness.'
  [The objector] says: The contentments characterized by acquisition and protection also involve defects of harm to others, and [such a defect] has been indicated in this one too. How, then, is the distinction between them to be understood?
  It is replied: No [difficulty], because of the difference in objects. There, the sense-enjoyer who is intent on acquisition and protection, by [the need to overcome] adversaries,
<s>Kārikā</s> 51

[The objector] says: Previously the eightfold <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) was indicated. Let that now be explained.
  It is replied:

children.text:
ūhaḥ śabdo 'dhyayanaṃ duḥkhavighātāstrayaḥ suhṛtprāptiḥ /
  dānañca siddhayo 'ṣṭau
children.translated_text:
Reflection (<s>ūha</s>), verbal instruction (<s>śabda</s>), study (<s>adhyayana</s>), the three kinds of removal of suffering (<s>duḥkhavighāta</s>), the attainment of a good friend (<s>suhṛtprāpti</s>),
  and giving (<s>dāna</s>) — these are the eight attainments (<s>siddhi</s>s).

children.text:
tatroho nāma yadā pratyakṣānumānāgamavyatirekeṇābhipretamarthaṃ vicāraṇābalenaiva pratipadyate, sādyā siddhiḥ tārakamityapadiśyate- tārayati saṃsārārṇavāditi tārakam / yadā tu svayaṃ pratipattau pratihanyamāno gurūpadeśāt pratipadyate sā dvitīyā siddhiḥ sutāramityapadiśyate / katham ? sukhamanenadyatve 'pi bhavasaṅkaṭāt tarantīti / yadā tvanyopadeśādapyasamarthaḥ pratipattumadhyayanena sādhayati sā tṛtīyā siddhiḥ tārayantamityapadiśyate / tadetat tāraṇakriyāyā adyatve 'pi avyāvṛtatvāt mahāviṣayatvāt tārayantamityapadiśyate / ta ete trayaḥ sādhanopāyairābrāhmaṇaḥ prāṇino 'bhipretamarthaṃ prāpnuvanti / āha ca- "sākṣātkṛtadharmāṇa ṛṣayo babhūvuḥ, te 'parebhyo 'sākṣātkṛtadharmebhya upadeśena mantrān samprāhurupadeśāya glāyanto 'pare bilmagrahaṇāyemaṃ granthaṃ samāmnāsiṣurvedañca vedāṅgāni ceti" / bilmaṃ bhāsanam- samyak pratibhāsāya viśiṣṭaḥ saṃketa uktaḥ / eṣāṃ tu sādhanopāyānāṃ pratyanīkapratiṣedhāya duḥkhavighātatrayam / duḥkhāni trīṇi- ādhyātmikādīni /
  tatra cādhyātmikānāṃ vātādīnāṃ siddhipratyanīkānāmāyurvedakriyānuṣṭhānena vighātaṃ kṛtvā pūrveṣāṃ trayāṇāmanyatamena sādhayati sā caturthī siddhiḥ pramodamityabhidhīyate / katham ? nivṛttarogā hi prāṇinaḥ pramodanta iti kṛtvā / yadā tvādhibhautikānāṃ mānuṣādinimittānāṃ siddhipratyanīkānāṃ sāmādinā yatidharmānuguṇena vopāyena pūrveṣāṃ trayāṇāmanyatamena sādhayati, sā pañcamī siddhiḥ pramuditamityabhidhīyate / katham ? anudvigno hi pramudita iti kṛtvā / yadā tu śītādīnyādhidaivikāni dvandvāni siddhipratyanīkāni svadharmānurodhena pratihatya pūrveṣāṃ trayāṇāmanyatamena sādhayati, sā ṣaṣṭhī siddhirmodanāmamityabhidhīyate / katham ? dvandvānupahatā hi prāṇino modanta iti kṛtvā / suhṛtprāptiḥ- yadā tu kṛśalaṃ saṃspṛṣṭaṃ sanmitramāśritya sandehanivṛttiṃ labhate, sā ramyakamiti saptamī siddhirapadiśyate / ramyo hi loke sanmitrasamparkaḥ, tasya saṃjñāyāṃ ramyameva ramyakam / dānam- yadā tu daurbhāgyaṃ dānenātītya pūrveṣāṃ trayāṇāmanyatamena sādhayati sāṣṭāmī siddhiḥ sadāpramuditamityabhidhīyate / subhago hi sadāpramudito bhavati, tasmāddaurbhāgyanivṛttiḥ sadāpramuditam / ityevametāḥ siddhayo 'ṣṭau vyākhyātāḥ / etāsāṃ saṃśrayeṇābhipretamarthaṃ yataḥ saṃsādhayantītyataḥ pūrvācāryāgataṃ mārgamārurukṣustatpravaṇaḥ syāditi /
  āha, kaḥ punaratra heturyena puruṣārthatvāviśeṣe sati guṇānāṃ sarvasiddhinimittaṃ tvanubhavatīti ?
  ucyate- yasmāt
children.translated_text:
Of these, '<s>ūha</s>' (reflection) is when one comprehends the intended meaning through the power of investigation alone, apart from perception, inference, and testimony — this is the first <s>siddhi</s>, designated as '<s>tārakam</s>' (the saving). It saves from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> — hence '<s>tārakam</s>.' When one who is impeded in self-realization comprehends through the instruction of a teacher, this is the second <s>siddhi</s>, designated as '<s>sutāram</s>' (the good crossing). How? Because through this, even in the present, they happily cross over the difficulty of existence. When one who is unable to comprehend even through another's instruction accomplishes it through study, this is the third <s>siddhi</s>, designated as '<s>tārayantam</s>' (the causing to cross). This is designated '<s>tārayantam</s>' because, even in the present, the action of crossing has not ceased and is of great scope.
  These three [types of] beings, up to and including <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, attain the intended goal through the means of attainment. And it is said: 'The <s>Ṛṣi</s>s had directly realized <s>dharma</s>. They communicated the <s>mantra</s>s through instruction to others who had not directly realized <s>dharma</s>. Others, weary of instruction, compiled this text for comprehension — both the <s>Veda</s> and the <s>Vedāṅga</s>s.' '<s>Bilma</s>' means 'illumination' — a distinguished convention is stated for proper comprehension.
  But for counteracting the adversaries of these means of attainment, there are the three removals of suffering. The three sufferings are: the <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self) and the rest.
  Of these, when one removes the <s>ādhyātmika</s> [sufferings] — wind disorders and the like — which are adversaries of attainment, through the practice of <s>Āyurveda</s> and accomplishes [the goal] through any one of the previous three [means], this is the fourth <s>siddhi</s>, called '<s>pramoda</s>' (delight). How? Because beings freed from disease rejoice.
  When one removes the <s>ādhibhautika</s> [sufferings] — caused by humans and the like — which are adversaries of attainment, through conciliation (<s>sāma</s>) and other means, or through means consistent with ascetic <s>dharma</s>, and accomplishes through any one of the previous three, this is the fifth <s>siddhi</s>, called '<s>pramudita</s>' (the gladdened). How? Because one who is untroubled is gladdened.
  When one repels the <s>ādhidaivika</s> [sufferings] — cold and other pairs of opposites — which are adversaries of attainment, through conformity to one's own <s>dharma</s>, and accomplishes through any one of the previous three, this is the sixth <s>siddhi</s>, called '<s>modanāma</s>' (having the name of joy). How? Because beings unafflicted by the pairs of opposites rejoice.
  The attainment of a good friend (<s>suhṛtprāpti</s>): When one who is weakly touched [by understanding], taking refuge in a good and trusted friend, obtains the removal of doubt — this is the seventh <s>siddhi</s>, designated as '<s>ramyaka</s>' (the delightful). For in the world, the company of a good friend is delightful; as its designation, '<s>ramyaka</s>' is indeed '<s>ramya</s>' (delightful).
  Giving (<s>dāna</s>): When one overcomes misfortune through giving and accomplishes through any one of the previous three, this is the eighth <s>siddhi</s>, called '<s>sadāpramudita</s>' (ever-gladdened). For one of good fortune is ever-gladdened; therefore, the removal of misfortune is '<s>sadāpramudita</s>.'
  Thus these eight <s>siddhi</s>s have been explained. Since through their combination one successfully achieves the intended goal, one who wishes to ascend the path received from the previous teachers should be devoted to it.
  [The objector] asks: What, then, is the reason that, there being no difference in [all things being for] the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, the <s>guṇa</s>s are not the cause of attainment for all?
  It is replied: Because —
The threefold prior obstacle (<s>aṃkuśa</s>) to <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) [is error, incapacity, and contentment]. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 51 //

children.text:
sādhyapratipattisāmarthyasāmānyamaṅgīkṛtyāha siddheriti / pūrvo viparyayāśaktituṣṭilakṣaṇaḥ aṃkuśa ivāṃkuśaḥ, nivartanasāmānyāt / nityapravṛttasyāpi pradhānātsiddhisrotaso viparyayāśaktituṣṭipratibandhātsarvaprāṇiṣvapravṛttirbhavati / viparyayāttāvatsthāvareṣu / te hi mukhyāḥ srotaso viparyayātmānaḥ / aśaktestiryakṣu / te hi tiryaksrotaso 'śaktyātmānaḥ / tuṣṭirdeveṣu / te hyūrdhvasrotasastuṣṭyātmānaḥ / mānuṣāstvarvāksrotasaḥ saṃsiddhyātmānaḥ / tasmātta eva tārakādiṣu pravartante / sattvarajastamasāṃ cāṅgāṅgibhāvaniyamādviparyayāśaktituṣṭibhiḥ pratihanyata iti na sarveṣāṃ sarvadā siddhirbhavati / ata etaduktaṃ siddheḥ pūrvo 'ṅkuśāstrividha iti /
  yathā ca sidddheḥ viparyayāśaktituṣṭayaḥ pratipakṣāḥ, evaṃ siddhirapi viparyayādīnām / sā hyutpannā sarvānetānnivartayati / katham ? aviparītajñānaṃ viparyayamatītānāgatavartamāneṣu sannikṛṣṭeṣu viprakṛṣṭeṣu indriyagrāhyeṣvatīndriyeṣu cāpratighātādaśaktiṃ puruṣasya prakṛtivikāravyatiriktasya darśanātsarvāsu bhūmiṣu tuṣṭim / evametāni srotāṃsi prāṇādayaḥ karmayonayaśca vyākhyātāḥ / eteṣāṃ mārge 'vasthāpanātparāṃ siddhikaivalyalakṣaṇāmacireṇa prāpnoti / āha ca
children.translated_text:
Having accepted the common capacity for attaining the goal, he says 'of <s>siddhi</s>.' The prior [obstacle], characterized by error (<s>viparyaya</s>), incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>), and contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), is like a goad (<s>aṃkuśa</s>) — because of the commonality of restraining. Even though <s>pradhāna</s> is ever-active, due to the obstruction of the stream of attainment by error, incapacity, and contentment, there is non-activity in all beings.
  Through error, in stationary beings (<s>sthāvara</s>s) — for they are principally of the nature of the downward stream of error. Through incapacity, in animals — for they are of the nature of the lateral stream of incapacity. Through contentment, in gods — for they are of the nature of the upward stream of contentment. Humans, however, are of the downward stream, of the nature of attainment. Therefore, they alone engage in <s>tāraka</s> and the rest.
  And because of the fixed rule of the principal-subsidiary relation of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, [attainment] is impeded by error, incapacity, and contentment — hence not all attain <s>siddhi</s> at all times. Therefore it is said: 'The threefold prior obstacle to attainment.'
  And just as error, incapacity, and contentment are the adversaries of attainment, so too attainment is [the adversary] of error, etc. For when it arises, it removes all of these. How? Non-erroneous knowledge [removes] error; unimpeded [vision] in past, present, and future, near and far, objects graspable by the senses and beyond the senses [removes] incapacity; and the perception of <s>Puruṣa</s> as distinct from the transformations of <s>Prakṛti</s> [removes] contentment in all stages.
  Thus these streams — the vital breaths, the sources of action — have been explained. By establishing [oneself] in the path of these, one quickly attains the supreme attainment characterized by <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). And it is said:
By directing those of measured births in the right path,
and by the purity of the streams, one should wander free from attachment.
// Thus ends the ninth lesson (<s>āhnika</s>) of the <s>Yuktidīpikā</s>. //
<s>Kārikā</s> 52
<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 21

children.text: ) iti tadvyākhyātam / atredānīmācāryāṇāṃ vipratipattiḥ / dharmādīnāṃ śarīramantareṇānutpatteḥ / śarīrasya ca dharmādyabhāve nimittantarāsambhavādubhayamidamanādi / tasmādekarūpa evāyaṃ yathaivādyatve tathaivātikrāntāsvanāgatāsu kālakoṭiṣu sarga iti / ācārya āha- naitadevam, kiṃ tarhi prākpradhānapravṛtterdharmādharmayorasambhavo buddhidharmatvāttasyāśca pradhānavikāratvāt / tatastadvyatiriktaṃ śabdādyupalabdhiguṇalakṣaṇaṃ guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhilakṣaṇaṃ cārthamuddiśya sattvādayo mahadahaṅkāratanmātrendriyabhūtatvenāvasthāya paramarṣihiraṇyagarbhādīnāṃ śarīramutpādayanti / ṣaṭsiddhikṣayakālottaraṃ tu guṇavimardavaicitryādrajastamovṛttyanupāti saṃsāracakraṃ pravṛttam /
children.translated_text: — that has been explained. Here, now, there is disagreement among the teachers. Since <s>dharma</s> and the rest do not arise without a body, and since the body has no other cause in the absence of <s>dharma</s> and the rest, both of these are beginningless. Therefore, this creation is of a single nature — just as it is in the present, so too in past and future ages. The teacher says: This is not so. Rather, prior to the activity of <s>pradhāna</s>, there was no existence of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, because they are properties of <s>buddhi</s>, and because <s>buddhi</s> is a transformation of <s>pradhāna</s>. Then <s>sattva</s> and the rest, aiming at a purpose distinct from that [initial state] — namely, the apprehension of sound and the like, and the apprehension of the difference between the <s>guṇa</s>s and <s>Puruṣa</s> — abiding as <s>mahat</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, <s>tanmātra</s>s, senses, and elements, produced the body of the supreme <s>Ṛṣi</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, and others. But after the period of the six attainments had expired, the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> began to turn, following the activities of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, through the variety of the clashing of the <s>guṇa</s>s.
Thus, what was previously indicated — the creation produced by conjunction —
The <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) does not [exist] without the dispositions (<s>bhāva</s>s),
and it subsists in the states of gods, humans, and animals — this is the completion of the sentence.
And there is no accomplishment of the dispositions (<s>bhāva</s>s) without the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body).
'Accomplishment' (<s>saṃsiddhi</s>) here means 'production' (<s>niṣpatti</s>).
That which is called <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) and that which is called <s>bhāva</s> (disposition) — therefore a twofold creation proceeds. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 52 //

children.text: so 'yaṃ liṅgākhyo bhāvākhyaśca ṣaṭsiddhikṣayakālādūrdhvaṃ bhavati / guṇasamanantaraṃ tu adhikāralakṣaṇaḥ / tasmād dvidhā sargaḥ adhikāralakṣaṇo bhāvākhyaśca / yeṣāṃ tu dharmādharmaśarīrayoḥ paryāyeṇa hetuhetumadbhāvasteṣāṃ kāraṇamastyavyaktamityatra (

children.translated_text: <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 16

children.text: ) prativihitam / ye 'pi ca sāṃkhyā evamāhuḥ- "dharmādharmādhikāravaśātpradhānasya pravṛttiriti" teṣāmanyataraparikalpanānarthakyamiti / katham ? yadi tāvadadhikāra evāyaṃ pradhānapravṛttaye 'lam, kiṃ dharmādharmābhyām ? atha tāvadantareṇādhikārasya pradhānapravṛttāvasāmarthyam, evamapi kimadhikāreṇa ? tayoreva pravṛttisāmarthyāt / tasmādadhikārabhāvanimitto dvidhā sargaḥ / tatra yathedaṃ śarīramavibhaktaṃ dharmārthakāmamokṣalakṣaṇāsu kriyāsu vibhaktaṃ bhavedityataḥ pāṇyādivikalpo 'sya bhavati, evaṃ sattvasargo 'pyavibhakto dharmārthakāmamokṣalakṣaṇāsu kriyāsu samartho bhavediti // 52 //
children.translated_text: ) has been addressed. And those <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s who say 'the activity of <s>pradhāna</s> is due to the authority of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>' — for them, positing either one separately would be purposeless. How? If the authority alone is sufficient for the activity of <s>pradhāna</s>, what need is there for <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>? If, without the authority, there is an insufficiency for the activity of <s>pradhāna</s>, then too, what need for authority — since those two [<s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>] have the power to produce activity? Therefore the creation is twofold, occasioned by the state of authority. Just as this body, being undifferentiated, becomes differentiated into activities characterized as <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s> — for which purpose it has the differentiation of hands and the like — so too the creation of <s>sattva</s> (the intellectual creation), though undifferentiated, becomes capable of activities characterized as <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>.

This [creation] called <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) and called <s>bhāva</s> (disposition) exists from after the period of the six attainments' exhaustion. But immediately after the <s>guṇa</s>s [begin their activity], it is characterized by [special] function (<s>adhikāra</s>). Therefore, creation is twofold: characterized by function and called <s>bhāva</s>. For those who hold that <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and the body are alternately related as cause and effect, [the proof is that] there is a cause — the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) — as is discussed here.
<s>Kārikā</s> 53
The divine [creation] is of eight kinds; the animal [creation] is fivefold; and the human [creation] is of one kind.

children.text: aṣṭau vikalpā asya so 'yamaṣṭavikalpaḥ / aṣṭaprakāro 'ṣṭabheda ityarthaḥ / tadyathā brahmaprajāpatīndrapitṛgandharvanāgarakṣaḥpiśācāḥ / tairyagyonaśca pañcadhā bhavati- paśumṛgapakṣisarīsṛpasthāvarāḥ / mānuṣyaścaikavidhaḥ ca jātyantarānupapatteḥ / āha kimetāvāneva bhūtasargavikalpaḥ, āhosvidanyo 'stīti ? ucyate- vikalpāntaramastyeteṣāmeva sthānānāmantargaṇabhedāt / ayaṃ tu āhosvidanyo 'stīti ? ucyate- vikalpāntaramastyeteṣāmeva sthānāmantaragaṇabhedāt / ayaṃ tu
children.translated_text: That which has eight varieties is '<s>aṣṭavikalpa</s>' (eight-varied). It means eight types, eight divisions. Namely: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>s, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Pitṛ</s>s (ancestors), <s>Gandharva</s>s, <s>Nāga</s>s (serpents), <s>Rakṣas</s>es (demons), and <s>Piśāca</s>s (ghouls). And the animal creation is fivefold: domesticated animals, wild animals, birds, reptiles, and stationary beings (plants). And the human creation is of one kind, because no other species [within it] is tenable. One asks: is this the entire extent of the elemental creation's varieties, or is there another? It is replied: there are further varieties through the subdivisions within these very stations. But this —
is the elemental creation in summary. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 53)

children.text: kim ? upadiṣṭa ita vākyaśeṣaḥ / tatra devānāṃ sādhyamarudrudrādibhedāt / tiraścāṃ grāmyāraṇyādibhedāt / mānuṣāṇāṃ ca brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviṭśūdrabhedāt / udbhidbhedaśca vistareṇāpadiśyamāna ānantyamāpādayet / tasmātsamāsato bhūtasargo 'padiśyate // 53 //
children.translated_text: What? 'Has been taught' — this completes the sentence. Among these, the divine [has further varieties] due to the subdivisions of <s>Sādhya</s>s, <s>Marut</s>s, <s>Rudra</s>s, and the like. The animal [creation has varieties] due to the subdivisions of domesticated, wild, and the like. And the human [creation has varieties] due to the subdivisions of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, and <s>śūdra</s>. And the subdivision of plant life, when expounded in detail, would lead to infinity. Therefore the elemental creation is taught in summary.
<s>Kārikā</s> 54

children.text:
āha, vikalpāntaravacanam, srotobhedāt / daivamānuṣatairyagyonā iti trividho bhūtānāṃ vikalpa upadiśyate / srotāṃsi tu catvāryuktāni / tasmādvikalpāntaraṃ vaktavyamiti /
  ucyate- na, guṇadharmasaṃgrahasāmarthāt / sattvabahulā ūrdhvasrotasaḥ / rajobahulā arvāksrotasaḥ / tamobahulāstiryaksrotaso mukhyasrotasaśca / tasmādanayorabhedenopadeśaḥ /
  āha, asurādyupasaṃkhyānaṃ kartavyam / itareṣvanantarbhāvādabhedena vopadeśaḥ kāryā na tu daivamānuṣatiraśca iti /
  ucyate- na, ukteṣveva tatsaṃgrahāt / asurāṇāṃ tāvadaindra eva sthāne 'ntarbhāvaḥ, pūrvadevatvāt / pūrvadevā hyasurāḥ / kiṃca paryāyeṇendratvāt / dhanviprabhṛtīnāṃ paryāyeṇendratvaṃ śrūyate / tathā yakṣāṇāṃ rakṣassvekarūpatvāt / kinnaravidyādharāṇāṃ gandharveṣu, samānaśīlatvāt / pretānāṃ pitṛṣvadhipatisāmānyāt / tasmāttrivikalpa eva bhūtasargaḥ / sa cāyam
children.translated_text: One says: another variety should be stated, because of the difference of streams. The threefold variety of beings is taught — divine, human, and animal. But four streams have been mentioned. Therefore another variety should be stated. It is replied: no, because of the capacity to be included in the classification by the properties of the <s>guṇa</s>s. Those predominating in <s>sattva</s> are the upward stream. Those predominating in <s>rajas</s> are the downward stream. Those predominating in <s>tamas</s> are the lateral stream and the primary stream. Therefore, through the non-difference of these, the teaching [is given]. One objects: <s>Asura</s>s and the like should be additionally enumerated. Since they are not included in the others, the teaching should be given either with them included, or one should not say 'divine, human, and animal.' It is replied: no, because they are included in those already stated. The <s>Asura</s>s are included in the very station of <s>Indra</s>, because they are the former gods. For the <s>Asura</s>s are the former gods. Moreover, because of their alternate <s>Indra</s>-ship. <s>Dhanvin</s> and others are heard to have <s>Indra</s>-ship by turns. Similarly, the <s>Yakṣa</s>s are of the same nature as the <s>Rakṣas</s>es. The <s>Kinnara</s>s and <s>Vidyādhara</s>s [are included] among the <s>Gandharva</s>s, because of similar character. The <s>Preta</s>s (ghosts) [are included] among the <s>Pitṛ</s>s, because of the commonality of ruler. Therefore the elemental creation is indeed threefold. And this —
Above, [the creation] is abundant in <s>sattva</s>;

children.text: ūrdhvamityanenāṣṭau devasthānānyāha / tatrāyaṃ sargaṃ sattvaviśālaḥ / piśācebhyo rakṣasām, rakṣobhyo nāgānām, nāgebhyo gandharvāṇām, gandharvebhyaḥ pitḥṇām, pitṛbhyastridaśānām, tebhyaḥ prajāpatīnām, tebhyo 'pi brahmaṇaḥ / evaṃ viśālagrahaṇaṃ samarthitaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: By 'above,' he states the eight divine stations. There, this creation is abundant in <s>sattva</s>. [There is greater <s>sattva</s>] in <s>Rakṣas</s>es than in <s>Piśāca</s>s, in <s>Nāga</s>s than in <s>Rakṣas</s>es, in <s>Gandharva</s>s than in <s>Nāga</s>s, in <s>Pitṛ</s>s than in <s>Gandharva</s>s, in the thirty [gods] than in <s>Pitṛ</s>s, in <s>Prajāpati</s>s than in them, and in <s>Brahmā</s> more than in them. Thus the word 'abundant' is justified.
But the creation from below is abundant in <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: mūlatastu sargastamoviśālaḥ / paśubhyo hi mṛgāṇāṃ prakṛṣṭataraṃ tamaḥ, mṛgebhyaḥ pakṣiṇām, pakṣibhyaḥ sarīsṛpāṇām, sarīsṛpebhyaḥ sthāvarāṇām /
children.translated_text: From below, the creation is abundant in <s>tamas</s>. For the <s>tamas</s> of wild animals is greater than that of domesticated animals, of birds greater than of wild animals, of reptiles greater than of birds, and of stationary beings greater than of reptiles.
In the middle, [the creation] is abundant in <s>rajas</s>.

children.text: devebhyastiryagbhyaścāvakṛṣṭāsu bhūmiṣu yathā yathā sattvatamaso nirhrāsaḥ, tathā tathā rajaso vṛddhiḥ / manuṣyāstūbhayormadhyamiti tatra paramaḥ prakarṣo rajasaḥ / arvāk srotasaḥ siddhirūpatvādatyantaṃ kriyāpravṛttatvāt / yathā ca mānuṣeṣu rajaḥprakarṣa evaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sthāne sattvasya, sthāvareṣu tamasaḥ / sa khalvayam-
children.translated_text: In the stations below the gods and above the animals, as <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> progressively decrease, so <s>rajas</s> progressively increases. Humans, being in the middle of both, have the maximum predominance of <s>rajas</s> there. [This is] because the downward stream has the nature of accomplishment, and because [humans] are exceedingly engaged in action. And just as the predominance of <s>rajas</s> [is maximum] among humans, so is [the predominance of] <s>sattva</s> in the station of <s>Brahmā</s>, and [the predominance of] <s>tamas</s> among stationary beings. This indeed —
extends from <s>Brahmā</s> to a blade of grass. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 54)
The creation that has been explained, with fourteen divisions and three varieties, in terms of the predominance and decline of <s>sattva</s> and the rest [with respect to each] domain.
<s>Kārikā</s> 55

children.text: atra jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ prānoti cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the conscious <s>puruṣa</s> experiences suffering caused by old age and death.

children.text:
jarākṛtaṃ maraṇakṛtaṃ jarāmaraṇakṛtam / tatra jarākṛtaṃ tāvadyathā balītaraṃgitagātratvam, daṇḍamantareṇa caṅkramaṇādiṣvapravṛttiḥ, sarvendriyāṇāṃ viṣayopabhogeṣvasāmarthyam, prabalakāsaśvāsatā, sāsrāvilekṣaṇatā, daśanānāmasthiratvam, varṇavikṛtiḥ, śaithilyamabhivyāhārasaṃgo mandā smṛtirityevamādi /
  maraṇakṛtamapi pṛthivyādīnāṃ śarīrabhāvenāvasthitau sahabhāvapratipakṣatā svabhāvabhedavṛttisaṃgrahapanthivyūhāvakāśadānāderupakārasya pracyutiḥ / indriyādhiṣṭhānavikārācchabdasparśarūparasagandhānāṃ satāmagrahaṇamasatāṃ ca grahaṇamabhūtākāraṃ sambhavaviparītaṃ vā sarvārthānāṃ grahaṇam / tadyathā paurṇamāsyāṃ dakṣiṇataḥ khaṇḍasyendumaṇḍalasya piśācādīnāṃ pāṇḍarasya ca nabhasa ityādi / tathā vātādivaiṣamyātsamupajanitānekaprakāravyādhiḥ prabhraśyamānasakalendriyavṛttiḥ srastāṅgaḥ tāmrapītāsrāvilekṣaṇo bhramadāhaśvāsādiparigamāntarmarmasandhirjalārthaṃ diśo 'valokayan sabrahmalokeṣvapi lokeṣu trātāramavindan rāgādyanekakālātpakvenātmagraheṇātmakāryakaraṇopahyimāṇabuddhirmandamandeṣvapi smṛtipralambheṣu dayitajanasyātmanaścānusmarandaśavidhātkuṭumbādyaḥ prabhraśyate so 'yamavaśyambhāvī sarvasattvānāṃ prakṛṣṭodvegakārī cāvyutpannaścāparihāryaścāniyatakālaśca mahātmabhiḥ paramarṣyādibhirandhatāmisraśabdenāpadiṣṭo maraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkham / taccedaṃ duḥkhaṃ pradhānamahadahaṃkāratanmātrendriyabhūtaviśeṣalakṣaṇasya tattvaparvaṇaścaitanyāsambhavātpuruṣa eva caitanyaśaktiyogādupalabhyate / tadapi samīkṣyoktamācāryeṇa atra jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpnoti cetanaḥ puruṣa iti /
  āha, janmakṛtasyopasaṃkhyānam / yathaiva hi jarāmaraṇaṃ cātmanaḥ prakṛṣṭodvegakārakamevaṃ janmāpi / tathā hyayaṃ māturudare jarāyupariveṣṭitaśarīro 'medhyaparisnuto vraṇamātrāyāṃ garbhadhānyāṃ yathāsukhasambhavātparipītitagātro māturaśanādibhiḥ pīḍyamāno garbhāvāse duḥkhamanubhūya paścātsaṃvṛtenāsthidvayavivareṇa nissṛto mūtrarudhirakalilaiḥ pariṣiktagātro bāhyena vāyunā karaiśca saṃsparśadasibhiriva tudyamānaḥ svasaṃvedyaṃ duḥkhamātmani vartamānamākhyātumasamarthaḥ svasukhaduḥkhasāmanyātparatra parikalpitasukhaduḥkhabuddhibhirdṛḍhagātrairupacitakleśaiśca yātyamāno janmaduḥkhamanubhavati / tasmāttadapi vaktavyamiti /
  ucyate- na, avyāpitavāt / mānuṣatiraścāmeva janmakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhavati na devānām / katham ? taḍidvilasitavatkṣaṇamātreṇa śarīraprādurbhāvāt / jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ tu teṣvapi na nivartate / tasmātprādhānyādetadevopadiṣṭaṃ netaraditi /
  āha, itaragrahaṇāprasaṃgaḥ, tulyatvāt / na hi devasthāneṣu jarāmaraṇaṃ vā śrūyate, tasmādavyāpitvāttayorapyagrahaṇaprasaṃgaḥ /
  ucyate- na, smṛtivacanāt / jīryate 'nayeti jarā kṣaya ityuktaṃ bhavati / sa ca devabhūmāvapi bhavati / kasmāt ? evaṃ hyāha-

children.translated_text: A staining of <s>rajas</s> on the limbs, discoloration, and the withering of flowers
arise for beings about to fall from the world of the gods.

Caused by old age, caused by death — [this is what is meant by] 'caused by old age and death.' Among these, [suffering] caused by old age is, for example: the body becoming wrinkled and creased, inability to walk without a stick, the incapacity of all sense organs for the enjoyment of objects, severe coughing and breathing difficulty, teary and clouded eyes, looseness of the teeth, discoloration [of skin], flaccidity, difficulty in speech, slow memory, and so forth. And [suffering] caused by death: when earth and the other [elements] are established in the form of the body, [death is] the loss of their mutual support — [the loss of] the accommodation of providing space through the cohesion of the nature, differentiation, activity, containment, and arrangement [of the elements]. Due to the alteration of the seat of the sense organs, there is non-apprehension of sounds, touches, forms, tastes, and smells that exist, and apprehension of those that do not exist — unreal in form — or the apprehension of all objects in a manner contrary to reality. For example, [seeing] on the full moon night a crescent moon-disc to the south, <s>piśāca</s>s, and a white sky, and so forth. Similarly, due to the imbalance of wind and the other [bodily humors], afflicted by diseases of many kinds, with all sensory functions collapsing, with limbs drooping, with eyes coppery, yellowish, and clouded, with vertigo, burning, and gasping seizing the vital joints internally, looking in all directions for water, finding no protector even in the worlds up to the world of <s>Brahmā</s> — with intellect being injured by self-identification and its effect-and-instrument, [an identification] ripened over a long time from passion and the like — in even the faintest lapses of memory, recollecting one's beloved and oneself, one falls from the tenfold family. This [death] is inevitable for all beings, produces the greatest agitation, is beyond [the knowledge of] the uninstructed, is unavoidable, and is of uncertain time. By great souls such as the supreme <s>ṛṣi</s>s and others —

children.text: śakrādīnāṃ vyādhiśravaṇāccharīrakṣayaḥ / evaṃ hyāha- "tvāṣṭrīyaṃ sāma bhavati indraṃ kṣāmamapi na sarvabhūtāni prasvāpayituṃ nāśaknuvaṃ stametena sāmnā tvāṣṭrīyeṇāsvāpayaditi /" tathā prajāpatervāyurakṣayīt / dakṣābhiśāpācca somasya kṣayaḥ / tathā "prajāpatirvai somāya rājñe duhitḥradānnakṣatrāṇi, sa rohiṇyāmevāvasat / tānyapekṣyamāṇāni punaragacchan / tasmāt svānanupeyamānā punargacchati / tānyanvāgacchattāni punarayācata / tānyasmai na punaradadāt / sābravītsarveṣveva samāsata vasātha te punardāsyāmīti / sa rohiṇyāmevāvasattasminnanṛte yakṣmo 'gṛhṇāt / candramā vai somo rāja yadrājānaṃ yakṣmogṛhṇāttadrājayakṣmasya janma / sa tṛṇamivāśuṣyat / sa prajāpatā anāthata / so 'bravītsarveṣveva samāvadvasātha tvāto mokṣyāmīti / tasmāccandramāḥ sarveṣu nakṣatreṣu samāvadvasati / taṃ vaiśvadevena caruṇāmāvasyāṃ rātrīmayā yajante nainaṃ yakṣmodamuñcadityādi /" tasmāddevabhūmāvapi jarākṛtaṃ duḥkhamasti / tathā maraṇakṛtaṃ bhūmyantaragamanāttatrotpannānāṃ yayātirudāharaṇam / yathā gopathabrāhmaṇam- "devānāṃ ha vā pañcadaśaśatāni āsaṃstāni brahmakilbiṣādakṣīyanta / tatastrayastriṃśadevāsata tadetadṛcāpyuktam / sodaryāṇāṃ pañcadaśānāṃ śatānāṃ trayastriṃśadudaśiṣyanta devāḥ / śeṣāḥ prāsīyanteti /" śvetāraṇye cāntakasya rudreṇa kṛtaṃ duḥkhamastīti / udāharaṇamātrādvā / athavodāharaṇamātrameva duḥkhānām / ādiśabdalopo vā vaktavyaḥ / jarāmaraṇakṛtamevodāharaṇatvenābhipretam / na punarduḥkhāntaram / kasmāt ? tatrāpi hyādiśabdalopa udāharaṇamātratvāt śaktyā parikalpayitumidamityucyate / na sarvaduḥkhāspadatvāt / sarveṣāṃ hi duḥkhānāmāspadaṃ jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ sādhāraṇam / katham ? tadbandhumitrāṇāmapyudvegahetutvāt / na tu janmakṛtam, sambandhināṃ praharṣanimittatvāt / yataśca brahmādau stambaparyante jagati jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ na kaścidativartate /
children.translated_text: For <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) and the others, there is bodily decay upon hearing of disease. For thus it is said: 'The <s>Tvāṣṭrīya</s> <s>Sāman</s> exists. <s>Indra</s>, though wasting, was unable to put all beings to sleep. With that <s>Sāman</s>, the <s>Tvāṣṭrīya</s>, he put them to sleep.' Likewise, the wind stole <s>Prajāpati</s>'s imperishable [essence]. And through the curse of <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Soma</s> suffered decay. As [the scripture says]: '<s>Prajāpati</s> gave his daughters, the <s>nakṣatra</s>s (lunar mansions), to <s>Soma</s> the king. He dwelt with <s>Rohiṇī</s> alone. The others, being neglected, returned. Therefore one who is not attended to returns. He followed them and asked for them again. They did not give themselves back to him. She said: dwell equally with all, and I will give them back to you. He dwelt with <s>Rohiṇī</s> alone. In that untruth, consumption (<s>yakṣma</s>) seized him. When consumption seizes a king — that is the origin of the royal consumption. He dried up like a blade of grass. He sought refuge with <s>Prajāpati</s>. He said: dwell equally with all, and I shall release you. Therefore the moon dwells equally among all the <s>nakṣatra</s>s. On the new moon night they sacrifice for him with the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> oblation, [but] consumption did not release him,' and so forth. Therefore even in the divine realm there is suffering caused by old age. Similarly, suffering caused by death — from going to another realm, of those born there — <s>Yayāti</s> is the example. As the <s>Gopatha Brāhmaṇa</s> [says]: 'There were fifteen hundred gods. They perished through the sin against <s>Brahman</s>. Thirty-three gods remained. This is stated by the <s>ṛc</s> also: Of the fifteen hundred co-born, thirty-three gods remained; the rest perished.'
Because the subtle body has not ceased [to transmigrate], therefore, in summary, there is suffering. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 55)

children.text:
sukhaleśasya tadvyāptatvāt / yāvadidaṃ liṅgaṃ na nivartate tāvadavaśyaṃ duḥkhena bhavitavyam / paryāyeṇa saṃskārasya sāmarthyāllokāntaropapatteḥ / tathā cāha-
  sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca hi saṃśayaṃ vāreṇāyaṃ sevate tatra tatra /
  kathampunarduḥkhena vyāptaṃ sukhamiti cet, ābrahmaṇo 'śuddhyātiśayopapatteḥ / tasyāśca duḥkhamūlatvāt / prajāpaterakṣirogaśravaṇāt, indrasya kāmopatāpāt / gautamaparibhāvād rambhāyāścābhiśāpātpāṣāṇabhāvopapatteḥ, nāgānāṃ sarpasatrāyāsāt, vaiśravaṇasya yaskābhiśāpāddhastibhāvopapattiḥ / jaratkāro pitḥṇāṃ ca garte 'valambanāt, piśācānāṃ mantrauṣadhimaṅgalaprayogairudvāsanānmānuṣatiraścāṃ pratyakṣata eva prāyeṇa duḥkhāspadatvāt / tasmānnāsti saṃsāre kaścitpradeśo yatra saha liṅgenātmānaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāvāpnuyādityata evaṃ prayatitavyaṃ yena liṅgasyaivātyantocchedaḥ / tato hi sarvaduḥkhānāmatyantopaśamaḥ / samāsagrahaṇaṃ tu sukhamohayoravakāśadānārtham / anyathā saṃsāre tayorabhāva evābhyupagataḥ syāt // 55 //
children.translated_text: Because even the slightest pleasure is pervaded by it [suffering]. As long as this <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) does not cease, suffering is inevitable, because of rebirth in another world through the power of accumulated impressions, in succession. And thus it is said: 'Pleasure, pain, and doubt — one experiences these here and there in turn.' But how is pleasure pervaded by suffering? Because even up to <s>Brahmā</s>, the excess of impurity is tenable. And because that [impurity] is the root of suffering. Because it is heard that <s>Prajāpati</s> had eye disease; because <s>Indra</s> suffered from the torment of desire. Because of <s>Gautama</s>'s humiliation, and because <s>Rambhā</s> was cursed [by Viśvāmitra], attaining the state of a stone; because the <s>Nāga</s>s suffered from the snake sacrifice; because <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera), through the curse of <s>Yakṣa</s>, attained the state of an elephant. Because <s>Jaratkāru</s> and the <s>Pitṛ</s>s hung in a pit; because <s>Piśāca</s>s are driven away by the application of <s>mantra</s>s, herbs, and auspicious rites; because for humans and animals suffering is directly evident for the most part. Therefore there is no place in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) where the self, together with the subtle body, does not experience suffering — hence one should make effort so that the subtle body itself is completely destroyed. For from that comes the complete cessation of all suffering. The word 'in summary' is for the purpose of allowing room for pleasure and delusion; otherwise, their complete absence in <s>saṃsāra</s> would be implied.
<s>Kārikā</s> 56
Having thus narrated the creation as it actually is, he now summarizes:

children.text:
ityeṣa prakṛtivikṛtaḥ pravartate tattvabhūtabhāvākhyaḥ /
  pratipuruṣavimokṣārthaṃ svārtha iva parārtha ārambhaḥ || 56 ||
children.translated_text: Thus this [creation], which is both a product and a producer, proceeds under the name of the 'evolution of principles' (<s>tattvabhūtabhāva</s>). For the liberation of each <s>puruṣa</s> individually, the undertaking — though seeming to be for its own sake — is for the sake of another. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 56)

children.text:
itikaraṇena sargasamāptiṃ dyotayati / eṣa ityuktamapi pratyāmnāyārthaṃ punarapekṣate / prakṛtyā kṛtaḥ prakṛtikṛtaḥ / anena vākyaparisamāptyarthaṃ vītāvītābhyāṃ siddhaṃ pradhānāstitvam / aṇvādipratiṣedhaṃ cāpekṣate / prakṛtikṛta eva nāṇvādikṛtaḥ / pravartata iti kriyāprabandhamāha / pravṛtto na pravartsyati kiṃ tarhi pravartata evānantānāṃ śarīrādibhāvena parasparānugraheṇa ca / neyaṃ kriyā kadācidapi bhūtabhaviṣyadrūpā bhavati / kintarhi vartamānarūpā / yathā vahanti nadyaḥ, tiṣṭhanti parvatā iti / tattvabhūtabhāvākhya ityuktānāṃ nigamārthaṃ pratyāmnāyaṃ karoti / tattvākhyo mahadādibhirbhāvākhyo vyomādiḥ / puruṣaṃ puruṣaṃ prati vimokṣaḥ pratipuruṣavimokṣaḥ / tadarthaṃ pratipuruṣavimokṣārtham / sarvapuruṣādhikāranibaddhāyāḥ sarvaśakternirākāṃkṣīkaraṇārthamityarthaḥ / svārtha iva parārtha ārambhaḥ / kāryakāraṇabhāvena / tatra kāryasya tāvacchabdādeḥ svārtha ivendriyāṇāṃ viṣayabhāvaḥ / indriyāṇāmaprāptaviṣayāṇāṃ laulyamadhiṣṭhānavikārānumeyaṃ svārthamiva / karaṇānāṃ ca saṃkalpābhimānādhyavasāyānāṃ viṣayadvāribhāvopagamanaṃ manaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ ca svapravṛttiviṣayatvam / mano 'haṃkārayośca buddhau svapravṛttyupasaṃhāro buddheśca śāntaghoramūḍhatvaṃ vyavasāyakartṛtvaṃ ca sattarajastamasāṃ ca prakāśapravṛttiniyamalakṣaṇairdharmaiḥ parasparopakāritvam / na caiṣa svārthaḥ, sarvasyāsyācaitanyāt / kiṃ tarhi parārtha evāyamārambhaḥ / saṃghātatvāditi /
  āha, yaduktaṃ pratipuruṣavimokṣārthamayamārambha iti tadayuktam / ācāryavipratipatteḥ / pratipuruṣamanyatpradhānaṃ śarīrādyarthaṃ karoti / teṣāṃ ca māhātmyaśarīrapradhānaṃ yadā pravartate tadetarāṇyapi / tannivṛttau ca teṣāmapi nivṛttiriti paurikaḥ sāṃkhyācāryo manyate / tatkathamapratiṣidhyaikā prakṛtirabhyupagamyate iti ?
  ucyate- na, pramāṇābhāvāt / na tāvatpratyakṣata eva tacchakyaṃ niścetum / pradhānānāmatīndriyatvāt / liṅgaṃ cāsandigdhaṃ nāsti / āptāśca no nābhidadhurato manyāmahe naitadevamiti / kiṃca ekenārthaparisamāpteḥ / aparimitatvādetadekaṃ pradhānamalaṃ sarvapuruṣaśarīrotpādanāya / tasmādanyaparikalpanānarthakyam / parimitamiti cedatha matam, parimitaṃ pradhānamiti na, ucchedaprasaṃgāt / evamapi tasyocchedaḥ prāptaḥ kṣīravat / tathā ca saṃsārocchedaprasaṃgaḥ / kiṃ ca anavasthāprasaṃgāt / ekasyeśvarasya yogino vecchāyogādanekaśarīratvam / tatparimitādayuktam / pratiśarīraṃ vā pradhānaparikalpane pradhānānavasthā bhavati / parimitaśarīrakāraṇatvābhyupagamādanyaparikalpanānarthakyam / tataśca pradhānaikatvameva / tasmādayuktaṃ pratipuruṣaṃ pradhānānīti / yattūktaṃ māhātmyaśarīrapradhānapravṛttāvitareṣāṃ pravṛtistannivṛttau nivṛttirityatra brūmaḥ- na, atiśayābhāvāt / yathā kṣetrajñānāṃ niratiśayatvāditaretarāpravartakatvamevameṣāmapi sātiśayatve vā pradhānānupapattiprasaṃgaḥ, vaiṣamyāt / tasmādyuktaṃ pratipuruṣavimokṣārthamekā prakṛtiḥ pravartata iti // 56 //
children.translated_text:
By the particle 'iti' he indicates the completion of creation. Though 'this' has been stated, it is again expected for the purpose of recapitulation. 'Made by <s>prakṛti</s>' means <s>prakṛtikṛta</s> (produced by primordial nature). By this, for the purpose of completing the statement, the existence of <s>pradhāna</s> established by both <s>vīta</s> (affirmative) and <s>avīta</s> (eliminative) [inference is recapitulated]. And it refers to the refutation of atoms and the like — 'produced by <s>prakṛti</s> only, not produced by atoms and the like.' 'Proceeds' states the continuity of action. It has proceeded and will not [merely] proceed in the future; rather, it proceeds continuously — of infinite [beings] in the form of bodies and the like, and through mutual assistance. This action never assumes the form of past or future; rather, it is always in the present form — just as 'the rivers flow' and 'the mountains stand.' 'Called <s>tattva</s> and <s>bhāva</s>' — he recapitulates for the purpose of summarizing what has been stated. 'Called <s>tattva</s>' refers to <s>mahat</s> and the rest; 'called <s>bhāva</s>' refers to space and the rest. 'For the liberation of each <s>puruṣa</s>' — liberation for each and every <s>puruṣa</s>; 'for that purpose,' meaning for rendering the omnipotent [<s>prakṛti</s>], which is bound to the qualification of all <s>puruṣas</s>, free from further expectation. The undertaking, though appearing to be for its own purpose, is for another's purpose — through the relationship of cause and effect. Among these, first, the serving as objects for the <s>indriyas</s> by sound and the like, as if for their own purpose. The restlessness of the <s>indriyas</s> that have not attained their objects — inferable from the modification of their substrata — is as if for their own purpose. The approaching of the door-keeper status of objects by the instruments — <s>saṃkalpa</s> (deliberation), <s>abhimāna</s> (ego-sense), and <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) — and the being the domain of their own operation for <s>manas</s> and the rest. The subsuming of their own operation into <s>buddhi</s> by <s>manas</s> and <s>ahaṃkāra</s>; and <s>buddhi</s>'s being tranquil, passionate, or deluded, and its agency of determination; and the mutual assistance of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> through their properties of illumination, activity, and restraint — none of this is for its own purpose, since all of this is non-conscious. Rather, this undertaking is for another's purpose alone — because it is a composite.
  [Objection:] The statement that this undertaking is for the liberation of each <s>puruṣa</s> is untenable — because of disagreement among teachers. The <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teacher <s>Paurika</s> holds that a different <s>pradhāna</s> creates the body and the like for each <s>puruṣa</s>, and when the <s>pradhāna</s> of the one with the great body operates, the others also [operate], and when that ceases, they too cease. How then is a single <s>prakṛti</s> accepted without refuting [this view]?
  [Reply:] No, because of the absence of a means of knowledge. First, it cannot be ascertained by direct perception, since the <s>pradhānas</s> are supersensory. Nor is there an unambiguous inferential mark. And the authorities have not taught us so — therefore we hold that it is not so. Moreover, because a single [<s>pradhāna</s>] suffices for the purpose. Since it is unlimited, this single <s>pradhāna</s> is sufficient for producing the bodies of all <s>puruṣas</s>. Therefore, postulating others is purposeless. If it is thought that <s>pradhāna</s> is limited — no, because there would be the consequence of destruction. If so, its destruction would follow, like milk. And thus the consequence of destruction of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Moreover, because of the consequence of infinite regress. A single Lord or yogin, through the power of will, has multiple bodies. That is untenable if [<s>pradhāna</s> is] limited. Or if a <s>pradhāna</s> is postulated for each body, there would be an infinite regress of <s>pradhānas</s>. Since the acceptance that a limited [<s>pradhāna</s>] is the cause of [limited] bodies makes postulating others purposeless, therefore <s>pradhāna</s> is indeed one. Therefore, the claim that there are <s>pradhānas</s> for each <s>puruṣa</s> is untenable. As for the statement that when the <s>pradhāna</s> of the one with the great body operates, the others also operate, and when it ceases, they also cease — to this we say: No, because of the absence of superiority. Just as the <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (knowers of the field), being without superiority, do not cause each other to operate — so too for these; or if they had superiority, the consequence would be the impossibility of <s>pradhāna</s>, due to unevenness. Therefore it is proper: a single <s>prakṛti</s> operates for the liberation of each <s>puruṣa</s>. // 56 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 57

children.text:
āha, tadanupapattirācetanyāt / ihācetanānāṃ ghaṭādīnāmuddiśya pravṛttiradṛṣṭā / sā cediyamacetanā prakṛtirasyā apyuddiśya puruṣārthaṃ pravṛttirnopapadyate / bhavati ceccaitanyaṃ tarhi prāptamasyā / tatra yaduktaṃ pratipuruṣavimokṣārtha prakṛteḥ pravṛttiriti etadayuktamiti /
  ucyate- na, dṛṣṭāntopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] No, because of the impossibility [of purposeful activity], since [<s>prakṛti</s>] is non-conscious. Here, the purposeful activity of non-conscious things like pots and the like is not observed. If this <s>prakṛti</s> is non-conscious, then its purposeful activity directed toward the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> is not possible either. And if it were conscious, then it would follow that it has consciousness. Therefore, the statement that <s>prakṛti</s> operates for the liberation of each <s>puruṣa</s> is untenable.
  [Reply:] No, because an illustration is available.
Just as the activity of non-conscious milk is for the nourishment of the calf,
so too the activity of <s>pradhāna</s> is for the liberation of <s>puruṣa</s>. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 57 //

children.text:
yathā kṣīramacetanaṃ vatsavivṛddhimuddiśya pravartate, evaṃ pradhānamapi puruṣavimokṣamuddiśya pravartate / na cāsya caitanyaṃ syāt / sādhyatvādayuktamiti cet syānmatam, sādhyametat kiṃ kṣīrasyoddiśya vatsavivṛddhiṃ pravṛttiḥ, atha neti ? tasmādudāharaṇaṃ sādhyatvādayuktamiti / etaccāyuktam / kasmāt ? tadabhāve 'bhāvāt tadbhāve ca bhāvāt / yatra nāsti vatsavivṛddhistatra na kṣīrasya pravṛttirupalabdhā / yatrāsti tatropalabdhā / yadyasmin sati bhavati tasya tadarthā pravṛttirdṛṣṭā / tadyathā ghaṭe kumbhakārasya / sa cāyamīdṛśo 'smākamuddeśo 'bhipretaḥ yaduta tādarthyam / tasmānnāstyudāharaṇasādhyatvamiti /
  asadbhāvābhidhānātsatkāryavirodha iti cenna, vyaktiparyāyatvāt / vyaktiparyāyo hi taditi śāstralokaprāmāṇyāt / śāstraṃ tāvat sattāmātro mahān vyaktimātra ityarthaḥ / loke 'pi nāstyasminkūpe salilamityucyate / na kvacidapi kūpe salilaṃ nāstyabhivyaktaṃ na tad bhavati / tasmānna satkāryavirodhaḥ /
  adṛṣṭapreraṇatvādasiddhiriti cedatha matam / dharmādharmapreritaṃ kṣīraṃ pravartate na vatsavivṛddhyarthamiti, tadapyayuktam / kasmāt ? doṣasāmyāt / dharmādharmāvacetanau vivṛddhikāle kṣīraṃ pravartayatastadavasāne ca nivartayataḥ / tasamāditthamapi parikalpyamāne samāno doṣaḥ / īśvarapreraṇāditi cet syānmatam īśvarastatra kṣīraṃ pravartayate vatsārthaṃ, na svayamiti / tadayuktam / kasmāt ? pratiṣedhāt / prākpratiṣiddhamīśvarakarma / tasmādidamapyayuktam / evaṃ cedavasthito dṛṣṭāntaḥ / vārṣagaṇānāṃ tu yathā strīpuṃśarīrāṇāmacetanānāmuddiśyetaretaraṃ pravṛttistathā pradhānasyetyayaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
  āha, kathamavagamyate tādarthyādutpannena vyaktena puruṣasya sambandho na punaḥ sānnidhyamātrāt, bhikṣuvaditi ?
  ucyate- na, anapavargaprasaṃgāt / sānnidhyamātrātpuruṣopabhogamabhyupagacchato nāpavargaprasaṃgaḥ syānnityasānnidhyāt / tasmādayuktametat /
  apravartayitāraṃ prati kāryakāraṇānāṃ pravṛttirayukteti cet syānmatam- apravartayitā kṛṣṇādīnāṃ bhikṣurato na teṣāmapi taṃ prati pravṛttiḥ / evamapravartayitā kāryakaraṇānāṃ puruṣaḥ / tasmātteṣāmapi taṃ prati pravṛttirayuktetyetadapyata evānaikāntikam / vatso hi kṣīrasyāpravartayitātha ca taṃ prati tasya pravṛttiḥ / tasmādyuktametapuruṣavimokṣārthā prakṛtteḥ pravṛttirna caitanyaprasaṃga iti // 57 //
children.translated_text:
Just as non-conscious milk operates directed toward the nourishment of the calf, so too <s>pradhāna</s> operates directed toward the liberation of <s>puruṣa</s>. And it would not be conscious. If it is objected that the illustration is what needs to be proved — one might think: it needs to be proved whether milk operates directed toward the nourishment of the calf or not. Therefore, the illustration is untenable because it requires proof. This too is untenable. Why? Because in its absence, there is absence [of the effect], and in its presence, there is presence. Where there is no nourishment of the calf, there the activity of milk is not observed. Where there is, there it is observed. When something occurs in the presence of [another thing], the activity of that is seen to be for the purpose of that — for example, the potter for the pot. And this is precisely the kind of purposiveness we intend. Therefore, the illustration does not need to be proved.
  If it is objected that the mention of non-existence contradicts the <s>satkāryavāda</s> (doctrine of pre-existent effect) — no, because [the word 'absence'] is a synonym for 'non-manifestation.' For 'that' [meaning absence] is a synonym for non-manifestation, on the authority of both the scripture and common usage. The scripture: '<s>Mahat</s> exists as mere being, as mere manifestation — this is the meaning.' And in common usage too, it is said 'there is no water in this well' — but in no well is water truly non-existent; it is merely not manifest. Therefore there is no contradiction with the <s>satkāryavāda</s>.
  If it is objected that there is no establishment because [milk] is impelled by the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) — the thought being that milk operates because it is impelled by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, not for the nourishment of the calf — that too is untenable. Why? Because the defect is equal. <s>Dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, being non-conscious, impel the milk at the time of nourishment and stop it at the end — therefore even under this interpretation, the same defect applies. If it is thought that God impels it — that God makes the milk operate for the calf, not by itself — that is untenable. Why? Because it was refuted. God's agency was refuted earlier. Therefore this too is untenable. Thus the illustration stands established. But according to the <s>Vārṣagaṇa</s> [school], just as the non-conscious bodies of women and men operate directed toward each other, so too [does] <s>pradhāna</s> — this is their illustration.
  [Objection:] How is it known that the relationship of <s>puruṣa</s> with the manifest [world], which is produced for its purpose, is [through purposiveness], and not merely through proximity, like a mendicant?
  [Reply:] No, because of the consequence of non-liberation. For one who accepts <s>puruṣa</s>'s enjoyment through mere proximity, the consequence of liberation would never arise, since the proximity is permanent. Therefore this is untenable.
  If it is objected that the activity of the body and instruments toward one who does not cause them to operate is untenable — the thought being: a mendicant does not cause <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the others to operate, therefore they do not operate for him; similarly, <s>puruṣa</s> does not cause the body and instruments to operate, therefore their operation for him is untenable — this too is inconclusive. For the calf does not cause the milk to operate, yet the milk operates for it. Therefore it is proper: the activity of <s>prakṛti</s> is for the liberation of <s>puruṣa</s>, and the consequence of consciousness does not arise. // 57 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 58

children.text: āha, na, apravṛttiprasaṃgāt / yadi pradhānasya puruṣakaivalyārthā pravṛttistena tadabhāve kaivalyaṃ siddhamevetyapravṛttiprasaṃgaḥ / atha kevale puruṣe pradhānaṃ pravartate na tarhyasya tadarthā pravṛttiriti /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] No, because of the consequence of non-activity. If the activity of <s>pradhāna</s> is for the isolation of <s>puruṣa</s>, then in the absence of that [activity], isolation is already established — hence the consequence of non-activity. Or if <s>pradhāna</s> operates while <s>puruṣa</s> is already isolated, then its activity is not for that purpose.
Just as people engage in actions for the sake of relieving their longing,
so too the unmanifest operates for the liberation of <s>puruṣa</s>. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 58 //

children.text: prāgevaitadapadiṣṭam- yathā dṛśyadarśanaśaktiyuktatvādanyatarābhāve ca tayorānarthakyātpradhānapuruṣayoritaretarasambandhaṃ pratyautsukyam / dṛṣṭā coparamārthāpi lokasyautsukyanivṛttyarthā pravṛttistathā pradhānasyāpyuparamārthā pravṛttiḥ / atha dṛśyadarśanaśaktyorautsukyanivṛttyarthaṃ pravartata ityekatra kṛtārthatvāditareṣvapravṛttiprasaṃga iti cet syādetat / pradhānamekasya puruṣasyātmānaṃ prakāśyoparamede dṛśyadarśanaśaktayorautsukyanivṛttirbhaviṣyati // 58 //
children.translated_text: This was explained earlier: since [<s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>] possess the powers of being-seen and seeing, and since in the absence of either, both would be purposeless, there is a longing for the mutual connection of <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>. And it is seen that the activity of the world, even though for the purpose of cessation, is for the sake of relieving longing — so too the activity of <s>pradhāna</s>, though for the purpose of cessation, [is for relieving longing]. If it is objected that, since [<s>prakṛti</s>] operates for the relief of the longing of the powers of being-seen and seeing, when it has accomplished its purpose for one [<s>puruṣa</s>], it should not operate for the others — this thought may arise: <s>pradhāna</s>, having displayed itself to one <s>puruṣa</s> and ceased, the relief of the longing of the powers of being-seen and seeing will have occurred. // 58 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 59

children.text:
apravṛttiścetyetadapi nopapannam / kasmāt ? dṛṣṭāntāntarasāmarthyāt / tadyathā kim ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text: And non-activity [as an objection] is not tenable either. Why? Because of the force of another illustration. Namely, what?

children.text: raṅgasya darśayitvā nivartate nartakī yathā nṛtyāt /
children.translated_text: Just as a dancer, having displayed [herself] to the audience, retires from the dance,
so too <s>prakṛti</s>, having displayed herself to <s>puruṣa</s>, withdraws. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 59 //

children.text: tatra nānāvarṇasvabhāvavijñānānāṃ prekṣārthināṃ puruṣāṇāṃ saṃghāto raṅga ityucyate / nartakyāśca tadārādhanā nṛttikriyānekapuruṣārthā / yadi vātra kaścid brūyāt nṛttācāryeṇa kuśīlavairvā dṛṣṭaiveyaṃ kasmānna nivartate ? katham ? akṛtārthatvāt / evaṃ sarvapuruṣāṇāṃ kāryakāraṇasambandhenautsukyavatāṃ nirākāṃkṣīkaraṇārthaṃ pravṛttā prakṛtiḥ kathamekasya puruṣasyautsukyanivṛttau kṛtārthā syāt ? tasmānnaikasya puruṣasyātmānaṃ prakāśya prakṛternivṛttiryukteti / atra ca-________
children.translated_text: There, the assembly of persons of various dispositions, natures, and cognitions, who desire to watch, is called the 'audience.' And the dancer's service to them — the act of dancing — serves the purpose of many persons. If someone here were to say: 'She has been seen by the dance-master or by the actors — why does she not retire?' — How? Because her purpose is not yet fulfilled. Similarly, <s>prakṛti</s>, having commenced activity for the purpose of rendering free from expectation all <s>puruṣas</s> who have longing through the connection with the body and instruments — how would her purpose be fulfilled by displaying herself to a single <s>puruṣa</s>? Therefore, it is not proper that <s>prakṛti</s> withdraws after displaying herself to a single <s>puruṣa</s>. And here: ________
<s>Kārikā</s> 64

children.text: ______ kāryakāraṇakriyāsākṣī puruṣaḥ / tasmādye bhautikāḥ śiraḥpāṇyādayo ye cāhaṃkārikāḥ śravaṇādayo vacanādayaḥ saṃkalpābhimānādhyavasāyāśca te lakṣaṇaviparyayāt- nāhaṃ nāṣṭau prakṛtayaḥ / tadetadevaṃ tattvānāmabhyāsaikāgramanaso yateḥ punaḥ punarabhyāsāt ekasyāpyasmitārūpasya parikalpitaviṣayabhedapratiṣedhamukhena
children.translated_text: ______ <s>Puruṣa</s> is the witness of the activity of the body and instruments. Therefore, those that are material — head, hands, and the like — and those derived from <s>ahaṃkāra</s> — hearing, speaking, deliberation, ego-sense, and determination — by the inversion of their characteristics [one realizes]: 'I am not [these], the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> are not [mine].' Thus, for the ascetic whose mind is focused through repeated practice of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles), through the repeated practice of negating the superimposed distinctions of objects even upon the single form of <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness) —
'I am not, not mine, not I' — completely, without remainder;
from the apprehension of the antidote, up to <s>prakṛti</s> [itself];
free from error;

children.text: pañcasrotaso 'syāvidyāparvaṇo nivṛtteḥ śāntaṃ dhruvaṃ sakalabhāvānubandhapratipakṣabhūtaṃ dharmādyāpyāyitasya buddhitattvasyāsandigdhamaviparītaṃ
children.translated_text: through the cessation of the five streams of [this] stage of ignorance, there arises for the one whose <s>buddhi</s>-principle is nourished by <s>dharma</s> and the rest, a peaceful, stable [knowledge] that is the antidote to all the bonds of existence — undoubting, non-erroneous —
pure and absolute knowledge arises. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 64 //

children.text:
āha, viśuddhaṃ kevalam / anyatarānabhidhānamarthābhedāt / yadeva viśuddhaṃ tadeva kevalamityarthābhedādanyataracchakyamavaktumiti /
  ucyate- guṇāntararūpanivṛttihetutvāt / rajastamodharmāṇāṃ tāvad grahaṇācchuddhaṃ saṃśayaviparyayavyatiriktaṃ ca kevalaṃ kṣetrajñaparijñāne 'pūrvameva iti // 64 //
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] 'Pure' and 'absolute' — one of the two need not be stated, since there is no difference in meaning. Since what is 'pure' is the same as 'absolute,' due to the identity of meaning, one of the two could be left unstated.
  [Reply:] Because [each] is the cause of removing a different form of the other <s>guṇas</s>. 'Pure' means free from the grasping of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> properties, and free from doubt and error. 'Absolute' means unprecedented in the knowledge of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field). // 64 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 67

children.text:
āha, tatsamakālameva śarīrasya pātaḥ prāpnoti / sati dha____vasthānenājñānahetukaṃ śarīramiti /
  ucyate- ajñānahetukaṃ śarīram / atha cāyaṃ nānātvadarśī /
children.translated_text:
[Objection:] At that very time, the fall of the body should follow. Since the body is caused by ignorance, given the presence of [knowledge]______
  [Reply:] The body is caused by ignorance. And yet this [liberated person] sees multiplicity.
When <s>dharma</s> and the rest are no longer causes,
[the liberated one] remains, sustained by the body through the force of <s>saṃskāra</s> (residual impressions), like the turning of a potter's wheel. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 67 //

children.text: ya___ śarīrāntaropārjitā dharmādayo na tāvatkāraṇam / buddhi___mupasaṃprāptā akṛtārthatvād buddhiśca pradhānaṃ tadā tiṣṭhatyayaṃ nānātvadarśī tasya saṃskārasya sāmarthyāt / ko dṛṣṭāntaḥ ? cakrabhramavaddhṛtaśarīraḥ / tadyathā kumbhakāraprayatnaviśiṣṭena daṇḍena ghaṭādiniṣpattiyogyakriyā cakrasya bhramaḥ / tena tulyaṃ cakrabhramavat / yathā cakrabhramaṇaṃ ghaṭārtham / niṣpanne ghaṭādiniṣpattiyogyakriyā cakrasya bhramaḥ / tena tulyaṃ cakrabhramavat / yathā cakrabhramaṇaṃ ghaṭārtham / niṣpanne ghaṭe pūrvasaṃskārānurodhānna nivartate na ca tadā nivṛttamiti kṛtvā saṃskārakṣaye 'pyavatiṣṭhate, evaṃ samyagdarśanārthaṃ śarīraṃ samyagjñānādhigame 'pi na nivartate pūrvasaṃskāravaśāt / na ca tadā nivṛttamiti kṛtvā saṃskārakṣaye 'pyavasthāpyata iti // 67 //
children.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s> and the like acquired in _____ another body are not yet the cause. <s>Buddhi</s> _____ having attained [its purpose], since the purpose is not yet fulfilled, and <s>buddhi</s> [being] <s>pradhāna</s> — then this one who sees multiplicity persists through the force of that <s>saṃskāra</s> (residual impression). What is the illustration? Like the turning of a wheel, sustained by the body. Just as the turning of a potter's wheel — the rotation of the wheel suitable for producing pots and the like, [set in motion] by the potter's effort applied through the stick — by analogy with that: like the turning of a wheel. Just as the wheel turns for the purpose of the pot, and when the pot is completed, it does not stop due to the momentum of the prior impression — and one should not think that because it has not stopped [it means] it has not ceased [in purpose] — for even when the impression is exhausted, it [eventually] comes to rest. So too, the body [exists] for the purpose of right knowledge; even when right knowledge is attained, it does not cease due to the force of prior impressions. And one should not think that because it has not ceased [it means] the purpose continues — for even when the impressions are exhausted, it [eventually] comes to rest. // 67 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 68

children.text: yadā tu saṃskārakṣaye tannimittasya śarīrasya bhedaḥ, ataḥ
children.translated_text: But when, through the exhaustion of <s>saṃskāras</s> (residual impressions), the dissolution of the body caused by them [occurs], therefore:
When the separation of the body is attained,

children.text:
dharmādharmau kṛtārthau kāraṇe buddhilakṣaṇe layaṃ gacchataḥ / yaścāsya bhūtāvayavaḥ śarīrārambhakaḥ sa sarvabhūteṣu bhūtāni tanmātreṣu, indriyāṇi tanmātrāṇi cāhaṃkāre, ahaṃkāro buddhau buddhiravyakte / seyaṃ tattvānupūrvī tadarthapradhānādutpannā parisamāpte punaḥ pradhāne pralayaṃ gacchatīti / pradhānamapyarthavaśādevāsya śarīrāṇi teṣu teṣu jātyantaraparivarteṣu karoti / sa cāryaścaritārthaḥ /
  ataḥ
children.translated_text:
<s>Dharma</s> (virtue) and <s>adharma</s> (vice), having accomplished their purpose, dissolve into their cause, which is characterized by <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). And the elemental portion of his [body] that constitutes the body — those elements [dissolve] into the <s>tanmātra</s>s (subtle elements), the senses and <s>tanmātra</s>s into <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> into <s>buddhi</s>, <s>buddhi</s> into the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>). This succession of <s>tattva</s>s (principles), having arisen from <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) whose principal [purpose] is the goal [of <s>Puruṣa</s>], when completed, dissolves again into <s>pradhāna</s>. <s>Pradhāna</s> too, driven by purpose, creates bodies for him in the various transmigrations from one birth to another. And that is the noble one whose purpose has been accomplished.
  Therefore:
Upon the cessation of <s>pradhāna</s>, because its purpose has been accomplished,

children.text: atīndriyamasaṃvedya laghu sarvatra sannihitaṃ praśastamanirmitaṃ viśuddhamakṣayaṃ niratiśayam
children.translated_text: [<s>Puruṣa</s>] attains [a state that is] beyond the senses, not experienced [by the senses], light, omnipresent, praiseworthy, uncreated, pure, imperishable, unsurpassed,
definitive, absolute, fearless — [this is] <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 68 //

children.text: etaccāvasthānaṃ bauddhairnirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇalakṣaṇamapavargo vyākhyātaḥ / etatparaṃ brahmaṃ dhruvamamalamabhayamatra sarveṣāṃ guṇadharmāṇāṃ pratipralayaḥ / etatprāpya sarvāyāsaiḥ sarvabandhanairanādikālapravṛttarāgadveṣaviyukto mukto bhavati / etadarthaṃ brāhmaṇā dayitaputradāradhanasambandhamapahāya guruśuśrūṣāparāḥ śarīramaraṇyeṣu yātayanti / kathaṃ nāmaikāntikamātyantikaṃ ca kaivalyaṃ syāditi yatraivotthānaṃ śāstrasya tatraivopasaṃhāra ācāryeṇa kṛtaḥ // 68 //
children.translated_text: This state of abiding has been explained by the Buddhists as <s>apavarga</s> (final release) characterized by <s>nirvāṇa</s> (extinction) without remainder of substrate (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>). This is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, permanent, pure, fearless — here all the properties of the <s>guṇa</s>s undergo dissolution. Having attained this, one becomes liberated from all exertions, all bonds, and the attachment and aversion that have been operating since beginningless time. For this purpose, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, having abandoned the company of beloved sons, wives, and wealth, devoted to the service of the teacher, mortify the body in forests — [asking]: How may there be definitive and absolute <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation)? The teacher has made the conclusion [of the text] at the very point where the text began. // 68 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 69

children.text:
āha, kimarthaṃ punaridaṃ śāstraṃ kena vā pūrvaṃ prakāśitamiti ?
  ucyate- yaduktaṃ kimarthamiti-
children.translated_text:
[The objector] asks: For what purpose is this scripture? And by whom was it first revealed?
  It is replied: As for what was asked 'for what purpose' —
This [scripture] is for the purpose of the goal of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the self).

children.text:
kathaṃ nāmājñānavaśāttatsaṃskāropanipatitānāṃ prāṇināmapavargaḥ syādityevamarthamidaṃ śāstraṃ vyākhyātam /
  yattūktaṃ keneti, ucyate-
children.translated_text:
How may there be final release (<s>apavarga</s>) for beings who, under the sway of ignorance, are beset by the dispositions produced by that [ignorance]? — it is for this purpose that this scripture has been expounded.
  As for what was asked 'by whom,' it is replied:
It was taught by the supreme <s>Ṛṣi</s> (sage) as a secret.

children.text:
guhyamiti gūhanīyam / rahasyamakṛtātmanāṃ yamaniyameṣvanavasthitānāmādarādapyanadhyeyam / paramarṣirbhagavānsāṃsiddhikairdharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryairāviṣṭapiṇḍo viśvāgrajaḥ kapilamuniḥ / tena kapilamuninā samākhyātam /
  samyagākhyātam, cirābhyastasya vidyāsrotaso nirvacanasāmarthyāt syādetat, kathamidaṃ guhyamiti ? ucyate- kathaṃ vedaṃ guhyaṃ na syāt ?
  bhavāgrotpannairapi sanakasanātanasanandanasanatkumāraprabhṛtibhiranityānāṃ
children.translated_text:
'Secret' means 'to be concealed.' It is a mystery that should not be studied, even with respect, by those who are unprepared and not established in <s>yama</s>s (restraints) and <s>niyama</s>s (observances). The supreme <s>Ṛṣi</s> is the blessed one, endowed with innate <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, detachment, and mastery, the first-born of the universe, the sage <s>Kapila</s>. It was taught by that sage <s>Kapila</s>.
  It was 'properly taught' (<s>samyag ākhyāta</s>), because of the capacity of exposition arising from long-practiced knowledge. [One might ask:] If so, how is this 'secret'? It is replied: How would the <s>Veda</s> not be secret?
  Even by those born at the beginning of creation — <s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, <s>Sanandana</s>, <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, and others — the non-eternal [aspects]
and the abiding, arising, and dissolution of beings are contemplated there. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 69 //

children.text:
tatra sthitistāvadrūpapravṛttiphalanirdeśenotpattirapi prakṛtermahānityādiḥ / pralayo 'pyavibhāgādvaiśvarūpyasyeti vacanāt / autsukyānuparamātprakṛtipuruṣayoḥ / sthitirutpattirdṛśyadarśanaśaktayoḥ sāpekṣatvāt / tathā coktaṃ-
  puruṣasya darśanārthaḥ kaivalyārthastathā pradhānasya /
  paṅgvandhavadubhayorapi saṃyogastatkṛtaḥ sargaḥ // iti (
children.translated_text: There, 'abiding' consists in the indication of the form, activity, and fruit [of creation]; 'arising' too — from <s>Prakṛti</s> [come] <s>mahat</s> (the great one) and the rest; and 'dissolution' —
<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 21
'Dissolution' is: when bodily separation is reached, upon the cessation of <s>pradhāna</s> because its purpose has been accomplished —
<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 68

Or alternatively, because of the refutation of momentary destruction, [there is] arising through transformation rather than the appearance of what was previously non-existent, [and this is] not from no cause — because of the impossibility of [production] without reason. And dissolution too, not from another cause but from their own nature — [referring to] even manifest beings that have attained completion. Thus <s>mahat</s> and the rest are also included.
  [The objector] says: Then <s>Puruṣa</s> and the rest are excluded. How is the word 'beings' (<s>bhūta</s>) [to be understood]?
  It is replied: Because it serves to negate the unreal. Whatever is real (<s>bhūta</s>) — of all of that, abiding, etc. are stated here. Because there is no distinction in the refutation of production and destruction. Even so, production and dissolution would apply to <s>Puruṣa</s> and the rest too. What is the reason? Because of non-distinction.
  It is replied: Qualification belongs to what is possible. In that case, there is only abiding for <s>Puruṣa</s> and the rest. For the others, however, there are abiding, arising, and dissolution — this we shall understand. // 69 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 70

children.text:
āha, kasmai punaridaṃ śāstraṃ paramarṣiṇā prakāśitamiti ?
  ucyate-
children.translated_text:
[The objector] asks: To whom, then, was this scripture revealed by the supreme <s>Ṛṣi</s>?
  It is replied:
The <s>muni</s> (sage), out of compassion, bestowed this most pure and supreme [teaching] upon <s>Āsuri</s>.

children.text:
tatra pavitraṃ pāvanāt / agryaṃ sarvaduḥkhakṣapaṇasamarthatvāt / pavitrāntarāṇi punarekadeśaṃ kṣālayantyadhamarṣaṇagaṅgādīni / tasmādidamevāgryaṃ munirāsuraye 'nukampayā pradadau /
  āha, sampradānasyākasmikatvam, dharmādinimittānupapatteḥ / na tāvatparamarṣerdharmārthaṃ śāstrapradānamupapadyate, phalenānabhiṣvaṅgāt / nārthakāmārtham, śiṣyāṇāmanāyāsaprasaṃgāt / na mokṣārtham, sāṃsiddhikenaiva jñānena tatprāpteḥ / tasmādviparītārthāsambhavāt pariśeṣādakasmādācāryaḥ śāstranidhānaṃ pradadāviti /
  ucyate- nākasmāt, kiṃ tarhi anukampayā pradadau / ādhyātmikādhidaivikādhibhautikairduḥkhaiḥ pīḍyamānamāsurimupalabhya svātmani ca jñānasāmarthyātsati kāryakāraṇasamprayoge duḥkhānāmapravṛttiṃ parijñāya śiṣyaguṇāṃśca kathaṃ nāma yathā mama sukhaduḥkheṣu jñānopanipātātsāmyamevamāsurerapi syāttaddvāreṇānyeṣāmapi puruṣāṇāmevamanukampayā bhagavānparamarṣiḥ śāstramākhyātavān /
  yathā ca paramarṣirāsuraye tathā
children.translated_text:
There, 'pure' (<s>pavitra</s>) — because it purifies. 'Supreme' (<s>agrya</s>) — because of its capacity to eliminate all suffering. Other purifiers — <s>aghamarṣaṇa</s> [hymn], the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and the like — cleanse only a portion. Therefore, this alone is supreme. The <s>muni</s>, out of compassion, bestowed [it] upon <s>Āsuri</s>.
  [The objector] says: The bestowal upon the recipient is without [specific] cause, because of the untenable nature of reasons such as <s>dharma</s>, etc. First, it is not tenable that the supreme <s>Ṛṣi</s> bestowed the scripture for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, because of his non-attachment to results. Nor for the sake of material gain or pleasure, because of the consequence that his disciples would not need to exert themselves. Nor for the sake of liberation, because that is attained through innate knowledge alone. Therefore, since contrary purposes are impossible, by elimination, the teacher bestowed the treasure of scripture without [any specific] cause.
  It is replied: Not without cause; rather, he bestowed it out of compassion. Having perceived <s>Āsuri</s> being afflicted by sufferings that are <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self), <s>ādhidaivika</s> (pertaining to destiny), and <s>ādhibhautika</s> (pertaining to other beings), and having understood through the power of knowledge within himself that when there is the conjunction of cause and effect, there is non-arising of suffering — and recognizing the qualities of his disciple — [thinking]: 'How may it be that just as, for me, through the impact of knowledge upon pleasure and pain, there is equanimity, so too for <s>Āsuri</s>, and through him for other <s>Puruṣa</s>s as well' — thus out of compassion the blessed supreme <s>Ṛṣi</s> taught the scripture.
  And just as the supreme <s>Ṛṣi</s> [taught] <s>Āsuri</s>, so too
<s>Āsuri</s> too
[taught] it to the tenth one, to the blessed <s>Kumāra</s> —

children.text:
pañcaśikhāya
  tena ca bahudhā kṛtaṃ tantram || 70 ||
children.translated_text:
<s>Pañcaśikha</s>.
  And by him the doctrine (<s>tantra</s>) was elaborated in many ways. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 70 //

children.text: bahubhyo janakavaśiṣṭhādibhyaḥ samākhyātam / asya tu śāstrasya bhagavato 'gre pravṛttatvānna śāstrāntaravad vaṃśaḥ śakyo varṣaśatasahasrairapyākhyātum // 70 //
children.translated_text: It was taught to many — <s>Janaka</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and others. But since this scripture originated before the blessed one [<s>Brahmā</s>], its lineage cannot be recounted even in hundreds of thousands of years. // 70 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 71
In brief, two [main lines] — the <s>Hāritavāddhalikairātapaurikārṣabheśvarapañcādhikaraṇapatañ</s>[jali] —
transmitted through the succession of disciples,

children.text:
bhagavānīśvarakṛṣṇaśca sāhāyakaṃ śāstram /
  pūrvācāryasūtraprabandhe gurulāghavamanādriyamāṇaḥ paurastyānyākhyānavyā___na garbhamatipramādaṃ dadātīti granthabhūyastvamupajāyate / taccedānīntanaiḥ prāṇibhiralpatvādāyuṣo granthata eva na sūpapādaṃ kiṃ punaḥ śravaṇaprayogābhyām / āha ca- caturbhiḥ prakārairvidyā sūpayuktā bhavati- āgamakālena svādhyāyakālena prayogakālena ca / tatra cāsyāgamanakālenaivāyuḥ paryupayuktaṃ syāttataśca śāstrānarthakyam / ityasya mandadhiyāmapyāśu grahaṇadhāraṇaprayogasampatsyāditi ṣaṣṭitantrādupākhyānagāthāvyavahitāni vākyānyekata upamṛdya śiṣyānukampārthaṃ yāvat
children.translated_text:
and the blessed <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s> also [composed] a supporting treatise.
  Not caring about the prolixity and conciseness in the sūtra-composition of the previous teachers, the eastern narratives and the digressions give rise to excessive prolixity in the text. And this, for beings of the present day, because of the shortness of their lifespan, is not easy to accomplish even from the text alone, let alone through hearing and practice. And it is said: Knowledge is properly applied through four means: the time for reception, the time for self-study, and the time for practice. And the time for reception alone would exhaust the lifespan, and consequently the scripture would be purposeless. Therefore, so that even those of dull intellect may quickly attain the success of comprehension, retention, and practice, [<s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>], having gathered together the sentences from the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> that were interspersed with narratives and verses, out of compassion for his disciples, [composed this] in as much [as needed].
By <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, this [was composed] in <s>āryā</s> [meter],
in seventy [verses],
condensed by one of noble intellect,
who was engaged in the welfare of all beings,
having properly understood the established doctrine. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 71 //

children.text: kathaṃ cāsya samyaksiddhāntavijñānasyāpyanekagranthaśatasahasrākhyeyaṃ sāṃkhyapadārthaṃ satattvamakhaṇḍamācāryāṇāṃ saptatyā saṃkṣiptavān // 71 //
children.translated_text: And how has one who properly understood the established doctrine condensed the Sāṃkhya categories — which, in their entirety and without omission, would require hundreds of thousands of texts to expound — into seventy [verses] for the teachers? // 71 //
<s>Kārikā</s> 72
And he says:
The subjects in the seventy [verses] are indeed the subjects of the entire <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>,
except for illustrative stories and without the refutation of opposing doctrines. // <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 72 //

children.text: yataśca nārāyaṇamanujanakavaśiṣṭhadvaipāyanapravṛttibhirācāryaiḥ pradhānapuruṣādayaḥ padārthāḥ parigṛhītāścopadiṣṭāśca praśastāścātaḥ svabhāvataḥ prasiddhamaiśvaryasya phalata ṛddhyā āryamārgamalaṃkartumiti bhagavadīśvarakṛṣṇena padārthasvarūpanirūpaṇanipuṇasāramatinā paramarṣyādiyathoktāgamena pramāṇatrayaṃ puraskṛtya tarkadṛśā vicāraḥ kṛtaḥ / na cāsya mūlakanakapiṇḍasyeva svalpamapi doṣajātamastīti // 72 //
children.translated_text: And since the categories — <s>pradhāna</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, and the rest — have been embraced, taught, and praised by the teachers whose lineage includes <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Manu</s>, <s>Janaka</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Dvaipāyana</s>, and <s>Pravṛtti</s>, therefore, by the blessed <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s> — who by nature has well-known mastery, who by result has accomplishment, who is skilled in ascertaining the essential nature of the categories, whose intellect has the essence of sharpness — with the scripture as received from the supreme <s>Ṛṣi</s> and others, placing the three means of valid knowledge at the forefront, an investigation has been made with the eye of reasoning in order to adorn the noble path. And of this [work], like a base of pure gold, there is not even the slightest trace of defect. // 72 //
And he says:
For the purpose of pacifying the darkness of ignorance, fallen from the moon of the <s>Ṛṣi</s>s,
the moonlight of knowledge is obscured by the turbid waters of the holy places.
Therefore, by the good and the unconfused, [let this] dispeller of the darkness of false views,
this illuminator of creation, this <s>Yuktidīpikā</s> (Lamp of Reasoning), be upheld!

children.text: sphuṭābhidheyā madhurāpi bhāratī manīṣiṇo nopakhalaṃ virājate /
children.translated_text: A speech that is clear in meaning and sweet does not shine on a whetstone for the wise.
Even though the sun's rays are thin-wombed, at the approach of winter they become tepidly warm.

children.text: nayanti santaśca yataḥ svaśaktito guṇaṃ pareṣāṃ tanumapyudāratām /
children.translated_text: Noble ones, according to their own capacity, bring even a small virtue of others to greatness.

children.text: iti prayātveṣa mama śramaḥ satāṃ vicāraṇānugrahamātrapātratām //
children.translated_text: Therefore, may this effort of mine attain the status of being a vessel merely for the gracious examination of the virtuous!

children.text: // iti yuktidīpikāyāṃ sāṃkhyasaptatipaddhatau caturthaṃ prakaraṇamekādaśaṃ cāhnikaṃ sampūrṇam //
children.translated_text: // Thus ends the fourth section and eleventh lesson in the <s>Yuktidīpikā</s>, following the method of the seventy <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [kārikās]. //
This is the composition of the revered <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s> (?)
